author: souhailbourhim
body:
Builds Phase 4B — SPEC §7.3's governed LLM stage and §8's bitemporal macro store, the two
things §2 calls differentiators and ADR-0008 split Phase 4 to protect.

**The acceptance is not met, and cannot be yet.** Three gates, all external, all verified by
probe rather than assumed:

| Gate | State |
|---|---|
| ADR-0003's model pin | **Ollama is not running.** Probed `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, the WSL2 gateway and `host.docker.internal` on :11434 — all refused |
| A FRED API key | **Required.** The live endpoint answers HTTP 400 `Variable api_key is not set` — checked before a line of the poller was written |
| 30 days of bronze | **Five days.** Staging spans 2026-08-18 → 2026-08-22, so the window closes 2026-09-17 at the earliest |

Neither of the first two blocks construction — every module is tested against `respx` and
`moto` — and the code refuses to run rather than producing garbage under them.

## What is actually in here

Two commits build 4B. **Four fix things that were merged, tested, and had never once run.**
That second half is the more useful half of this PR, so it is first.

---

# Four things that shipped and never executed

Every one passed its tests, passed CI, and applied cleanly. All four were found by *running*
things, and three of the four were found only because the first one forced a look.

### 1. `make clean` had silently killed ingestion for ten hours

`commit_staged` failed on every run from 14:05 UTC on 2026-08-22. `make clean` deletes
`.cache`, which is bind-mounted into the Airflow containers, and deleting the host directory
while they are up breaks the mount **at the inode level** — the container's view survives as a
directory with **link count 0** and every `mkdir` inside it fails with ENOENT.

The Makefile already carried a comment saying precisely this, with the recovery command, since
2.E. **A comment is not a guard**, and this failure is invisible: nothing alerts on a local
DAG failing, so ten consecutive failures produced no signal anywhere.

No data was lost — the pollers are Lambdas and kept staging to S3, so 1,738 objects merged in
one catch-up run. That is Phase 1's replay guarantee working: staging is a queue and the MERGE
is on `ingest_id`. Cost: ~$0.002 of re-downloaded staging, because `clean` had also wiped the
read-once cache that normally makes a re-sync free.

**The first version of my guard was wrong the same way, within the hour.** It protected
`.cache` and nothing else — but compose also mounts `./data` and `./out`, and running
`make clean` to test the guard broke both. `/opt/signal/out` is where the 07:00 brief writes
its HTML: the send would have failed on the first morning of 4A's acceptance, caused by the
fix meant to prevent exactly that. `MOUNTED_PATHS` is a variable tracking the `volumes:` block
now, because **a guard derived from an incident is only as good as its inventory.**

### 2. `brief`, `market`, `maintenance` and `resolve` had never run

Airflow pauses newly-discovered DAGs by default. Nothing here overrode it.

So **4A's entire local half was built, merged, deployed and inert.** The AWS half — nine
Lambdas on EventBridge — ran the whole time, which is exactly why nothing looked wrong: bronze
kept filling, the brief stayed buildable by hand, and the one thing SPEC §12's 4A acceptance
turns on (a mail at 07:00) had never happened once.

All four unpaused; `DAGS_ARE_PAUSED_AT_CREATION=false` so it cannot recur. The trade goes the
other way for a half-written DAG and that is the lesser failure: a run that fails loudly beats
a phase that quietly was never running, and `catchup=False` bounds what a premature start can
do.

**Verified, first-ever runs:** `market` → 1,134 rows across 18 tickers. `resolve` → success.
`ingest_monitor` → success, 8 sources 0 not ok.

### 3. `gold.brief_items` did not exist, and 4A's acceptance turns on it

`information_schema` said it plainly: **the `gold` schema held zero tables.** The feedback
loop — *"you read it three mornings running and the feedback loop records your marks"* — had
never worked.

The DDL was written in Trino's dialect rather than Athena's, wrong in three independent ways:

| Wrong | Right | Athena's complaint |
|---|---|---|
| `WITH (table_type = 'ICEBERG')` | `LOCATION '...' TBLPROPERTIES (...)` | `no viable alternative at input` |
| `map(varchar, double)` | `map<string, double>` | `no viable alternative at input` |
| `rank integer`, `id varchar` | `rank int`, `id string` | `type expected at the position 0 of 'integer'` |

All three are valid Trino **in a SELECT or INSERT**. The dialects meet inside one module,
which is why `MAP(ARRAY[...], ARRAY[...])` is correct twelve lines below a `map(...)` that is
not.

**Every test passed** because the fake Athena client records SQL without parsing it — what
makes it good for asserting on the DELETE's WHERE clause and exactly why it cannot see a
syntax error. One assertion was *actively pinning the bug*, checking for the unquoted
`table_type = 'ICEBERG'` only the broken form produces.

Then the 02:00 sweep turned out to fail on it too, unrelatedly: Athena stamps every Iceberg
table it creates with `write.object-storage.path`, which the pinned Iceberg runtime has
deprecated and **raises** on. It cannot be fixed where the table is created — Athena rejects
that key in `CREATE TABLE` *and* in `ALTER TABLE UNSET`, both verified — so `maintain_table`
drops it before compacting.

**Verified against the account:** brief builds end to end (2,979 clusters, 1,031 company
links, 8 sources 0 not ok, 10 items recorded), `signal feedback <id> up` records and reads
back, `gold.brief_items` compacts 3 files → 2.

### 4. `resolve` could never have found its entity dictionary

Found by pre-flighting a DAG *before* triggering it, having learned the lesson three times
already.

`DEFAULT_PATH` was relative, so it resolved against the process's cwd — `/opt/airflow` inside
the containers. And `./warehouse` was not mounted at all, so no path would have worked.
`resolve_dag` would have raised `FileNotFoundError` on its first run; it never did, because it
had been paused since 3.C and Phase 3 ran the resolver locally from the repo root.

**Compose already knew about this class of bug** — it sets `SIGNAL_DATA_ROOT`,
`SIGNAL_OUT_ROOT` and `SIGNAL_CACHE_ROOT` absolutely under a comment saying exactly why. The
dictionary path was the one relative path with no setting behind it, so it was invisible to
that fix.

`tests/test_compose_paths.py` pins the class, not the instance: every relative path setting
must be overridden absolutely, the dictionary must exist, and `MOUNTED_PATHS` must cover every
mounted directory `clean` could delete. It asserts the defaults are still relative, so it
cannot quietly become vacuous.

---

# Phase 4B

## The corpus reshaped the enrichment stage before it was written

Measured against the deployed lake first:

| Bucket | Clusters |
|---|---:|
| `sec.gov` | **5,818** |
| other web | 3,957 |
| tech press | 411 |

**57% of clusters are SEC filings**, every one single-article, and a sample of eighty heads
shows what they are: `ABS-EE`, `N-PX`, `NPORT-P`, `424B2` — routine fund administration that
will never appear in a brief.

So the literal reading of §7.3 ("run against cluster heads") would spend **most of every
inference budget on documents nobody reads**. Enrichment runs over the *ranked* head instead —
which is what ADR-0003's capacity paragraph already assumed when it sized the measurement at
"a 40-head batch". No circularity: `WEIGHTS` has no enrichment component.

That also drove the topic enum. It is fitted to this corpus, not borrowed: `sec-filing` exists
because 57% of clusters are one, and the editorial half leans `ai-ml`/`software-engineering`/
`security` because that is what HN and tech press actually publish. A taxonomy led by
`earnings`/`m-and-a`/`funding` would mislabel most of it.

## Decisions worth review

- **One Ollama call per cluster, not three.** §7.3 says "three jobs"; §9's schem

author: claude-for-evoskamp
body:
## Summary

The review pipeline's second fan-out — one `counterexample-verifier`
per disproved theorem — had no deadline. Step 9 requires a verifier
verdict on every `DISPROVED` theorem, and its disposition table had no
row for a verifier that never reports, so a verifier that dies without
notifying parks the round before step 10, the same way an unreturned
disprover did before #317.

## What changed

`plugins/sdlc/agents/theorem-based-pr-reviewer.md`:

- Step 8 states the verifier wait as a resume loop — one verdict per
  `<task-notification>`, then end the turn — and a turn ended with any
  verifier outstanding reads as an in-progress status carrying no
  verdict block, tally, or findings.
- That wait is bounded at 15 minutes after the last verifier spawn.
  The reasoning is stated inline: no verifier measurement exists, a
  verifier's work is a strict subset of a disprover's (one
  counterexample against one head tree, no search), so the disprover's
  measured worst case is reused rather than a shorter deadline guessed
  from the subset relation — the cost of guessing short is `TaskStop`ing
  a verifier that was about to report, which drops a real check.
- Step 9's disposition table gains the row that disposition settles:
  state `disproved`, `state-detail: unverified`, no finding, no
  severity, named in the posted review, live again next round. The row
  carries its reasoning inline, naming why the malformed-twice row
  (a returned artifact that exhausted the re-spawn remedy, resolving
  toward filing) and the unsettled rows (right severity outcome, false
  state) were both rejected.
- `TaskStop`'s sanctioned use extends to a verifier past that deadline
  and no further.

Swept the prose the added row would have falsified:

- The "these last two rows" sentence and step 9's stamping sentence now
  address rows by name rather than by position.
- The disposition table's disprover-deadline row and step 11's cleanup
  sentence say which of step 8's two deadlines they mean.
- The review body's *Disproved theorems* section covers an entry whose
  verifier never reported — consequence as the disprover proposed it,
  no `→ Finding N` cross-link — which keeps sections 4/6/7 a partition
  of the round's live list.
- "The theorem records block" documents `unverified` as a
  `state-detail` value on a `disproved` record, and a nearby sentence
  that used "unverified" loosely for a malformed disprover report now
  says "malformed".
- The report-back tally counts the unverified theorems and states they
  never reach severity.

`docs/plugin-authoring-constraints.md` → "Fanning out parallel agents:
one home for the procedure": the generic deadline paragraph was written
for a single fan-out and named review's disprover deadline as its
worked instance. It now states that a procedure fanning out twice needs
a deadline on each fan-out, why the second is the easier one to leave
unbounded, and that an unmeasured second stage reuses the first's
measurement rather than deriving a shorter deadline from doing less
work.

## Sweep decisions

- `plugins/sdlc/skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md` and
  `plugins/sdlc/skills/git-review-pr/SKILL.md` describe the review's
  stages but state no deadline and no disposition vocabulary, so
  neither needed an edit.
- `plugins/sdlc/skills/theorem-agents-interface/SKILL.md` owns what a
  consequence class means for a report an agent *returns*. This
  disposition exists because no report arrived, and it assigns no
  class, so nothing there changed.
- No step was inserted, so the reviewer's bare step-number references
  needed no renumbering sweep.

## Testing

`npx markdownlint-cli2` is clean on both edited Markdown files, and
`plugins/sdlc/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` parses. The repo has no test
suite covering these files — they are agent prose, exercised by a real
review round.

`plugins/sdlc` version bumped 0.24.0 → 0.24.1.

Closes #331

author: nightloot-jpg
body:
### Cambios
- Las fotos nuevas ya no se suben a Supabase Storage.
- `PhotoUploader` solicita una URL firmada a la nueva Edge Function `r2-media` y sube el archivo directamente a Cloudflare R2.
- Se mantiene Supabase únicamente para guardar metadatos en la tabla `photos`.
- Límite de imagen aumentado a 60 MB.
- Nueva función `r2-media` reutiliza las credenciales R2 existentes y permite `photos`, `covers` y `avatars`.
- Seguridad: la función valida JWT, usuario propietario y tipos/tamaño de imagen.
- La función usa `R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` para devolver la URL pública del archivo.

### Importante
La Edge Function `r2-media` ya está desplegada en el proyecto Supabase. Para que las fotos se vean tras recargar la página, `R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` debe apuntar al dominio público/custom domain del bucket R2. Las credenciales R2 existentes se reutilizan.

author: josecxz
body:
Al tirar de las dos escenas que la primera version senalaba como nuevas resulto que las dos estan PERFECTAS. `Dark Queen [4K]` (3459506773) mide 4.23 de media y `Samurai - Cyberpunk 2077` (2311315748) 5.39 ---por debajo de tres de las cuatro rotas conocidas--- y son obras deliberadamente negras: una corona y un demonio encendidos sobre penumbra. Comparadas con el preview de su autor, nuestro render coincide.

O sea que cualquier umbral absoluto que cace las rotas se lleva por delante el arte oscuro: las rotas miden 0.00-4.07 y estas 4.23-5.39. No hay hueco.

Lo que si separa es el PREVIEW del autor, que es un fotograma de la escena tal como debe verse. La razon `nuestro / preview` no solapa:

    2968771936  0.00 / 144.63 = 0.00   rota
    3577990983  1.95 /  68.07 = 0.03   rota
    1518454472  3.88 /  70.09 = 0.06   rota
    3624053922  4.07 /  70.67 = 0.06   rota
    3459506773  4.23 /  11.32 = 0.37   arte oscuro, correcta
    2311315748  5.39 /  21.29 = 0.25   arte oscuro, correcta

Se marca apagada por debajo del 15% de su preview. El preview es material del autor ---a veces un recorte o arte promocional en vez de una captura fiel--- asi que la razon es aproximada y el umbral, generoso; sin preview se cae al criterio absoluto de media < 8.

Pasada completa con el criterio nuevo: 4 apagadas ---las cuatro ya conocidas--- 3 sospechosas, 0 regresiones, 0 que no rendericen, en 316 s.

author: crazz
body:
## Summary

Fixes the repeated `System.OutOfMemoryException` container kills during geocoding reported in #13. The container climbed to ~1.5 GB over 1–2 days and was OOM-killed; logs pointed at `FindCountry` and NTS `DistanceOp` on country boundaries.

`FindBundledCountryFromMemory` tested containment as:

```csharp
PreparedGeometry.Covers(point) || Geometry.Distance(point) <= 0.00015
```

The STRtree returns every country whose **bounding box** contains the point, and country bounding boxes hugely overstate their footprint — antimeridian crossings (USA/Alaska, Russia, NZ, Fiji) and distant overseas territories (France, UK, Netherlands, Denmark, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Chile) make several very large countries candidates for most points on earth. Every candidate that failed `Covers()` then paid a full `Geometry.Distance()`.

That path is worse than it looks:

- `Geometry.Distance` computes an **exact** minimum, so it cannot short-circuit at the 16 m tolerance.
- NTS `DistanceOp.ComputeMinDistance` reads `LineString.Coordinates` per ring, and that property is `_points.ToCoordinateArray()` — **a fresh `Coordinate[]` copy on every call, no caching**. The NTS source comments the inner loop `// brute force approach!`.

So ordinary lookups deep-copied entire country coastlines onto the large object heap, which isn't compacted. RSS ratcheted up until the kernel intervened.

### Changes

1. **Two-pass containment** — `Covers()` alone first; the boundary tolerance runs only if nothing contained the point.
2. **Indexed tolerance test** — a small rectangle instead of `Distance()`, reusing the prepared geometry index and routing through NTS `RectangleIntersects`. Applied to the equivalent per-row checks in `OvertureDataAccess` and `GadmDivisionsService` too.
3. **Workstation GC + `mem_limit`** — Server GC (the ASP.NET default) allocates one heap per core and collects lazily; with no container limit, .NET sized heaps against total host RAM and never felt pressure.

### Measured impact

Per lookup, against the real 155 MB bundled dataset:

| Location | Before | After | Garbage before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Berlin | 2.71 ms | 0.02 ms | 2,596 KB → 2.2 KB |
| Paris | 2.22 ms | 0.01 ms | 2,524 KB → 2.2 KB |
| London | 2.24 ms | 0.02 ms | 2,520 KB → 2.2 KB |
| Reykjavik | 2.39 ms | 0.01 ms | 2,488 KB → 2.2 KB |
| Tokyo | 1.38 ms | 0.01 ms | 1,541 KB → 1.7 KB |
| Anchorage | 0.87 ms | 0.01 ms | 810 KB → 1.7 KB |
| Atlantic (ocean) | 0.87 ms | 0.31 ms | 962 KB → 295 KB |
| **Total (9 points)** | **13.00 ms** | **0.41 ms** | **13.7 MB → 310 KB** |

~32x faster, ~44x less allocation. Berlin drops from 2.6 MB to 2.2 KB per lookup — about 1180x less garbage.

## Testing

- [x] App build — `npm run build`, 0 warnings / 0 errors, no suppression flags
- [x] Non-integration tests — `npm run test`, 74/79
- [x] Docker build — `docker build` with the unmodified Dockerfile; boots, serves HTTP 200, 28.59 MiB idle under `--memory=2g`
- [ ] Docs build — **not run**, `zensical` was not available in my environment. Anchors in the new docs links were verified against their target headings by hand.
- [x] Manual check — benchmarked before/after against the real bundled dataset

The 5 failing tests are all Legacy `PoiService` (`SQLite Error 1: near ","`). They reproduce identically on a pristine tree with these changes stashed, and persist unchanged on the newer SQLite, so they are a genuine SQL bug in that path rather than anything introduced here. `ImmichReverseGeo.Legacy` only references `Core` — never Overture or Gadm — and is not referenced by the Web project at all, so it is not in the shipped container. **`master` is already red on these.**

New tests build a synthetic two-country database so they run without the LFS-backed dataset. Reverting only the service fix makes `PointInsideCompactCountry_DoesNotScanTheSprawlingCountrysBoundary` fail at 1,588,688 bytes allocated — the guard has teeth.

## Notes

**The dependency bump is reviewable on its own (`chore:` commit).** `dotnet restore` currently fails outright on `master`: `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite` 10.0.5 resolves SQLitePCLRaw 2.1.11, whose SQLite build is affected by CVE-2025-6965 (GHSA-2m69-gcr7-jv3q, high). `NuGetAudit` raises `NU1903` and `TreatWarningsAsErrors` turns it into a build failure, so nothing compiles locally, in CI, or in Docker. Pinning `SQLitePCLRaw.bundle_e_sqlite3` to 2.1.13 in `Directory.Build.props` overrides it everywhere at once.

This is a real fix, not a suppressed warning: 2.1.13 bundles **SQLite 3.53.3**, past the 3.50.2 release that fixed the CVE, verified by querying `sqlite_version()` against the resolved package. `NuGetAudit` stays enabled and the Dockerfile is untouched. Note the GitHub advisory page reports "Patched Versions: None", which is why this was checked empirically rather than trusted.

**`mem_limit: 2g` is deliberate, not arbitrary.** The bundled country index alone occupies **~722 MB** of managed heap once loaded (measured). A 1 g limit would put the GC hard limit at ~768 MB — below the steady-state working set — and OOM immediately. Since `installation.md` includes `docker-compose.yml` verbatim from `master`, this setting appears in the published docs as soon as this merges, so the installation and troubleshooting pages were updated to explain it. **Existing installs will not pick it up until users edit their own compose file**, which the troubleshooting entry calls out.

**Behaviour change:** exact containment now always wins over a within-16 m neighbour. Previously both set `GeometryContainsPoint`, so a neighbour with a tighter bounding box could outrank a true containment. This looks like a correctness improvement, but it is a change and is noted in both changelogs.

**Pre-existing limitation documented, not fixed:** the STRtree is queried with the bare point envelope, so the 16 m tolerance can only ever apply to points already inside a country's bounding box — a point just outside resolves to nothing. `PointOutsideBoundingBox_IsNotRescuedByTolerance` documents this. Widening the query envelope would change it, at the cost of more candidates per lookup.

**Known follow-up, deliberately out of scope:** the ~722 MB baseline itself. NTS stores each coordinate as a ~40-byte `Coordinate` object versus 16 bytes packed; loading the index with a `PackedCoordinateSequenceFactory` would cut it roughly 3x. Left out to keep this change focused.

author: phynars
body:
<!--
Refs vs Closes convention:
  Closes #N  — auto-closes issue N on merge; use only when this PR
               implements the issue's acceptance criteria.
  Refs #N    — cross-link without closing; use for spec/docs PRs,
               partial work, follow-ups. Docs-only diffs that say
               "Closes" on a code issue are downgraded to "Refs"
               automatically (see closes-guard.ts).
-->
### Generated by /code

**Agent:** June Hallow
**Prompt:** `Read issue #1372 via read_issue(1372), understand the scope, then do a SPEC PASS before any code: restate the issue as an executable spec in one short block — exact files to change, acceptance criteria, what is OUT of scope, and the key symbols involved. If the issue is vague, derive the specifics from the codebase (grep/read) and state your assumptions in the spec. Only then implement the fix, and keep the diff inside your own spec. For incremental changes to existing files use \`edit\` (it only emits the changed region — much safer than \`write\` on files over ~500 lines, which can truncate at max_tokens). Use \`write\` for new files or true whole-file rewrites. Apply the actual changes — don't ask permission. Keep the scope to what the issue describes.  End your reply with \`Refs #1372\` (the PR body will inherit your reply, so this auto-closes the issue when merged). SELF-VERIFY before open_pr: re-check the staged diff against your spec — every acceptance criterion covered, no out-of-scope edits, no placeholder or truncated content. Fix gaps first, then open the PR. If open_pr returns ok:false with a gate reason, that is actionable feedback: fix the diff and call open_pr again (at most 2 retries). Do not end the session with staged work and no PR attempt. body: Adds Microsoft [Fluent Emoji](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui-emoji) as a CDN preset next to Twemoji, OpenMoji, and Noto. ## Usage ```ts const color = await emojiToSvg("😀", { source: "fluent" }); const flat = await emojiToSvg("👍", { source: { preset: "fluent", style: "flat" } }); const image = await emojiToImage("👍🏻", { source: "fluent", size: 48 }); ``` Supported styles: `color` (default), `flat`, `high-contrast`, and `3d` (PNG wrapped in SVG). ## Defaults Both `emojiToSvg` and `emojiToImage` now default to `"twemoji"`. `"native"` remains an explicit `emojiToImage` option for system-font rendering. ## How it works Fluent does not ship a flat `{codepoint}.svg` tree. This change: - Generates a compact Unicode → folder/tone map from official `metadata.json` files (`npm run generate:fluent-map`) - Pins jsDelivr to Fluent commit `62ecdc0d7ca5c6df32148c169556bc8d3782fca4` - Builds name-based URLs such as `Grinning face/Color/grinning_face_color.svg` ## Coverage notes Fluent’s upstream set is incomplete versus Twemoji/OpenMoji/Noto. Country flags and some ZWJ families (for example 👨‍👩‍👧) are missing and throw `EmojiNotFoundError`. High-contrast has no skin-tone variants. ## Testing - Unit tests for mapping, styles, skin tones, 3D wrap, and unmapped glyphs - Browser e2e fetches live Fluent color, flat, and skin-tone SVGs - Image default now uses Twemoji (same as SVG)

author: sourcehawk
body:
## Description

Closes #168

A `CamundaCluster` no longer accepts an effective version below the one its brokers run. Camunda does not support a downgrade of a running cluster, and since #157 the operator performs that very edit itself during a restore, so the two cases had to be told apart by the operator rather than by a CAUTION. The controller now refuses the move as a pre-check failure and a restore sanctions its own write with an annotation that the controller consumes once the brokers carry the version. A user who sets that annotation by hand can still downgrade on purpose, and the brokers then go unhealthy over newer data, which the docs state first.

## Changes

- The `CamundaCluster` controller compares the effective version (spec merged over the preset) with the tag of the broker image on the applied broker StatefulSet. A lower value is refused: `Ready: False / VersionDowngradeRefused`, one Warning event `VersionDowngradeRefused` per distinct refusal, nothing applied. This covers a lowered `spec.version`, a removed `spec.version` over a lower preset, and a preset whose version is lowered. The controller also stamps the running version on every bound broker claim as `camunda.io/broker-version` and reads it back when no StatefulSet exists, so a cluster deleted with retained volumes and recreated under the same name at a lower version is refused too.
- The annotation `camunda.io/allow-version-downgrade: "<x.y.z>"` sanctions a move to exactly that version. The controller removes it with a merge patch once the StatefulSet carries that version, and as soon as it names a version the cluster is not asked to run, so no sanction stands longer than the move it permits. A hand downgrade therefore sets the annotation in the same edit as the version, or after the refusal.
- `LogicalRestoreElasticsearch` and `LogicalRestoreRDBMS` write the annotation in the same server-side apply as `spec.version`, under the existing `camunda-operator/restore-version` manager, and write it again for as long as it is missing and the brokers have not converged, so a pre-declared version or a pruning tool cannot strand the restore on a refusal. The #157 order and its no-finalizer decision are untouched. `PointInTimeRestore` writes no version and is unchanged.
- `pkg/components/camundacluster` gains the pure rules `VersionDowngrade` and `RetainedVersion`, the shared `ImageTag` helper (`pkg/restore` now uses it), and the two annotation key constants. The keys stay there, next to `camunda.io/config-hash` and the other operator annotations, rather than in the `api` module: that is the existing precedent, and a consumer of `api/` types the string as documented.
- `api/v1`: `ReasonVersionDowngradeRefused` and a `Version` GoDoc that names the guard; CRD manifests regenerated.
- Docs: a `Version` section on `docs/crds/camundacluster.md` with the condition, the event, the annotation, and the hand-downgrade procedure; the three restore pages and `docs/guides/backup.md` state the rule and drop the #157 CAUTION that said the operator accepts a hand downgrade; `docs/guides/presets.md` says a lower preset version is refused by each cluster.

## Challenges

The guard lives in the controller and not in a validating webhook or a CEL transition rule, although issue #168 proposed the webhook. An admission rule on the cluster object sees a write to the cluster and nothing else. The effective version also moves backwards when `spec.version` is removed over a lower preset, which the restore pages tell the user to do, and when the preset itself is lowered, which rolls every cluster that references it. Only the controller sees all three, and it already holds the merged spec and the applied StatefulSet. The decision and its alternatives are recorded on #168.

## Related

- #157 decided that a restore writes `spec.version` and keeps it; this PR sanctions that write.
- #152 left the hand-downgrade case open; this PR takes the validation option.
- Follow-ups knowingly left: a guard for a skipped minor version (8.9 to 8.11, equally unsupported, same comparison site), and whether `version` belongs in a `CamundaClusterPreset` at all. Neither has an issue yet.

## Testing

`make test` (all envtest suites), `go -C api test ./...`, `make lint` (0 issues), `make manifests generate` with a clean `git status --porcelain config api`, `go vet -tags=e2e ./test/e2e/`, and `mkdocs build --strict` all pass on the branch.

New coverage: testify units for `VersionDowngrade`, `RetainedVersion`, and `ImageTag` (`pkg/components/camundacluster/downgrade_test.go`, `image_test.go`), for `refuseDowngrade`, `consumeDowngradeSanction`, `stampBrokerVersion`, and `brokerStorage.runningVersion` (`internal/controller/camundacluster/downgrade_test.go`, `storage_test.go`); four envtest specs on the cluster controller (a lower `spec.version` is refused with the condition and exactly one event, a sanctioned move is applied and the annotation is consumed, a removed `spec.version` over a lower preset and a lowered preset are refused, a cluster recreated on retained stamped claims is refused); `pkg/restore` asserts the version apply carries the annotation; one e2e spec in the `CamundaCluster` flow lowers `spec.version`, asserts `VersionDowngradeRefused` and the event, restores it, and asserts `Ready` recovers. The restore e2e flows are same-version by construction, so the sanction path end to end rests on the envtest and unit coverage. Reviewers who want to poke: set `spec.version` below the running tag on a cluster with and without the annotation, then watch `kubectl get camundacluster -o yaml` and `kubectl get events`.

author: eilandert
body:
> M1 of `PLAN-hitpath-2026-08-23.md` — resolves `PERF-PROFILE.md`'s largest
> unattributed run-A symbol and the `unresolved_symbol_pct` blind spot it
> exposed. Docs + one-line metric fix, no hit-path behavior change.

## TL;DR

`PERF-PROFILE.md` recorded run A's largest self-time entry as an unresolved
hex address while the same document claimed `unresolved_symbol_pct=0.00%`
for that run — those two claims can't both be true. Resolved the address via
debuginfod and fixed the metric's blind spot that let it read 0.00%.

`0x000000000026368a` is `ossl_fnv1a_hash` in `libcrypto.so.3` — OpenSSL 3.x's
internal property/provider-fetch hashtable function. `ci/tools/perf-profile.sh`'s
`unresolved_pct` awk block only matched a `[unknown]`/`unknown` row (no DSO
mapping at all); it never matched perf's other unresolved form, a bare
`0x...` symbol column (DSO known, no symbol table entry for it). Widened the
match to catch both.

**Severity:** `Low` (`tooling/observability — a reference doc's numbers were
internally inconsistent, and the metric had a blind spot; no runtime or
hit-path code changed`)

## Resolution

Address maps into `libcrypto.so.3` (confirmed via `perf report -i perf.data
--sort=dso,symbol -g none --no-children`). It's a local symbol, stripped
from the shared object's dynamic symbol table (`nm -D` has no entry for it
or the name), which is why `perf`'s own resolver — reading only the DSO's
symtab — could place the sample in the DSO but not name it:

```console
$ DEBUGINFOD_URLS=https://debuginfod.debian.net \
    eu-addr2line -f -e /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcrypto.so.3 0x26368a
ossl_fnv1a_hash
./build_shared/../crypto/hashtable/hashfunc.c:20:14
```

No package install was needed — `eu-addr2line` (elfutils, already present)
speaks the debuginfod protocol directly via `DEBUGINFOD_URLS`.

**Not the cache-key digest.** `cache_turbo`'s digest (`EVP_sha256()` +
`EVP_DigestInit_ex()`, `src/ngx_http_cache_turbo_blob.c:95`) triggers this
cost — OpenSSL 3.x re-resolves the SHA-256 provider on every call rather
than caching a fetched `EVP_MD *`, and `ossl_fnv1a_hash` is that lookup's
hash function — but the symbol itself is fetch machinery, not the SHA-256
compression (`sha256_block_data_order`, a separate row in the same profile).

## unresolved_symbol_pct fix

`ci/tools/perf-profile.sh`'s metric was correct for what it checked (rows
with no DSO mapping) but that's a strict subset of "unresolved symbol" —
its name promised the wider claim. Added a `$3 ~ /^0x[0-9a-fA-F]+$/` arm.
A fresh run-A capture on the same profile build now reports
`unresolved_symbol_pct=11.32` (283 such rows, all in `libcrypto.so.3`)
instead of 0.00.

## Testing

- `bash -n ci/tools/perf-profile.sh` — syntax check.
- Ran `ci/tools/perf-profile.sh` run A (`WORKERS=1`, 20s, `-c8`) against a
  fresh `ci-build.sh nginx 1.31.3 profile` build; confirmed the address still
  appears (now 1.62% self-time — box-condition dependent, per
  `PLAN-hitpath-2026-08-23.md`) and the fixed metric reports `11.32` instead
  of `0.00` against that run's `perf-report.txt`.
- `.claude/skills/_shared/review-lint.sh --branch main` — clean except
  pre-existing `shfmt` style debt in the touched file (unrelated lines,
  ledgered to `TODO.md` rather than fixed here).

author: team-bulls-app
body:
## Objetivo
Fazer uma manutenção conservadora do Team Bulls após as últimas entregas de dieta, procurando pontos que possam gerar falhas intermitentes, regressões ou diagnóstico incorreto, sem reescrever o núcleo nem alterar estruturas de dados existentes.

## Principais achados e correções

### 1. Módulos opcionais podiam desaparecer em rede lenta
O loader diferido tinha apenas uma tentativa com timeout curto. Se um módulo demorasse mais do que a janela em uma rede móvel instável, o script era removido e o app continuava sem aquela funcionalidade até uma nova recarga.

Agora cada módulo opcional recebe **uma única segunda tentativa**, apenas quando há conexão, depois de 250 ms e com timeout maior de 6,5 s. A ordem sequencial existente foi preservada para não quebrar os wrappers/hotfixes atuais.

### 2. Testes antigos ainda olhavam a regra Firestore 26
O `firebase.json` atual aponta para `firebase/firestore_27_compacto.rules`, mas os checks históricos ainda mantêm a regra 26 como baseline. Isso criava um ponto cego: CI verde não significava necessariamente que a regra efetivamente configurada para deploy estava sendo auditada.

Foi criado `scripts/production-audit-check.mjs`, que lê o caminho diretamente do `firebase.json` e valida a regra ativa. Ele confirma, entre outros pontos, que `dietCalculations/{uid}` é trainer-only e não possui caminho `activeOwner` para o aluno.

### 3. Mensagem de erro orientava regra antiga
O núcleo legado ainda cita `firestore_26_compacto.rules` na mensagem de permission-denied. Para não alterar o arquivo central de ~700 KB, foi adicionada uma camada final pequena que apenas corrige essa orientação em runtime para `firestore_27_compacto.rules`.

### 4. Diagnóstico das extensões recentes de dieta
A camada final também verifica se matemática da dieta, calculadora/evolução e tabela de porções realmente terminaram de carregar. Se uma extensão continuar indisponível depois do retry, há diagnóstico no console sem derrubar o restante do app.

## Limpeza e otimização sem risco
- Nenhuma coleção ou formato Firestore foi alterado.
- Nenhuma regra de negócio de treino, dieta, cardio, relatórios ou fotos foi reescrita.
- Nenhum arquivo histórico/rollback foi apagado.
- O núcleo, CSS e HTML continuam sob os limites de tamanho conservadores do projeto.
- O loader agora valida que todos os módulos declarados existem e que não há entradas duplicadas.
- A tabela de porções continua totalmente estática e sem leituras Firestore.
- A calculadora continua isolada em `dietCalculations`.

## Novos checks
- `scripts/loader-retry-check.mjs`
- `scripts/production-audit-check.mjs`

Os dois foram integrados ao workflow de qualidade; a auditoria de produção também roda no workflow de segurança.

## Documentação
Foi adicionado `docs/production-audit-2026-08-22.md` com o escopo, riscos encontrados, decisões e itens deliberadamente preservados.

## Observação Firebase
Este PR **não publica regras automaticamente**. O repositório está configurado para `firebase/firestore_27_compacto.rules`; se essa regra ainda não estiver publicada no Firebase real, o deploy deve ser feito separadamente após aprovação.

## Revisão
Alteração intencionalmente pequena: 7 arquivos, 1 commit, sem mudanças no schema e sem merge automático. Revisar antes de colocar na main.

author: opaland
body:
Trois tests restés verts alors que le défaut était remis, **dans la même nuit**, et trois fois la même cause : une assertion sur le DOM répondait à une autre question que celle qu'on croyait poser.

| Assertion | Ce qu'elle accepte | Où ça a mordu |
|---|---|---|
| `toBeVisible` | un élément écrêté par un ancêtre en `overflow: hidden` | les 4 tests du constat U3, sur une feuille repliée haute de 52 px |
| `toContainText` | le `textContent`, `display: none` compris | « rien ne parle de glisser », affirmé sur un texte présent (U12) |
| une mesure unique | l'état intermédiaire d'une transition | 821 px relevés là où la feuille en fait 52 — deux fois, dans deux constats |

La section dit quoi demander à la place : ce qui est **peint** au centre de l'élément (`document.elementFromPoint`, soit `estAlEcran` dans les helpers), la **visibilité** plutôt que la présence du mot, et `expect.poll` dès qu'une transition CSS peut courir.

Et elle énonce la règle dont ces trois cas ne sont qu'une instance :

> Une assertion qui pourrait passer pour une raison qu'on n'a pas voulue n'est pas une assertion.

Elle se place en §1bis parce qu'elle prolonge §1 — « un test qui ne peut pas échouer ne prouve rien » — au cas particulier des tests de bout en bout, comme §6bis prolonge §6.

author: danielguez16
body:
Deux changements sur le même écran, et ils se cumulent : la vignette réduit ce que chaque portrait coûte, la virtualisation réduit combien en coûtent à la fois.

## La clé nue était une limite du moment, pas un arbitrage

`Image` décode avant de réduire : une photo occupe sa taille en pixels en mémoire **quel que soit le cadre** où on la pose. Vingt portraits d'origine tenaient leur pleine taille dans des cadres de 132 points.

L'historique tranche la question, et c'est pour ça que je l'ai cherché plutôt que de trancher d'avis à avis :

| | Quand |
|---|---|
| Le repli de la route (`cle_d_origine`) | 14 août 16:32 |
| `deposer_un_avatar` — original, vignette, aperçu | 21 août 17:17 |
| La grille de l'annuaire, la clé nue, et le test | 22 août 10:09 |

Les deux existaient quand le choix a été fait. La raison écrite ne couvre qu'un cas — « sans abonnement la clé porte déjà l'aperçu flouté, et la resuffixer ne rendrait rien ». C'est vrai de ce cas-là, et l'autre le payait. `urlDuPortrait` les sépare.

**Le suffixe aveugle ne casse rien, il gaspille.** `@apercu@vignette` n'est pas un 404 : la route voit la terminaison, la retire, trouve l'aperçu, sert la bonne image. Le coût est une lecture de dépôt perdue par portrait, pour rendre exactement ce qu'une clé nue aurait rendu.

**Le test change ce qu'il attend, pas ce qu'il regarde.** Sa note de mutation — « c'est la terminaison qui distingue les deux » — parle de la solidité de l'assertion, pas de la justesse de la clé. La terminaison reste, le cas de l'aperçu est intact, et les deux sens tombent sous mutation.

## La pile du téléphone est virtualisée

« Voir plus » empile vingt créatrices par appui : quatre-vingts portraits montés d'un coup après quatre appuis, sur le format le plus utilisé.

**La grille reste un bloc au-dessus du seuil.** Trois colonnes en `flexWrap` ne sont pas une liste, et le contrat de `liste` rend un élément par rangée sans notion de colonnes. Changer la disposition pour pouvoir virtualiser serait prendre le problème par le mauvais bout — `FlatList` porte `numColumns` et ce sera une ligne le jour où quelqu'un mesure la grille large.

**Les deux chemins partagent la même fabrique de morceaux.** Ce qui change entre eux est la façon de poser les fiches, pas ce qu'elles portent : deux corps finiraient par diverger, et c'est celui que personne ne regarde qui dériverait.

**Pas de crochet de fin de liste, et il n'en faut pas.** « Voir plus » est un appui explicite, donc il vit dans le pied et défile sous la dernière fiche.

---

1392 tests, **4 mutations vérifiées** : l'aperçu resuffixé, la clé nue pour tous, le pied retiré de la liste, l'entête retirée.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: aphoristicartist
body:
Audit of the tool surface against two sources, then four fixes.

## How it was checked

- Anthropic's [tools reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference) — 44 built-in tools.
- `getAllBaseTools()` in the Claude Code 2.1.240 binary — 80 tools, 36 of them undocumented.
- Live: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointed at a local server, reading the `tools` array out of `/v1/messages`.

Two things held up. The `Off, permanently` table was exactly the documented list minus the six coding tools and the four capabilities — 30 for 30, no invented names. And `--tools` is a real closed allowlist, not advice: Claude Code compiles it into deny rules (source `toolsNarrowing`) covering every built-in the session does not name. Nothing re-opened it — `--brief`, `--advisor`, `--agents` with its own tool list, `--allowedTools TodoWrite,Workflow,Monitor`, `--permission-mode plan`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` / `_ENABLE_REFRESH_MCP_TOOLS=1` / `_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1` / `_SKILL_PROPOSALS=1` all still produced exactly six tools.

## What this changes

**`ReadMcpResourceDirTool` joins the MCP capability.** It sits beside the other two resource tools in the registry and expands a directory resource that `ListMcpResourcesTool` can otherwise only name. Without it the capability was incomplete.

**The table no longer claims to be exhaustive.** It covers the documented tools. The binary also carries claude.ai design and project tools, plugin and connector suggestions, a REPL, memory-store tools, self-hosted runner tools. They stay off too — the note says so instead of the summary implying the table already listed them.

**Background `Bash` gets its caveat.** The tool advertises `run_in_background`, but `TaskOutput` and `TaskStop` are off, so a detached command cannot be read or killed before it exits.

**`--mcp-config` without the switch is spelled out.** Passing it replaces the empty config the wrapper would otherwise supply, so those servers load and their tools reach Claude. That is the documented precedence rule working as intended; it just was not said where a reader would look.

## Verification

- `./tests/test.sh` — passes. The MCP assertion now expects the five-tool list, and a new check fails the build if the README stops naming any tool the switch adds.
- `shellcheck bin/claude-kiss install.sh tests/test.sh build-release.sh` — clean.
- Live, against 2.1.240: baseline `Bash Edit Glob Grep Read Write`; `CLAUDE_KISS_WEB=1` adds `WebFetch WebSearch`; `CLAUDE_KISS_MCP=1` with a stdio MCP server now sends `ListMcpResourcesTool ReadMcpResourceTool ReadMcpResourceDirTool` alongside the server's own tools.

author: tvanhens
body: ## What changed The documented way to filter a query by entity id — `Query.is(Comment.id, p.root)` — lowered to `[?e, ":db/id", v]`. `:db/id` is not an attribute, so the engine rejected it with `unknown attribute :db/id`. There was no working spelling of that filter. This PR: 1. Special-cases `:db/id` in `lowerFact`: unify the e-position with the value (`ground` for a constant / param; share a name or `=` for two vars) instead of emitting a `:db/id` data pattern. 2. Adds `Query.byId(id)` as the blessed, serializable filter stage (same IR as `is(N.id, id)` — a query value the peer executes, not a client-side post-filter). 3. Tests against the real engine for `is(N.id, constant)`, `is(N.id, param)`, and `byId`, plus a lock that the raw `[?e, ":db/id", v]` pattern still throws so we cannot regress by inventing `:db/id` as an attribute. 4. Docs (`guides/queries.mdx`, `reference/client-api.mdx`) teach `byId` as the blessed form and keep `is(N.id, …)` documented as equivalent. ## Verification - `bun test packages/ramose/test/db/kernel-query.test.ts` — 43 pass, including the new lowering + engine cases. - `bun run typecheck` — clean. - `bun run test` — 842 pass, 0 fail. ## Out of scope Remaining #188 / API-review work stays on the GitHub issue. author: torstendittmann
body:
## Summary

- provide `Psr\Log\LoggerInterface` through constructor injection with a newline-delimited JSON logger that writes to `STDERR`
- create or preserve a safe `X-Request-ID`, expose it as an injectable request-scoped `RequestId`, and attach it to every handled response
- report every `5xx` exactly once in development and production with request ID, method, path, status, and the original exception
- keep expected `4xx` responses quiet and keep production `500` bodies free of internal details
- fall back to the built-in stderr logger if an application logger fails, without changing the response or stopping the RoadRunner worker
- remove the unreleased static logger/trait API in favor of PSR-3 constructor injection
- extend the local RoadRunner boundary contract to verify structured error collection and worker recovery

## Design decisions

- PSR-3 is a direct public dependency; no logging backend is imposed. A discovered `#[Service(as: LoggerInterface::class)]` replaces the default without entrypoint registration.
- The default logger accepts only standard PSR-3 levels and safely normalizes arbitrary context, invalid UTF-8, recursive arrays, resources, `Stringable` failures, `JsonSerializable` failures, and closed streams.
- Automatic request context is intentionally limited to `request_id`, `http.method`, `http.path`, `http.status_code`, and `exception`. Query strings, bodies, headers, cookies, identity, and client IP are never captured automatically.
- Incoming request IDs must be a single 1–128 character value matching `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}`. Missing or unsafe values are replaced with 16 random bytes encoded as 32 lowercase hex characters.
- A request-local report guard covers both routed and outer middleware failures, preventing duplicate `5xx` records if error rendering also fails.
- RoadRunner worker output follows the documented boundary: Gustav writes application records to `STDERR`; `STDOUT` remains reserved for the worker protocol.

References: [PSR-3](https://www.php-fig.org/psr/psr-3/), [RoadRunner logger](https://docs.roadrunner.dev/docs/logging-and-observability/logger), [RoadRunner stdout protocol](https://docs.roadrunner.dev/docs/error-codes/stdout-crc).

## Verification

- `composer format` — pass
- `composer dump-autoload --optimize --strict-psr` — pass (4,836 classes)
- `composer test` — pass (168 tests, 482 assertions)
- `composer check` — pass (PHPStan, 103 files)
- `composer lint` — pass
- `composer audit --format=plain` — pass, no advisories
- `composer validate --strict --no-check-publish` — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass
- `composer test:transport` — pass
  - JSON request: `200`
  - malformed JSON: `400`
  - request-scope sequence: `200 -> 418 -> 200`
  - server failure: production-safe `500 -> 200`, with `transport-request-500` collected from worker `STDERR`

author: vitali87
body:
## Summary

Adds AST-based clone detection so users can find copy-pasted functions and methods — exact, renamed, and lightly edited copies — and apply DRY with structural evidence. No embeddings involved: everything is derived from the tree-sitter AST.

### How it works

- **Index time**: each Function/Method body is normalized into a *skeleton* — identifiers, literals, and comments blanked; operators, keywords, and structure kept — then Merkle-hashed bottom-up (`blake2b`, 16-hex digests). Three new optional node properties: `ast_fingerprint`, `ast_fingerprint_nodes`, `ast_branch_fingerprints` (digests of statement-level subtrees ≥ 5 skeleton nodes).
- **Exact clones (Type-1/2)**: group-by fingerprint — renames and literal changes hash identically.
- **Edited copies (Type-3)**: Jaccard overlap of branch-fingerprint sets ≥ threshold (default 0.8). Candidates come from an inverted index with a hot-fingerprint cap and a size-ratio prefilter, merged with union-find — never O(n²).
- Analysis runs client-side over `fetch_all` (same pattern as dead-code); `--min-size`/`--threshold` changes never require reindexing.

### Surfaces

- `cgr duplicates` — table/JSON output, `--threshold`, `--min-size`, `--exact-only`, `--exclude`, `--output`, `--fail-on-found` for CI. Reports how many symbols had no fingerprint (pattern-tier languages, bodiless declarations) instead of silently ignoring them.
- `find_duplicate_code` agentic tool (read-only, registered in the RAG orchestrator).

### Also included

- `codec/schema.proto` fields + regenerated `schema_pb2` (protoc 33.5); protobuf round-trip test extended
- Graph schema registration (NODE_SCHEMAS + docs/architecture/graph-schema.md) — passes the conftest graph audit
- Illustrated user guide `docs/guide/duplicates.md` (inline SVG figures, light/dark theme aware) + mkdocs nav + CLI reference + agentic tools table regen

## Test plan

- [x] `test_ast_fingerprint.py` — skeleton equivalence (rename/literal/comment invariance), operator/structure sensitivity, branch collection, cross-language smoke
- [x] `test_duplicates_collect.py` — grouping, Jaccard threshold, hot-fp cap, size prefilter, union-find, excludes, exact-only
- [x] `test_duplicates_command.py` — CLI table/JSON, fail-on-found, error paths
- [x] `test_duplicates_ingest.py` — end-to-end ingest props (incl. graph audit)
- [x] Full suite (full dev env: `uv sync --extra treesitter-full --extra test --extra semantic --group dev`): 7657 passed, 80 skipped, 1 failed — the sole failure (`test_dead_code_well_known_symbols.py::test_javascript_well_known_symbols_liveness_roots`) reproduces identically on main and is unrelated to this change
- [x] `mkdocs build --strict` green; ruff + ty clean (pre-existing warnings only)
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added structural duplicate-code detection for functions and methods, including exact and similar matches.
  * Added the `cgr duplicates` command with similarity, minimum-size, exact-only, exclusion, table/JSON output, and CI failure options.
  * Added interactive duplicate-code detection support.
  * Reports duplicate groups, similarity, locations, skipped symbols, and whether results were truncated.

* **Documentation**
  * Added user guides, CLI reference details, examples, limitations, and navigation for duplicate detection.

author: saud-alnasser
body:
Closes nothing. Decision work has no ticket, so a specification and its plan land as their own `docs:` pull request, the way #221 and #745 did. The effort is #754 on the tracker and it stays open, with #755, #756 and #757 under it.

Bottom of a four branch stack: this, then #760, #761 and #762.

## 🎯 Changes

**The control plane's own database is a file on whoever ran it.** `database.ts` falls back to `file:./control-plane.db` when `CONTROL_PLANE_DATABASE_URL` is unset, and there is such a file in `apps/control-plane/` right now. Accounts, workspaces, membership and sessions, everything that decides whether a person may open their workspace, live in one developer's working directory.

Nothing in the package was built for that, which is what makes this worth an effort rather than a shrug. The client is `@libsql/client` and its own comment says why: a `file:` URL locally and a `libsql://` one once this is deployed, through the same client. `drizzle.config.ts` declares `dialect: 'turso'` for the same reason and already reads the URL and the token from the environment. `.env.example` already documents both. The support is built and unused.

### The five decisions the spec settles

- **Remote by default, with a `file:` URL still legal and announced as local.** Development, the test suite and an offline day all need the file. What none of them needs is it arriving by accident, which is the thing a required variable ends.
- **A pure `resolveDatabase(env)` beside a `connectOrExit(report)`**, rather than a `connect()` that throws and is caught in four entrypoints. What lost: no module but an entrypoint should be able to end the process, and it costs the same three lines in four files.
- **The URL's scheme decides whether a token is required.** `file:` is local, every other scheme is hosted. What lost: requiring a token only for `libsql:`, `https:` and `wss:`, so an unauthenticated local sqld would work, because a typo that downgrades a real hosted URL to `http:` would then be accepted in silence. The condition that reopens it is written down rather than left to be rediscovered: the first person who wants `turso dev`.
- **Live provisioning happens during implementation**, one authorised step at a time. The group on this account is delete-protected and refuses to delete the databases inside it, so a database created for this cannot be removed from here, and the free tier's hundred is a number worth watching.
- **The live check runs against a second hosted database that is reused, never created per run.** What lost: a throwaway database per run, which the delete-protected group turns into a permanent one per run. Not considered acceptable at all: pointing the live test at the real database, which writes test rows into the records the control plane serves from.

### One defect found while planning, corrected in place

Acceptance criterion 7 asked that a sign-up whose workspace record fails leave neither a workspace row nor a membership row. `createWorkspace` cannot reach that state: the losing side of the race throws `RaceLost` before it has written anything, so its rollback is unobservable, and a criterion resting on it would pass without measuring the property. It now asserts the transaction directly, and the old wording is kept underneath it rather than deleted.

**The spec is one file through both phases.** `/aep:specify` wrote Problem through Risks, and `/aep:plan` extended the same file with Architecture, Interfaces, Technical Approach, Testing Strategy and Technical Risks. There is no `plan.md`.

## ✅ Checklist

- [ ] I have added or updated the tests related to the changes made.

No tests, and nothing to test. Both files in this pull request are under `.aep/`: the effort's spec and the regenerated index. No source, no configuration, no behaviour. The tests are in #760 and #762.

author: burrows99
body:
Answering the gap I flagged earlier: *nothing tells you a declared locator stopped resolving until a run breaks on it.*

## The gap, measured

I pinned the Grafana example's container to `grafana:10.4.0` — a description written for 13.2, run against a version it was never written for.

| | |
|---|---|
| `action run` | **1** breakage, **47s** (30s of it a timeout), then fix and re-run for the next |
| `check drift` | **3** breakages, **7.7s**, exit 1 |

## The first version was wrong, and the control caught it

It swept every declared locator across every declared route. On 10.4 that found all eight breakages in 21 seconds. Then I ran it against **13.2 — the version the description was written for, which `action run` passes green against** — and it reported eight more findings, six of them false:

- `connectionCard` matched **226** elements. That is the entire point of the `store` that uses it.
- `usersTable` matched twice on `profile`, a route no step ever uses it on.
- `Skip` matched nothing, because it only exists on the interstitial after a click, and a URL sweep can never get there.

A checker that cries wolf is worse than no checker — the first false positive teaches everyone to ignore the true ones.

## So it does not sweep

It reads the **claims the description already makes**: a step's locator *and* the route a `goto` put the page on. Those pairs are the only thing that can be judged without guessing, and they are already written down.

Each of these rules cost a false positive to learn, and each has a test:

- after a `click`, `fill` or `press` the page is somewhere no URL reproduces → **nothing is claimed again until the next `goto`**
- a `store` reading a list is entitled to find it **empty**; only a single-element `store` is broken by matching nothing
- more than one match is wrong **only where the step needs one** (`expect count:` and `store all:` are excluded)
- the sign-in action's own steps are checked **before anybody is signed in** — a login form is unreachable once you are in
- a composed action's claims are counted **once**, not once per composition
- a route that **redirects** is `unchecked`, not `gone` — the app deciding you may not be there would otherwise report every locator on that screen as missing

## What it says now

Against 13.2, the version it was written for:

```
all 7 claims still hold
exit=0
```

Against 10.4:

```
3 of 7 claims no longer hold

Nothing matches these any more — a run will time out on them:
  grafana.openDashboards · expect  testId=data-testid CreateNewButton New button — nothing matches it on dashboards
  grafana.startADashboard · expect  text=Add a panel to visualize your data — nothing matches it on newDashboard
  grafana.browseConnections · type  placeholder=Search Grafana plugins — nothing matches it on addConnection

exit=1
```

With no sign-in action named it refuses to guess:

```
all 7 claims still hold (4 could not be checked)

Not checked:
  grafana.openDashboards · expect  …/dashboards sent us to …/login — name an action that signs in, and this can be checked
```

Exit code 1 on drift so a pipeline can gate on it. Added to the generated `SKILL.md` and the README.

330 unit tests (9 new, one per false positive), typecheck clean.

author: tristanmatthias
body:
Two changes. The second is what makes the first honest.

## 1. A newtype displayed as a pointer once it was nested

`emit_value_to_string` describes itself as

> THE value-level string converter — the single dispatch shared by the public `string()` emitter, **the newtype path**, and the optional present branch

It had no newtype arm. The unwrap sat one level up in `emit_int_to_string`, the public entry, so it fired for a bare `MP` and never for one reached through another layer. `emit_optional_to_string` strips `MP?` to `MP` and re-enters the shared dispatch, which didn't recognise it and fell through to the **integer** path:

```avra
let m: MP? = MP("x")
"${m}"        // 4335581486   — the string pointer, printed as a decimal
```

Fixed by recursing in the shared dispatch, so every composition works instead of one hand-picked depth — `MP?`, `MP??`, and a newtype over a newtype, which the top-level unwrap never handled either. The duplicate at the public entry is **removed**: one definition, not two.

Guard: `newtype_display_depth_test.av`, 7 specs.

## 2. ModulePath (t-y2i7.3 section 14)

`bind_rows(module: string)` stamped a bare string across every row of a feature's manifest. The ticket's motivating example is emit.av's `b.module != "features.grammar"` — a hand-written literal where a typo is silent.

Now `ModulePath?`, **optional**, with `null` for a row `bind_rows` hasn't stamped. Unstamped is the *absence* of a module, not an empty one.

I first wrote this as required-with-`ModulePath("")` **because of bug 1** — an empty-string sentinel, in a ticket whose entire subject is removing stringly-typed sentinels. Fixing the display bug removed the reason for the workaround, so the sentinel is gone rather than documented.

58 `bind_rows` sites wrapped across 41 files, plus the comptime **synthesis** path — `typed_builders.av` now emits a `ModulePath(...)` call, so generated rows sit on the same footing as hand-authored ones.

Both existing gates earned their keep here: the nominal `==` gate (t-tzt0) and the struct-field identity gate (t-5qi0) each caught real sites, including the ticket's own example.

## Verification

- **Negative control**: unwrapping one `bind_rows` literal yields exactly 1 F1000; restored. (Confirmed the mutation applied first — a silent control proves nothing.)
- grammar 1331/1331 · typeck 429/429 · core 351/351 · parse 294/294 · fn_decl 50/50
- `@std::avrac` lib probe: exit 0, zero F1000

## Scope

**t-y2i7.3 stays open** — BuildName (110 sites) and FeatureName (2) remain, plus the section-12 decision.

## Label

`intended-strictness-change` — bare strings into these slots are now rejected.

author: awesomekling
body:
Reduce style engine overhead during large DOM mutations and repeated connect and disconnect cycles.

Grow the C++ reverse mapping once before registering a subtree, and recycle retired style node identities only after published transaction outputs can no longer reference them. This keeps dense relation and lookup columns bounded by the live document rather than every element ever connected.

Apply staged tree deltas without comparison-sorting materialized relation tuples. Radix-sort fixed-width node identities before materialization and track depth-recompute roots in a sparse set, keeping scratch storage proportional to the staged rows instead of the largest node identity.

Update transaction-order expectations for recycled identities and add coverage for automatic identity reuse, radix sorting, and sparse depth membership for high node identities.

author: xian55
body:
Five things, all in the character viewer.

## Switchable animations

Sixteen per character — Stand, Walk, Run, the three Ready stances, Attack, Dance,
Cheer, Salute, Bow, Talk, Roar, Sit, Loot, Jump — picked by the client's own names
from `AnimationData.dbc` rather than by guessed ids, and chosen from a control beside
Animate.

The model still ships only its idle. All sixteen inline took a character from 245 KB
to 560 KB, paid by every visitor who only wanted to look at a tabard, so the rest live
in a `.anm` sidecar fetched the first time someone reaches for the picker. Same
encoding both sides, one reader, so they cannot drift apart. The choice is remembered
by NAME across the re-mount every equip causes: a race that lacks one animation shifts
every index after it.

## Playback that isn't jittery

The loop rendered on every rAF while advancing the movers on a 33 ms gate, so half the
frames redrew a pose identical to the last one and motion arrived in 33 ms jumps
against a 60 Hz display — full GPU cost, and judder was what it bought. Now a tick
that is not due draws nothing, and every frame drawn carries a fresh pose.

The turntable keeps its 30 fps budget (0.37° per frame at 17 s a revolution) and so
halves its draws; the animation takes the display's rate and pays for it in pose maths.
On a machine that can't hold 60 the budget steps down to an even 30 — measured on the
achieved gap between drawn frames, since the render call returns long before the GPU is
done and reports a fast machine on a slow one.

Measured headless: turntable 60 → 30 fps for the same motion, animation 5.1% → 3.9% of
a core while stepping twice as often, still 0% idle or hidden.

## The eyelid the game keeps hidden

A character carries the eyelid twice — one animated for blinking, one for sleeping and
dying — and the client shows exactly one. It hides the spare in whichever of two ways
the artist chose, and both were wrong here, on different races, which is why this
arrived as several unrelated reports:

- **Goblins** hide theirs with alpha 0 on the `M2Color` the texture unit points at —
  not on the mesh, not on the material — so the submesh looks entirely valid and is
  something the game never draws. Now dropped at export, judged over the animations we
  ship rather than the whole file (in animation 145 the spare IS shown; that is how a
  corpse closes its eyes).
- **Blood elf males** hide theirs with a bone scale of exactly `(0,0,0)`, and
  `v[a] || 1` turned it back to full size — a flat quad over the eyes. Human males
  escaped only because their lid is hidden by a global track, a different code path.

Blinking itself is a global sequence: a clock of its own that runs whatever is playing.
Filed under the played clip it blinked at the clip's rate — twice per 2.7 s Stand
instead of three times per 6.6 s, differently again in Dance. `.m2b` v6 gives those
tracks their own section and their own clock, and a still model rests at the phase the
cycle actually holds (a tauren female's blink straddles the loop boundary, so t=0 is
her lid shut).

Visibility in an M2 is not a property of the mesh: it is spread across the geoset
selection, the bone's scale, and an alpha track reached through a colour index.

## Compatibility

The reader takes v4, v5 and v6, and both sidecar magics. A format bump reaches R2 and
the deployed code at different moments, and v4's single animation read as a v5 list
takes the duration for a count — garbage, not an error. Models are already published.

## Tests

`bun run smoke` — 302 pass, 0 fail. Four new: the animation picker, the frame-pacing
ratio (the turntable must draw ~half what the animation does), a hidden mesh staying
hidden, and the resting phase. Two of them assert the strong thing only where the data
exists, so they stay honest against an origin still serving older models.

Also adds `__mv.bodyAtlas()` and `__mv.globalClock()`, which is how the above was
measured rather than guessed — the composite proved pixel-exact against the source
BLPs, which moved the search from textures to geometry.

author: chetan-guevara
body:
## What this is

A delegated `aiosd_` token could read **no** hand-entered tasks or decisions — anything a person typed
into a project through the dashboard. An agent got everything synced from Linear or meetings and
nothing typed, so it answers *"there's no task about that"* when you wrote one down.

**RULING (Chetan, 2026-08-22):** an agent granted a project should read what a person typed into it.

The arm is now **gated on the token's effective project set** instead of closed. In-scope hand-entered
rows are served; out-of-scope ones are not. **Member behaviour is unchanged.**

## This deliberately reverses part of AUDITFIX-1

AUDITFIX-1 states a token "never" sees such rows. That closure existed because scope was being ignored
*entirely* — an empty-scoped token received the whole team's hand-typed content. **The protection it
actually added is kept**: the arm is gated on authority, not reopened. And the claim it rested on —
*"a null-source row cannot be tested against that scope"* — was **false**: those rows carry
`project_id`, written by the dashboard create actions in the same insert as `created_by`, and both leg
queries already join `projects`. The token path computed the project set and **discarded it**.

The route test that encoded the old rule is **converted, not deleted** — it seeded its hand-entered
rows *inside* the token's scope, so it could only ever express "closed for every token". It now
asserts both halves.

## Measured on production first (read-only, 2026-08-22)

⚠️ **A spec round corrected my measurement by 136×, and the corrected number is what matters.**

I counted `source_item_id is null` and called it "hand-entered". The arm also requires
`created_by is not null` — and *unsourced* does not imply *typed by a human*: `ON DELETE SET NULL`
turns purged-source rows back into null-source rows, and the task CLI writes no author.

| | |
|---|---|
| tasks, `source_item_id is null` | 136 |
| **tasks, unsourced AND authored** — the population the arm admits | **1** |
| decisions, unsourced AND authored | **0** |
| the project holding it | `aios-team-brain` — **not granted to any group** |
| projects on the fleet | 19 total, **2 granted** |
| **delegated tokens in existence** | **0** |

**This admits zero additional rows on this fleet, and that is correct** — no token's authority covers
that project, so under the ruling an agent should not see what was typed into it. **Nobody should
expect a behaviour change from merging this.** Making that project reachable by an agent requires an
**operator grant**, not a code change.

**Also found, not fixed here:** 66 `origin='ui'` tasks carry no `created_by` (one window,
2026-06-28→07-01; `createTaskAction` sets it today). They fail the authorship conjunct and are
invisible to **every** principal. AC5 pins that this slice neither repairs nor worsens them.

## Deliberately not in this slice

**AUDITFIX-19** — requiring a project scope at mint. `project_scope: args.projectScope ?? null` makes
the *lazy* path the *permissive* one, which is the shape the previous slice existed to remove.
**AUDITFIX-20** — the agents admin page; there is none today, which is why zero tokens exist.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| unit (`npm run coverage`, what CI runs) | **3,369 passed** |
| data-mechanics, affected | **6 passed** |
| tsc · lint · docs-drift | clean (lint 0 errors, 16 pre-existing warnings) |
| spec gate | `SPEC_READY`, no findings |

**Mutations — verdicts pasted from `scripts/mutate.mjs`, not narrated:**

| mutation | reddens |
|---|---|
| M1 token admission widens to `"all"` | union · TS owner · both SQL owners |
| M2 an empty token set stops closing explicitly | `token with an EMPTY set → closed` |
| M3 semijoin owner drops the project conjunct | its own SQL assertion |
| M4 TS owner stops checking set membership | out-of-scope TS case |
| M5 the loud denial goes silent | AC12 |
| M6 the route carry is dropped | the route wiring guard |
| M7 `delegatedVisibleItemIds` returns `[]` when unscoped | **the unscoped route test** |
| M8 the carry property leaves the AST walk | guard non-vacuity |
| M9 the external-delegation refusal is deleted | the coupling guard |
| M10 the forward-shape rule is removed | guard non-vacuity |
| M11 the error-path gate is removed | the error-path test |
| M12 assignment rule reverts to `principal`-only | guard non-vacuity |
| M13 the `Object.assign` arm is removed | guard non-vacuity |

**Four mutations SURVIVED during the build and were fixed.** M3 because I asserted only one of the two
SQL owners — the spec had already said "one mutation per owner" and I under-implemented it. M11, M12
and M13 because **I applied a review fix and wrote nothing that fails when it is removed.**

## Known-flaky, proven NOT this diff

`graph-cdc`, `nda-gate`, `neo4j-tier-wiring` and `mutation-flow` fail non-deterministically in full
`npm run coverage` runs — all spawn processes and race under parallel load. **I checked out untouched
`origin/main` and reproduced it there: 8 failures in a full run, against 5 on this branch.** All four
pass in isolation here.

## Review — Reviewed by Fable code-reviewer + Codex gpt-5.6-sol — verdict CLEAR and CLEAR-WITH-CONDITIONS after two BLOCKED spec rounds; neither could construct a token reading an out-of-scope row, and each found defects the other missed

**Spec rounds (Codex, before any code): BLOCKED, then BLOCKED on the fold.** Round 1 found I had missed
a **third owner** of this contract — the compiler named it the instant the old function was removed —
and corrected the measurement above. Round 2 found **no criterion pinned an unscoped token**
(`projectScope: null` is not `[]`): an implementation returning `[]` there passes every scoped test and
**silently blinds every unscoped agent**. It also showed a discriminated union does not enforce itself,
and that fail-closed on a missing `project_id` is *data-loss-shaped* because that column is `NOT NULL`.

**Fable (diff): CLEAR.** Could construct no out-of-scope read; verified the compile-time claims with a
real probe file. Found **a false coverage claim I had written** — my comment said both SQL forms were
executed against a real database; only one is. Found a **safety coupling written nowhere**: the token
arm skips a posture check, safe only because a *different* file refuses external-tier agents. Now
guarded from both ends. And an **error path that widened**: on a substrate read failure my change
served hand-typed rows while suppressing everything else.

**Codex (diff): CLEAR-WITH-CONDITIONS**, and it found two things Fable did not. **The carry was not
required by the type** — `{ visibleItemIds, principal: "token" }` type-checked and silently restored
pre-slice behaviour, and the provider seam restated the shape while omitting the field. It is a
**discriminated union** now, verified by probe that the unsafe shape is a compile error. And the **AST
guard had a mutation bypass** — build the literal correctly, mutate it one line later. Closing that
exposed a further defect in my own fix: the `Object.assign` arm reused the string-argument test, which
read as coverage and provided none.

AIOS-Work: AUDITFIX-7

author: patocanz
body:
The Status box showed **two Enriched numbers that disagreed on every row**. The chip read `enrich_pulse` — the 0–9 PULSE high-water folded from `place_enrichment_events`. The detail prose directly beneath it read `enrich_level`, a rival 0–3 stage level derived from `place_research`. On the catalog's one place that is 0 against 3: *"Seeded — nothing after it has landed"* sitting above *"Profile persisted — the Enricher finished."*

PR #1074 deleted `placeEnrichProgress`, but `placeEnrichLevel` survived and kept shipping on both payloads. That survivor is what produced this.

## What changes

`placeEnrichLevel` and `ResearchFacts` are deleted, with their tests. **Both `place_research_facts` RPC calls go with them** — computing that level was their only purpose, so the catalog search and the place editor each lose a round-trip.

`enrichedDetail` is rewritten off the same number the chip renders, and now names the rung the queue reached *and* the rung that has not completed — the question an operator looking at a stalled place is actually asking.

## MESITA-1222 folds in

Its own description asks for this ("worth folding into whichever of MESITA-1218 / MESITA-1219 lands first rather than doing separately"), and it edits the same lines.

- **`PULSE_PIECE_META.index` was nine hand-typed literals** beside the array that already defines the order, with nothing tying them together. `pulseHighWater` iterates the array and returns the META index, so a reorder updating only one would skip or repeat a number — and drift the `S<n>` written to the DB. Derived now, and a test pins it.
- **The rung labels ride on both payloads** as `enrich_pulse_labels`. web-admin kept its own positional copy with no shared import, no test and no CI gate; a reorder would have put the wrong name beside every row. Both `?? 9` fallbacks go too.
- **Rung 9's failure promised a net that does not exist** — "lazy backfill remains the net", while `embedAndPersistPlaces` has zero callers anywhere in the repo (verified). It now says to re-enrich.
- **Five stale piece-index comments**, one beyond what MESITA-1222 listed: research claimed pieces `1,2,3,4,6,8` (it owns **1,2,3,4,7**), analysis called `images` piece 7 (it is **5**), contents claimed 5 and 9 (it owns **6, 8 and 9**).

## Deliberately not here

**The data half.** Pressing Re-enrich on Strana spends real Firecrawl/Apify/OpenAI budget and overwrites a live profile, so it is an operator call, not an agent one. The code is correct at any catalog size and makes that run's result legible when it happens.

**Dropping `place_research_facts`.** The DB function is now orphaned. Dropping it is a schema change on a singleton backend and deserves its own deliberate PR, not a passing mention in this one — filed as a follow-up.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `deno check supabase/functions/` | clean |
| `deno task lint` | 383 files, clean |
| `deno task test` | **479 passed, 0 failed** |
| web-admin `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| web-admin `eslint` | clean |
| web-admin `vitest run` | **86 passed** |

One correction worth recording: an audit flagged absence-as-failure pinning hours-less places at rung 1. That was verified **stale** — #1077 (MESITA-1219) already fixed it, and `pulse`/`details` are both unconditional `pieceDone` on main. Not carried over.

Closes MESITA-1218
Closes MESITA-1222
