author: saud-alnasser
body:
Closes #755. Part of #754. Stacked on #759, and the first of the three build tickets.

## 🎯 Changes

Where the control plane's own database is was the one input with no startup refusal, while `TURSO_API_TOKEN`, `TURSO_ORG` and `TURSO_GROUP` each ended the process when unset. Two failures came out of that.

Unset, `CONTROL_PLANE_DATABASE_URL` fell back to `file:./control-plane.db`, so a process meant for a hosted database built a stray file beside itself and served every account out of it. Set to a `libsql://` URL with no token, the process started, listened, and answered `/health` with a 503 that named no cause, because the route deliberately keeps the reason out of the body. That is the exact failure the guard beside it exists to prevent.

`resolveDatabase(env)` now reads the two variables and answers with a configuration or with the sentence to print before exiting. It is pure and takes its environment as an argument, which is what puts four of the five criteria at a level a test reaches directly rather than through a spawned process. `connectOrExit(report)` is the thin thing around it that the four entrypoints call, and it is the only place a process reads the real environment.

Six cases resolve: an unset or blank URL, a URL that will not parse, a URL carrying `authToken` in its query, a `file:` URL, and any other scheme with and without a token. Both values are trimmed before they are judged, which is what makes a whitespace-only token a refusal rather than a token.

**A `file:` URL stays legal and is announced as local.** What the process prints is built from the scheme and the host, or from the configured path for a file, and never from the raw URL: libSQL accepts `?authToken=` inside one, so a line that passed the URL through is a line that can print a credential.

`drizzle.config.ts` imports the resolver rather than carrying a second copy of the rule, so a migrate and a running control plane cannot disagree about which database is configured. drizzle-kit does bundle a config that imports from `src/`, which was the one thing the plan left to be decided here, and it was checked with one migrate against a `file:` URL.

### What the review changed

Two axes ran over the diff and every finding has an outcome.

**A hosted URL that names no host is now refused.** `C:/dev/control-plane.db` parses with `c:` as its scheme, so it never reached the missing-scheme refusal, and with a token set it would have been accepted as a hosted database and announced as `hosted c://`. This repository is developed on Windows, so that path is the ordinary way to write the mistake. A `libsql:` URL written without the `//` is the same defect from the other side.

**Three tests were strengthened after being shown to pass over the defect they name.**

- the `authToken`-in-query test set no token, so deleting the guard left the same input refused by the blank-token rule, in a sentence that still satisfied every assertion. It now sets the token and matches the words only that refusal uses
- `connect` was covered by a `select 1`, which any database that opens will answer, so a transposed URL passed. It now writes a row and asserts the configured file is the one that exists
- the structural guard read what a file imports, so a fifth entrypoint calling `createClient` with its own `process.env` read would have been invisible to it. A second assertion now fixes where the two variables may be read at all

Each of the three was confirmed by mutation: apply the defect, watch the test fail, restore.

### What is deferred, said plainly

**Every drizzle-kit command refuses now, not only the ones that connect.** `generate` reads `schema.ts` and `migrations/`, and `check` reads `migrations/`; both worked on a clone with no `.env` while the fallback existed, and now do not. Deferring the refusal behind a getter on `dbCredentials` was tried and does not help, because drizzle-kit reads the property while validating the config. #758 carries the decision, and `drizzle.config.ts` records the whole of it so the next reader does not rediscover it.

**No changeset.** No user can observe this, and no control-plane change has ever carried one.

The documentation is #761 and the hosted database is #762. Neither is this pull request's, and both wait on it.

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] I have added or updated the tests related to the changes made.

Thirteen added in `src/database/tests/database.test.ts`, and the suite goes from 138/136/2 to 151/149/2.

- **nine over the resolver and the announcement**: the unset variable and where it points, a URL with no scheme, a hosted URL with a token that is absent, empty or whitespace, the trimming, a `file:` URL announced as local, a relative path not announced as an absolute one, an announcement that identifies the database and carries no credential, a token in the query string, and a URL that names no host
- **one that opens a real file** and asserts the configured path is the one that exists, rather than that something answered `select 1`
- **one that spawns `prune-sessions`** with the variable blanked, asserting a non-zero exit and the message, which is what proves a refusal ends a process rather than only returning a sentence
- **two structural**: every entrypoint opens through `connectOrExit`, and no entrypoint reads the two variables for itself

body:
## 摘要

昨晚首次定时运行失败：仓库没有 `upstream-merge-needed` 标签，`ensure_label` 又把 `gh label create` 失败吞掉，随后 `gh issue create --label` 整单退出，106 个 behind commit 没有开出跟踪 issue。

本 PR 把跟踪身份改成标题前缀 `[upstream-merge]`：先建 issue，再尽力贴 label；label 失败只警告，不阻断建单。下次运行按标题去重，避免因缺 label 重复开单。

## 风险

常规风险。只改 notify 脚本、工作流注释和 SOP 表述；不改网关、鉴权、schema。不关闭 #1775，不改 `upstream-issue-watchdog.yml`。

## 验证

- `python3 scripts/upstream/notify-merge-needed.py --selftest`：42/42 通过，覆盖「label 创建失败仍能建单」和「无 label 时按标题更新」
- `python3 scripts/test_upstream_merge_preflight_anchor.py`：4 tests OK
- `./scripts/preflight.sh`：除本机 `go generate ./ent` 与已提交 generated 代码的工具链漂移外全绿。本 PR 未改 `backend/ent/schema/`；GitHub PR 模式会跳过该段。合并后需手动 `workflow_dispatch` `Upstream Merge Needed`，才能补开昨晚没开出的 issue。

## 提交

- `015fb6da2` fix(ci): 缺 label 时仍能开 upstream-merge 跟踪 issue
- 最新提交：`015fb6da2`

author: lukislp
body:
## Summary
Live feedback: with 14+ namespaces, the sidebar nav appeared to spill past the footer instead of scrolling within itself when a long section is expanded.

Reproduced locally with a synthetic 14-namespace inventory at a deliberately short viewport - Material's own `.md-sidebar__scrollwrap` already seems to handle this correctly on its own (auto-scrolls to keep the active section visible, stays bounded). Adding an explicit `max-height`/`overflow-y` reinforcement anyway - cheap, matches Material's intended behavior, and doesn't depend on that staying true across theme updates.

Given I couldn't perfectly reproduce the exact window dimensions from the original report, this is a safe, low-risk reinforcement rather than a fix for a root cause I could pin down with certainty - worth confirming on the real deployed site.

## Test plan
- [x] Full server suite green (61 passed) - CSS-only change
- [x] Reproduced a 14-namespace nav at multiple constrained viewport sizes locally, confirmed no regression and the scroll wrapper stays properly bounded
- [ ] Live: confirm the original overflow no longer reproduces in the real browser/window size where it was seen

author: pquarterman17
body:
Closes P1 item R3 from `plans/POST_SPRINT_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW.md` (#205), through four review rounds.

## The audited defect (verified, then fixed)

`commit()`'s re-probe compared the fresh checksum only against the *preview's* snapshot — a row recorded as checksum A that previewed `unknown` (null preview checksum), was individually escalated, then re-probed as checksum B at commit sailed through and silently replaced recorded provenance A with B. Commit now looks up the live dataset per row and recomputes the verdict from its **recorded** provenance against a fresh probe: a fresh conflict refuses unconditionally (escalation approves "unverifiable", never "verified-different"); an escalated still-unknown row commits but preserves the original recorded fields (only the path moves — no fabricated provenance); a dataset removed or identity-changed between preview and commit fails closed per row.

## What the review rounds added

- **Consent guard restored and strengthened**: an escalated row also refuses when the fresh probe contradicts what Preview *showed the user* — at checksum level when available, stat level otherwise.
- **Guard-level stat fallback** (final round): both commit-time guards previously inherited `sourceChangeVerdict`'s "never demote a recorded checksum to stats" display rule, which made them verify *nothing* whenever the checksum leg was unconfirmable — the dominant desktop path (see below). A dedicated `guardVerdict` falls back to size/mtime comparison inside the guards only; the display verdict and the backfill/preserve decision keep the strict rule, so a stat match on an unconfirmable checksum is never mistaken for confirmation.
- **Provenance backfill**: a legacy dataset with nothing recorded that clears the consent guard genuinely acquires the confirmed probe's provenance (the documented gap-fill), instead of staying blank forever.
- **Write-window TOCTOU closed**: the pre-write re-check requires referential identity of the exact `source` object each verdict was computed against — a same-path provenance swap (project reload, undo) during the awaited probes fails closed.
- **Honest per-bucket reporting**: refusal toasts distinguish "conflicts with recorded provenance", "changed since Preview", "could not be re-verified", "unreachable", and "moved/reimported", with escalation advice shown only for rows the panel actually offers "use anyway" on.

## KNOWN LIMITATION (documented, deliberately not "fixed")

The consent-model investigation (review round 3) found candidate paths are **never read-consented** in the desktop app — `pick_files` grants per-file on a real dialog gesture, `pick_directory` deliberately grants nothing, and `grant_source_paths` is hardened to the declared-source set — so candidate probes carry null checksums and every checksum-dependent branch degrades to stat-level verification there. Per the no-consent-widening ruling, no backend change was made; the limitation is documented in `store/relink.ts` and pinned by a consent-accurate degradation test. Whether relink should gain a real per-file dialog gesture (which would enable checksum verification) is an owner product decision, booked in the plan.

## Gates

Every fix red-first (guard scenarios verified against reverted patches). New pure `lib/relink.ts` (`evaluateCommitProbe` + `guardVerdict`, 8-case unit suite); `store/relink.ts` under the 500-line ceiling. tsc + eslint clean; full `vitest run` 8117 green pre-merge; post-merge with main (#207–#209): bundle OK under the integrated budget, relink suites 68/68.

author: papi-ux
body:
## summary

- stop the exact session-owned Steam app lineage before requesting full client shutdown
- require the pinned `gameprocess_log.txt` stop event plus a five-second settle before `steam -shutdown`
- hard-kill only captured private Steam pidfds when ownership, app quiescence, log identity, or native shutdown is incomplete
- keep Steam `SIGTERM` out of fallback teardown so it cannot re-enter the crashing destructor path

## why

this is a follow-up to #525. the guarded native shutdown path fixed the raw pidfd `SIGTERM` race, but a later smoke exposed a second failure inside Steam itself.

Polaris requested `steam -shutdown` while Steam was still removing the game process graph, stopping recording, releasing compatibility state, and running AutoCloud exit work. Steam then asserted in its Depot Download HTTP client and crashed before the client root exited.

this change makes app teardown and client teardown separate ordered phases. it matches both NUL-separated and space-delimited `SteamLaunch AppId=<id>` forms, revalidates `/proc` identity around pidfd capture, freezes and drains token-stripped descendants, and fails closed on every ambiguous boundary.

## verification

- regression RED against the old ordering
- focused GREEN after implementation
- sabotage RED with app quiescence removed, then restored GREEN
- reviewer-remediation RED for split argv, prefix boundaries, empty-root barrier bypass, moved-helper waits, and frozen-process recovery
- second sabotage RED with split matching disabled and the empty-root bypass restored
- Steam shutdown tests: 24/24
- full CTest: 18/18
- web tests: 506/506
- lint: pass
- production web build: pass
- npm audit: zero vulnerabilities
- production non-test binary build and version probe: pass
- independent exact-diff review: approved

exact-head CI, including the sanitizer lane, is still required before merge.

## boundaries

no deployment, service restart, device work, tag, release, or branch cleanup is included here.

author: saud-alnasser
body:
Closes #756. Part of #754. Stacked on #760, whose behaviour it documents.

## 🎯 Changes

Both files said the opposite of what #760 made true. `.env.example` presented `file:./control-plane.db` as the default and the token as something only a hosted database needs; the README described a copy somebody is running locally and said nothing about where its records live.

A hosted Turso database is now the ordinary configuration and a local file is the development one. Neither is a default: the URL is required, the token is required where the URL is hosted, and the refusal each produces is quoted from what the code prints rather than paraphrased.

### The example file names no database

`CONTROL_PLANE_DATABASE_URL=` ships empty, which is what the three Turso variables in the same file already do for the same reason. A copied, unedited `.env` then refuses on the variable that is actually missing:

    CONTROL_PLANE_DATABASE_URL is not set. See .env.example, the control plane has
    no database to open without it.

It carried a `libsql://PASTE_YOUR_..._HERE` placeholder until review, and that was wrong in a way worth recording. The placeholder parses, it has a host, and it is therefore a valid hosted configuration: paste a token beside it and the process starts, listens, and answers `/health` with a 503 naming no cause. That is verbatim the second of the two failures #760 exists to end, reintroduced by the file documenting the fix.

### What the review found stale

Two claims in the README described the code as it was before #760, and one of them sat two hundred lines from a new paragraph asserting the opposite.

- **The startup line no longer prints the URL.** `describe` builds it from the scheme and the host, or the path for a file, because libSQL accepts a token inside a URL. The health-check section still said the URL goes to stdout.
- **`db:migrate` does not create a hosted database.** It applies migrations. A Turso database is created by a Platform API call, and neither file had a step that produced one. Both the *Running it locally* sequence and the *Run it* block said it did, the second in a comment the first draft never touched.

Three more, each raised by one axis and fixed here:

- the refusal rule was reduced to two cases when there are four, and the one a reader will actually hit is a Windows path, which parses with its drive letter as the scheme and is refused for naming no host
- the token's expiration is a deadline the spec records and neither file did, so `expiration=3d` now carries its consequence: a token minted that way takes the control plane down three days later
- the sentence explaining why libSQL is the client here kept its "which is why" and lost the argument behind it, which is restored

The enumeration of what refuses now names `generate` and `check` alongside the migrate and the process, and points at #758, which carries that decision.

**No changeset.** Nothing here is user-visible, and no control-plane change has ever carried one.

The hosted database itself is #762, and so are `references/turso` and `references/drizzle-kit`. This pull request documents the configuration; it establishes nothing about a database that exists.

## ✅ Checklist

- [ ] I have added or updated the tests related to the changes made.

No tests. Both files are documentation, `.env.example` and the control plane's README, so there is no source and no behaviour to cover. The suite is unchanged at 151/149/2.

author: quartermile02
body:
## Summary

Builds the proposal from `known-issues/2026-08-22-roll-vinyl-migrate-pass-proposal.md` into working code, per instruction.

**No database migration is required.** `accept_family_proposal` (182) and `add_variant_to_existing_material` (183) are already fully generic over `material_type_id` and already fail loudly on a missing variant multiplier — confirmed by reading both, not assumed. Roll proposals reuse them unchanged.

## Part 1 — type-aware migrate screen

The screen was hardcoded to one material type (`page.tsx`: `.eq('material_type_id', substrateType.id)`) — any row of any other type was never fetched, not filtered-to-zero, just invisible. That's exactly what hid 5 real "Substrates" rows behind a tab reading "NEW (1)" in the prior investigation.

- `?type=` URL param + a plain `<select>` over `material_types`
- `FAMILY_CONFIGS`: material-type-name → `FamilyAxisConfig` lookup
- an unconfigured type shows an explicit banner + a flat, dismissible row list — **never** an empty screen (empty is indistinguishable from "nothing to do", the exact bug that hid the 5 rows)
- per-type NEW counts in the picker, computed with explicit, unbounded pagination (`dbAllOrThrow`, new in `lib/db.ts`)
- the `shopvox_materials` row fetch itself is now paginated — Roll Materials is 368 today but Accessories is already 469; PostgREST silently truncates at 1000
- the NEW counter comes straight from the paginated fetch, never from `proposals`; a client-side check compares the two and surfaces a red banner if they ever disagree, instead of trusting the invariant silently

## Part 2 — ROLL_FAMILY_CONFIG

Confirmed against all 368 live NEW "Roll Materials" rows (full investigation in the known-issues doc):

- **Axis**: oz (weight, 48 rows) or Mil (thickness, 224 rows) — mutually exclusive, zero overlap.
- **Mil vs ML**: the regex lives in its own plain-JS module (`src/lib/roll-axis-regex.js`) specifically so it's provable with zero build step. "Mil" cannot structurally match "ML" (ink volume tokens like `700ML`) — literal `mil` needs an `i` that `ml` doesn't have. Proven in `scripts/verify-roll-axis-regex.mjs` — run `node scripts/verify-roll-axis-regex.mjs`.
- **Width**: includes the bare quote-inch form (`54"`) from the start — one real row uses it without ever writing "in".
- **Brand/product-line** (Oracal 651, Avery SW900, 3M 180C) is FAMILY-DISTINGUISHING, confirmed by Ruben. Extended `FamilyAxisConfig` with an optional `findAxisSpan` (roll-style: axis is a bounded token, unlike substrate's "rest of string" `findAxisStart`) and added `brand` as a new `FamilyProposal` field — folded into the grouping key and the generated family name. **No new database column** — nothing reads it as structured data.
- **89 no-axis rows** (Pre-Mask Tape, some vinyl grades named only by brand/model) group by line/brand alone, flagged medium confidence — correct and honest per instruction, not an error. This required loosening "no axis → forced singleton", but **only** for configs that opt in via `findAxisSpan` — substrate behavior is untouched (see regression check below).
- **"Grommet"** (no width in the name, no stored width) now forces LOW confidence via a structural `p.width == null` check, not special-cased by name.
- **No length_increment/cut-to-length** path added — checked directly, nothing in the live dataset needs it (the 9 DB-width-null rows: 8 carry an explicit width in the name, the 9th is Grommet). Substrates' existing cut-to-length handling (`stripCutToLengthWidth`, the 12in Polycarbonate increment) is untouched.
- Never invents a multiplier or cost.

## Regression check — substrates unchanged

Ran the same `buildFamilyProposals` call against the live 235-row Substrates dataset, once against the committed `HEAD` parser and once against this branch's parser (all-status, since all 235 rows are already MIGRATED and there are 0 NEW rows to exercise otherwise):

```
Total families: 96
Families by confidence: { high: 69, medium: 4, low: 23 }
```

**Identical both times.** This does differ from Build 1b's historically-reported "102 families" — confirmed that gap is pre-existing (present in `HEAD` before this branch touched anything), i.e. data drift since that report, not a regression introduced here.

## Dry run — final numbers

368 NEW Roll Materials rows, this branch's `ROLL_FAMILY_CONFIG`, live data:

```
Total families: 170
Families by confidence: { high: 62, medium: 19, low: 89 }
Rows by confidence:     { high: 172, medium: 107, low: 89 }   (sums to 368)
```

This differs from the read-only investigation's 191/76/2/113 **on purpose**: that investigation's throwaway script forced every axis-less row into its own singleton, while this build implements "group by line/brand alone" per this session's explicit instruction. Not a silent drift — flagged here as requested.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npm run lint` on every file touched this session — clean (project-wide lint has ~285 pre-existing errors/warnings in unrelated files, untouched by this PR)
- `npm run build` — succeeds
- `node scripts/verify-roll-axis-regex.mjs` — all 13 checks pass
- All scratch scripts that read `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` were deleted before this PR; `git status --porcelain` is clean of them

author: saud-alnasser
body:
Part of #757, which stays open, and part of #754. Top of the stack, on #761.

**This is the test and the rules around it.** The databases it runs against do not exist yet, and creating them is the human's, so #757 does not close here.

## 🎯 Changes

`src/database/tests/hosted.test.ts` migrates the control plane's own database over the wire, serves a sign-in and a mint from it, reads every row back out with a separate query, and asserts that a transaction which throws leaves nothing behind. That last one is the whole reason this exists: the effort rested on the assumption that a remote honours an interactive transaction, and an assumption converted is the difference between the wire being tested and being trusted.

**It provisions nothing on Turso.** The platform is `tursoInMemory()` and the workspace database the mint opens is a file in a temporary directory, so no database is created on anybody's account. Provisioning already has its own live test, and a second one would leave databases behind that the delete-protected group will not give back.

### What the review changed

Two axes ran independently. Ten findings, and two of them would have cost a live run for nothing.

**A `file:` URL would have passed all four tests without leaving the machine.** The configuration was hand-written as `{ kind: 'hosted' }` and `describe` branches on `kind`, so both guards over it were tautologies: a `file:` URL was announced as `hosted file://`, `createClient` ignores an `authToken` on one, and the migrate, the sign-in, the transaction and the `select 1` all succeeded against a file on disk. The live variables now go through `resolveDatabase` under the names it reads, which derives the kind instead of declaring it and inherits every other rule with it. Measured: with a `file:` URL all four now fail, and no file is created.

**The sign-in test could not have passed.** It asserted that the platform was asked for no workspace database, which contradicted the assertion three lines above it that sign-up returned a workspace. Sign-up creates one; what keeps it off a real account is the stub being the platform, not the count being zero. Two more counts went the same way and are now properties rather than arithmetic: the mint mints twice, once to open the workspace database and once to answer, and the migration path opens more connections than a test should be counting. What is asserted is that every token was for a database this test's own stub created.

**Cleanup was keyed on an account id read after three assertions**, so the paths that actually leak rows skipped it. The account row is written before provisioning runs, so a sign-in that failed part-way left one behind in a database that is reused and cannot be deleted. It is keyed on the Google subject now, which is known before the request is sent, and it runs unconditionally.

**Requirement 7 asks for a mint and acceptance criterion 7 omits it.** The spec outranks, so the mint is covered. It cannot be asked at the version the workspace is already at, because the route's declared body puts `minimum: 1` on `schemaVersion` and a workspace just created sits at 0, so a mint always migrates. That is what the file-backed workspace database is for.

Every assertion in the sign-in test was then reproduced against a file-backed control-plane database with the identical plane, since a hosted one does not exist: health, sign-in, the four row read-backs, the mint at version 5, the version recorded, the platform counters, and the cleanup.

### The rules this widened, said rather than absorbed

`.aep/rules/testing.md`, under *Tests that reach a live remote*, enumerated two live tests and named the property each was admitted for. There are three now, and the third has a property the other two do not: whether a remote honours what the client asks of it. A `file:` database cannot answer that. It is written into the rule with the date and the ticket, along with a note that the count in the heading is the thing that goes stale, and that a fourth is a decision somebody takes in that section rather than a file that quietly appears. `.aep/rules/credentials.md` said "one declared exception" and now defers the count to where it belongs.

**One flag arms every live test in the package.** `RENTABLE_LIVE_TURSO=1` is read by `provisioning.test.ts` too and the suite glob collects both files, so setting it in a `.env` provisions two `ws-` databases per run whether or not that was wanted. The test's docstring, `.env.example` and the rule all say so, and all three point at the single-file invocation instead. `.env.example` deliberately does not list the opt-in among the values to fill in.

### What is deferred

Criteria 6 and 8, and the live half of 7. The two databases have not been created, no token has been minted, nothing has been migrated, and `references/turso` and `references/drizzle-kit` are untouched, because what they record is what a live run establishes rather than what a test file claims. That run is the human's to authorise, one step at a time, and #757 stays open until it has happened.

**No changeset.** Nothing here is user-visible.

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] I have added or updated the tests related to the changes made.

Four added in `src/database/tests/hosted.test.ts`, and the suite goes from 151/149/2 to 155/149/6. All four are skipped unless `RENTABLE_LIVE_TURSO=1` is set, so an ordinary run and the gate are exactly what they are today, and the skip reaches the summary line with its reason.

- **every migration in this build applies to a hosted database**, with every table in `schema.ts` present afterwards and `__drizzle_migrations` holding one row per `.sql` file in `migrations/`
- **the control plane serves a sign-in from a hosted database**, with the account, session, workspace and membership rows read back out by a separate query, and a mint answered
- **a transaction that throws leaves nothing behind**, which is the assumption this file exists to convert into a measurement
- **the hosted database answers**, the connection itself

author: rilegu
body:
A device identity is a segment of the topic it publishes to, so on an anonymous broker the claim to be dev-000042 in site-00 is made by the publisher and checked by nobody. Any client able to reach port 1883 could publish as any device, retire one with a false Last Will, or subscribe to the whole fleet. Nothing downstream re-checks it, by design: re-verifying identity at every stage would put an authentication decision in the hot path of a service whose job is throughput. So it is established once, at the edge.

Mosquitto now listens on 8883 with a certificate from a project CA, requires a client certificate signed by the same CA, and derives the MQTT username from the certificate Common Name. An access control list grants each device exactly its own three publish topics and its own command topic. Ingest holds a separate identity with the fleet-wide subscription. Plaintext survives in a second configuration file, bound to loopback and selected by name; nothing falls back to it.

Permissions are written per device rather than as a pattern. The only substitution mosquitto offers is the username, and the site segment sits ahead of the device id in the topic, so the closest available pattern would let a device publish under its own name into another site, corrupting that site aggregates with no error anywhere. Reasoning in ADR-0009.

tools/pki issues the tree, in Go rather than as a shell script around openssl: the dashboards are Windows applications, so a bootstrap step assuming openssl on PATH fails on the platform most likely to be used here, and the access control list has to be generated from the same fleet naming the simulator uses. That naming moves to contracts/naming.go, because a device identity now appears in four places that must agree exactly -- the topic, the certificate, the username derived from it, and the list entry -- and when they disagree the broker simply denies the publish and the device goes quiet with nothing in its own logs to explain why.

Keys are P-256. The stress profile provisions ten thousand devices, and that many RSA keys costs minutes of CPU where the elliptic curve equivalents cost seconds.

Four things this got wrong first, none of them visible without running it.

tls.Client needs ServerName set explicitly. tls.Dial infers one from the address it was given; tls.Client is handed an already-open socket and cannot. Go then refuses the handshake before sending a byte, which the broker reported as unexpected eof while reading, 2903 times, with no mention of certificates anywhere. The fleet logged itself as connected and published nothing.

Two access control grants were defined and never rendered into the file. That hid because the healthcheck exits on subscribe acknowledgement and passes even when the subscription was denied. There is now a test that every capability reaches the file.

The healthcheck spoke only TLS, so the plaintext configuration never started: the broker stayed unhealthy and every dependent refused to launch. It now tries secure and falls back to plaintext, which cannot mask a broken TLS setup because 1883 does not exist in that configuration.

.dockerignore did not exclude the generated tree. A key baked into an image layer stays there even when a later layer deletes it.

tools/security_test.py tries to cross each line rather than trusting the configuration: impersonation, cross-site publishing, a fleet-wide subscription from a device, an untrusted CA, an anonymous connect, and an unauthenticated session on the plaintext port. Denial is observed from a subscription, because MQTT 3.1.1 gives a publisher no way to learn that its message was refused, and every negative case is paired with a positive control -- all of them would otherwise pass against a broker that was simply down. Confirmed by granting one device a wildcard and watching three scenarios go red.

The chaos suite now holds a test-harness certificate. Injecting messages as devices that were never provisioned is exactly what this change prevents, so the capability is named and granted deliberately rather than obtained by leaving the broker open.

CI provisions a tree before starting the stack and runs the new suite after the contract checks.

author: elfensky
body:
## What

`lintle verify` and `lintle dedup` printed nothing between the roster and the final results table when stdout is not a terminal — on the full corpus, `verify --orbit` was 2 h 05 m of silence in a redirected log (issue #221; measured in the archived 2026-08-11 corpus run). `clean` already had the off-TTY per-file branch; `UnitTable` had no counterpart.

## How

The off-TTY policy moves into the shared base as `_LiveTable._plain_line` (plain `markup=False` print when not live, no-op on a TTY):

- `UnitTable.finish` emits one line per completed unit — string cells in column order; renderable cells (the progress bar) have no plain form and are skipped.
- `UnitTable.phase` prints each **new** label once (repeat labels don't reprint; `phase(None)` never prints).
- `ProgressDisplay.file_done` routes through the same helper instead of its own branch.

Piped output now looks like:

```
[1/2] tle01 — size 420B, records 3, hard 0, soft 0
[2/2] tle02 — size 420B, records 3, hard 0, soft 0
sorting records and checking contradictions…
writing 04-verify…
```

This restores the ARCHITECTURE.md contract that verify/dedup render the same way as clean, off a TTY included.

## Decisions (from the issue's verified-approach comment)

- The test pinning the old silence (`test_off_a_tty_prints_the_roster_then_the_results`) is updated to expect the per-unit lines.
- verify's per-unit line carries **stream-time** hard/soft (usually 0 — real counts are attributed post-pass via `update`, which stays silent); the final table carries the truth. Accepted rather than dropping the cells: the line stays one definition of "what a finished unit reports".
- Line volume: phase relabels are throttled by the callers (every 250k records in verify's sort → a few hundred lines on the full corpus; every 10k in dedup's write → tens of thousands worst-case, ~1 MB of log on a 49 m run). Accepted as-is; a further throttle can land later if it proves too chatty.

Out of scope (noted in the issue): `cli_progress.status(...)` still returns `nullcontext()` off a TTY, so dedup's/extract's spinner messages remain silent.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest` — 1085 passed
- `uv run ruff check .` / `uv run ruff format --check .` — clean
- Smoke: piped `verify` + `dedup` on a tiny generated corpus show the lines above; TTY rendering unchanged.

Closes #221 (manual close — develop-targeted PRs don't auto-close here).

author: juanmicrosoft
body:
## Summary

- **Task**: v0.14 nullability task #5 — pin or narrow `object.ToString()` / `StringOp.ToString` result annotation.
- **Decision**: **NARROW**. `StringOp.ToString` (aka `(str x)`) is now stamped `Annotated` at bind time; every other STRING-returning `StringOp` (Substring, Trim, ToUpper, Concat, Format, …) stays `NotAnnotated` per BCL contract.
- **Why narrow (not pin)**: `object.ToString()` returns `string?` per modern BCL — subtype overrides can and do return null. The prior `NotAnnotated` stamp was theoretically unsound: `§B{s:string} (str x)` silently passed Calor0272 even though the initializer could be null at runtime. Sound analysis is worth the small chance of extra diagnostic noise; downstream `.unwrap` / null-check catches any real cases.
- **Fallout**: zero. `Calor.Compiler.Tests` (7574 total, 7569 pass, 5 local corpus skips) and `Calor.Semantics.Tests` (37 pass) stay green. No downstream Calor0272/0273/0274 misfires.

## Change

`BindStringOperation` in `src/Calor.Compiler/Binding/Binder.cs` now splits STRING-returning ops into two soundness buckets and stamps `StringOp.ToString` results as `Annotated`. The comment block documents both buckets so a future refactor won't accidentally regress. `StringBuilder.ToString()` is unchanged (real BCL contract is non-null).

## Test plan

- [x] Added `Calor0272_Fires_For_StringOperation_ToString_Bound_To_NonNullString` — exercises the full lex→parse→bind pipeline, asserts Calor0272 fires with source annotation `'Annotated'`, plus belt-and-braces bound-tree assertion on the initializer's `NominalBoundType.NullableAnnotation` so the diagnostic can't silently disappear from a stamp regression.
- [x] `dotnet test tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/` — 7569 pass, 0 fail (5 skips are local corpus-submodule / network — expected in CI to be 3).
- [x] `dotnet test tests/Calor.Semantics.Tests/` — 37 pass.
- [x] Existing `Calor0272_DoesNotFire_For_StringOperation_Trim_Bound_To_NonNullString` and `..._Substr_...` still green — the narrow is scoped to `StringOp.ToString` only.

author: johnnyt
body:
Fixes st-dmfg.

Spec 6.2 requires a session terminating before a delay elapses to discard the message without delivering it. The library implemented that only in `terminate/2`, but `:done` deliberately idles the process rather than stopping it, so an idled session's timers stayed armed and a delayed `<send>` scheduled before the halt still fired and delivered. test187's invoked child was the observed case - masked today only by the parent-side 6.4.3 live-table drain guard, which no non-parent route has.

- `perform_instruction({:halt, _})` now calls `discard_pending_timers/2`: `:done` and `:cancelled` both mean `exit_interpreter/1` ran, so both cancel every live timer ref and reset the timer tables.
- `:budget_exhausted` keeps its timers armed - the core is still `running` and only a later `cancel/1` terminates it; that cancel's own halt then discards.
- A new `handle_info/2` clause covers the in-flight race: a timer message already mailboxed when the halt ran is discarded unrecorded and undelivered.
- Two regression tests observe the discard from the receiving end of a cross-session `{:session, sid}` route (the one with no receiver-side guard), for the `:done` and `cancel/1` paths. Sabotage verified: each half mutated alone stays green, the pair mutated together reddens both tests.
- Session's moduledoc and `docs/durable-timers.md` updated; the durable host's delivery-time liveness contract is unchanged.

Full `mix quality` green: 2,520 tests, 96.3% coverage, regression ratchet passed.

author: beahead-ab
body:
Fas 1a ur kravmatrisen (`ST-04`, `ST-05`, `DV-05`, `DV-06`). Tre tillstånd som ytan saknade form för — och, efter granskningen, två sätt cachen kunde visa fel sak för fel person.

**Vem det är för:** en befintlig användare med data märker ingenting i normalfallet. Det som ändras är dagen som saknar mätning, dagen utan nät och kontot som är en dag gammalt.

## 1. Cachen tillhörde ingen — nu tillhör den ett konto

Den första versionen nycklade den lagrade dagen på ingenting. **Två personer som delar en dator hade läst varandras måltider, vikt och sömn.**

Rättat i tre lager:

- **Sessionsgränsen städar.** `applyToCache` anropas från alla fyra vägar in och ut — återställd session, ny inloggning, utgången session, utloggning. Regeln finns på **ett** ställe just för att en glömd väg annars vore en läcka.
- **Ingen identitet, inget minne.** En session utan `user.id` varken läser eller skriver. Att falla stängt kostar en omhämtning.
- **Varje läsning och skrivning namnger sitt konto.** Stämmer inte ägaren *raderas* lagringen i stället för att bara nekas — nästa person som loggar in tar första läsningen, och då är den förras dag redan borta.

Utloggning städar även när servern inte svarar.

## 2. Datumet kunde visa en annan dag

Att bläddra till ett annat datum lämnade den gamla dagen på skärmen medan den nya laddades — och om laddningen föll utan cache, för gott. Ett datums siffror under ett annats rubrik.

- Varje laddare **nollställer först**: dagen, historikfönstret, passgenvägen och pågåendemärket. De hörde till dagen de lästes för.
- En misslyckad hämtning faller tillbaka på **det datumets egen cache** eller på ingenting alls. Aldrig en granndag.
- Renderingen går genom `dayOnScreen`, som vägrar en dag vars datum inte är datumet i rubriken. Den finns för svaret som landar efter att läsaren bläddrat vidare.

## 3. En nolla är inte tystnad

`0 av 165 g` klockan sju säger att ett mål missats. Det tomma tillståndet har nu en egen form: tankstreck där talet står, skalan som streckad kontur, ringen som streckad cirkel, kurvan som baslinje utan linje. Höjden är oförändrad, så ingenting hoppar när första mätvärdet landar.

`measured` skiljer **tystnad** (rita tomt) från **frånvaro** (utelämna raden) — två begrepp som en nolla annars slår ihop.

## 4. Vad som faktiskt fungerar utan nät

[`docs/OFFLINE.md`](https://github.com/beahead-ab/bealegend-web/blob/claude/forsta-dagen/docs/OFFLINE.md) säger det rakt ut, inklusive vad som **inte** gör det.

| Fungerar | Fungerar inte |
|---|---|
| Dagen på Idag, med »Senast hämtat 07:12« | Historikfönstret — kurvor och veckans pass |
| Startsidans form (dashboardkonfigurationen cachas) | Dagens pass och »Pågår« |
| Passkörningens kö, idempotent | Samtalet och inloggningen |
| Tomma tillstånd och vägarna in | |

**Offlinekravet är alltså delvis uppfyllt.** Dagen och ytans form finns; fönstret och passgenvägen gör det inte. Dokumentet säger det, och matrisen har `ST-05` som delvis av samma skäl.

## Verifierat

| | Utfall |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | **209 pass, 0 fail** — 174 fanns, 35 är nya |
| `npm run build` (`tsc -b` ingår) | grönt |
| `npm run lint` | inga nya fel |

Testerna för isoleringen körs mot **den riktiga `localStorage`**, inte mot en attrapp: kontobyte, utgången session, utloggning, en ägarlös lagring från ett äldre bygge, skräp i lagringen, en rad under fel datum, och datumspärren.

Formerna renderade i huvudlös Chromium — riktiga komponenter, riktig CSS — i ljust och mörkt, på 390 px och 1100 px, inklusive felraden när ingen cache finns.

## Versionsnivå

**1.3.0 → 1.4.0**, minor. Tre tillstånd en användare kan nå fick en form de saknade. Bakåtkompatibelt. `package.json` följde med — testet som binder den mot `VERSION` fångade det innan bygget hann ljuga.

## Kvar, medvetet

`rangeBar` behåller ordets egen mening i värdet (»Inget mätt i natt«) i stället för tankstreck. Den formen granskades och mergades i fas 2b och ligger utanför den här leveransen — men den gör att två tomma vokabulärer syns på samma kort. Värt ett beslut, inte värt att smyga in här.

author: selamet
body:
Closes #65.

Section 19 asks that `ruff check`, `mypy` and `pytest` all pass. Section 8.8 asks for N+1 detection in CI. Two of those five things were being checked.

## mypy: 736 errors, none of them silenced

`[tool.mypy]` was there — `strict = true`, both Django plugins, stubs installed — and nothing ever called it. The first run:

```
$ uv run mypy .
Found 736 errors in 63 files (checked 162 source files)
```

Where they were:

| | errors | |
|---|---:|---|
| `apps/`, `core/`, `config/` | 184 | 4 missing annotations, 180 real |
| `tests/` | 552 | 505 of them a missing `-> None` |

Shipped code is now clean at full strict — no `ignore_errors`, no module dropped from the run. The 180 were not noise. In descending order of what they were worth:

**The tenant managers were untyped, by typo.** `SoftDeleteQuerySet(models.QuerySet["Any"])` — a *string* forward reference to a name the module never imported. Every read through `objects` came back as `Any` and carried it into whatever the caller returned, which is where a third of the "returning Any" errors came from. They are generic over the model now, so `Elevator.objects.first()` is an `Elevator`.

**Thirty-odd views read `company_id` straight off `request.user`,** which DRF types as `User | AnonymousUser` because a view is allowed to be public. All of them sit behind a permission class that has already refused the anonymous case — but had one ever slipped through, the answer would have been a 500 from an `AttributeError`, not the 401 or 403 it should be. `core/requests.py` holds three accessors that make it the right status code, and the union disappears at the call sites.

**Three annotations were comfortable lies.** `_WithCompany.objects` was declared `Manager[Any]` and returns a QuerySet. `next_contract_number(company_id: str)` is passed a `UUID` by all three of its callers. `TokenPair.refresh_expires_at` was `object`, and was being handed to `set_cookie(expires=...)`.

**Serializers and viewsets now name the model they serve** — `TenantViewSet[Building]`, `ModelSerializer[Contract]` — which is what makes `perform_destroy(self, instance: Building)` in a subclass the obvious thing to write rather than an override error.

### What is relaxed, and why

One thing, and it is written down in `pyproject.toml` beside the entry that does it: `tests.*` is not asked for its own annotations. `disallow_untyped_defs`, `disallow_incomplete_defs`, `disallow_untyped_calls` and `disallow_any_generics` are off for the test package only.

That is the 505 `-> None`s. Adding them would have been a five-hundred-line diff that finds nothing, and it would have buried the part of this change that matters. **Every rule that finds a mistake stays on for tests** — a test calling a service with the wrong type, or reading an attribute a model does not have, still fails the gate. It found twenty such, all fixed here: `timezone.timedelta` in four files (it is not part of that module's API), an `__exit__` annotated `-> bool` and therefore promising it might swallow exceptions, a monkeypatch reaching through a module's re-export rather than at the module itself.

Turning the four back on is a mechanical afternoon. The comment in `pyproject.toml` says so, and says it should happen the next time the suite is touched wholesale — not as the price of having a gate at all.

Six libraries publish no type information (`environ`, `boto3`, `botocore`, `qrcode`, `weasyprint`, `django_filters`, `zen_queries`) and are named one by one rather than by switching `ignore_missing_imports` on globally, so the day one of them starts shipping types is not silently absorbed. Three `type: ignore`s remain in shipped code, each with the reason above it: two manager overrides django-stubs does not model, and drf-spectacular's unannotated `__init_subclass__`.

## N+1: django-zen-queries, and it found one on the first run

One of the two tools 8.8 names, wired into the test run through an autouse fixture in `tests/conftest.py`. While a list is being serialised, the database is closed. The rows are fetched first — with whatever joins and prefetches the view declared — and a query after that means the serialiser is reaching for something the queryset did not bring, which is the definition of the thing.

Every list-endpoint test already in the suite is now also an N+1 test, at no per-test cost. Production is untouched: a slow page there is still better than a 500.

The premise of the issue was that the joins were already right and only the guardrail was missing. That turned out to be true for eight of the nine list endpoints.

**`GET /api/v1/contracts/` was a live N+1.** The read serializer renders every line of every contract, and sums the open ones for the monthly total, against a queryset that declared `select_related("customer")` and nothing else. With the guard on, seven existing tests went red immediately:

```
zen_queries.decorators.QueriesDisabledError: SELECT "contract_elevator"."id", ...
  FROM "contract_elevator" WHERE (... AND "contract_elevator"."contract_id" = %s)
  ORDER BY "contract_elevator"."added_at" DESC
ERROR django.request: Internal Server Error: /api/v1/contracts/
```

In counts, with the guard removed so the numbers are visible:

```
E  AssertionError: The contract list costs 12 queries for one contract and 39 for four.
   A list whose cost depends on its length is the N+1 in section 8.8.
E  assert 39 == 12
```

Fixed here with the `Prefetch` it always needed.

## Proof the guard catches something

Deleting `.select_related(*ADDRESS_JOIN)` from the customers list — one line, no test asserts on it, the response body is identical:

```
$ uv run pytest -q
FAILED tests/test_customer_api.py::TestBillingAddress::test_the_list_carries_the_names_too
1 failed, 578 passed, 2 skipped

zen_queries.decorators.QueriesDisabledError: SELECT "neighborhood"."id", "neighborhood"."district_id",
  "neighborhood"."name", ... FROM "neighborhood" WHERE "neighborhood"."id" = %s LIMIT 21
ERROR django.request: Internal Server Error: /api/v1/customers/
```

Deleting the `Prefetch` from the contracts list:

```
$ uv run pytest -q
FAILED tests/test_filters.py::TestFilteringByRelation::test_contracts_by_customer
FAILED tests/test_n_plus_one.py::TestTheContractListStaysFlat::test_the_query_count_does_not_grow_with_the_rows
2 failed, 577 passed, 2 skipped
```

Both reverted. And because a guard nobody has seen fail is indistinguishable from one that inspects nothing, `tests/test_n_plus_one.py` makes it fail on purpose and keeps doing so — a three-field serializer walking one un-joined foreign key, asserted to raise; the same serializer with the join, asserted to be quiet; and the contract list's query count asserted not to move with its length, which holds even if the guard itself is ever disabled.

## Cost

Measured on the runner, comparing this branch against the CI run for the commit it sits on ([`a354ba0`](https://github.com/selamet/shiftlush-api/actions/runs/32606743709) vs [this branch](https://github.com/selamet/shiftlush-api/actions/runs/32606858161)):

| step | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| Types (new) | — | **10s** |
| Tests | 75s | 79s |
| backend job, end to end | 1m58s | 2m16s |

**mypy costs 10 seconds**, cold, with no cache — a shade under 9% of the job. It is placed before the tests, so a type error is reported before the Postgres service and the migrations have been paid for. No `.mypy_cache` is restored between runs: a cache keyed on the lockfile would mostly miss on a branch that changes source, and restoring it costs about what the check does.

**The N+1 guard is not separable from noise.** Tests went 75s → 79s, and four of this PR's new tests are inside that number. Locally, across three runs each: 16.0 / 19.2 / 20.0s with the guard, 14.9 / 17.3 / 17.6s without — overlapping spreads. The mechanism says why: one context manager per list serialisation, and no extra queries. The remaining 4s of the job delta is the `apt-get` step, which took 6s on

author: bjmeetsfo
body:
The keep-alive pool reconnects and sends the request again whenever a pooled socket
fails. For the case it was written for that is exactly right: the server reaps idle
sockets, the next exchange on one fails immediately with a reset or a broken pipe or
an EOF, nothing was ever served on it, and reconnecting is transparent.

It was doing the same thing after a timeout, and a timeout is not that. The peer
accepted the request and did not answer in time. It may have processed it. Sending
it again on a fresh socket applies a write twice.

This sits one layer below the routing guard that just stopped re-sending writes of
unknown outcome, and it would have undone that guard from underneath: the routing
layer can decline to retry all it likes while the transport quietly retries for it.

Now a pooled exchange that fails with a timeout returns the error. Every other
failure still reconnects and re-sends, so the reaped-socket path -- the reason the
fallback exists -- is untouched.

Deliberately applied to all requests rather than only writes. The transport does not
know a write from a read, and threading that through every caller would put the
decision in more places than can be kept honest. Reads lose nothing that matters:
the routing layer above already refreshes and retries a read on any backend failure,
so the recovery is still there, one layer up, where it can see what it is retrying.

Measured by counting what the server received: the request arrived twice before this
change and arrives once after. The test fails with "left: 2, right: 1" if the guard
is removed.

author: 0xsolace
body:
## Root cause

MEMORY op:search treats every query as a keyword lookup. Enumeration-style history questions ("what have we talked about lately", "recent logs", "catch me up", "last few days") are TIME-SLICE requests, not keyword lookups: BM25/keyword scoring against phrases like "recent logs" matches rows that literally contain "recent" or "logs" and misses everything the user actually means.

**Live symptom (sol-dev, 2026-08-22):** days of covenant history (the dmarz entropy/simulation roof talks, the Alexis supplements) sat in the messages table while op:search returned only literal matches, so the reply enumerated a fraction of the week.

## Fix

- `RECENT_HISTORY_PATTERNS` / `isRecentHistoryQuery()` classify enumeration/time-slice queries.
- `buildRecentHistoryDigest()` renders a chronological cross-room digest of the sender's rooms over the last 7 days and prepends it to the search result. It never replaces the keyword results; the model gets both.
- **Owner-exclusive gating:** cross-room recall is deliberately privileged. The digest renders ONLY when `revalidateOwnerExclusiveDisclosure` allows the live delivery audience on the `OWNER_PRIVATE_DESTINATION_DISCLOSURE_BASIS` (owner DM, or a room whose entire census is {owner, agent}) — the same rule `relevant-conversations` enforces. In a mixed room, or on an `internal_agent_turn` basis, it degrades to `null` and the caller keeps the room-scoped keyword scan, so other participants never see private-room content. Digest failures degrade the same way; recall never fails the search.
- Rendering: connector ingestion prefixes stripped, double-persisted twin rows (same entityId+text) dedupe to one line, synced-corpus rows excluded, and a per-DAY line budget so no middle day silently drops out of a busy window.

## Test coverage

`packages/agent/src/actions/recall-history-digest.test.ts` (11 tests):
- **Gate open:** owner-private destination renders the cross-room chronological digest (both rooms present, oldest-first ordering, agent speaker labels).
- **Gate closed:** denied disclosure returns no digest and leaks nothing; `allowed:true` on a non-owner-private basis (`internal_agent_turn`) also stays closed.
- **Classifier:** five enumeration phrasings match; a plain keyword lookup ("find the postgres migration") does not (and never consults the disclosure gate).
- **Dedupe:** double-persisted twin rows render once.
- **Window:** rows older than 7 days stay out of the digest.

Existing `memories.test.ts` (29 tests) passes unchanged. 40/40 total.

author: kecbigmt
body:
Part 6 of the #218 series: the workflow surface moves onto the ratified
configuration language (`docs/language/workflows.md`, `plecture.schema.json`).
This is the last runtime surface; the sweep (part 8) is what remains.

Closes #233.

## What changed

A `workflows/*.toml` file is a **definition document**: a `[<id>]` table
declaring `kind = "workflow"`. Identity is the table name, so a filename is
free-form and one document may declare several workflows.

- `display`, node `inputs` and `event.channel` `inputs` are **values** over
  each surface's declared roots (`docs/language/values.md`), evaluated through
  `lang.Eval`. `display` observes `workflow.outputs.*` and
  `session.inputs.*` only, which is what keeps a listing free of network reads.
- `workspace_provider_inputs` is literal data, and no longer string-only: the
  provider's own `inputs_schema` decides each parameter's type.
- `[tick]` and `[healthcheck]` are closed tables, which is how the retired
  `stale_when` / `max_stale_when` / `[tick.movement_source]` now report
  themselves. So are a node's and a channel's own fields; a node's `uses` is
  required, and `id` defaults to the referenced definition's id (its last
  segment for a catalog-qualified reference).
- `lang.WorkflowNodes` reads a workflow's topology and rejects a cyclic one,
  and `lang.NodeReads` is the single derivation both it and the runtime's
  execution order use — so a load-time check and a plan cannot disagree about
  what a wiring declares. That un-defers
  `testdata/config-language/workflows/node-cycle.invalid.toml`.
- **The registry bridge is gone.** `config.taskReferenceRegistry` registered a
  workflow declaration assembled from the legacy decoder; it now registers the
  parsed one, so a chain naming an unknown workflow or an input its contract
  closes fails at load against the real parse.
- **`text/template` is gone from the workflow surface.** `task.RenderInputs`
  converted with both its consumers at once (`dispatch/render.go`'s channel
  delivery and `task.go`'s node inputs), `task.RenderOutputsTemplate` (display)
  went with them, and `render` / `renderWith` / the `get` and `shellQuote`
  helpers had no remaining caller. Survivors, unchanged, are the sweep's
  enumerated list: `internal/plugins/bin.go` (bin-reference scanning) and
  `internal/template/template.go` (the instruction body's carried pass, which
  retires with the control-flow decision `docs/language/tasks.md` defers).

`docs/migrations/workflow-surface-migration.md` carries the procedure.

## Behaviour changes a host must act on

Three, all stated in the migration doc:

1. **The cascade appends only `nodes`.** `[[event.channel]]` entries no longer
   append across layers, and `inputs_schema` is no longer combined with
   `allOf` — a field a shallower layer set is a redeclaration error. This is
   `lang.MergeLayer`, ratified in an earlier slice; adopting it is this part's
   job.
2. **A mixed template is now a valid literal.** `title = "{{.Workflow.outputs.owner}} orchestrator"`
   loads and renders the template text verbatim. Nothing can reject it — a
   literal string is what the surface accepts — so the doc gives the `expr`
   rewrite and a `grep` that finds the survivors. Found by running the
   procedure, not by reading it.
3. **A workspace-dir overlay may declare `nodes` and nothing else.** The rule
   is an allowlist now rather than a list of forbidden fields, so
   `workspace_provider_inputs` — which the old check happened to miss in
   untrusted clone content — is rejected there too.

## Verification

- `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt` clean in every module; `go test ./...` and
  `go test -tags integration -count=1 ./...` green in `app`, each
  `contracts/*` and each module under `plugins/`.
- **Golden records regenerated and byte-identical**: `PLECT_UPDATE_EFFECT_RECORDS=1
  PLECT_UPDATE_GATE_RECORDS=1 PLECT_UPDATE_CHANNEL_RECORDS=1
  PLECT_UPDATE_PROVIDER_RECORDS=1 go test -tags integration -count=1
  ./internal/task/ ./internal/channel/` leaves no diff under
  `plugins/*/testdata/`. That is the characterization evidence that the
  conversion changed no shipped invocation.
- `scripts/check-agent-config.sh`, `check-comment-references.sh`,
  `check-provider-boundary.sh` and their selftests pass;
  `scripts/config-language-check` reports `100 fixtures checked, 40
  diagnostics documented, 0 failures`.
- **The migration procedure was run**, not read: an isolated config home
  (`PLECT_CONFIG_HOME` + `XDG_*`) holding a copy of this machine's four host
  workflows, with the shipped catalog mounted from this worktree. The
  pre-migration state failed with `PLECTURE-CFG-KIND-MISSING` as documented;
  after conversion `plect workflow list` listed all four and
  `plect workflow show <id>` printed each display value and node input back.
  Both the mixed-template trap and a false-positive `grep` recipe were found
  and fixed that way.

## Design documents corrected

Two current-state design documents specified behaviour this change replaces,
and both now describe present behaviour. Owner ruling 2026-08-23: this is
present-state fact maintenance of already-ratified decisions, so it stays in
this PR and is non-gating rather than making this an owner-gated design PR.

- `docs/design/plugin-packaging.md` — its same-id table said user-owned layers
  merge by adding nodes *and event channels*, and that workflow input schemas
  combine with `allOf`. The rows and the partial-override bullet now state the
  ratified cascade.
- `docs/design/template-vocabulary.md` — its subject was five template
  surfaces, four of which are values now. Narrowed to the one that survives,
  the Markdown instruction body, with its control flow named as what
  `docs/language/tasks.md` defers.

## Deliberate non-changes

- **Plugin-layer workflows stay the cascade base.** `declarations.md` says a
  same-id user definition does not extend a plugin-owned workflow; how
  `plect up --workflow <id>` resolves an id across plugin and user layers is
  the discovery model, which no plugin exercises (none ships a workflow) and
  which the packaging design owns. Converting the surface without changing the
  namespace model keeps this part's blast radius to the grammar.
- `docs/design/task-nesting.md` keeps its `{{.Nodes...}}` / `{{get .Inputs ...}}`
  examples. That is the effect surface #228 retired, not this PR, and the sweep
  already has the present-state correction booked (owner-confirmed
  2026-08-23).
- `WorkflowFile` keeps its name even though it is a declaration rather than a
  file, matching what the other converted surfaces did with theirs.

## Tests dropped rather than converted

Three whose subject no longer exists, all named here so their loss is a
decision and not an omission:

- `internal/task/bin_test.go` — three tests exercising `{{bin ...}}` through
  `render`. Bin resolution on the surviving path is covered by
  `health_bin_test.go` and `shipped_bin_alias_test.go`.
- `TestRender_Get` / `_GetWithoutDefaultFails` / `_ThreeArgGetMatchesIfElseDefaultIdiom`
  and `_SelfAndTasks` / `_MissingKeyIsError` — the `get` helper and the
  renderer are retired; `default` / `optional` semantics live in
  `internal/lang`'s own tests, and three new
  `TestResolveNodeInputs_*` cases cover them at this surface.
- `TestResolveSessionInputs_WorkflowSchemaCompilesWithHyphenatedName` — a
  hyphenated workflow id is unreachable now, since the id grammar excludes
  one and `internal/lang` pins that.

The three number-normalization tests were **converted**, not dropped: a large
integer-valued float reaching a script as `3.052179e+06` is a live risk on
`lang.Eval` too, so they now resolve through `cleanupRoots` /
`nodeInputsRoots`.

## Benefit

Every workflow — the surface every session is dispatched through — is now
load-time checked: a projection of a root its surface does not observe, a
misspelled clock field, a node reading an output no upstream declares, and a
cyclic wiring are all load errors i

author: scottdensmore
body:
A repository should not be policing its own instruction files. This removes the check that did.

`tests/instructions.sh` enforced that `CLAUDE.md` stayed under 220 bytes and 4 non-blank lines, that `AGENTS.md` cleared a byte floor, that certain `## ` headings appeared exactly once, that no legacy workflow section survived, and that the managed-block markers were present and paired.

None of that is this project's business. The managed block belongs to the adoption tool, which has its own check that the installed copies are current — `adopt.py --dry-run --keep-existing .`, already in the Verification Map. `CLAUDE.md` is a pointer whose only job is to route agents to `AGENTS.md`, and its wording is not something a build should have an opinion about.

## It had teeth it should not have had

A freshly adopted `CLAUDE.md` is 308 bytes and 7 non-blank lines. So `ctest` went red on a tree whose only sin was being re-adopted from a clean slate — a formatting opinion, reported as a broken build, in the middle of a C test suite.

## What goes with it

The script, its `add_test` registration, and every reference:

- `CMakeLists.txt` — the registration, and a comment naming it as the house pattern for passing `${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}` (`score` is now genuinely the only other test doing that).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — a comment calling it "the one test that walks the tree". Verified true after removal: `analyze.sh` takes its sources from the CMake target rather than globbing, `workflow.sh` globs only `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `help.sh` opens `sst.doc` by name. Nothing scans the repo root.
- `.gitignore` — a comment about the path it exempted.
- `AGENTS.md` — two rows. A Development Commands row prescribing `tests/instructions.sh .`, deleted; and the Verification Map row for instruction-file edits, **rewritten rather than emptied**. Its only other command is conditional on a sibling checkout, and the row is matched before the catch-all, so emptying it would route an agent editing `AGENTS.md` to a row with nothing runnable and no fall-through. It now says to run the adoption dry-run when `../agent-skills/` exists, and otherwise to report `NOT RUN` rather than treat the row as satisfied.

## What is genuinely lost

Two things nothing else covers, recorded as the cost rather than as an objection:

- A `find` sweep for `CLAUDE*.md` anywhere in the tree — a second source of truth appearing in a subdirectory. No external tool checks that.
- An existence check on the three subagent definitions. That one is partly the tool's job rather than the project's: `check_self_adoption.py` in `agent-skills` does exactly it.

## How it was verified

Both documented CI gates: `ci-debug` and `ci-release`, each **exit 0, 12 tests, 11 passed**, down from 13/12 — the removal, and nothing else. `workflow` is **SKIPPED** in both for a missing `actionlint`; recorded as `NOT RUN`, not as passed. `tui` ran and passed (204s, tmux 3.6 supplied the pty).

The adoption dry-run is owed here, since this touches `AGENTS.md` and the sibling checkout exists. On this branch it reports the installed workflow **stale** — skills `d98f7d26 → 36978cf3`. That is inherited from `main` and not caused by this branch, which touches no installed file; the companion branch is the fix. Flagged so it does not read as green.

Code review: `APPROVED`. It verified that "nothing local reads these files" is true rather than plausible, by grepping every test, workflow and CMake file for the instruction-file names and confirming the only hits are prose in comments, and by checking there is no Markdown linter in CI.

## Landing order

Land **after** `chore(agents): upgrade the agent workflow`. They no longer conflict, but this removes the only local check of the adopted agent set, and that check passed on the other branch. Whichever lands second yields a merged tree no gate has seen — re-gate it.

body: ## Independence check - [ ] Moves CashSnapshot, activation, receipt verify, or paid pilot forward? - [x] If no, briefly justify why this PR should still merge: this is ops-visibility plumbing behind the FOUNDING → PROVEN pricing-ladder gate (≥100 settled picks) — it makes the *existing* settlement pipeline's progress toward that milestone visible per-sport, so an operator isn't guessing which sport's opening week is the highest-volume lever before NFL kickoff. No new pipeline, no new data collection, read-only. ## What this does `CARDS_PROOF_LADDER.md` PL4/PL5/PL6, continuing the Proof Ladder deck (PL1-PL3 already merged in #570/#571/#573): - **PL4** — `loadCanonicalSampleBySport()` in `apps/web/lib/ops/canonical-sample-posture.ts`: per-sport breakdown mirroring `loadPublicPerformancePolicy`'s exact settled-filter (result WIN/LOSS/PUSH, isPublished, !isBootstrap, non-seed model). Each sport's counts are isolated in their own `try/catch` so one sport's query failure can't blank the others — a failure surfaces via an explicit `error` field, never a fabricated zero. - **PL5** — `scripts/ops/settlement-progress-snapshot.ts`: read-only CLI (`npm run ops:settlement-snapshot`) printing the per-sport table + cumulative PROVEN-floor total. Imports `getInSeasonSports()` rather than hardcoding sports. No `create`/`update`/`delete`/`upsert`/`$executeRaw` anywhere in the file — grepped and confirmed. - **PL6** — `canonical-sample-posture-import-boundary.test.ts`: locks the ops-only import boundary (only `app/api/ops/**` may import `canonical-sample-posture.ts`) in as a regression test, now that PL4 adds a second export to the file. Verified it actually fails against a deliberately-broken fixture (temporarily injected the import into `app/performance/page.tsx`, confirmed red, reverted) before committing clean. **One deliberate deviation from the card spec:** PL5 ships as `.ts` run via `tsx`, not literally `.mjs` — because it reuses real cross-package TS loaders (PL4's function, `loadPublicPerformancePolicy`, `getInSeasonSports`) instead of re-deriving their filters inline, matching this repo's existing convention for scripts with cross-package TS imports (`scripts/edge-lab/gate-slate-phase-c-counts.ts`, `scripts/check-nflverse-currency.ts`). A plain `.mjs` can't resolve apps/web's TS + `@/*` alias without a loader, so it would either silently fail or require the same `tsx` invocation anyway. Wired as `npm run ops:settlement-snapshot` with `TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH` baked in. ## Verification Each card's own deterministic verify command, run and green: ``` cd apps/web && npx vitest run __tests__/canonical-sample-posture.test.ts && npx tsc --noEmit cd apps/web && npx vitest run __tests__/canonical-sample-posture-import-boundary.test.ts && npx tsc --noEmit node --check scripts/ops/settlement-progress-snapshot.ts && DATABASE_URL=stub npm run ops:settlement-snapshot; test $? -eq 2 ``` Plus the full `apps/web` `tsc --noEmit` and the four related test files together (30/30 pass). --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01NsaVxNnq9bXhuxNAAEkPAY)_ --- ## Summary by cubic Adds per-sport canonical-settled counts and a read-only snapshot CLI to show progress toward the PROVEN floor. Previously we showed only a cumulative total; now we show per-sport rows and surface per-sport query failures via an explicit error field. **Review notes** - `loadCanonicalSampleBySport` mirrors `loadPublicPerformancePolicy`’s settled filter (result in WIN/LOSS/PUSH, `isPublished`, `!isBootstrap`, not the seed model), scoped by `game.sport.key`. Each sport runs in its own try/catch; failures set `error` without fabricating totals. - `scripts/ops/settlement-progress-snapshot.ts` uses `@prisma/client`, `getInSeasonSports`, and existing loaders to print a per-sport table plus the cumulative total; it performs no writes and exits with code 2 if `DATABASE_URL` is missing or stubbed. Run via `npm run ops:settlement-snapshot` (uses `tsx`). - `canonical-sample-posture-import-boundary.test.ts` enforces that only `app/api/ops/**` imports `canonical-sample-posture.ts`, keeping the module internal to ops. - No pipeline, schema, or public surface changes; this is read-only visibility. **Rollout** - Required to run: set `DATABASE_URL` and execute `npm run ops:settlement-snapshot`. No migrations or config changes. Written for commit 2a83b9aa963c47e42553ce7a41a2cd04bb653664. Summary will update on new commits.

body:
`roadmap.md` (1,437 lines) and `roadmapplan.md` (2,359 lines) are deleted, along with `docs/live-gates-and-remainders.md` — that one was organised entirely around plan section numbers and could not outlive them. All three remain in git history.

## They were not inert

**263 references pointed at them from 146 files** — code comments, ADR headers, SQL migration comments, dashboard CSS and JS. Deleting the documents alone would have left that many pointers into nothing.

The citations are removed and any prose they carried is kept inline, which is where it belonged. Bare `§` section markers went the same way, for the same reason.

## Three passes reverted rather than shipped

Each caught by a dry run or by reading the diff before committing:

| Attempt | Damage |
|---|---|
| Whitespace tidying | Mangled a generated LSP protocol file, 74 lines |
| Orphan-punctuation joining | Joined **every CSS class selector** onto the previous line — selectors start with `.` |
| Empty-parenthesis removal | Turned `os.Getwd()` into `os.Getwd` |

Applied migrations, dashboard assets and ADRs were then edited by explicit before/after pairs instead. A regex loose enough to catch every citation shape was loose enough to break them.

## TODO.md is now the master list

Two tracks, as requested: **what an agent can do unattended**, and **what needs you** — either because it needs another person or because it is a decision about what this product is.

It leads with a claims section, separating what is defensible today from what is not:

- The opencode comparison rests on **one Python repository, five tasks, one model** — and the gap grew from 19% to 63% when runs were added, so n=5 may still be too few
- Coverage is **31.3%** against a stated 80% bar; 19 of 74 packages have no test file
- Demand paging remains unmeasured, which is why it defaults to off

The purpose of that section is that Aux only says true things about itself.

body:
## Summary
Hardens the SNA industry-deflator collector against the actual year-label formats used by Cabinet Office / e-Stat workbooks.

## Fix
- Adds a compatibility runner that recognizes Western years and Japanese-era labels such as `平成6暦年`, `令和元年`, `令和6暦年`, and full-width numerals.
- Keeps the core collector unchanged and injects the broader year parser at runtime.
- Adds regression tests for Western, Heisei, Reiwa and Showa year labels.

## Workflow hardening
- Runs the year-parser regression test before downloading official SNA files.
- Uses the compatibility runner for collection.
- Requires generated history to reach at least 1994.
- Requires every industry’s latest observation to equal the selected SNA vintage.
- Retains the exact nominal/real/deflator identity-gap validation.

## Why
The official SNA/e-Stat tables may use Japanese-era calendar-year labels. The original collector only recognized 4-digit Western years, so it could fail to identify the matrix even though the official files were available. Merging this PR also retriggers the initial-data workflow on `main`.

author: fzyzcjy
body:
## Problem

- SSE encoding transfers owned Rust opaque values before the complete message has been validated.
- If a later argument fails to encode, an earlier transfer remains committed even though no message reaches Rust.
- The failed serialization path also leaked its temporary SSE buffer under Valgrind.

## Fix

- Validate opaque transfers before committing them.
- Roll back pending transfers and release the SSE buffer when encoding fails.
- Add regression coverage for a failed later argument, duplicate transfers, and wrapped web exceptions.
- Restore the disposed-opaque test under Valgrind; this PR no longer needs the parent PR's targeted skip.

## Validation

- `./frb_internal precommit-generate`
- `./frb_internal generate-internal-frb-example-pure-dart`
- `./frb_internal test-dart-native --package frb_example/pure_dart` (4377 tests passed)
- `./frb_internal test-dart-valgrind --package frb_example/pure_dart`: all Dart tests passed; definite and indirect leaks are both zero. The local ARM64 Valgrind process still exits nonzero for known Dart VM invalid-access reports, so the x64 Linux CI job is authoritative.

## Stack

- Base: #3374
- Merge #3374 independently; this PR contains the underlying SSE bug fix.

author: snoopy147
body:
## The flake

Night-8 private-editor CI ([run 32580694134](https://github.com/pascalorg/private-editor/actions/runs/32580694134)) failed three tests in `packages/editor/src/components/tools/shared/pointer-support-cap.test.ts`:

- `discovers a plugin-declared top surface without a kind-name list`
- `never elects the node the active interaction is placing or moving`
- `uses a plugin-declared top as the wall construction surface`

all with `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'definition.capabilities.surfaces')` at `pointer-support-cap.ts:163`. The same tree passed 752/752 locally twice (forced).

## Root cause: order-dependent test pollution

`nodeRegistry` is a module singleton and bun runs a package's test files sequentially in **one process**. `floorplan-registry-layer.test.ts` registers capabilities-less fixture definitions (`cabinet`, `cabinet-module`, `linked-floorplan-test`) after a `nodeRegistry._reset()` and never restores. Bun's test-file order differs between platforms (macOS local vs CI Linux) — when the floorplan file runs **before** `pointer-support-cap.test.ts`, the leaked entries hit the top-surface enumeration:

```ts
.filter(([, definition]) => definition.capabilities.surfaces?.top !== undefined)
```

and only the three tests that pass `includeNodeTopSurfaces: true` crash — exactly the CI signature.

**Reproduced deterministically** on unmodified `main` with `bun test --randomize --seed=1` on the two-file pair: same three tests, same TypeError, same line.

## The fix (both sides + a gate)

1. **Test hygiene** — new test-only `nodeRegistry._snapshot()` (captures definitions + plugin bookkeeping, returns a restore fn). Applied in:
   - `floorplan-registry-layer.test.ts` — both mutation sites now snapshot/restore
   - `wall-drafting.test.ts` — the mid-test `_reset()` no longer strips the registry for later files
2. **Production honesty** — `definition.capabilities?.surfaces?.top`. `capabilities` is typed required, but the resolver enumerates *every* registered kind and a plugin bundle can bypass the type at runtime; a minimal definition must read as "no top surface", not crash the election.
3. **Gate** — a test registers a capabilities-less definition then calls `resolvePointerSupportSurface`: no throw, and the platform's declared top is still elected. Verified failing against the unguarded code, passing with the chain.

Bonus: seed-22 randomized verification surfaced a second latent flake of the same class (`apply-alignment.test.ts` inheriting a leaked building fixture through the scene/viewer store singletons — confirmed pre-existing on unmodified `main`). Pinned its empty-scene context explicitly.

## Verification

- Repro before fix: seeds 1/2/4/6 fail on the two-file pair with the CI signature; green after
- Full editor suite `bun test --randomize` x10 fresh seeds: 753 pass / 0 fail each
- `bunx turbo run test --filter=@pascal-app/editor --force`: 753/753 (752 + new gate test)
- Full repo `bunx turbo run test`: 13/13 tasks green
- `check-types` (editor + core) and Biome on changed files: clean

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Mostly test isolation plus optional chaining on a registry enumeration path. Production behavior only changes for malformed/minimal definitions that previously threw.
> 
> **Overview**
> Stops order-dependent CI flakes from tests mutating the process-wide `nodeRegistry` (and scene/viewer stores) without restoring them. Bun runs a package’s tests in one process, so a leaked capabilities-less fixture crashed later `pointer-support-cap` files when file order differed on Linux.
> 
> Adds test-only `nodeRegistry._snapshot()` to capture definitions plus plugin bookkeeping and restore them. Floorplan registry and wall-drafting tests now snapshot/restore around `_reset()` and throwaway registrations.
> 
> `resolvePointerSupportSurface` now uses optional chaining on `capabilities`, so a kind without that field is skipped instead of throwing. A gate test registers a capless definition and still elects the platform top. Alignment tests also pin an empty scene/selection so a leaked building fixture cannot break world-axis alignment.
>
