body:
Part of the workstation toolchain unification epic (Lodestar-7oc0). `live/` is the
terragrunt harness people actually run by hand, and it carried no committed tool
versions, so a local run used whatever the workstation defaulted to. This pins it to
the pair `_spacelift/stacks.tf` drives the fleet with.

CHANGES MADE:
- `live/.opentofu-version`: new, `1.12.5`. Matches the fleet default in infra-live
  `_spacelift/stacks.tf` (`terraform_version` for every `OPEN_TOFU` stack) and the
  `TOFU_VERSION` already baked into `live/Dockerfile` and `live/tests/Dockerfile`.
- `live/.terragrunt-version`: new, `1.1.2`. Same source; matches `TERRAGRUNT_VERSION`
  in both Dockerfiles.
- `.gitignore`: negation for `**/.terragrunt-version`. The existing `**/.terragrunt*`
  pattern is there for `.terragrunt-cache` and also swallows the version file. Same
  shape as the existing `!.terraform.lock.hcl` exception three lines up.

A follow-up infra-live PR registers both new files with `_bin/check-tofu-pin-sync.sh`,
which already fetches four CPI files unauthenticated from raw GitHub. That PR is
sequenced after this one: the checker 404s on these paths until this merges.

THINGS I DIDN'T TOUCH (intentionally):
- `azure-config/.opentofu-version`: already `1.12.5` and already a checked pin site.
  It is an operational input to `azure-config/lib/tools.sh`, not a dev convenience file.
- No `.terraform-version`, here or at the repo root. Nothing in CPI runs the `terraform`
  binary (the harness sets `TG_TF_PATH=tofu` in `live/tests/run.sh:39`), and every module
  here declares `required_version >= 1.11.1`, so pinning the fleet's Terraform 1.5.7
  would be a trap rather than a match. A root-level pin on a public repo also reads as a
  support claim we are not making.
- `live/tests/run.sh` and `DEPLOYMENT.md` still instruct a bare `tgenv use` / `tofuenv use`,
  which mutates state shared by every parallel session. Left for a separate docs pass in
  the same epic, so this PR stays a pure pin change.

POTENTIAL CONCERNS:
- Blast radius is local-only. Nothing in CI reads these files: `live/Dockerfile` and
  `live/tests/Dockerfile` pin their own `ARG TOFU_VERSION` / `ARG TERRAGRUNT_VERSION`,
  and this PR does not change those. The effect is confined to a developer running
  terragrunt from `live/` on a machine using tofuenv/tgenv.
- Anyone whose workstation lacks OpenTofu 1.12.5 or Terragrunt 1.1.2 will now get an
  explicit "version not installed" error from the version manager instead of silently
  running an older pair. That is the intent, but it is a behaviour change for them.

author: mr-b042
body:
Bright asked to raise the Multi Corner Storage Shelf from ₦11,500 to ₦12,000 — *"but i want to start counting new order… i hope it wont effect the previously sold item"*.

It would have. Badly.

Nothing stored the cost that applied when an order was sold. Every report recomputed COGS as `quantity × TODAY'S unit_cost`, so that one edit would have erased **₦48,500 of reported profit across 90 delivered orders back to 25 July** — weeks already reported on and already used to pay bonuses.

A delivered order's cost is now settled, the same way a closed week is.

## Four things that had to be exactly right

**A frozen snapshot always wins over live pricing.** Five COGS readers now go through `resolveOrderCogs`: Period Close, Weekly Overview, customer retention gross contribution, manager bonuses, sales leads. Missing one would leave some reports on the old cost and some on the new — worse than either.

**Every one of those queries also had to start SELECTing `cogs_snapshot`.** Without it the resolver sees `undefined`, falls through to live pricing, and the freeze becomes a **silent no-op that looks like it worked**. Seven selects widened.

**Freezing happens BEFORE the price moves.** Doing it after would snapshot history at the *new* cost and permanently bake in the exact restatement this exists to prevent. Order matters absolutely.

**A snapshot of 0 is still a snapshot.** Treating zero as "missing" would un-freeze every order that genuinely cost nothing — free replacements, written-off goods — and let a later edit move them.

Only **Delivered** orders freeze. An order still in flight hasn't incurred its cost and may ship from stock bought later.

## Self-service, which is what was asked for

Editing **Cost per Unit** now shows the impact before applying it:

> ⚠️ **This affects 90 past orders**
> 97 units already sold at ₦11,500. Left unfrozen, reported profit on those orders would fall by **₦48,500**.
> ☑ Freeze those orders at ₦11,500 first

Ticked by default, with a blunt warning if unticked. Every change is recorded in `product_cost_changes` — who, when, previous cost, new cost, how many orders were frozen.

`POST /api/products/freeze-cogs` freezes all **1,818** delivered orders at today's costs. Idempotent, Owner-only, safe to re-run.

## Migration

237 applied and verified on prod **before** merge: 3 columns, 1 audit table, 1 RLS policy.

## Checks

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- `npm run build` clean, 22 live-UX guard checks pass
- `npm run lint:hooks` 0 errors
- `npm --prefix backend test` — **518 pass**, 13 new

author: zane-0x5a
body:
## Why

v0.3.0's version gate made a workspace created by an older release fail `check-env` — but the repair ("re-copy the pinned dependency block, re-run `npm install`") was documented as a **manual user step** (the v0.3.0 release notes even instruct it). That's wrong on two counts: the orchestrator is an agent that can and should do mechanical work itself, and "overwrite the dependency block" is a clobber risk for workspaces where the user added their own deps — merging needs a judgment call that shouldn't be freelanced per-run.

## What changes

- **`check-env.mjs --fix`**: before checking, deterministically repairs engine-dep drift in the workspace — merges the plugin's pinned `dependencies`/`devDependencies` blocks into the workspace `package.json` (**only pinned keys are set; the user's own entries are preserved**), runs `npm install`, then the same run re-verifies everything (deps present, all pinned remotion packages at the pin, skill pairing, ffmpeg).
- **Failure hints** for missing deps and version drift now point at `--fix`.
- **`create/SKILL.md` Step 0**: repairing the engine gate is explicitly the orchestrator's job, never the user's — with `--fix` as the sanctioned path and an explicit ban on freelancing a different repair (e.g. `npm install remotion@latest`, which breaks the pin). Skill/ffmpeg gaps get the same treatment: the orchestrator offers and runs the install itself (`npx skills add remotion-dev/skills -g`, winget/brew/apt ffmpeg) — the user is only ever asked for one confirmation, since these write outside the workspace. Consent, not labor.
- **READMEs**: document `--fix` for manual use.

## Validation

Synthetic drifted workspace (`remotion@4.0.477` + a user-owned dep, no `node_modules`): one `--fix` run merged the pinned set (user dep intact), installed, and closed green — `engine version matches pin (4.0.515, all 11 remotion packages)`.

## Note

This is the robustness follow-up to the v0.3.0 upgrade path: after this lands, "existing workspace from an older release" is self-healing in the pipeline instead of a documented manual step. Worth cutting as v0.3.1.

A follow-up sweep for every place that still handed labor to the user found three, all fixed here: check-env's skill/ffmpeg hints now address the orchestrator directly (offer to run the install; one confirmation, consent-not-labor); create Step 0 explicitly exempts the fresh-workspace case (engine deps are missing by definition before Step 1 — don't escalate, fix); and both READMEs tell users none of the prerequisites are manual chores in a real run. author: lemikaelf
body:
## Description

Implements a subroutine-threading JIT compiler for VDBE bytecode programs using Cranelift. The JIT compiles each prepared statement to a native function whose body is a sequence of direct calls to existing opcode implementations, with bytecode-level control flow lowered to native branches. This removes per-instruction interpreter overhead (instruction fetch, bounds check, opcode dispatch, interrupt/tracing bookkeeping) while preserving all opcode semantics — opcode bodies stay single-source between the interpreter and the JIT.

### Key Features

- **Subroutine-threading architecture**: Generated code calls existing `extern "C-unwind"` opcode wrappers, so panicking opcodes unwind correctly through JIT frames (unwind info registered via `.eh_frame` on Linux-gnu; other platforms fall back to the interpreter).
- **Specialized helpers**: The opcodes that dominate scan and aggregation loops — Integer, Copy, Move, arithmetic, If/IfNot/IfPos, AggStep, comparisons (Eq..Ge), Column/ColumnRange, and the scan skeleton (Next, Rewind, SorterNext/Insert/Data, Compare, Jump, SeekRowid, ResultRow) — have slim entry points that bake operands in as immediates and report branch decisions through return codes, so generated code branches natively instead of re-reading `state.pc`. Helpers that hit a case needing the interpreter's resumable state machinery bail losslessly to the generic wrapper.
- **Compilation gates**: Statements only compile after proving the compile will amortize — either the current execution alone is long enough (1M+ steps) or the same prepared program has been reused 4+ times, with a per-instruction step threshold that permanently excludes straight-line mega-programs (e.g. multi-row INSERTs). Failed checks back off exponentially.
- **Eager compilation API**: `Statement::jit_compile()` lets applications that prepare statements during initialization and reuse them for the process lifetime compile immediately, skipping the reuse gates while keeping the safety gates. Best-effort by contract: it can never turn "won't compile" into an application error.
- **Interrupt/connection-closed checks**: Run on every backward branch and dynamic dispatch, ensuring every bytecode cycle contains a check.
- **Comparison coercion cache**: Per-site, per-operand, content-keyed memoization of texts known not to convert under numeric affinity, so repeated comparisons against the same non-numeric constant (date strings, most commonly) skip the failed parse each row.
- **Configurable via environment**: `TURSO_JIT` (enable/disable), `TURSO_JIT_THRESHOLD` (min steps before compile; `0` forces immediate compilation), `TURSO_JIT_MAX_INSNS` (max program size to compile).

## Measured performance

All numbers are query time only: statements are prepared (and for the reused group, eagerly compiled) outside the measured region, so no series includes prepare or compile latency.

**CodSpeed (simulation instrument), interpreter vs JIT within one run** — `core/benches/jit_benchmark.rs` runs every shape twice on identical in-memory data, once with the JIT disabled and once with it enabled, so the delta is runner-independent:

| shape | interp | jit | query time |
|---|---|---|---|
| TPC-H Q1 pricing summary (scan + group by) | 756.9 ms | 594.8 ms | **−21.4%** |
| top-100 by price (filter + order by + limit) | 126.1 ms | 98.4 ms | **−22.0%** |
| daily revenue (indexed join + group by + top-k) | 420.7 ms | 371.4 ms | **−11.7%** |
| TPC-H Q6 forecast revenue (predicate-heavy scan) | 123.3 ms | 110.5 ms | **−10.4%** |
| Q14-style conditional aggregate | 102.8 ms | 95.5 ms | **−7.1%** |
| reused point lookup (rowid seek, prepared once) | 3.1 ms | 2.0 ms | **−35%** |
| reused small aggregate (128-row range scan) | 6.4 ms | 5.0 ms | **−21.9%** |
| reused point UPDATE (write-path guard) | 7.8 ms | 7.4 ms | −5.1% |

**Pre-existing benchmarks vs main** (same final CodSpeed run, these route through the JIT automatically once the gates open): `count_groupby[1000000]` **+28.8%**, graph `e_activity_agg` **+29.7%**, graph `c_edge_counts` **+25.3%**, `execute_group_by` **+22.6%** — with **zero regressions** and 2076 benchmarks unchanged across the corpus. The compile-amortization gates exist because an early CodSpeed run caught unamortized compiles regressing bulk-write benchmarks; since the gates landed, every run has been regression-free.

**Local instruction counts** (valgrind/cachegrind, TPC-H SF-1 on-disk, JIT vs interpreter, cumulative across the six increments): Q1 **−15.9%** (112.8G → 94.9G), Q6 **−18.2%** (21.3G → 17.4G), Q14 **−15.9%**. Each increment's commit message records its individually measured delta against an exact-baseline build.

### Memory

- **Default builds: zero impact.** Every JIT field and code path is behind the `jit` cargo feature (off by default), and the CodSpeed memory-instrument CI, which builds without the feature, reports no change on this PR.
- **Feature on, JIT idle** (gates closed — the normal state for short statements): no compilation happens, so no code memory exists; the overhead is a few dozen bytes of extra `ProgramState`/`PreparedProgram` fields, plus a small comparison-cache vector allocated lazily only once specialized comparisons actually run.
- **Per compiled statement** (RSS, measured on an idle process): **~55 KiB** for a TPC-H-Q6-sized program (~60 instructions) — a prepared-but-uncompiled statement is ~1 KiB — scaling with program size up to ~850 KiB for the largest shape measured (Q1, the size cap region). Fully reclaimed on statement drop: 600 compile+drop cycles grow RSS by 0–4 KiB total, i.e. no leak.
- **One-time cost on first compile**: ~3.3 MiB (Cranelift's lazy ISA/context initialization and allocator high-water), paid only if some statement ever crosses the gates or is compiled eagerly.

### Implementation Details

- New `core/vdbe/jit/mod.rs` (~2.7k lines) with the compiler, wrappers, specialized helpers, and unwind-info registration.
- `ProgramState` extended with JIT-specific fields: exit-result handoff slot, execution counters for the compile gates, comparison-cache slots.
- `PreparedProgram` caches compiled code in a `OnceLock<Option<Arc<JitCode>>>`.
- `Statement::jit_compile()` for eager compilation; `Connection::set_jit_enabled()` to toggle the JIT per connection.
- Benchmark suite (`core/benches/jit_benchmark.rs`) measuring interpreter vs JIT on TPC-H-shaped and OLTP-style statement shapes; the CodSpeed workflow builds with the `jit` feature.
- Feature-gated behind the `jit` Cargo feature (off by default; `bindings/rust` and `cli` expose passthrough features).

### Safety Model

- Generated code only calls opcode implementations or helpers that forward to them; panics unwind through registered unwind info.
- Non-Step results (rows, I/O, errors) are stashed in `ProgramState::jit_exit_result` and handled by the interpreter loop exactly as interpreted results; `state.pc` is materialized before every opcode call so error paths, I/O suspension, and interrupt exits observe exactly the interpreter's program state.
- Specialized helpers either complete with interpreter-identical effects or bail to the generic wrapper before making any state change.
- Validation at every increment: the full core suite runs green with `TURSO_JIT_THRESHOLD=0` forcing every statement through compiled code (2351 lib + 53 integration tests), conformance sqltests report the identical failure set as the interpreter, and all 11 in-tree TPC-H queries return byte-identical output JIT vs interpreter.

## Motivation and context

JIT compilation amortizes well for statements that are either long-running (big scans/aggregations) or frequently reused (prepared statements executed many times). The per-instruction overhead of the interpreter loop (dispatch, bounds checks, metrics bookkeeping) becomes significant for hot code paths. This implementation targets those cases while avoiding compile overhead for one-shot statements.

## Summary

Body IR v0 method lowering (#1102) declared every ordinary method parameter's `LocalDecl` as `IncanType::Unknown`, because `TypeCheckInfo` only retained resolved parameter bindings for top-level `def` functions, never for `MethodDecl` items. This PR records the typechecker's resolved method callable signatures — keyed by declaration span, overload-safe — and consumes them during Body IR lowering, so ordinary method parameters carry their real checked type instead of `Unknown`.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / maintenance
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI / tooling
- [ ] RFC (adds/updates `docs/RFCs/*`)

## Area(s)

- [ ] Incan Language (syntax/semantics)
- [x] Compiler (frontend/backend/codegen)
- [ ] Tooling (CLI/formatter/test runner)
- [ ] Editor integration (LSP/VS Code extension)
- [ ] Runtime / Core crates (stdlib/core/derive)
- [ ] Documentation

## Key details

- **User-facing behavior**: none. Internal compiler IR only.
- **Internals**: adds `DeclarationArtifacts::method_bindings_by_span`, reusing the existing `FunctionBindingInfo` shape (no parallel struct) and keyed by declaration span, mirroring `function_bindings_by_span`'s existing collision-safe keying for top-level overloads. `method_span: Span` is threaded through `check_method_with_owner_type_params`/`check_method_with_self_ty` (model, class, newtype, enum, and trait-default call sites), which now records one binding per checked method declaration after resolving each parameter's type exactly once — avoiding a double `resolve_type_checked()` call that would double-emit annotation diagnostics. `lower_method_body` in Body IR looks up the binding by declaration span and types ordinary parameter locals from it, falling back to `IncanType::Unknown` only when the typechecker genuinely produced no fact. The receiver local (`self`/`mut self`) is untouched — owned by #1102.
- **Risks**: low, additive. No existing binding table's shape changed; the new table is populated at the same choke point every method already passes through, so nothing that previously typechecked can now fail to. Newtype/enum methods also populate the table (they share the same choke point) but this is inert — Body IR still doesn't lower their bodies (#1102's own pre-existing exclusion).

body:
Builds the first production-oriented shared Identity boundary on top of the current `main` architecture without merging the stale historical Identity branch.

What this PR does:
- adds a real provider-token-backed `/api/identity/session` exchange that overrides the previous placeholder authenticated response
- validates the provider user and calls the live `get_identity_context()` contract
- issues a short-lived HMAC-signed HttpOnly ATLAS session containing only server-derived organization, role, permission, module and AAL context
- adds `requireIdentity()` for server-side permission/module/AAL enforcement
- adds `/api/identity/context`, `/api/identity/authorize`, `/api/identity/health`, session read and logout
- introduces `atlas-entry.js` as the shared top-level gateway for both Cloudflare and the sovereign portable runtime
- adds optional `ATLAS_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_CONNECT=true` protection for all Connect routes, defaulting off until the current Identity UI and deployment config can bootstrap real sessions
- preserves all existing Durable Object exports and runtime behavior
- adds unit/smoke coverage for token verification, signed sessions, organization isolation, permission/module/AAL checks, tamper rejection, Connect enforcement and logout
- documents the live Identity tables/RPCs already verified in the active `atlas-core` Supabase backend

Important rollout rule:
This PR does not claim Connect is production-protected yet. The enforcement flag must remain disabled until real login/session bootstrap is wired and tested with real accounts. Network Fabric #296 must use this trusted context and must not trust browser-supplied tenant headers.

Validation includes `check:identity-core`, portable runtime, provider independence and Wrangler dry-run.

# Risks

**Medium.** This changes the browser-side identity and lifecycle of Stripe card-checkout attempts and adds a server-side principal precondition.

The implementation fails closed when durable browser coordination is unavailable. Browsers or embedded WebViews without secure Web Locks, durable localStorage, or secure UUID generation receive actionable guidance instead of starting an uncoordinated checkout.

Ambiguous checkout outcomes deliberately retain their idempotency key. A stale different-amount checkout requires reconciliation instead of silently rotating payment identity.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Replaces per-mount card-checkout UUIDs with one durable, cross-tab intent per organization.
- Serializes intent reservation, session binding, and exact cleanup through Web Locks and compare-and-swap localStorage records.
- Reuses the same key for the same initiating user, organization, and amount; rotates it on principal or submitted-amount changes.
- Treats sessionStorage only as a best-effort success-page pointer and falls back to an exact localStorage namespace scan.
- Pins the UI principal in checkout requests with `expectedUserId` and `expectedOrganizationId`.
- Rejects a changed principal with `409 CHECKOUT_PRINCIPAL_CHANGED` before catalog, order, customer-authority, or Stripe work.
- Invalidates delayed responses synchronously on unmount or principal changes before bind/navigation.
- Disables the amount and card/crypto controls while a checkout request is pending.
- Clears only the exact session after authoritative `success: true` verification.
- Keeps verified payment success visible if non-authoritative browser cleanup fails, with an accessible warning.
- Adds canonical English i18n entries and regression coverage.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking).

## Out of scope

- No Stripe webhook, settlement, refund, database schema, or customer-authority policy change.
- No crypto/direct-wallet checkout behavior change.
- No hardware-checkout contract change.
- No pricing, amount-limit, or amount-step policy change.
- No real Stripe charge was made by the visual evidence harness.

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require project-documentation changes. User-facing English strings were added to the canonical locale.

## Detailed testing steps

Automated coverage verifies concurrent tabs, ambiguous retry/remount reuse, principal and amount rotation, stale callback invalidation, denied/corrupt storage, unavailable Web Locks, exact success cleanup, server-side principal switching before side effects, partial principal preconditions, legacy/hardware compatibility, pending controls, and verified-success cleanup warnings.

author: pointpu
body:
Closes #1059

## Предмет

Потолок ТЕМПА заведения аккаунтов (#618, влит этой же волной) допускает три
заведения в час на одну личность. Сквозная волна iam заводила **восемь**
аккаунтов под **одним** человеком церемонии, у которого посев уже занял два
допуска. Итого **10 списаний при потолке 3**: проходило первое, остальные
получали `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, и падало не то место, которое полку исчерпало, —
падали шаги, шедшие следом за несозданным аккаунтом (83 упавших утверждения на
прогоне `32612214045`).

Отказ **верен**. Неверна была форма пробы: человек заводит себе аккаунт, а не
восемь подряд. Прод-код не тронут ни строкой.

## Перепись класса

Единица счёта — шаг сгенерированной коллекции, ЗАХВАТИВШИЙ идентификатор
аккаунта (тот же признак, что у соседнего гейта объёма; ответ 200 признаком не
является — кейс занятого имени получает 200 и `Operation.error`, строки за ним
нет).

По всему дереву `POST /iam/v1/accounts` — **23** шага в 34 коллекциях iam;
в остальных семи наборах и на крае — только чтение. Из 23 заводят аккаунт
**восемь**, и все восемь шли под `jwtHumanCeremony`.

| место | исход |
|---|---|
| `iam-account` · CR-CRUD-OK | своя личность `AccCrud` |
| `iam-account` · CR-BVA-NAME-MIN | своя личность `AccBvaMin` |
| `iam-account` · CR-BVA-NAME-MAX | своя личность `AccBvaMax` |
| `iam-account` · LSOP-CRUD-OK | своя личность `AccLsop` |
| `iam-account-redesign` · RD-CR-OWNER-DERIVE-OK | своя личность `AccRdDerive` |
| `iam-account-redesign` · RD-CR-SAGA-TWO-ID-OK | своя личность `AccRdSaga` |
| `iam-account-redesign` · RD-DL-NONEMPTY-RESTRICT-NEG | своя личность `AccRdRestrict` |
| `rbac-visibility-set` · SET-PRJ-LABEL-EXACT-OK | своя личность `RbacVisSet` |
| остальные 15 шагов `POST /accounts` | без изменений — заведения не происходит |

Пятнадцать неизменённых — это шесть синхронных отказов формы запроса, два
анонимных, пять машинных предъявителей (отказ по роду принципала) и кейс
занятого имени, чьё заведение принимается синхронно и отменяется уникальностью
имени раньше, чем отложенный триггер списывает допуск.

## Почему «поднять потолок» не выбрано ни в одном месте

Задача предлагала второй исход для мест, где аккаунт — лишь фон. В newman он
**неисполним by construction**: величина живёт одной строкой на вид
(`account_admission_rate_limits`, уникальность по виду среди действующих), а
стенд у волны один. Поднятая «для полосы», она поднимется и для семи мест, чей
предмет — сам аккаунт, и там проба обязана идти по умолчанию продукта.

## Баланс каждой личности назван числом

Зеркало первого входа заводит личный аккаунт (+1, безусловная ветвь вставки
окна допуска), проба заводит один (+1) — **2 при потолке 3**, запас единица.
Человек церемонии остаётся на своих двух (личный + собственный аккаунт посева)
и в волне не заводит ничего.

## Чем класс держится дальше

Новый гейт `deploy/scripts/assert-identity-admission-rate-headroom.py` —
статический, стенда не требует, падает до подъёма первого кластера. Считает
списания КАЖДОЙ личности по сгенерированным коллекциям в порядке волны; порядок,
формы заведения и разбиение по личностям берёт у соседнего гейта объёма и у
единственного объявления церемонии, своей копии не держит.

Доказан инъекцией в обе стороны:

* довправочное дерево (все восемь заведений возвращены на человека церемонии) —
  **`НАХОДКА: личность церемония списывает 10 допусков при потолке 3`**;
* дерево этой ветки — **`наибольшее списание 2, наименьший запас 1`**;
* самопроверка — 23 утверждения, включая законного близнеца (те же три
  заведения, но у каждого своя личность → не находка).

Сверх того перемерены три соседа, которые после раскола перестали бы читать
свой предмет:

* **гейт объёма** считал ОДНУ личность и на расколотом дереве нашёл бы ноль
  созданий («предикат ослеп»); теперь считает по каждой и берёт худшую. Базовый
  уровень стал по-личностный: раздача аккаунта посева всем подряд завышала его
  на единицу у восьми личностей, то есть давала находку там, где её нет.
  Кому достаются аккаунты посева — объявлено, и объявление держится сверкой с
  числом, выведенным из исходника посева;
* **гейт уровня входа** держал перечень человеческих предъявителей литералом из
  двух имён — шаги слотов выпали бы из-под него молча; теперь перечень выводится
  из объявления (8 слотов → 18 предъявителей), и пропажа объявления названа
  предпосылкой;
* **замок посева** «предъявителя чеканят тому, чьё зеркало дождались» читал
  только `main`; чеканка появилась во второй функции, и он остался бы зелёным,
  честно проверив не то место. Теперь читает каждую чеканящую функцию.

Запись `jwtHumanCeremonyStepUp` снята из `CEREMONY_ONLY_ENV` по её собственному
правилу: ни один шаг дерева её больше не называет (все чувствительные шаги
переехали к личностям слотов вместе с аккаунтами, которых касаются). Что это
стоит и чем оплачено — сказано у самой записи.

## Что проверено локально

| проверка | исход |
|---|---|
| `run-gate-self-tests.sh` | 61/61 зелёные |
| `ci-local.sh go` (сборка, vet, `-short`, golangci-lint, gosec) | 8 проверок, 0 отказов |
| `go test ./internal/repohygiene/...` | ok |
| гейты объёма · темпа · уровня входа · объявления церемонии | RC=0 каждый |
| `check-newman-suite-gates.py`, `assert-generated-scripts-parse.js` (34 коллекции, 3864 скрипта) | ok |
| связность переменных окружения (`TestNewmanVariablesAreDefined`) | ok |
| самопроверка посева (стадии 6 и 8г) | 25 утверждений, PASS |

**Сквозной прогон `e2e iam` локально НЕ выполнялся, и это сказано прямо.**
Поднятый стенд принадлежит другим сессиям (восемь чужих пробросов портов, k6-под,
1151 аккаунт) и **не несёт миграции потолка темпа** — предикат
`to_regclass('kacho_iam.account_admission_rate_limits')` на его базе пуст. Прогон
там вынес бы вердикт о дереве, которого нет. Вердикт по волне остаётся за
конвейером этого PR.

This collector makes ModelRegistryV2 the single discovery and resolution authority while preserving every current built-in name, alias, decorator, and compatibility view. The four smaller PRs remain review surfaces only, so `main` never passes through a partially authoritative startup state.

Review stack #1468: #1446 -> #1447 -> #1448 -> #1449. Depends on #1440.

Only this collector may merge into `main`; the four review-layer PRs must remain unmerged.

## Summary

- Support external models through `lmms_eval.models` entry points without editing the built-in catalog.

- One squash landing after every review layer is approved.

- Any extra cleanup or conflict-resolution edit in the collector.

author: yegamble
body:
Both `contract` and `frontend-e2e-backed` have been RED on `main` since core#69,
so every frontend PR inherits two failures it did not cause. Neither is a
frontend regression — both are `vidra-core` phase-3/phase-4 work landing on the
other side of the contract. This unblocks the queue.

## 1. `contract` — regenerated `lib/api/generated.ts`

Generated only, no hand edits: `npm run codegen` (`scripts/codegen.mjs`) against
`vidra-core` main @ `802b5ae`.

**The diff is exactly the two expected waves and nothing else.** Nothing
unrelated came along:

- **Phase 3 (CMAF)** — the media file route reshapes: `rendition` is now either
  a rung-height directory (`720p`) for MPEG-TS or the `cmaf` pseudo-rendition,
  `file` gains the CMAF names (`stream.mpd`, `media_N.m3u8`, `init-N.mp4`,
  `chunk-N-NNNNN.m4s`, `iframe-N.*`), and the 200 response gains
  `application/dash+xml` and `video/mp4`.
- **Phase 4 (core#74)** — new `POST /api/v1/videos/{id}/playback-session`
  returning `PlaybackSession`, plus `packaging_format` and `dash_url` on the
  video detail response.

### `playback_token` is optional, as it must be

The spec's `PlaybackSession` carries `required: [session_id, video_id]` only, and
the generator produced `playback_token?: string` / `expires_in?: number`.
Verified in the diff, not assumed.

That is load-bearing rather than incidental. The backend mints a token only for
privacy `password`, because any request carrying `?pt=` is treated as
credentialed, and a credentialed media request is never cached, never presigned
and never redirected — a session that minted one for every viewer would silently
make all media delivery origin-only. Typing it required would encode the
opposite invariant and push the error into consumer code later.

No consumer needed changing: `lib/api/types.ts` derives every named type from
`generated.ts`, and both waves are additive. I did **not** add a
`PlaybackSession` alias to `types.ts` — nothing imports it yet; that belongs with
whichever PR actually adopts the session call.

## 2. `frontend-e2e-backed` — `e2e-backed/hls-playback.spec.ts`

CI reported line 41 (`expect(masterBody).toContain("16p/playlist.m3u8")`), but
that was just the first hop to fail. The test then rebuilt the variant and
segment URLs from the same convention, and the two trees are mutually exclusive
— `internal/httpapi/hls.go` 404s a TS name against a CMAF video *and the
reverse* — so those hops were about to fail too.

### Why not just swap in the CMAF string

`TRANSCODING_PACKAGER` is documented as `cmaf|ts`, the format is recorded **per
video** at transcode time (`migrations/0108`, `streaming_playlists.format`), and
there is deliberately no re-packaging job. A back catalogue transcoded before the
switch serves TS forever, and the documented rollback would re-red this test the
moment anyone exercises it. Pinning to exactly one packager just moves the
breakage.

### What it does instead

It no longer builds a URL from a naming convention at all. It reads the URI each
`#EXT-X-STREAM-INF` advertises, resolves it relative to the document that
advertised it, and follows it: **master → media playlist → segment**.

That is **strictly stronger** than the string it replaces. A master advertising
something this origin will not serve now fails; a convention-built URL could not
see that. It still fails on a broken or empty master, which yields no variants.

So it has not gone vacuous, it also pins:

| assertion | proves |
|---|---|
| every variant URI matches one packaging, and they all agree | a master mixing both shapes is corrupt |
| shape agrees with detail's `packaging_format` | the declared format cannot drift from the bytes |
| `dash_url` present **iff** CMAF, and the MPD resolves | the second manifest is the whole point of CMAF |
| `#EXT-X-MAP` init segment fetched (CMAF), absent (TS) | an fMP4 stream is unplayable without its init |
| variants ≥ ladder rungs | CMAF publishes one per (codec, rung) pair — with HEVC/AV1 on there are *more* variants than rungs, never fewer |

The `packaging_format` check tolerates the field being absent, so this still
passes against a core predating phase 4 — same forward-compatibility posture as
the `OWNER_CLAIM_TOKEN` seam.

### `renditions.length > 0` — left as-is, deliberately

Flagged as landing red if audio-only seed data is ever added, and that is real:
an audio-only CMAF tree gets **no rendition rows at all**
(`internal/media/cmaf.go` — no 0p rung by design).

But it cannot reach this test. This spec uploads its **own** 16x16 clip via
`seedPublishedChannel`, so it never reads shared seed data. Filtering to video
rungs would change what it proves — it would stop proving the ladder *is* the
video ladder — so I left the assertion and instead spelled it out as "positive
height and width", making the shape this test depends on stated rather than
implied. That is a strengthening, not a weakening.

## Verification

Green locally:

- `npm run typecheck` ✅
- `npm run lint` ✅ (0 errors; the 4 warnings are pre-existing on `main`)
- `npm run lint:icons` ✅
- `npm run test` ✅ 164 files, **1538 tests**
- `scripts/check-contract.mjs` ✅ 190/190 frontend-referenced paths resolve
- `npm run codegen` re-run is a no-op against core main — the committed file is
  fresh, which is exactly what `contract-ci` asserts
- `npx playwright test --list` parses the rewritten spec

**Not run locally: the backed Playwright suite.** The host's disk is at 100%
(`165Mi` free of `460Gi`), so `docker compose --profile core up --build` dies
with `input/output error` writing the buildkit metadata DB and `docker system df`
itself errors on a corrupt blob. I could not stand the stack up, and I did not
free space on a shared machine to try. **The e2e fix is unverified against a live
backend — CI is the proof.**

To compensate, the parse and URL-resolution logic was dry-run against the *exact*
playlist bytes `vidra-core`'s own Go tests assert on (`internal/httpapi/hls_test.go`,
`internal/media/cmaf_test.go` — as **served**, i.e. with the `?v=` rewrite
applied), across three shapes plus negative controls:

```
CMAF master (2 rungs + audio group)  -> variant, init and segment all resolve
CMAF master (single 16p rung)        -> matches this fixture exactly
MPEG-TS master (rollback)            -> variant and segment all resolve
empty / header-only / STREAM-INF-with-no-URI -> 0 variants, test fails as intended
```

## Not merging

Leaving this for review. Once it lands, `main` goes green and the
`prod/phase4-quality-id` PR (#59) should pick both fixes up on its next run.

author: takashikasuya
body:
## 背景

`docs/schema/swagger.yaml` はコミット済みで aspida 生成の入力にもなるが、**ソースと一致しているかを誰も検証していなかった**ため乖離が黙って蓄積していた。実例：`dff86a6` で XML doc を変更した際の `control-audit` の summary が `0ff5d6e`（#347）まで古いまま残っていた。

Fixes #354

## 既存の自動コミットが機能していなかった理由（調査結果）

`generate-swagger.yaml` は「main への push で再生成し、差分があれば自動コミット」する設計だった。**実行履歴を確認したところ、直近 10 回中 5 回が failure**、しかも乖離を生んだ `dff86a6` の回も failure だった。

失敗ステップは `Commit and push changes` で、原因は：

```
! [rejected]        main -> main (fetch first)
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/gutp-bim/gutp-building-os-ri'
```

ブランチ保護ではなく**競合**である。このリポジトリでは main へのマージ直後に必ず `chore(argocd): update image tags ... [skip ci]` が push されるため、ビルドと生成に数分かかるこのワークフローは push 時点で常に古い ref を持つことになる。**構造的に競合するので、直しても安定しない。**

なお名誉のために書いておくと、`Run generate_swagger.bash` と `Check for changes` は **success** しており、**検知自体は正しく働いていた**。壊れていたのは反映方法だけである。

## 変更内容

### 1. PR 時点で検査する（`pr-check.yml`）

既存の `dotnet-check` ジョブにステップを 1 つ追加し、再生成して `git diff --exit-code` する。**push しないので競合しない**し、乖離が main に入る**前**に止まるので自動コミットより早く気付ける。

新規ジョブではなく既存ジョブへの相乗りにした理由：

- Release ビルドを再利用できる（スクリプト内の `dotnet build` は増分で実質 no-op、ローカル実測 1.85 秒）
- swagger CLI は `DotNet/.config/dotnet-tools.json` に **10.2.3 で固定済み**（プロジェクトの Swashbuckle と同一）で、同ジョブの `Restore tools` が既に restore している → **ツール導入ステップ不要**
- `generate_swagger.bash` は env を自前で export し、**DB 接続は行わない**（接続文字列は読まれるだけ）→ **service container 不要**

### 2. paths フィルタに `docs/schema/swagger.yaml` を追加

検査は `dotnet-check` の中にあるため、これが無いと「swagger を手編集する」という**唯一の乖離手段**が**唯一の検査スキップ手段**になってしまう。

### 3. `generate-swagger.yaml` を削除

上記のとおり構造的に競合して成立しない。加えて、恒常的に赤いワークフローは「失敗を無視する」習慣を作るため、放置は有害。

## 検証（ローカルで両方向を実証）

| ケース | 結果 |
|---|---|
| 現状のまま再生成 | `exit 0` で生成 → 差分なし → **GREEN** |
| `///` コメントを 1 行変更して再生成 | 差分を検知 → **RED**（復元後は再び差分なし） |

**途中で自分の検証が無効だったことに気付いた点も記録しておく**：`dotnet tool restore` していない状態では `swagger` コマンドが見つからず、**生成されないまま「差分なし」＝無意味な GREEN** になっていた。CI では `Restore tools` が先行するため問題なく、またその場合スクリプトが `exit 1` で終わるのでステップとしても失敗する（＝サイレントに通ることはない）。

## 既知のリスク

author: arcadia-1
body:
`plan/` becomes an untracked local working area. **618 files, −61,101 lines.**

## The rule was right; the vehicle was not

The gate's value was never the plan file. It is this:

> changing implementation code requires a written, cross-checked statement about test impact

The vehicle was a dated directory with five prescribed sections — which accumulated **229 of them** at the repository root.

The declaration is now a **commit trailer**, so it travels with the diff through `git log`, `git blame`, and the PR instead of living in a parallel file that can drift from it:

```
Test-Impact: tests-updated
Test-Impact: no-test-change — <evidence>
```

## The enforcement is unchanged

`pnpm test:impact` still cross-checks the claim against the diff, and CI still runs it:

- `tests-updated` requires a changed test file
- `no-test-change` requires that none changed, **plus** evidence
- a bare `no-test-change` is rejected — it asserts the conclusion without the reason

Verified both directions on this very PR: the gate **failed** on a placeholder trailer, then **passed** once the real declaration was written.

CI already passed `--base` to the script, so its wiring needed **no change**.

## What else went

- `scripts/check-gate-review.mjs` — it only ever read plan files and was never wired into CI.
- `plan/**` path filters in `ci.yml` / `cloudflare.yml`, and `plan/**` from the gate catalog.
- **12 provenance links from ADRs into `plan/`** — removed rather than left dead for anyone cloning. One experience note's "detailed chronology" pointer now names the committed evidence instead.

author: chelsealong
body:
Fixes #92672.

## Root cause

With `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`, `GatewayRunner.start()` registers declarative shell hooks and outbound webhooks exactly once, at process startup, against the root/default profile's config (`gateway/run.py`, the `register_from_config` call site right before `self.hooks.discover_and_load()`). That call runs before any profile scope exists.

Secondary profiles are started later, in `_start_one_profile_adapters()`, which runs each profile's turns under its own `_profile_runtime_scope` (its own `HERMES_HOME` override) and already calls `discover_plugins()` there so per-profile *plugins* work — but it never called `agent.shell_hooks.register_from_config()` / `agent.outbound_webhooks.register_from_config()` for that profile's own `config.yaml`. Because `hermes_cli.plugins.get_plugin_manager()` caches one `PluginManager` per resolved home, a secondary profile's turns dispatch through its own manager, which never received the root profile's (or its own) hook callbacks. Result: a secondary profile's `hooks.pre_tool_call` / `hooks.outbound` block is silently inert — no error, no webhook fires, and a security gate (e.g. a deny-writes hook) never runs.

Additional wrinkle noted in the issue: `agent/shell_hooks.py`'s `_registered` idempotence set (and the analogous one in `agent/outbound_webhooks.py`) was keyed only by `(event, matcher, command)` / `(event, url)`, with no home/profile scoping. Even after wiring the registration call into the secondary-profile startup path, two profiles configuring an *identical* hook would have the second call see the triple already in `_registered` and skip wiring it onto its own (different) plugin manager.

## Fix

- `gateway/run.py`: inside `_start_one_profile_adapters()`, within the profile's `_profile_runtime_scope`, load that profile's own config and call `agent.shell_hooks.register_from_config()` / `agent.outbound_webhooks.register_from_config()` against it (mirrors the exact call shape used at root startup, including `accept_hooks=False` so `hooks_auto_accept` in the profile's own config is honored). Failures are logged and never block startup, matching the root startup call site's behavior.
- `agent/shell_hooks.py` / `agent/outbound_webhooks.py`: the module-global idempotence sets are now keyed by resolved Hermes home in addition to the existing fields, so identical hook/webhook configuration in two different profiles registers independently on each profile's own plugin manager instead of the second profile's attempt being dropped as a duplicate.

## Test plan

Added `TestSecondaryProfileHookRegistration` to `tests/gateway/test_multiplex_adapter_registry.py`, asserting that `_start_one_profile_adapters()` calls both `agent.shell_hooks.register_from_config` and `agent.outbound_webhooks.register_from_config` with the secondary profile's own config.

Confirmed the new test fails without the fix:

```
$ git stash push -- gateway/run.py agent/shell_hooks.py agent/outbound_webhooks.py
$ python3 -m pytest tests/gateway/test_multiplex_adapter_registry.py -q -k TestSecondaryProfileHookRegistration
FAILED ...::test_registers_shell_hooks_and_webhooks_for_secondary_profile
AssertionError: assert ('shell', {...}) in []
1 failed, 18 deselected in 0.89s
$ git stash pop
```

And passes with it, alongside the full surrounding suites:

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/gateway/test_multiplex_adapter_registry.py -q
19 passed in 1.89s

$ python3 -m pytest tests/gateway/ -q -k multiplex
159 passed, 2 skipped, 5983 deselected in 12.82s

$ python3 -m pytest tests/agent/test_shell_hooks.py tests/agent/test_shell_hooks_tree_kill.py tests/agent/test_shell_hooks_consent.py tests/agent/test_outbound_webhooks.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins.py -q
158 passed in 14.53s

$ python3 -m ruff check gateway/run.py agent/shell_hooks.py agent/outbound_webhooks.py tests/gateway/test_multiplex_adapter_registry.py
All checks passed!
```

## Notes

Authored with AI assistance; the diff, reproduction, and test were verified manually (real test runs, real ruff run, and a stash-based before/after check of the new regression test) before pushing.

author: sundar1207
body:
💡 **What**: Optimized the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) brute-force function by removing explicit array allocations from the hot loop, replacing them with incremental cost calculations. Implemented dynamic branch-and-bound early pruning.
🎯 **Why**: Brute-forcing permutations is O(N!). Constructing a new array (via `list()`) inside every iteration of an O(N!) loop creates massive overhead and memory allocation strain. Without pruning, the algorithm explores all sub-optimal paths fully, even when they demonstrably cannot improve the best known path cost.
📊 **Impact**: Reduces execution time dramatically for graphs with 10+ nodes (measured at ~63% reduction on a 10-node graph in local profiling), scaling better while retaining the brute-force pattern.
🔬 **Measurement**: Validated via `cProfile` and `time` module metrics before and after the change on an identical graph input. Behavior and style verified via `python3 TSP.py` and `flake8`.

author: olegfx
body:
**PR 1 of 3** in the outbox rebuild. `#53` carries the diagnosis that motivated it and is closed; this branch starts from `main` rather than continuing there, because the growth threshold is measured from first submission and that base had taken `+2008` lines across eight review rounds.

`+285 −39` across three files.

## Two defects, and the second is what made the first hard to fix

**The state was re-derived on every question.** `load_consent_outbox` read the file and judged it afresh each time, so a transient failure flipped the answer mid-session — the same file read twice gave two verdicts, and every rule built on the second silently disagreed with the first. It is resolved **once** per client session now, and everything else is a thin read of that.

Per **session**, not per process: the cache outlives the client, so a second `sdk.new()` would inherit the first one verdict — and on a game engine a process restart means relaunching the editor, so one transient failure would fail closed for the rest of the day.

**The read had two answers for four situations.** `read_failed` was set both when the read THREW and when it returned something that is not a record. Those do not mean the same thing to anyone: one says look at the device, the other says look at the file. Four states now — `absent` / `readable` / `unusable` / `silent`.

Both halves predate the rebuild: the conflation is in `main` today, in the original loader.

## What is new rather than refactored

`consent_denial_possibly_undelivered` now carries a **`cause`**, derived from the resolution observations rather than stamped, so it cannot disagree with a resolution a later branch has moved on. It is declared as a stat initialised to `0` rather than appearing only when set — an alarm whose absence and whose zero look identical cannot be alerted on, and this one means *there are undeleted personal data behind an unaccounted denial*.

The resolution also hands out **copies**. Returning its own list would make the caller mirror and the resolution the same table, so every mirror mutation would silently edit the resolution and the two could not disagree even where they should — which is the entire point of asking it anything.

## Evidence

Every test on `main` passes unmodified, on 5.1 and 5.4 — this changes no behaviour beyond adding the diagnostic.

Six mutants, one per fact, each killing only its own test, including **both directions** of the four-valued split (collapsing `silent` into `unusable` and `unusable` into `silent` each fail, at different lines) — collapsing either way is the defect, so a mutant in one direction alone would not have proven it.

## What is deliberately not here

No successor key, no freeze, no merge. PR 2 replaces the whole-list write with `append` / `drop` operations, which makes three findings from `#53` unexpressible rather than fixed. PR 3 rules on superseding an unreadable state, on the condition measured and recorded in the plan.

author: kyber775
body:
## Summary

Extracts a shared GitHub API client (`scripts/github_api.py`) combining automatic list endpoint pagination (`get_all`) and bounded retries on transient errors (5xx, 429, and secondary rate limits) across repository maintenance scripts (`scripts/request_reviewers.py` and `scripts/notify_broken_main.py`).

## Why This Change

Previously, `scripts/request_reviewers.py` and `scripts/notify_broken_main.py` each maintained duplicate implementations of `GitHubAPI` that diverged:
- `request_reviewers.py` implemented pagination via `get_all`, but lacked retry logic, causing dropped writes on 503s or secondary rate limits that left pull requests without assigned reviewers.
- `notify_broken_main.py` implemented bounded retries for 5xx, 429, and 403 secondary rate limits (fixed 5s delay or `Retry-After`), but lacked pagination.
- Sharing one unified client gives all repository scripts resilient retry handling and complete pagination.

## What Changed

- **`scripts/github_api.py`**:
  - Created shared module containing `GitHubAPI` with `request`, `get`, `get_all`, `post`, `patch`, and `delete`.
  - Configured bounded retries on 5xx, 429, secondary rate limit 403 (`Retry-After` / `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`), and transient `URLError` network failures (using `Retry-After` capped at 60s or fixed 5s delay).
  - Implemented `get_all` automatic pagination across multi-page list endpoints.
  - Added configurable `user_agent` support with fallback to `kube-agents-scripts`.
- **`scripts/request_reviewers.py`**:
  - Replaced local `GitHubAPI` class with `from github_api import API_ROOT, PER_PAGE, GitHubAPI, log`.
  - Configured `user_agent="kube-agents-request-reviewers"`.
- **`scripts/notify_broken_main.py`**:
  - Replaced duplicate base request and retry definitions with `class GitHubAPI(BaseGitHubAPI)`.
  - Removed duplicate shadow definitions of `REQUEST_ATTEMPTS`, `REQUEST_RETRY_SECONDS`, `REQUEST_RETRY_CEILING`, `_rate_limited`, and `_retry_delay` so the shared client's knobs are live.
  - Preserved script-specific domain helpers (`run`, `history`, `open_issues_for_workflow`, `ensure_label`, `create_issue`, `update_issue`, `comment`, `close_issue`).
- **`scripts/test_github_api.py`**:
  - Added unit test suite covering header injection, `get_all` pagination across single and multiple pages, 5xx retries, 429 rate-limit retries, 403 secondary rate-limit retries, non-retried 403s, `tolerate` handling, and HTTP verbs.
- **`scripts/test_notify_broken_main.py` & `scripts/test_request_reviewers.py`**:
  - Added standalone `sys.path` bootstrapping for isolated test execution.
- **`agents/platform/scripts/test_session_manager.py`**:
  - Sanitized `HERMES_SESSION_ID`, `HERMES_USER_ID`, and `HERMES_SENDER_ID` in `setUp`.
- **`tests/test_docker_entrypoint.py`**:
  - Wrapped `sys.executable` execution in a temporary shell script wrapper in `_run_step_2_6b`.

## Context

Closes #838.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest scripts/test_github_api.py`: 10 tests passed.
- `python3 -m unittest scripts/test_notify_broken_main.py`: 70 tests passed.
- `python3 -m unittest scripts/test_request_reviewers.py`: 48 tests passed.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: 362 tests passed.
- `make docs-check`: Passed all link checks, terminology checks, map coverage, and instruction budgets.
- `cd k8s-operator && go test -count=1 ./...`: Passed.

### Live validation

Not live-tested against a live cluster or running deployment. Changes are strictly confined to deterministic helper extraction in repository scripts (`scripts/github_api.py`) and unit test fixtures.

## Self-Review

Passes executed in fresh isolated subagent context (`sa-0-0d9dd69b`):
- **Adversarial code review (`review-adversarial`):**
  - Verified that `GitHubAPI` subclassing in `notify_broken_main.py` leaves `github_api`'s retry configuration authoritative and removes dead shadow variables.
  - Verified that `get_all` pagination termination condition (`len(batch) < per_page`) handles empty, single-page, and multi-page responses without infinite loops.
  - Verified that out-of-scope production image modifications were removed to keep the pull request strictly scoped.
  - Verified retry policy uses bounded fixed delay (5s) or `Retry-After` capped at 60s without unbacked claims of exponential backoff.
- **Docs-drift review (`review-docs-drift`):**
  - Verified that `scripts/` documentation headers and execution instructions remain accurate.

## Risk & Rollout

Low risk: Scoped entirely to repository maintenance automation scripts under `scripts/`. Revert by reverting the commit.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a backend-only, tool-using Gemini investigation layer that synthesizes evidence from database-grounded tools while keeping ML risk prediction independent.
- Ensure investigations are auditable, tool-grounded, validated with Pydantic, and cannot perform financial actions or call arbitrary functions.
- Make Gemini configuration explicit and bounded (model name + timeout) and treat outages as non-fatal to ML prediction flows.

### Description
- Add a controlled Gemini orchestration service `app.services.gemini_agent.GeminiInvestigationAgent` that exposes an allowlist of tools (`get_transaction`, `get_customer_history`, `get_previous_disputes`, `get_device_history`, `get_related_transactions`, `get_merchant_policy`, `create_evidence_report`, `recommend_action`), enforces bounded tool-call rounds, rejects unknown tool names, and validates the final JSON result with `InvestigationResponse` before using it.
- Persist investigation artifacts via a new `AgentInvestigation` ORM model linked to `RiskCase` that stores `model_name`, `tool_calls_json`, `evidence_references_json`, and `result_json` for traceability.
- Add `POST /api/v1/cases/{case_id}/investigate` endpoint to run the controlled investigation, persist the validated trace/result, and append a `GEMINI_INVESTIGATION_COMPLETED` case history event, while converting Gemini failures to HTTP 503 errors.
- Add configuration fields `GEMINI_MODEL` and `GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` with validation in `app.core.config.Settings`, add `.env.example` entries, and document Phase 7 behavior in `README.md`.
- Add developer-facing safety in the service to operate even when `google-genai` is not installed by failing with a descriptive `GeminiAgentUnavailable` (so ML flows remain separate).  Add `google-genai` to backend `pyproject.toml` dependencies.
- Add tests `backend/tests/test_gemini_agent.py` exercising: controlled tool execution (provider double), rejection of disallowed tools, structured-output validation grounding, and a controlled Gemini outage that does not prevent `POST /api/v1/risk/predict` from working.

### Testing
- Ran compilation and static checks: `python -m compileall -q app tests && git diff --check` — succeeded.
- Verified application startup and route registration: `python -c 'from app.main import create_app; assert "/api/v1/cases/{case_id}/investigate" in create_app().openapi()["paths"]'` — succeeded.

author: pizzato
body:
## The bug

Anything typed into the cover Re-generate popover's *tell it how* box was ignored. The plumbing was all fine — the frontend sent it, the endpoint threaded it, the worker used the built prompt — but `build_cover_prompt` appended it to the **very end** of the ~1500-character cover prompt, which ends with the negative list:

```
... No watermark, no UI elements. Avoid: text, letters, words, numbers, writing,
captions, subtitles, typography, lettering, signage, poster text, watermark, logo,
blurry, low resolution, messy layout, too much clutter, distorted faces, deformed
hands, boring flat lighting, plain background.. make it all robots, no humans
```

Two failure modes at once:

1. **It reads as part of the avoid list.** A clause tacked onto `Avoid: a, b, c…` is one more thing to leave out — the opposite of the intent.
2. **Tail position carries almost no weight.** ~30 tokens at the end of 1500 characters of hard directives ("CRITICAL:", "must", "never") don't move the image.

A third problem survived even a well-placed steer: the subject hint states the film's own imagery as fact (`Key visual elements from the video: a woman walking through a rainy street at night`). Concrete, earlier, and specific, it beat any conflicting direction.

## The fix

The steer now **leads** the prompt and is labelled as outranking what follows, and when a steer is present the scene elements are demoted from required content to optional reference:

```
make it all robots, no humans. That direction outranks everything below — where they
conflict, follow it. Create a high-impact YouTube thumbnail background for a video.
Video visual style: … Visual elements from the video, to draw on only where they fit
that direction: A woman walking through a rainy street at night | …
```

The style line and the no-text rule are untouched, so a steered cover still looks like a frame from the same production and the title is still composited afterwards.

Deliberately kept in `pipeline/cover.py` rather than adding a `${instruction_line}` placeholder to `prompts.yaml`: a user override of `cover_image_notext` saved from the prompt editor would lack the new placeholder and would drop the steer entirely.

## Verification

- An un-steered cover prompt is **byte-identical** to before (asserted in the new test).
- New tests cover the lead position, the ordering against `Avoid:`, and the subject-hint demotion.
- Full suite: 1744 passed.

Docs: [docs/manual/edit-film.md](docs/manual/edit-film.md) Cover image section now describes what the caret does.

author: dachhack
body:
The founder's "let's build them all" — both research lists, plus the new 📜 SALARY commissioner section holding every option.

## 0219 — salary mechanics, in-season
- **`team_payroll` becomes the whole ledger**: deals held (minus salary retained by former teams, minus IR'd salary when the relief rule is on) + your retained-salary ghosts + your dead money. **`team_cap`** = league cap + traded cap room. The deferred contract trigger and `execute_trade` both judge against these.
- **Salary retention on trades**: the sender keeps eating $1..salary−1 of a traded deal (validated per-slug against what's already retained); the receiver pays the net.
- **Raw cap-space trading**: cap dollars move like a pick, behind a commissioner switch defaulting OFF. A pure cash deal is judged at execute — over-cap refuses whole.
- **IR cap relief** (toggle): an IR'd deal comes off the books.
- **`contract_market_value`**: the league's own market pricer (top-5 positional salary average) — feeds the tag, extensions, and the cap sheet's value read.
- **`set_salary_rules`**: dead-money %, tag raise %, extension discount %, and the retention / cap-trading / IR-relief / RFA switches.
- Cap check now waits for the draft room to close; `_start_draft_now` pre-docks every seat's auction budget by its carried payroll.

## 0220 — the contract offseason
- **Carriage (the keystone)**: `rollover_league` carries live deals at years−1, walks expiring untagged players to the pool, decrements dead money, brings retained ghosts along with their contracts; traded cap room deliberately resets.
- **Dead money**: cuts on multi-year deals leave dead_pct% of the cutter's share for the deal's remaining life; retained ghosts harden into the retainer's dead money.
- **`franchise_tag`** (one per team: max(top-5 positional market, salary+raise%)), **`extend_contract`** (1–3yr at discount% of market, stored years+1 so rollover lands it exactly), **RFA** (`rfa_tender`/`rfa_bid`/`rfa_resolve` — bid, match-or-walk; unresolved tenders lapse at rollover).
- `_contract_originate` skips 'keeper' rows (carriage writes the real carried deal); `league_trades` v3 carries the salary terms so the accepting manager sees them.
- Two lineage catches: `_start_draft_now`'s current body was 0193 (the battery's pinned rs5b error caught the 0190 clobber before it shipped); `league_trades` re-created from 0183.

## Client
- Commish section becomes **📜 SALARY**: cap + max length, three percents, four switches, live payrolls vs per-team caps.
- **Cap sheet = the whole book**: net salaries with retained splits, per-deal market read (`mkt $N`), ghost lines, dead-money lines, 🏷 tags — and in the offseason, 🏷 TAG / ⤴ EXT / 🪧 TENDER on your expiring deals plus the RFA board (bid / match / walk).
- Both trade builders (web + app) grow retention steppers and an I-SEND / I-ASK cap-dollars row; trade rows print the money terms.

## Verification
- Full scratch-DB battery green on a fresh cluster — **64 suites**; contract suite now §1–§14 (~90 assertions) covering retention payroll splits, over-retention refusal, cap-dollar trades and their over-cap refusal, IR relief on/off, the cut that hardens ghosts + charges 50%, tag pricing, 85% extensions, the RFA walk, and full rollover carriage incl. the pre-docked next-season auction.
- Web + app typecheck clean; `check:parity` passes.

**On merge, `migrate.yml` auto-applies 0219+0220 to production.**

author: cornfy
dereuromark
body:
Closes #1509 `
` is a navigation landmark unconditionally - unlike `
`, which maps to `generic` until it is named - so a table-of-contents nav with no accessible name is an entry in every landmark list reading only "navigation". Measured on the pinned build rather than taken from the report, and it is worse than one anonymous entry. Registering both extensions renders **two navs that are byte-identical, including their absence of a name**: ```html
  • One
  • One
``` A document may also write `::: toc` more than once, and a surrounding site template contributes its own nav. Indistinguishable entries are the defect; a single anonymous one is only how it starts. ## Derived or authored: authored, so it gets a key This is the decision the ticket asks for, and §1.5 states the test. Three buckets, and the nav lands in the third: - **Derived from the document** - a tab's `[label]`, an admonition title, a task item's own text. Not this: the directive's content is empty and nothing on the page names the nav, so there is no string to derive from. - **No fixed English default** - a diagram fence defaults to its own class word, so it stays an option. Not this either, and the near miss is worth stating because `toc` *is* this extension's class word: an abbreviation a reader hears spelled out is a worse landmark entry than the prose it abbreviates, and "Table of contents" is ordinary English a host's catalog already holds. - **A fixed English default the extension does not already expose as an option** - which gets a `labels` key. Measured: no configuration puts an `aria-label` on the nav in any engine, so §1.5's "unless" does not fire. So: **a new `labels` key `tocNav`, default `Table of contents`** - and no option, which is the half §1.5 says must not be doubled. ### It is not the `summary` string wearing a second hat That objection is the reason to measure rather than reason. `collapsible` turns the standalone extension's output into `
` with a `` and **no `
` at all**: ```html
Table of Contents
  • One
``` The two shapes are mutually exclusive, one string is a landmark's accessible name and the other is visible text in a disclosure widget, and `TocPlacement` has no such option and always renders the nav. So `summary` stays option-only under carve#1510 and this key does not collide with it. §1.5 now says so directly, because the near-identical defaults otherwise read as a contradiction. The map is also the one seam all three engines already honor, which matters here: `markup-carve/carve-rs` has neither `collapsible` nor `summary` (`markup-carve/carve-rs#1243`), so routing the name through an extension option would mean inventing an option in an engine that has none. ## Both extensions, and the author still wins `TocPlacement` and `TableOfContents` read the same key, so the navs stay byte-identical - the contract §8b.3 names. And §8b.1 already carries the author's `{#id .class}` onto the `
`, so an authored `aria-label` is simply kept with no label added beside it, by §1.5's existing precedence. That needed only to be stated - it is already the behavior, verbatim from the pinned build: ```html
``` The match is on the attribute name **case-insensitively**, as §16a already rules for the shapes carve#1468 closed. Worth pinning, because an author writing `ARIA-LABEL` currently has it echoed through in that spelling. ## No corpus case, and why §8b.3 states it: `::: toc` is Tier-3, its embedded output carries per-implementation block indentation, and it is **not** corpus-pinned - the cross-impl contract is the nav fragment itself. A corpus case here would be three declared skips, which is the silence the repo's own adapter test exists to prevent. The pins are instead: - `tests/every-labels-key-reaches-the-output.test.mjs` - the key is read off the §1.5 table, so a row with no probe (or a probe with no row) fails. - `resources/examples-tier3.md` - the fence IS the expectation and is compared live against the pinned build. ## The key is declared ahead of the pin, not asserted into silence No engine writes this string yet, so both pins would go red. `examples-tier3` already has `AHEAD_OF_PIN` for exactly this; the labels test had no such window, which meant the only way to land a labels ruling was to leave the key out of the tables until an engine caught up - and a key nobody documents is a key nobody implements. So the same window is added there, **inverted** the way the Tier-3 ledger is: a declared key must still be MISSING from the output, so the commit that moves the pin deletes the entry because leaving it fails. Its own liveness case rejects an entry naming a key no table documents or no probe reaches, which is the carve#755 shape this repo keeps finding.

author: lcy-seso
body:
## Problems

- The nav opened with Design — contributor-facing pages mirrored from TileOPs — while the site had no user-facing guide at all.
- Skills pages embedded agent-facing instructions from the TileOPs skill definitions, which is not what a documentation site is for.
- Nothing explained how to call an op under `torch.compile`, or how a vendor brings new hardware in as a backend.
- API Reference rendered every docstring section as a four-column table, so an op with fourteen constructor parameters became a grid the size of the page.
- Formulas in docstrings reached the API pages as the literal text `.. math::` (the docstrings themselves are fixed by tile-ai/TileOPs#1969).
- The Performance Guides landing page said "Guides coming soon".
- Body type was a step larger than Material's default, prose was capped narrower than every table beside it, and long nav labels wrapped to two lines.
- README named one of the five plugins the site needs and listed a `blog/` directory that does not exist; CLAUDE.md claimed a missing TileOPs checkout only warns.

## Changes

- Six nav sections in the order a reader asks: Home, User Guide, API Reference, Benchmarks, Performance Guides, Design.
- New page, `torch.compile` integration: how dynamo decides what enters a graph, why the compile boundary sits at the op layer, `RMSNormFwdOp` in code, the three guarantees, five calling conventions, and the measured cost of the boundary.
- New page, adding a hardware backend: the division of work between op layer and backend, the three concepts (target, `detect`, `build_kernel`), the protocol as four names plus an entry point, and the CPU package as a template — drawn from the multi-backend RFC.
- Skills section removed: 11 pages, the authoring template, the `hooks.py` link rewrites, and the sparse-checkout paths both workflows needed for it.
- Performance Guides routes to the nightly benchmark numbers and the in-kernel trace guide instead of promising future content.
- API pages render docstring sections as definition lists, drop the `Bases: Op` line, and set symbol headings in mono at close to body size.
- `pymdownx.arithmatex` + MathJax render formulas; the config re-typesets after Material's instant-loading page swaps.
- Page TOC moves to the right column, which frees the left one for navigation and allows `navigation.indexes`; nav labels shortened to one line each.
- Body type down one step, Chinese prose at the Latin size with looser leading, sheet widened to 76rem (82rem past 100em), and prose, tables and code blocks sharing one width.
- Chinese pages under `/zh/` for the home page, both new guides, and Performance Guides — written as Chinese prose, with the two guides authored in Chinese and translated into English.
- README and CLAUDE.md corrected and rewritten to match the site.

Build is clean: no warnings other than griffe's notes about missing annotations in TileOPs docstrings.

author: altisinfonet
body:
## Summary

Cloudflare Pages Functions have no build step, so nothing about them reaches `dist` and the bundle isolation guard was structurally unable to see them. `functions/_seo.ts` carried three production literals — project ref, anon key, site origin — behind a "default to production when unset" rule, so a lane that forgot to set them silently became production and emitted production canonical URLs into that lane's crawlable HTML.

The three lane values are now **required** (unset throws, set-but-empty throws), and the guard scans `functions/` from source so a re-introduced literal fails the build instead of shipping.

## Scope

- [ ] Touches judging code (hooks/pages/edge functions/migrations under judging surfaces)
- [x] Touches non-judging code only

---

## What changed

**`functions/_seo.ts`** — `PRODUCTION_PROJECT_REF`, `PRODUCTION_ANON_KEY` and `PRODUCTION_SITE_ORIGIN` deleted. `laneValue()` no longer takes a default; an absent variable throws. Every lane's Pages project must define `SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` and `SITE_ORIGIN`.

**`scripts/verify-bundle-isolation.mjs`** — extra scan roots alongside `dist`. `functions/` is scanned **on by default** when the directory exists, because an opt-in scan would have to be requested identically by CI *and* by the Pages build command, and the day one of them forgot, the failure would be silent. New rule **R11**: a `functions/` directory excluded from explicitly-named roots fails the build, with escape hatch `ISOLATION_ALLOW_UNSCANNED_FUNCTIONS=1`. `.ts` added to the scanned extensions, since Functions ship as source. The PASS line now names its roots.

**`scripts/test-isolation-guard.mjs`** — 8 new cases, 4 new mutants. Cases now run in a scratch cwd: R11 keys off a `functions/` directory *relative to cwd*, which made the harness's own working directory a hidden input the moment that rule existed. Hermeticity is not only about env vars.

**`functions/pages-runtime.d.ts`** (new) — the new unit test pulls `functions/_seo.ts` into the TypeScript program for the first time, surfacing `HTMLRewriter` as an undeclared Workers global. Declared narrowly, covering only what `functions/` uses.

**`src/__tests__/seoLaneRequired.test.ts`** (new) — 11 tests pinning that each reader throws on unset and on set-but-empty, that a staging env yields no production value, and that the source file carries no production literal.

## Verification

All four gates run locally on `ef037c7` before the push:

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` | 0 errors |
| `node scripts/test-isolation-guard.mjs` | 44 cases, 0 failures, mutations detected/held **16/16** |
| `npx vitest run src/__tests__/seoLaneRequired.test.ts` | 11 passed |
| `npx vitest run` | 165 files passed, 1 skipped — **2292 passed, 1 skipped** |

Both lanes were also built and guarded locally against the real `functions/` tree:

```
staging:    ISOLATION-GUARD PASS: expected=ztzutckwdhetphwghuzj present; forbidden=[jtdtehuqtinjxropkkcn] absent;
            host=cdn-staging.50mmretina.com present;
            forbidden-hosts=[cdn.50mmretina.com,www.50mmretina.com,https://50mmretina.com] absent;
            271 assets scanned across 2 root(s): dist, functions.

production: ISOLATION-GUARD PASS: expected=jtdtehuqtinjxropkkcn present; forbidden=[ztzutckwdhetphwghuzj] absent;
            host=cdn.50mmretina.com present;
            forbidden-hosts=[cdn-staging.50mmretina.com,staging.50mmretina.com] absent;
            271 assets scanned across 2 root(s): dist, functions.
```

## ⚠ Deploy prerequisite — this is not a CI-checkable condition

Removing the defaults means the **production Pages project must already define `SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`**. Its variables were last observed as `ISOLATION_FORBIDDEN_REFS`, `NODE_VERSION`, `VITE_SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID`, `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` — neither of the two new ones. No gate in this PR can catch that gap: every check above passes and SSR would throw on the first request after deploy. Confirm the variables exist in both lanes' Pages projects before this reaches production.

## One defect in the patch as supplied, applied verbatim and flagged rather than edited

`src/__tests__/seoLaneRequired.test.ts` contains two assertions written as:

```ts
expect(v).not.toContain("[www.50mmretina.com](https://www.50mmretina.com)");
```

That is a markdown autolink artifact of `"www.50mmretina.com"`. The string it now searches for can never appear, so both assertions are vacuous — they pass without testing anything. They are not *wrong*, just inert, and the surrounding assertions (`jtdtehuqtinjxropkkcn`, the `eyJhbGciOi` JWT regex) still do real work, so the file's guarantee is weakened rather than broken. Left exactly as supplied because the instruction was to apply the patch without editing a character; a one-line follow-up restoring the bare hostname would close it.

body:
O configurador estava verdadeiro e ilegível ao mesmo tempo. Mesmo no nível
essencial, a primeira coisa no ecrã eram vinte e duas competências numa
grelha plana, cada uma com título e descrição — quarenta e quatro linhas
de texto antes da primeira decisão. Os catorze meios e as quinze recusas
repetiam o padrão: cinquenta e um cartões seguidos.

A profundidade não muda; a arrumação muda.

· CATEGORIAS. Competências pela família que já existe no grafo (organizar
  e operar, trabalho manual, técnica e digital, comercial, gestão,
  criativa, cuidar e ensinar); meios e recusas por grupos novos declarados
  em `perguntas.ts`. O agrupamento é DADO, não desenho — assim o
  componente não ganha uma segunda taxonomia que diverge em silêncio.

· PASTILHAS. A escolha passa a um alvo de uma linha. As descrições não
  desaparecem: ficam no interruptor «Mostrar descrições», que vale para as
  três secções.

· SECÇÕES DOBRÁVEIS. Cada secção fecha e, fechada, resume o que já lá está
  («até 5 000 € · 2 meios»). Há um «fechar todas as secções»: 3 817 px de
  formulário passam a 1 417 px a 390 px de largura. Abertas por omissão —
  nada fica escondido de quem chega pela primeira vez.

· «O que mais mudaria o resultado» deixou de ser aviso e passou a atalho:
  cada linha abre a secção certa e sobe sozinha o nível de configuração
  onde essa pergunta vive.

Também: procura de competências que ignora acentos; o nível de cada
competência saiu de dentro das pastilhas para uma lista à parte, só com as
escolhidas; controlo segmentado para os três níveis, com rótulos que cabem
a 360 px.

Verificado: build limpo, 3 263 testes, 0 vulnerabilidades high,
`descobrir:e2e` nas quatro combinações, e axe sem violações no
configurador em quatro estados × dois temas × 360/1280 — incluindo o modo
escuro com a classe `.dark` mesmo aplicada, que o `colorScheme` do
Playwright sozinho não liga nesta app.

## Why

Thirteen ledger rows were blocks whose keys the script supplies (`<resource> = value_field`, `value_set[country_flag] = bool`, `<ship_categories> = scope[country]`, `$localisation_parameter = scalar`, `int = <trait.leader_trait>`), plus `create_species.pop_ethics`, a scalar arm beside an anonymous value list. The field model only knew literal keys.

## What

- `partitionBlock` splits a block into named groups and one open key filter; `openMapValue` lowers the open part to a `MapValue` (key label, key reference targets, value, comparison flag, cardinality). Computed keys of type `<typeRef>`, `value_set[...]`, `scalar`, `int`, `float` qualify; anything else — including a computed key holding a block, which keeps `switch` on SDK-249 — stays `computed-field-key`.
- A map-only block IS the argument: `setTradeConversions(values: { readonly [resource: string]: ScriptValue })`, `setCountryCodeFlags({ readonly [countryFlag: string]: boolean })`, `addAttunement`, `setAgreementTerms` (five key families merged, value union). A mixed block gets one member at the first computed key's position, named after the key type — `addResourceFromDebris({ resources?: {...}; system?; mult? })` — or `entries` for `scalar`/`int`/`float` keys (`createLeader.traits.entries` beside `trait`; vanilla writes 197 numeric-key and 116 `trait =` entries).
- Map keys stay `string` (a branded ref cannot key an object); key reference targets are kept in the meta and recorded as `ContentRefUse` per key; `cardinality.min` is enforced at runtime (`setCountryCodeFlags({})` throws, `setTradeConversions({})` writes the empty block vanilla uses). Entry order is the authored object order.
- `scalarOrFields` → `scalarOrBlock` over `BlockValue = fields | map | valueList`: `checkEconomicProductionModifierForJob.resource` accepts a ref or a comparison map; `createSpecies.popEthics` accepts `"no" | "random" | EthicRef | string` or a 1..4 tuple union (SDK-281). The nested scalar arm now records its content ref like every other ref-bearing scalar.
- `referenceTargetsOf` is extracted from `unionFor` as the one pure authority for "every form is a typed reference"; nested entry arrays are named by their sink (`entriesNested0Nested0`), which also fixed a latent self-push at two block levels (test included).

Newly emitting: `addAttunement`, `addResourceFromDebris`, `addResourceToLocalStockpile`, `cloneLeader`, `createLeader`, `createSavedLeader`, `customTooltipWithParams`, `releaseVivariumFaunaCount`, `setAgreementTerms`, `setCountryCodeFlags`, `setTradeConversions`, `createSpecies`, trigger `checkEconomicProductionModifierForJob`. Ledger 17 → 4 (the parallel #213 removes two more; SDK-249 the last two).

## Verification

`npm run codegen`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (3281 tests), `npm run build`, `npm run codegen:check`, `npm run example` — all pass. Goldens from vanilla: `add_resource_from_debris = { minerals = 1000 system = ... }`, `set_trade_conversions = { trade = 0.5 energy = 0.5 }` and the empty block, `set_country_code_flags = { colonizer = yes }`, `release_vivarium_fauna_count.owners`, the `"MIN" = ...` parameters block, `create_species` both arms.

Closes SDK-250. Closes SDK-281.

body:
## Why
Game `revision` cannot be the cursor for future Room subscriptions because comments, Controller transitions, Join/connection state, Room phase, and semantic presence can change without a game move. Reusing streams only by Room ID would also risk crossing private projections.

## Changes
- add persisted, backward-compatible `roomSeq` to GameRoom and every Human/Agent snapshot
- normalize legacy Rooms to `roomSeq = 1`
- centralize all post-initialization state writes through one commit path
- increment and broadcast only when the semantic Room signature changes
- advance for game revision/status, comments, Controller/binding/temp-Bot changes, Room phase, Join claim, and semantic Actor-status transitions
- do not advance for heartbeat-only `lastSeenAt` refreshes or credential-only viewer recovery
- normalize collection order before comparison
- add pure sequence tests plus a source contract proving all writes/broadcasts remain centralized
- document that future subscriptions are keyed by origin + Room + authorized principal/credential scope + projection type/version

## Scope
This PR establishes the event cursor and commit invariant only. It does not enable the currently disabled Human browser WebSocket route, add `wait_for_room_update`, or implement local-bridge connection pooling yet.

## Release state
This remains part of the unpublished `0.1.0-alpha.9` source candidate. npm `@alpha` remains `0.1.0-alpha.8`.
