author: bradgroux
body:
## Summary

`buzz channels add-member --pubkey <own-pubkey>` fails with relay error 400: "invalid: missing p tag" because the SDK builder does not call `.allow_self_tagging()`.

When a user adds or removes themselves as a channel member, nostr 0.44's `EventBuilder::sign_with_keys` silently strips the `p` tag matching the signer's pubkey. The relay's `validate_admin_event` then calls `extract_p_tag`, which returns `None`, and the event is rejected.

This is the same class of bug as #4906 (PR #4975), which fixed `build_message`, `build_forum_post`, and `build_forum_comment`. The e2e test `add_member_ws` already uses `.allow_self_tagging()` with a comment explaining the behavior — the SDK builders used by the CLI did not.

Added `.allow_self_tagging()` to `build_add_member` (kind 9000) and `build_remove_member` (kind 9001).

Per review feedback from @Chessing234, also added `.allow_self_tagging()` to the DM builders with the same shape:

- `build_dm_add_member` (kind 41011) — the relay's `handle_dm_add_member` rejects events with no `p` tags, so a self-add would fail identically to the channel add-member bug.
- `build_dm_open` (kind 41010) — the self `p` tag is redundant (the relay adds the signer automatically), but `.allow_self_tagging()` makes the signed event match the caller's intent and is consistent with the other builders.
- The CLI's manual DM open builder in `buzz-cli/src/commands/dms.rs` (which adds a `d` tag the SDK builder doesn't accept).
- The desktop's `build_dm_open` in `desktop/src-tauri/src/events.rs`.

### Related issue

Closes #6568

### Testing

Five new unit tests in `buzz-sdk`:

- `add_member_self_target_preserves_p_tag` — signs a kind 9000 event where the target pubkey equals the signer; asserts the `p` tag survives signing.
- `add_member_self_target_with_role_preserves_p_tag` — same, with a `role` admin tag; asserts both tags survive.
- `remove_member_self_target_preserves_p_tag` — signs a kind 9001 self-removal; asserts the `p` tag survives.
- `dm_open_self_target_preserves_p_tag` — signs a kind 41010 event where the only pubkey is the signer; asserts the `p` tag survives signing.
- `dm_add_member_self_target_preserves_p_tag` — signs a kind 41011 self-add; asserts both `h` and `p` tags survive.

The existing tests for all four builders (which use a non-self target) continue to pass unchanged, confirming the fix does not affect the normal path.

Verification: `cargo test -p buzz-sdk --lib` (267 pass), `cargo clippy -p buzz-sdk --lib` (clean), `cargo check -p buzz-cli` (clean).

author: nidhisharora
body:
🎯 Build a Dynamic Mentorship Matchmaking Algorithm

📋 Summary

This PR introduces a recommendation-based mentorship matchmaking system that analyzes student and alumni profiles to identify the most relevant mentorship opportunities.

The system calculates a weighted match score for available alumni and presents the student's top three recommendations directly in the Mentorship portal.

🎯 Problem

With hundreds of alumni available for mentorship, manually browsing profiles makes it difficult for students to identify the most relevant mentors.

This can result in:

  • Information overload

  • Poor mentor discovery

  • Time-consuming profile comparison

  • Lower mentorship engagement

  • Students overlooking highly relevant mentors

✨ Changes

  • Added a weighted mentorship matching algorithm.

  • Added matching based on academic major.

  • Added matching based on previous club memberships.

  • Added matching between the student's desired industry and the alumni's current industry.

  • Implemented a normalized match score from 0–100%.

  • Added ranking of eligible alumni based on match score.

  • Added Top 3 personalized mentor recommendations.

  • Added match explanations describing why an alumnus was recommended.

  • Added handling for incomplete profile information.

  • Added deterministic ranking for mentors with equal scores.

⚖️ Matching Logic

The recommendation score considers:

Matching Factor | Weight -- | -- Desired Industry ↔ Current Industry | Very High Same Major | High Shared Club Memberships | Medium

The final score is normalized to a percentage between 0% and 100%.

🔄 Recommendation Flow

Student Profile
      ↓
Extract Matching Preferences
      ↓
Fetch Available Alumni
      ↓
Compare Major
      ↓
Compare Club Memberships
      ↓
Compare Industry
      ↓
Calculate Weighted Match Score
      ↓
Rank Alumni
      ↓
Select Top 3
      ↓
Display Recommendations

🖥️ Mentorship Portal

A new Top Recommendations for You section displays the highest-ranked mentors.

Each recommendation includes:

  • Mentor profile

  • Match percentage

  • Relevant shared attributes

  • Current industry

  • Matching explanation

Example:

95% Match

Jane Doe

Also participated in the Tech Club
Works in your desired industry
Same academic major

🧪 Testing

Added tests covering:

  • Exact major matches.

  • Industry matches.

  • Shared club memberships.

  • Multiple matching factors.

  • No matching attributes.

  • Partial profile information.

  • Match-score boundaries.

  • Correct score normalization.

  • Alumni ranking.

  • Top 3 recommendation selection.

  • Equal-score tie handling.

  • Empty alumni datasets.

  • Incomplete student preferences.

⚡ Performance Considerations

The matching process is designed to efficiently evaluate available alumni without unnecessary repeated profile lookups.

Only the highest-ranked recommendations need to be returned to the frontend after scoring.

🔍 Compatibility

The matchmaking system extends the existing Mentorship portal without changing existing alumni profiles or mentorship request workflows.

✅ Expected Result

Students should receive three personalized mentor recommendations based on their academic background, previous club involvement, and career interests, helping them discover relevant mentors without manually browsing hundreds of profiles.

🔗 Related Issue

Closes #4149

author: stephen-mcelhose
body:
Follow-up to PR #35 (Initiation Package template packs). Captures four findings from that work and applies them to the shared process doc and all 5 package agent prompts so future milestones (Planning, Execution, Monitoring & Control, Closure) benefit:

1. **Stale worktree risk** — the worktree used for #9-#12 predated a commit adding the very prompt file it needed. Added a Step 0 / "Environment setup" step: `git fetch && git rebase origin/main`, plus `make install` if `.venv` is missing.
2. **"Parallel" was underspecified** — research (fetching PRINCE2 URLs, reading `document.ttl`) has no shared state and parallelizes cleanly, but ontology gap-checking does not: documents in the same package often need the same or overlapping properties (e.g. multiple docs touching `pm:Project`), so concurrent edits to `ontology/modules/*.ttl` risk duplicate/conflicting properties. Reworded "Your job" sections to call out: parallelize Step 1, consolidate Step 2, parallelize Steps 3-4 again once ontology is validated.
3. **Silent fetch-tool failures** — `web-fetch` returned empty content for some `prince2.wiki` pages with no error. Documented the `curl -s <url>` + tag-stripping fallback.
4. **Dependency chains must be verified, not inferred** — caught a case where a document's real `:hasHardDependency` in `document.ttl` differed from what the issue table's ordering would suggest. Added an explicit constraint to check `entry.yaml` dependencies against `document.ttl` triples.

No functional/ontology changes — docs only.

body:
## Liminal Engine — Batch 2: geometry warps + time-loops

Eight new effects and two new vibe presets, all loop-safe (every animated quantity is a pure function of `phase01` with integer cycles, so exported GIFs wrap seamlessly).

### 🔩 Geometry warps
- **Shear** — sine row-pair slide, breathing in/out across the loop
- **Astigmatism** — directional multi-tap blur at any angle
- **Contours** — crawling elevation lines on luminance boundaries (topo-map ink)
- **Gravity wells** — seeded sinkholes that pinch/pull pixels; wells orbit closed paths so the loop wraps

### 🕰 Time & weather

author: pseudoseed
body:
Main has been red since #49 merged. One failing test, and it's mine.

## What broke

#44 replaced the instruction

```
Read the full consultation prompt from this file: <path>
```

with an actual `-f` attachment, because opencode auto-rejects reads outside its working directory and the consult sandbox is an `mkdtemp` dir under the OS temp root. The lane was receiving an instruction pointing at a path it could not open, holding **no prompt at all**, and still producing a verdict.

`src/commands/consult/__tests__/opencode-lane.test.ts` asserts that old string.

## Why I missed it

I verified against `src/__tests__/consult.test.ts` and `src/commands/porch`. The stale test is in `src/commands/consult/__tests__/`. Two directories with similar names; I checked the wrong one and never ran the suite that covers the exact function I changed.

## The fix

The test now pins the behaviour that replaced it: the prompt is **attached** rather than described, `-f` carries a `.md` path, and `--` sits immediately before the positional so yargs' `[array]` flag can't swallow it.

Full package suite this time rather than a subset: **5751 passed, 48 skipped, 0 failures.**

Related: #27 is about `test.yml`'s worker-crash guard never firing. Not this failure — this one is a genuine assertion mismatch — but it is why a red run here is harder to read than it should be.

author: bravocompanion
body:
## v0.68 Major Survivor Progression

Large progression update built on top of v0.67 weight inventory without turning the horror game into a damage-scaling RPG.

### Leveling
- Levels 1–30
- deterministic curved XP requirement
- +1 Talent Point per level gained
- +1 Stat Point every even level
- anti-grind event claims
- no repeat XP from normal resource farming or threat kills

### XP sources
- map discovery
- evidence collection
- Forest clue synthesis
- first craft per recipe
- generator start/repair
- night survival
- first Tenant/Darkness observation
- co-op revives

### Stats
- Endurance
- Fitness
- Fortitude
- Focus
- Dexterity

Effects are deliberately conservative: stamina/carry tolerance, small movement efficiency, metabolism, flashlight-panic handling, and vulnerable action time. No large HP/damage growth.

### Talent Trees
20 authored talent nodes across:
- Survival
- Scout
- Technician
- Investigator

Includes rank caps, level gates and prerequisites. Talents improve efficiency/information; no threat immunity, permanent radar, unlimited sprint or free permanent generator power.

### Knowledge
20 authored entries across Survival / Technology / Wildlife / World / Threat / Anomaly. Evidence, exploration, threat observation, crafting and survival unlock knowledge. Investigator talents reveal deeper analysis without changing threat protection rules.

### Weight integration
- v0.67 base remains 32 kg
- Endurance adds +0.10 kg/point
- Load Bearing adds +1 kg/rank
- Pack Discipline shifts LOADED from 70% to 75%
- HEAVY/OVERWEIGHT contracts retained
- stack/type caps remain disabled

### Multiplayer
- progression is personal per survivor, not party-shared
- host-authored evidence/revive events award the correct remote peer over reliable RPC 68
- each survivor has a local progression profile so multiplayer clients retain progression without owning the host world save

### Persistence
- normal host world save includes progression_v68
- separate local survivor profile: `user://dont_look_back_progression_v68.json`
- checkpoint death/team wipe does not roll survivor progression backward
- old saves without progression data remain supported
- deleting the save also resets/deletes progression profile

### UI
- desktop: P opens Survivor Progression; ESC closes
- K remains Save, L remains Load
- mobile: responsive PROG button
- tabs: Overview / Stats / Talents / Knowledge
- mutually exclusive with Inventory / Crafting / Stash / Field Status / Journal

### CI
Adds dedicated `Progression Regression v0.68` gate covering level cap, point economy, stat/talent effects, prerequisites, evidence anti-grind, knowledge persistence, carry integration, profile/save semantics and horror guardrails. Existing canonical, weight, Web and native export CI remain required.

### Assets
Mandatory new runtime assets: **NONE**.
P1 polish: 5 stat icons, 4 tree icons, 6 knowledge-category icons, XP badge/frame, rank pips, restrained level/talent/knowledge SFX, subtle UI unlock pulse, optional co-op build badges.

author: traali
body:
## Description

**One branch off `main`** with the full companion + underway work. Merge this instead of stacking #9 then #10.

Adds a **React + Leaflet skipper cockpit** at `apps/web-pwa` (does **not** replace Flutter `web/`) and stops weather refetching on every GPS tick while underway.

This is the app that loaded on **iPhone 11 or 12 + Chrome on Friday 21 Aug 2026**. Chrome on iOS is WebKit (`CriOS`), not Chromium.

Supersedes [#9](https://github.com/traali/navikka/pull/9) and [#10](https://github.com/traali/navikka/pull/10) (same two commits: `d64cff9` + `440b11b`).

## Type of Change
- [x] 🚀 `feat`: New feature
- [x] 🐛 `fix`: Bug fix (iPhone Chrome + weather-always-fetching)
- [x] ⚡ `perf`: Performance improvement
- [ ] 🔧 `refactor`: Code restructuring
- [x] 📚 `docs`: Documentation
- [x] 🧪 `test`: Test changes
- [ ] 🔨 `chore`: Maintenance

## What and why

### Why a companion instead of replacing Flutter web

`web/` is the Flutter PWA (Cloudflare Pages, `flutter build web`). Putting a Vite tree there would break CI and the production deploy. The companion lives in `apps/web-pwa` so Flutter `lib/`, `web/`, and `pubspec.yaml` stay untouched.

### Why iPhone Chrome needed extra work

Friday's field test: **the app loaded** on iPhone 11 or 12 + Chrome. That is the floor, not the ceiling.

| Fact | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Chrome on iOS = WebKit (`CriOS`) | Blink-only APIs (Clipboard, Wake Lock, `randomUUID`) are flaky or missing |
| iPhone 11 = 375×812 @2x | 4-column HUD that fits 390 can clip at 375 |
| iPhone 12 = 390×844 @3x | Matches this session's 390×844 viewport |
| iOS zooms inputs < 16px | Search field is 16px |
| Notch + home indicator | `viewport-fit=cover` + `env(safe-area-inset-*)` + `100dvh` / `-webkit-fill-available` |
| Clipboard often blocked | SOS falls back to `execCommand`, then `navigator.share` |
| Wake Lock is flaky | Request on navigate, retry on `visibilitychange` |

### Why weather fetched all the time while boating

MET Norway URLs used `toFixed(4)` (~11 m). A 6 kn boat moves that far in a few seconds, so every poll was a new, uncacheable request. Weather + ocean + national AIS also shared one 120 s timer.

| Signal | Fresh | Gate | Hidden tab |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weather (MET locationforecast + ocean) | 10 min | `0.05°` cell (~5.5 km) | skip |
| AIS (Digitraffic) | 60 s follow/nav, 180 s idle | 0.4° around own ship | skip |
| GPS apply | 500 ms **or** 15 m | high accuracy | n/a |
| Map follow pan | 12 m | no animation if SOG > 2 kn | n/a |

16 s of demo motion at ~6 kn: **1 weather fetch, 1 AIS fetch**, then both skipped. HUD keeps last good weather and shows age (`juuri` / `N min sitten`) instead of a perpetual spinner.

Skill for the next agent: `.agent/skills/navikka-underway/`.

### What the cockpit does

- SOG / COG / UKC / wind HUD over a Leaflet chart (Helsinki start)
- Device GPS when allowed, otherwise a demo track
- Harbors, fairways, speed-limit boxes (Kauppatori 5 km/h no-wake, Lauttasaari 15 km/h)
- Fishing zones + catch log with statutory minima (kuha 42 cm, taimen/lohi 60 cm)
- MET Norway weather + COLREG 19/35 fog status
- AIS (Digitraffic when CORS allows, else seeded Helsinki traffic + CPA)
- Route tap-to-add, MAYDAY readout, 112 and MRCC Turku
- FI/EN, five bridge themes including Red Watch, rough-sea 56px targets

Disclaimer stays: this is **not** an official Traficom chart.

## Changes Made
- Add `apps/web-pwa` React + Leaflet cockpit (standalone Vite app)
- iPhone 11/12 Chrome CSS: `100dvh`, `-webkit-fill-available`, safe-area, 16px inputs, 44px targets, 375px HUD media query
- iOS JS fallbacks: clipboard, Share Sheet, `newId` without `crypto.randomUUID`, Wake Lock retry
- Snap MET query to 2 decimal degrees; TTL 10 min; keep last good weather on error
- Decouple AIS (60/180 s) from weather; bbox around own ship
- GPS apply-throttle; pause demo tick + polls when the tab is hidden
- Leaflet subscribe only on pos/cog/layers/ais/waypoints; pan throttle
- HUD + weather panel show freshness
- 61 `node:test` cases (geo, catalog, rules, store, iPhone contracts, fetch policy)
- Path-filtered CI: `.github/workflows/web-pwa.yml`
- Underway skipper skill: `.agent/skills/navikka-underway/`
- CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` + README pointer
- **Does not** modify Flutter `web/`, `lib/`, or `pubspec.yaml`

## Testing
- [x] Companion unit tests pass (`cd apps/web-pwa && npm test` → **61/61**)
- [ ] All tests pass (`flutter test`) — not run here; no Dart files changed
- [ ] Zero analyze issues (`flutter analyze`) — no Dart files changed
- [ ] Code generation up-to-date (`build_runner build`) — N/A
- [x] Tested manually on: **iPhone 11 or 12 + Chrome (Friday 21 Aug 2026, user field test — app loaded)**
- [x] Playwright re-check with CriOS UA:

| Viewport | Overflow | Console errors | Tiles | Input font | SOS 112 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 11 375×812 @2x | no | none | 36 | 16px | yes |
| iPhone 12 390×844 @3x | no | none | 36 | 16px | yes |

- [x] Playwright underway watch (iPhone 12 / CriOS UA, 16 s of demo SOG ~6 kn):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Weather fetches | **1** then skipped |
| AIS fetches | **1** then skipped |
| Perpetual "Haetaan merisäätä…" | **no** — chip shows "juuri" |
| Overflow | none |
| Console errors | none |
| Live MET | 11.9 m/s / 042°, vis good, 0.6 m seas |

## Commits on this branch (from `main`)

1. `d64cff9` feat(web-pwa): add React companion with iPhone Chrome tests
2. `440b11b` perf(web-pwa): underway fetch policy — stop refetching weather on GPS

## Screenshots/Recordings

Cockpit HUD, weather, menu, SOS were captured on both iPhone 11 and 12 viewports during Playwright QA. Live preview of the same cockpit is the in-chat app.

- [x] Single branch off `main` — no stacked merge required

author: aglinxinyuan
body:
### What changes were proposed in this PR?

**Why it was never populated.** `DatasetSearchQueryBuilder` joins the owner row and then never projects a column from it. `constructFromClause` writes the join, but the select list comes entirely from `mappedResourceSchema`, and `UnifiedResourceSchema.apply` defaults `userEmail` to `DSL.inline("")` (`UnifiedResourceSchema:74`) — a slot the dataset schema never named. So `toEntryImpl` reads `owner.getEmail` out of a record that has no owner in it.

Two steps turn the missing projection into a `null`:

```
schema slot  userEmail = DSL.inline("")        <- default, never overridden
                 |
SQL          '' as email                       <- USER is joined, never read
                 |
translateRecord  dedupes by ORIGINAL field, and jOOQ compares fields by
                 rendered SQL, so projectsOfWorkflow / userName / userEmail /
                 projectColor -- all DSL.inline("") -- collapse to ONE entry
                 keyed on the first of them
                 |
record       no `email` column at all  ->  record.into(USER) = empty User
                 |
entry        DashboardDataset.ownerEmail = null      (not "")
```

**Change.** Name the slot. One line in the schema; `toEntryImpl` is untouched.

```scala
ownerId = DATASET.OWNER_UID,
userEmail = USER.EMAIL,
did = DATASET.DID,
```

Before → after, on the rendered projection and the entry:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| projection | `'' as email` | `texera_db.user.email as email` |
| `DashboardDataset.ownerEmail` | `null`, every row | the dataset owner's address |
| `leftJoin(USER)` | joined, selected from, never read | read |

`WorkflowSearchQueryBuilder` is the sibling that shows the step that was missed: it opts into the USER column it reads (`userName = USER.NAME`, plus `USER.NAME` in `getGroupByFields`), and it already filters on `USER.EMAIL` for the `owners` query param — the email was reachable through the join all along, only the projection was absent. `HubResource:316` and file-service's `/dataset/list` both populate the same field correctly; dataset search was the one producer that did not.

Scope of the impact, stated precisely because it is narrower than it looks: `DashboardEntry.ownerEmail` (`dashboard-entry.ts:132`) receives the null, and no frontend code reads that field for datasets today, so no screen was visibly wrong. It was a trap rather than a broken page — `dataset-selection-modal.component.ts:127` builds the storage logical path `/${ResourceType.Dataset}/${ownerEmail}/${name}/${version}` out of a `DashboardDataset`, and only escapes `/dataset/null/...` because it lists via file-service.

### Any related issues, documentation, discussions?

Closes #7874

### How was this PR tested?

`DatasetSearchQueryBuilderSpec` goes from 18 tests to 21, reusing the fixture and lakeFS loopback stub #7855 built.

| test | what it pins |
|---|---|
| `carry the owner's email address` | the value on the entry — the assertion that kills the mutant below |
| `take the email from the dataset's owner, not from the caller` | fetched as `otherUid`, who reaches the dataset only because it is public, so a lookup that echoed the signed-in caller back would fail |
| `project every dataset column under the alias its schema slot names` (extended) | `user.email as email` in the SELECT, so a slot dropped back to a literal fails at the projection instead of as a null three layers down |
| `stay union-compatible with the workflow and project branches` | new — see below |

The mutation #7855 recorded as surviving now dies. Replacing `record.into(USER).into(classOf[User])` with a fresh `User`:

| | before this PR | after |
|---|---|---|
| `new User` mutant | survives the whole suite (equivalent mutant, given the defect) | `succeeded 19, failed 2` — both owner-email tests |

Verified in order, one sbt JVM each:

| run | result |
|---|---|
| new tests against the builder as it stands on main | `succeeded 18, failed 3, canceled 0` — projection missing `user.email`, plus `null was not equal to "dataset_search_owner@mail.com"` twice |
| with the change | `succeeded 21, failed 0, canceled 0` |
| change + `new User` mutant | `succeeded 19, failed 2, canceled 0` |
| the 7 dashboard suites together | `Suites: completed 7, Tests: succeeded 108, failed 0, canceled 0` |
| `scalafmtCheckAll` + `Test/scalafixAll --check` | clean |

```bash
sbt "WorkflowExecutionService/testOnly org.apache.texera.web.resource.dashboard.DatasetSearchQueryBuilderSpec"
```

Two notes for a reviewer:

**The union test earns its place.** This change swaps a column in one branch of the three-way `unionAll` that `DashboardResource.searchAllResources` builds for the dashboard's default view, from an untyped `''` literal to `varchar`. Nothing in the repo executed that union, so a type incompatibility would have shipped as a runtime failure on the default view with nothing failing to compile. The new test executes it.

**`canceled` is the failure mode to watch, and it moved.** The stub binds the configured port (`localhost:8000`) rather than an ephemeral one, because `LakeFSStorageClient.apiClient` is a `lazy val` capturing `StorageConfig.lakefsEndpoint` once per JVM and amber runs every suite in one unforked JVM. If something else holds that port — a local `bin/local-dev.sh up` — the stub-dependent tests cancel, and that count goes from 4 to 6 with the owner-email pair added. A cancel is quiet: sbt prints `All tests passed` at exit 0. Measured here, with the port held and `size` mutated to `0L`, the run reports `succeeded 15, failed 0, canceled 6` and still exits green — so the owner-email pair is disarmed alongside the rest of the `toEntry` half. The class comment carries these numbers and I updated them. CI has no lakeFS in this job, so it is deterministic there.

### Was this PR authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?

author: sabas0ba
body:
## 概要

Tang Nano 9K 内蔵 PSRAM（HyperBus，W955D8MBYA 相当）のコントローラを実装し，実機で memtest PASS を達成した。PR #4（IR0 読み出し spike まで）の続きで，物理層からバス IF までを通した v1 一式を含む。

実機結果（CK 13.5 MHz）:

```
PSRAM INIT=1 MEMTEST=PASS ERR=0000 K=00000 RD=00000000
```

## 主な変更

| 領域 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 物理層 | `PsramPhy`（ODDR/IDDR 版）に加え，IOLOGIC を使わない `PsramPhySdr` を追加．IOBUF ＋ファブリック FF のみで 1 CK = 4 位相を生成し，DQ/RWDS を 90° オフセットで駆動する |
| コントローラ | `PsramCtrl`（RESET#/tVCS→CR0→R/W の FSM）．位相イネーブル `i_en` により 1/4 レートで駆動する |
| バス IF | `PsramAxiBridge`（std::axi4_lite_if）と自作 `CdcHandshake` による 27↔54 MHz のクロック交差 |
| 自己診断 | `PsramMemtest`（UART 出力，初回不一致の K/RD 診断付き） |
| 検証 | 合成後ネットリスト検査 `verif/psram_phy/`（yosys/nextpnr 実行後に接続・配置・クロックを検査）と CI への verif ジョブ追加 |
| ツール | コンテナ実行ラッパ `scripts/fpga-run.ps1` ほか |

クロック構成は rPLL 54 MHz（`clk_mem`）で PSRAM サブシステムを駆動し，CK は 13.5 MHz。AXI 側は 27 MHz で，ブリッジの CDC は実機で検証済み。

## 設計上の判断: DDR phy ではなく SDR phy を採用

当初は ODDR/IDDR による DDR 駆動を実装したが実機で動作せず，原因を切り分けた結果，apicula（nextpnr-himbaechel/apycula）の ODDR ではデータ／OE 経路がファブリック基準で約 2.5 サイクル遅延し（文書仕様は 1 サイクル），CK 経路が先行することを確認した。この先行により RAM が CA 窓を先取りし，先頭バイトが High-Z（FF = CA47:46:45=111）となって全アクセスがレジスタ空間リード化していた（ERR=0400，偶然の INIT=1，RD=005F005F をすべて説明する）。

遅延補償版 DDR phy も試作したが，ループバックでの整列までは達成したものの実 RAM が無応答のままのため**保留**とし，v1 では IOLOGIC 非依存の SDR phy を採用した。調査記録と再開手順は [docs/psram.md](docs/psram.md)「apicula ODDR 実挙動の調査」「遅延補償 DDR phy の試行」節に残してある。`PsramPhy`（DDR 版）は復帰時の起点として残置している。

## 既知の制限・残課題

- 帯域は CK 13.5 MHz 相当。DDR 復帰による倍化は保留（上記）

body: ## What still breaks dev After #12080 got past the container-count check, `gcloud` itself crashes: ``` ERROR: gcloud crashed (ValueError): Invalid secret path 'projects/based-hardware-dev/secrets/cloud-run-gmp-config' in annotation ``` `_merge_secret_annotation` wrote the config secret into `run.googleapis.com/secrets` using the project **ID**. gcloud parses that annotation with a regex whose project segment is numeric (`googlecloudsdk/command_lib/run/secrets_mapping.py`): ```python _PROJECT_NUMBER_PARTIAL = r'(?P[0-9]{1,19})' _REMOTE_SECRET_FLAG_VALUE = r'^projects/' + _PROJECT_NUMBER_PARTIAL + r'/secrets/' + _SECRET_NAME_PARTIAL + _REMOTE_SECRET_VERSION + r'$' ``` `based-hardware-dev` is not numeric, so the path is rejected. The fix resolves the project number and writes that. ## Why this was expensive to find Cloud Run accepts the attach with either form. The annotation is only re-parsed by the **next** `gcloud run deploy` against that service. So the deploy that introduces the bad annotation succeeds, and a later deploy — touching nothing related — crashes inside a vendored tool. Nothing in the failing run points at #11998. That is the shape of the new failure class this declares: `FC-metadata-format-validated-only-on-next-read`. The guard artifact is a test that asserts the annotation against gcloud's *actual* regex copied verbatim, so a vendor upgrade that tightens the rule fails locally instead of on the next deploy. ## Production Production has no sidecar attached, so it has never written this annotation and does not carry the defect today. On its current code it would have written the bad form on its first deploy and crashed on its second — the same delayed trap as #12080, one layer down. ## Note on the live dev service The dev `backend` service still carries the bad annotation from the earlier attach. This PR stops it being rewritten, but the existing value needs a one-time repair before dev deploys succeed; that is an operational fix, not a code one. ## Verification `patch_service` stays pure — `attach_sidecar` resolves the number and passes it in, so no test needs a subprocess, and a numeric project is passed through without calling gcloud at all. All 8 tests in `tests/unit/test_attach_cloud_run_gmp_sidecar.py` pass; the new ones fail against the current script. Failure-Class: new

author: m0rdr3x
youknowone
body:
Two independent workstreams share this branch (it is the shared work branch on a
tree several sessions write to). They touch disjoint files; the commit list
separates them cleanly.

## A. `pyre/check.py` — the startup subtrahend, and the wasm ratio allowances

`3663a4c3591`, `cbc5e40a2b7`, `3ef94baf33b`, `44be0f13e7a`, `748a0f70bd7`
(plus one line of `pyre/bench/synth/str_getitem_len_hot.py`)

### 1. Startup was measured once and subtracted from benches that ran for the next ten minutes

`measure_startups` ran one sampling pass upfront; `_exec_time` subtracted its
median from every bench for the rest of the job. The comment above
`STARTUP_SAMPLES` rests the median-over-minimum choice on *"the estimate has to
come from the same load conditions as the run it is subtracted from"* — and a
single upfront pass cannot meet that. One macos job read every interpreter's
startup at about twice its neighbour's while raw bench times moved by a fifth of
that; the difference lands whole in `exec` and collapsed a 0.074s exec to 0.009s.

- `_sample_startups` / `_adopt_startups` split out, and `maybe_refresh_startups`
  re-samples once the estimate in hand is `STARTUP_REFRESH_S` old.
- Called at the top of `run_bench` / `run_synthetic_bench` — a **fixture**
  boundary, never between one fixture's backends, because the pairing argument
  requires a fixture's numerator and denominator to be reduced by one estimate.
- A target whose empty program exits non-zero on a refresh **keeps its previous
  estimate** and renders `[unsampled]`; the single pass had written `0.0`, which
  is the right no-subtraction default at t=0 and a silent inflation of every
  later `exec` mid-job.
- `measure_startups` now runs **after** `warmup`. It used to sample whatever
  state the cargo build left behind — cold page cache, every core just busy —
  while the benches it is subtracted from run one process at a time.

**`STARTUP_REFRESH_S` is sized from the logs, not guessed.** The phase between
the startup line and the last comparison is 592s on ubuntu, 402s on macos, 661s
on windows — the rest of those 45–70min jobs is cargo. 300s crosses that 1/1/2
times; **120s** crosses it 4/3/5. Each pass now prints its own wall cost so the
next sizing reads a measurement.

### 2. `str_getitem_len_hot` outgrew its allowance, and the ceiling paragraph had two wrong statements

Post-#1425 the fixture reads **2.87x / 2.94x** across two ubuntu runs of one
base, against the `4.8x` its header carried and the `4.0x` global. Its own note
named the condition for removal — the leg crossing out of the trace module once
per iteration — and #1425 is what changed it. Directive deleted.

The paragraph above `WASM_MAX_DYNASM_RATIO` said the constant *"came back to
4.0"* (the sequence is 3 → 4 → 3.5 → 3.8 → 4.0, so that reads as a restoration
of a value it never came back to) and *"No fixture carries an allowance today"*
while three did. Both corrected, and the census that actually bounds the
constant put in their place.

### 3. An allowance the backend has outgrown used to look exactly like one holding a fixture up

`wasm_ratio_allowed` carried `(name, ceiling)` and the summary printed the
ceiling alone. Finding the 4.8x-over-2.9x case above took parsing 434 comparison
rows out of a job log. It now carries the measured ratio — taken from the values
the gate judged, so a median retry is what gets reported — and the summary reads:

```
wasm/dynasm ratio raised above 4x by `# pyre-check: max-wasm-ratio` for:
  builtin_folds_hot 13x (measured 9.2x), math_folds_hot 13x (measured 3.9x)
```

`WASM_RATIO_FIT_HEADROOM = 1.15` — the margin allowances are already fitted with
— gates the "outgrown" call. Without it `math_folds_hot` (3.93x under a 4.0
ceiling) is named as outgrown on the strength of 0.07x, **on a host that is not
the one its 13x was fitted to**: its header records darwin-arm64 at 8.1–11.3x,
which no ubuntu run measures. The line says the reading is this host's and points
at the fixture's own note.

### Measurements this adds to the file

Two ubuntu runs on base `9be6297e7dd` (PRs #1432 and #1382) gate 273 fixtures in
common:

| | |
|---|---|
| worst **without** an allowance | `short_circuit_boxed_int_cross_fn` 3.01x → 3.50x |
| next | `pickle_terminal_raise_resume` 3.43x / 3.42x |
| run-to-run `\|Δ\|/max` over the 273 | median 4.7%, p75 8.8%, **p90 14.9%**, tail 67% |

So under the plus-15% rule the ceiling's floor is **4.03x — 4.0 is the fitted
value, not slack**, and 3.5 is breached rather than merely tight. And the
`wasm_ratio_gate` docstring's claim that 15% was chosen over *"the ~3% ubuntu
shows between runs"* is wrong: 15% is that runner's p90. Both corrected.

**No gate was widened.** The only movement is one dead allowance removed.

### Verification

`ast.parse` clean; unit checks over `_adopt_startups` (adoption, failed-target
hold, timer gating, `--no-startup-subtract` no-op, `_exec_time` tracking the
refresh) and over the outgrown predicate; `check.py --no-build --backend dynasm`
runs of `--no-synthetic` (10/10) and single fixtures, with `STARTUP_REFRESH_S`
forced low to fire a refresh at every boundary.

⚠️ The code inside `if backend == "wasm"` is **not** exercised locally — this box
has no wasm build. CI is the gate for it.

## B. `jit-trace` build prepass and Charon extraction

`9200d5d8d21`, `85ed655effc`, `819e58589e2` — `scripts/llbc_extract.py`,
`pyre/pyre-jit-trace/build{.rs,/prepass.rs}`, `pyre/scripts/extract-llbc.py`,
the `Cargo.toml`s and one CI workflow line.

**These are another session's commits on this shared branch, not mine.** Their
own messages carry the reasoning and measurements (`--hide-marker-traits`:
96.8s → 81.3s user, artefact 781MB → 752MB, with the cross-process determinism
set compared byte-equal). I could not reach the author — a cross-session message
went unanswered — so I am not representing that reasoning here beyond pointing
at it.

Two things I did do, because this PR carries them:

**`ac160492314` — fixed the `prepare Charon/LLBC (macos-latest)` failure they
caused.** `charon toolchain-path` shares its stream with rustup, which announces
an install when the runner does not have the pinned nightly yet; both call sites
read the capture whole, so `charon_host_triple` built a `rustc` path out of the
notice and macos died before `cargo test` and `check.py` could run. Now routed
through `charon_toolchain_path`, which takes the last non-empty line.
`charon_host_triple` is introduced by `9200d5d8d21` and is not on `origin/main`,
so this was a branch-only regression.

**Audited the `prepass` feature split for a consumer that turns defaults off
without naming it** — the failure mode would be a build script silently writing
placeholder JIT tables. Every site is covered:

| turns defaults off | how `prepass` still arrives |
|---|---|
| workspace `pyre-jit-trace` | `pyre-jit`, its only inheritor, forwards `dynasm`/`cranelift`/`prepass` one by one |
| `pyre-wasm` → `pyre-jit` | names `features = ["prepass"]` |
| `pyre-wasm` → `pyre-jit-trace` (does **not** name it) | only reachable via `wasm-host`, which turns on `pyre-jit/prepass`; unification covers it |
| CI `-p pyre-jit-trace --no-default-features` | `,prepass` added by `85ed655effc` |
| `check.py` / `cpython_tests/run.py` backend builds (`-p pyrex --no-default-features`) | `--no-default-features` applies to the selected package only, and `pyrex` keeps `pyre-jit`'s defaults |
| `-p pyre-jit --no-default-features` in the LLBC extraction | the one path that drops `prepass` on purpose — the point of the change |

No other CI step or script builds either crate with `--no-default-features`.

> **Correction.** That table audits the **`prepass`** axis only. The workspace
> entry's `default-features = false` drops *both* of `pyre-jit-trace`'s defaults,
> and the `dynasm` axis had a real gap: a `pyre-jit` naming no backend (wasm32)
> left `pyre-jit-trace` with neither feature, which stopped it compiling. Two CI
> jobs were red on it; fix

author: snissn
body:
## Summary

- publish the last fully reconciled native HNSW graph through reusable contiguous search views
- serve production searches from the immutable published view while the writer mutates the canonical graph
- keep the published-view search decision lock-free through mutation reconciliation and view publication
- bind each response's results and candidate/rebuild diagnostics to the same held view
- publish only after coverage certification, reject a published view behind the current native root, and preserve prior-view-before-ack / new-view-after-ack semantics
- serialize live native-runtime vector mutation admission so every successful public write publishes its own searchable view before acknowledgment, while non-vector and snapshot-bound column-graph writes retain shared admission
- keep publication non-blocking behind retired readers, recycle one completed generation through a bounded atomic spare slot, release additional or larger retired graphs, and refresh persisted status metadata without copying the graph

## Why

H-B R7 isolated the mixed-workload failure to search blocking behind serialized native HNSW mutation: 500/s p99 reached 283.14 ms and 1,000/s exceeded the frozen backlog gate while CPU, EBS, memory, network, and client capacity were not saturated. This removes that lock coupling without an asynchronous scheduler or a second index implementation.

## Validation

Exact PR head `c74933f71ce1fcf5c9fbfabd26ed44fd6d77cec4`:

- focused publication-order, DB-wide cross-manager admission, collection-scoped cross-manager baseline, stale-manager rejection, stale-validation published-view recovery, buffered publication, no-op publication, column-graph shared-admission, and non-vector-combiner tests: 20 consecutive passes
- the same focused concurrency set under the race detector: 20 consecutive passes
- `TestSearchVectorIndexWithBufferNativeRuntimeSteadyStateAllocations`: pass at zero steady-state allocations
- oversized retired-view shrink/reuse regression: 50 consecutive passes and 20 race-detector passes
- direct idempotent insert / absent tombstone no-publication regression: 50 consecutive passes and 20 race-detector passes
- unchanged full/delta persistence no-publication regression: 50 consecutive passes and 20 race-detector passes
- persisted-status atomic refresh and writer-drain regression: 50 consecutive passes and 20 race-detector passes
- prepared async-flush admission, synchronous forced-drain invalidation, and stale-manager full-rebuild regressions: 20 consecutive passes and 20 race-detector passes
- delayed and stale snapshot waits for announced async publication: 20 consecutive passes and 20 race-detector passes
- next public vector mutation waits for announced async publication without blocking the publisher: 20 consecutive passes and 20 race-detector passes
- vector-index create/drop waits before taking exclusive admission so an announced async publisher can complete: 20 consecutive passes and 20 race-detector passes
- synchronous cross-manager flush and read-triggered/no-index buffered publication wait behind admitted vector work, preserve the publishing manager's certified graph, and invalidate stale peer coverage
- snapshot persistence acquires publication admission before coverage and mutation locks, matching the async publication lock order
- current-main chunk-lifecycle coordination is integrated without replacing either coordinator field
- non-vector indexed async-backpressure behavior remains outside the vector wait gate: 20 consecutive passes
- the broader native-vector coverage and finalizer lock-order set: 5 consecutive passes
- `go test ./TreeDB/collections -count=1`: pass (`293.214s`; wall `295.23s`, max RSS `951,056 KB`)
- `go test ./TreeDB/documentservice -count=1`: pass (`14.840s`; wall `25.45s`, max RSS `1,423,852 KB`)
- `git diff --check`: pass

Frozen production H-B R8 was captured before the correctness-only review follow-up, from measured commit `bc90885066d0e5c0ac84031c2de58ed3912a807e` and binary SHA-256 `62496b...`, on a c6i.8xlarge server and separate c6i.4xlarge client. The workload was Small Cohere 100K/768D FP32 native runtime, M16, efConstruction 128, efSearch 64, topK 100, command-WAL durable:

- R7 mixed search: 603.30 QPS at 283.14 ms p99
- R8 candidate mixed search: 5,153.55 QPS at 1.710 ms p99
- R8 candidate baseline search: 9,616.69 QPS at 1.379 ms p99
- R8 candidate mixed insertion: 265.16 s versus 200 s ideal, about 377.1 vectors/s
- recall, p99, visibility, route, and zero-search-error checks pass
- insert-rate and mixed-QPS floors remain below the frozen H-B gate

The EC2 profiles put the next limiter in HNSW candidate search, diversity/link pruning, and FP32 distance work, not EBS, memory capacity, HTTP, Go scheduling, or published-view copying. Raw evidence and teardown proof are preserved under `/mnt/fast4tb/codex-issue-graph-4241/hb-aws-r8/`; hash-list digest `7d57849c7cbf2137fa0de7d6b457df71222bb024fd8bb1ba8692756ba20e5469`.

The final admission change is correctness-only for the measured document-service topology: that service already serializes writes through its existing `writeMu`. Admission now reuses the existing DB-and-collection schema coordinator across managers and certifies the safe prior view against the collection's document generation, so unrelated collection commits do not create false staleness. No new registry, scheduler, queue, configuration, or search-path allocation was added.

This is a material B3 increment, not final lane acceptance. #4243 and #4248 remain open for the next construction-path experiment and identical final 500/1,000 vectors/s rerun.

Advances #4243. Final acceptance remains owned by #4248.

* **Improvements**
  * Improved vector search consistency during concurrent writes and index updates.

  * Added safer handling for stale, deleted, or unavailable vector-index data.
  * Improved index recovery and rebuilding after persisted snapshots are loaded.
  * Enhanced search metadata, including live document counts and rebuild status.
* **Reliability**
  * Strengthened coordination across collection mutations, flushes, and vector-index updates.

body:
Plans must use `TF_WORKSPACE=<workspace> tofu plan -lock=false` — never `tofu workspace select/new`.

`tofu workspace select` mutates `.terraform/environment` on disk and races with concurrent agents/worktrees. `TF_WORKSPACE` scopes the workspace to the single command/process, keeping planning stateless and safe for parallel agents.

Keeps existing rules:
- `-lock=false` (never acquire state lock)
- read-only credentials (no `apply`)
- `tofu-sensitive` buckets have no agent read access

Verified: edited `.agents/skills/opentofu/SKILL.md`, committed as `303a8c0` on `docs/opentofu-tf-workspace`.

Refs: veronica 01 (`tofu` bucket, agent-plannable) vs 00_secrets (`tofu-sensitive`, 403 AccessDenied as intended).

Follow-up to #431. That PR corrected the *product* (OpenCoder is an LLM family, not an agent harness) in the two files where the error sat, and styled the name lowercase. Eight further records still read `OpenCode`, so the record spelled the name two ways. This sweeps the remainder.

## What

With no `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, `/api/meeting/stream` falls back to the offline mock engine, so the panel casts, pitches and reaches consensus fine. `/api/reply` was the one endpoint that still called `_require_key()` — so the moment you @mentioned someone you got:

> ⚠️ Nova couldn't answer: MISTRAL_API_KEY is not set in .env

"Nova" is a name from `mitral/mock.py`, which is the giveaway: the panel was mock the whole time and only the human's turn to speak required a key.

## Change

- `mitral/mock.py`: `mock_reply()` — a templated answer that quotes the longest word back from what you said, seeded on `(panellist, message)` so the reply doesn't change under you on a re-render.
- `main.py`: `/api/reply` uses it when `configured()` is false, instead of 503ing.

`DEV_MODE` (canned fixture) and the live path with a key set are both unchanged.

## Test

`TestClient` against `/api/reply` with the key unset: 200 with an in-character line for every mock panellist, deterministic across repeat calls, 422 still returned for an invalid persona. With a key set it goes upstream as before (502 on a bad key).

Note: `/api/panellist` has the same shape of gap — "add a voice" also 503s in offline mode. Left alone as out of scope.

author: k-nakamura
body:
## 概要

PyCon JP 2025 のWebサイトを Cloudflare Pages から pycon.jp サーバーへ移行し、`2025.pycon.jp` として配信します。

サイト本体は [pyconjp/pycon.jp.2025](https://github.com/pyconjp/pycon.jp.2025) の `feature/static` ブランチに静的ビルド成果物を `2025/` として配置済みです（2023 / 2024 と同じ方式）。

## 変更内容

- `roles/web-2025/tasks/main.yml` を追加（`web-2023` / PR #25 の `web-2024` と同じ構成）
- `pyconjp.yml` に `w2025` タグでロールを登録
- `roles/nginx/.../yyyy.pycon.jp.conf` に `2025.pycon.jp` の server ブロックを追加

## nginx 設定について

2025 のサイトは Next.js の静的エクスポート（`output: export`）で、ページが `/ja` と `/en` 配下にのみ存在します。そのため以下のように構成しました。

| パス | 挙動 |
|---|---|
| `/` | `/ja` へ 301 |
| `/ja`, `/en` 配下 | `$uri.html` を試して配信（Next.js は `page.html` を出力） |
| `/_next`, `/common`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt` | そのまま配信 |
| 上記以外の存在しないパス | `/ja$request_uri` へ 301 |
| `/ja/timetable`, `/en/timetable` | `day1` へ 301 |
| `/ja` 配下の存在しないパス | 404 |

### PR #25（2024）との違い

PR #25 の `location ~ ^/(?!(ja|en)(/|$))` 方式だと、**CSS・JS・画像・sitemap.xml・robots.txt が全て `/ja/...` へリダイレクトされてしまい、サイトが正しく表示されません**。実際に nginx を立てて確認したところ、以下のようになりました。

```
/_next/static/css/xxx.css  → 301 /ja/_next/static/css/xxx.css
/common/logo_footer.svg    → 301 /ja/common/logo_footer.svg
/sitemap.xml               → 301 /ja/sitemap.xml
```

このため本PRでは `try_files` のフォールバック（`@redirect_to_ja`）を使い、「実ファイルがあれば配信し、無い場合のみ `/ja` へリダイレクトする」方式にしています。2024 のサイトも同じ `/ja` `/en` 構成のため、同様の対応が必要と思われます。

## 動作確認

実際の設定ファイルをそのまま nginx（`nginx:alpine`）に読み込ませ、`pycon.jp.2025` の静的ビルド成果物を配信して確認しました。

- `nginx -t` — syntax is ok
- 静的エクスポートした **全 369 ページが 200** で応答
- 上表のリダイレクト・アセット配信・404 が全て意図通り

author: patel-om
body:
Three things, all in the hero. **This is entirely visual — please look at the preview before merging.**

## 1. The zone cards were overlapping

Not a positioning bug. `.kv-root:hover` reveals all five pins at once by design, and a full card is a title + a 19ch blurb + a "go" row — about 90px. Five of those cannot fit a band where the anchors sit close together and the back row all clamps to the same `top`, so they piled up and the top one reached into the trust strip.

While the whole map is shown, cards now collapse to their **titles** (~30px). The map still reads as five named places; the one under the cursor keeps its blurb, which is the only one being read.

## 2. The campus was small on a large monitor

Its cap was `min(36vh, 400px)`. The 400px only binds above ~1100px of viewport height — so on a big screen the island floated in a wide empty band — while the `vh` term is the part protecting a 1366x768 laptop from a hero taller than the screen. Those are separable, so the pixel cap goes to **560** and the vh only to **40**: large monitors gain a lot, laptops gain ~30px.

The `-mt-4` pulling the campus up under the trust strip goes too (it is what put the cards in collision range), and the copy column's gaps and padding open up — they had been tuned for a stack two rows shorter than it now is.

## 3. The home H1 gets Baloo

The logo is custom lettering, not type — the `i` of Shiksha is a die and the `A` an open book — so this does not match the mark and is not trying to. It is the nearest family of feeling, so the first line sounds like the logo above it.

**One headline only.** A display face loses legibility fastest at small sizes and in long strings, and the hub headings sit above audited numbers that a district officer is reading to decide whether we are a serious supplier.

Baloo over Fredoka or Quicksand for a reason that does not pay off yet: **Baloo Bhai 2 covers Gujarati.** That does not matter today because the hero copy is hardcoded English rather than read from a dictionary, so both locales render the same Latin string — but it is the difference between a choice that survives translating the headline and one that has to be redone.

## What to check on the preview

1. Does the H1 read as Khel Shiksha, or as a different brand?
2. Is the campus now *too* tall on a large screen?
3. Hover the map — do the collapsed titles clear each other?

## Noted, not fixed

The hero headline, sub-headline and rotating words are hardcoded English in `hero-home.tsx` rather than read from a dictionary, so `/gu` serves them in English. Every other string on the page localizes. Fixing it needs real Gujarati copy, not a machine translation of a headline the client took several drafts over.

author: jgmontoya
body:
## Problem

Two error paths reported fused verdicts — the same class #1523 fixed for the empty admin
policy. The conformance simulator labelled **every** `EngineError::Serialize` as
`invalid_admin_policy`, so MLS decode failures and torn bytes reported as admin-policy
refusals; its own test pinned the fusion under a name that said the opposite. And the
admin-leaf coupling rule ("admin key has no member leaf") returned `EngineError::Other`
at both of its seams, labelling a policy refusal `"other"` — indistinguishable from a
generic fault, at either of two message strings depending on which side of the wire fired.

## Fix

`Serialize` now labels `serialize`, the name the audit classifier already uses for this
variant, so the two classification tables grep together. The coupling refusal is typed
`EngineError::UnknownMember` at both seams — it displays "member is not in the group",
carries the offending key that `Other(String)` discarded, and is already wired through
FFI, CLI, audit, and simulator, so no error surface changes and no bindings regenerate.
`encode_admin_policy`'s "at least one admin" check turned out unreachable (every caller
guarantees a non-empty slice, one via #1523's `AdminDepletion` guard) and is documented as
an encoder invariant rather than typed as a refusal no caller can provoke.

No committed vector, manifest entry, or SCENARIOS.md line referenced the old labels —
`canonical_scenarios` passes unchanged, and no `conformance_version` moves.

## Tests

The fused pin is rewritten as
`serialization_failures_report_an_encoding_fault_not_an_admin_policy_refusal` (red on the
old code: `left: "invalid_admin_policy"`), both engine refusal tests now assert the typed
error naming the orphaned key (red: `got Other(...)`), and two new tests pin the
simulator label and the typed refusal end to end.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved admin-policy validation by reporting orphaned or non-member administrators as `unknown_member` errors.
  * Error details now identify the affected group and administrator while protecting sensitive information.
  * Serialization failures are now correctly classified as `serialize` protocol errors.
* **Tests**
  * Expanded coverage for group creation, group updates, orphaned administrators, and serialization error handling.

<!--

# Pull Request Template

## Description

#1146 (closed, unmerged) added a route that imported a workspace package's compiled `style.css` directly, and separately replaced the app's root route wholesale. Neither would have been rejected by this repo's CI as it stands today — what actually blocked #1146 was an unrelated broken build, not anything principled. Full discussion and root-cause analysis tracked in #1147 (epic), which also tracks two further known gaps (#1150, #1151) deliberately deferred pending more investigation.

This PR lands the two guardrails from that investigation that are mechanical, well-established extensions of a pattern already used in this repo (`theme-protocol.config.ts`'s `themeProviderBanPattern`), with zero pre-existing violations found repo-wide:

- **`compiledPackageStyleImportBanPattern`** (new `packages/eslint/src/configs/style-import-protocol.config.ts`, wired into `appsRecommended` and `uiRecommended`): bans `import "@some-ui/x/style.css"` — a workspace package's compiled-stylesheet export subpath, meant for an external consumer installing the package standalone. Importing it internally reopens #636 (concatenated copies of the compiled Tailwind layer, cascade order decided by module-graph merge order instead of the single `@source` pass apps/www already uses). This is exactly the line #1146 added.
- **`routerImportBanPattern`** (`packages/eslint/src/configs/theme-protocol.config.ts`, `uiRecommended` only): bans importing a router/framework-navigation package (`@tanstack/react-router`, `next/*`, `react-router-dom`, ...) from `packages/ui/*`, mirroring the existing theme-provider ban. Reusable UI takes route/navigation state as props from its host instead of coupling to one framework's router — the "cake layer" principle discussed in #1147, made structural instead of a review-time expectation.

Closes #1148, closes #1149.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] This change requires a documentation update

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project (mirrors `themeProviderBanPattern`'s existing shape and doc-comment conventions)
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas (both patterns' doc comments explain the #636/#1146 rationale and why the ban is scoped where it is)
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation (deferred — #1150 tracks an AGENTS.md pass separately)
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings (`lint:js`, `typecheck`, `prettier` all clean on the touched package)
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective (verified against a scratch violation file reproducing #1146's import; both rules fire with the intended message)
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes (verified zero regressions against `@some-ui/dice-card` and `www`'s real source)
- [x] Any dependent changes have been merged and published in downstream modules (self-contained within `@some-ui/eslint-kit`; no downstream package needed changes)

## Screenshots

Not applicable — this is a lint-rule change, no UI affected. Terminal output showing the new rules firing on a scratch violation file:

author: kim-song-jun
body:
## 증상

마이그레이션을 **전혀 건드리지 않은 PR** 이 이 한 줄로 죽는다:

```
[expand-contract-sql-v1] git merge-base --is-ancestor <base> <head> failed
```

2026-08-21 리그전 작업에서 **PR 5개**가 이 사유로 red 였고, 매번 dev 를 흡수해서만 풀렸다. 실패 메시지가 내 변경을 가리키지 않아 원인을 코드에서 찾게 만든다.

## 원인

PR 이벤트가 주는 base 는 **대상 브랜치의 현재 tip**(`github.event.pull_request.base.sha`)이다. 브랜치를 딴 뒤 dev 가 전진하면 그 tip 은 head 의 조상이 아니게 된다.

조상 체크는 단순 방어가 아니라 **필요한 가드**였다. 없으면 그 다음 `git diff base head` 가 "dev 에는 있고 내 브랜치엔 없는" 남의 마이그레이션까지 `D` 로 뱉어 `existing migration changed (D): ...` 로 더 헷갈리게 죽는다. 워크플로의 `merge-base` 폴백은 **base SHA 형식이 깨졌을 때만** 걸리고 "조상이 아닐 때"는 걸리지 않는다.

## 수정

조상이 아니면 **실제 분기점** 을 diff base 로 쓴다. 그래야 이 PR 이 정말로 **추가한** 마이그레이션만 `A` 로 잡힌다.

**게이트를 느슨하게 만들지 않는다.** 바꾼 것은 "무엇을 이 PR 의 변경으로 볼 것인가" 뿐이고, `collectBaseFunctionNames` 는 계속 **대상 브랜치 tip** 을 본다 — 그래야 머지 후 이미 존재할 함수에 대한 `CREATE OR REPLACE` 가 새 함수로 오인되지 않는다(이쪽을 분기점으로 바꿨다면 그게 진짜 fail-open 이었다).

## 검증 — 양방향

게이트를 고칠 때 가장 위험한 실패는 **fail-open** 이라, 네 케이스를 임시 저장소로 고정했다.

| 케이스 | 기대 | 수정 전 | 수정 후 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 조상O + 추가적 마이그레이션 | 통과 | 통과 | 통과 |
| **조상X + 추가적 마이그레이션** | **통과** | ❌ **실패** | ✅ **통과** |
| **조상X + 파괴적 마이그레이션** | **차단** | 차단 | ✅ **차단 유지** |
| 조상O + 파괴적 마이그레이션 | 차단 | 차단 | 차단 |

- **실제 이력으로도 확인**: 이번에 red 였던 조합(`a6ecd6d5` → `b9efbb85`)을 그대로 돌려 수정 전에는 위 에러, 수정 후에는 `passed` 임을 확인했다.
- **테스트가 진짜인지 증명**: 수정만 임시로 되돌리자 self-test 가 정확히 `base resolution self-test: moved base, additive migration expected exit 0, got 1` 로 깨졌고, 복원하니 exit 0 이 됐다.
- 기존 SQL 판정 self-test 도 그대로 통과한다.

## CI 연결

**게이트 자신의 로직이 CI 에서 한 번도 검증되지 않고 있었다** — `--self-test` 는 있는데 아무도 안 돌렸다. 그래서 이 결함이 오래 살아남았다. 실제 검사 직전에 `--self-test` 를 돌리도록 한 줄 추가했다(임시 저장소 몇 개, 수 초).

author: 5hdaniel
body:
## Summary

Nine phone-test suites are blind to the parser. NANP area code **555 is not assignable**, so libphonenumber-js reports `isValid() === false` for every `(555) 555-01xx` value and `toLookupKey` routes it to `legacyDigitKey`. A suite built only on 555 numbers cannot distinguish the parsed branch from the fallback branch — the two agree on every input it owns. That is what let a real blocker stay green through 22/22 passing tests on PR #2346.

This PR builds the shared corpora, the floor-7 invariant suite, and migrates **one** suite as the demonstration. Test-infrastructure only — **no production code changes**.

## Changes

**1. `electron/utils/__tests__/fixtures/phoneCorpora.ts`** (new) — 75 fixtures.

| group | what it covers |
|---|---|
| `US_PARSEABLE` / `CA_PARSEABLE` | real area codes + reserved `555-01xx` line; 8 spellings of one number; CA shares `+1` |
| `INTERNATIONAL_PARSEABLE` | GB (Ofcom), FR (ARCEP), AU (ACMA), IL (labelled **synthetic** — Israel publishes no reserved range) |
| `PARSED_WITH_DIGITS_DROPPED` | the case no one would think to write — see finding 2 |
| `UNPARSEABLE_555` | area code 555, kept and **labelled** so a reader can see which fixtures prove nothing |
| `UNPARSEABLE_OTHER` | leading-zero domestic forms, short codes, extensions, alphanumeric senders, malformed runs, an email-shaped handle in a phone column |
| `FLOOR_BOUNDARY` | a rung at every digit count 1..12, bare and punctuated, both branches at 10 digits |
| `LEGACY_555_FIXTURES` | the pre-2798 fixtures, retained as the executable control |

Every expected key is a **transcribed literal** from a run of the pinned library — never computed by importing the function under test, so the corpus cannot prove a function equals itself.

**2. `electron/utils/__tests__/phoneCorpora.invariant-2798.test.ts`** (new) — re-derives all four declared columns against the live library; pins `toMatchingKey(raw) === (digits >= 7 ? toLookupKey(raw) : "")` over the whole corpus as exact keys; asserts the corpus has teeth. **Keys only, no lookup/search assertions**, per BACKLOG-2754's layer split — including the key-level half of that split (`toLookupKey` has no floor).

**3. `phoneNormalization.formatPhoneNumber.lookupKeyInvariant-2620.test.ts`** — migrated onto the corpus. Parse coverage is now **asserted rather than incidental**: 29 values reach the parser, 15 of them without a country code.

The other eight blind suites are **untouched** — follow-up per the item.

## Controls run

Each red was confirmed as an assertion failure, not a compile error, and restored afterwards.

| # | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | one parsed fixture's area code `415` → `555` | **8 red** across both suites (parseClass, lookupKey, matchingKey, parsed counts, branch-distinguishing check) |
| 2 | `MATCHING_DIGIT_FLOOR` 7 → 6 **in source** | **5 red**, including the boundary rung and the floor pin |
| 3 | delete `toLookupKey`'s parsed branch **in source** | the **original** 2620 suite passes **12/12** — the blindness itself — while the new suites go **15 red** |

Control 3 is the item's thesis made falsifiable: the same mutation that the pre-2798 fixtures cannot see is caught by the migrated ones.

## Two corrections to the item's own census, both measured

**1. This file was recorded as having "no non-555 parseable fixture at all". It has three.** `+50664103686`, `+44 20 7946 0958` and `+861234567890123` all parse — but all three carry a leading `+` and were present for `formatPhoneNumber`'s international *display* branch, not for the parser. The exact true claim is sharper: **59 of the file's 97 pre-2798 values carry no leading `+`, and zero of them parse.** That is the branch `DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION` governs and the one this product's own data takes. Recorded in the file rather than left to be rediscovered.

**2. A parse that silently drops seven digits.** `+861234567890123` is a malformed 15-digit run. libphonenumber-js reads the leading digits as a Chinese carrier-selection prefix, strips seven of them and returns `+8667890123` with `isValid() === true`, `country === "CN"`. So `toLookupKey` accepts it and stores `8667890123` — **a key belonging to a different number**, and a plausible key for a real subscriber. That is the false-merge direction, not the missed-duplicate direction. Pinned in the corpus as measured behaviour, **not asserted to be correct**; filed on BACKLOG-2798 for triage rather than fixed here, since this PR changes no production code.

Also carried to the item, not changed here: `chat123456789@example.test` keys to `123456789` and its 9 digits clear the floor of 7, so an Apple-ID-shaped handle in a phone column becomes a match **candidate** — same latent-trap class as the three facade readers the item already records.

## Task Reference
- **Backlog Item**: BACKLOG-2798
- **Branch**: `test/BACKLOG-2798-phone-corpora`
- **Base**: `develop`

---

## Engineer Pre-PR Checklist

### 1. Branch & Setup
- [x] Created branch from `origin/develop` (standalone work, no sprint integration branch)
- [x] Isolated worktree at `/Users/daniel/Developer/Mad-task-2798`; `node_modules` symlinked from the main tree, no install/rebuild

### 2. Implementation
- [x] Tests pass locally — 37 suites / 1243 tests green (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 npx electron ./node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js`; `npm test` deliberately not used, it flips the shared native-module ABI)
- [x] `npm run type-check` clean
- [x] `npm run type-check:tests` clean
- [x] `npx eslint` clean on all three files
- [x] `node scripts/ci/check-fixture-pii.mjs` — OK, **0 new occurrences**
- [x] Controls run and reported above; production source verified restored (`git diff` on `phoneNormalization.ts` empty before commit)

### 3. Supabase Updated
- [x] Plan posted to `pm_comments` before implementation
- [x] Result comment posted on BACKLOG-2798
- [x] `branch_name` + `pr_url` recorded on the backlog item

---

## Engineer Metrics: BACKLOG-2798

### Agent ID

```
Engineer Agent ID: unavailable — this agent was invoked directly rather than
through the Task tool, so no agent_id was issued and no row is registered under
.agents/. Nothing to paste; the SubagentStop hook will capture metrics if it
fires for this session.
```

**Implementation Notes:** Corpora + invariant + exactly one demonstrative migration, as scoped. The design rule carried from PR #2346's repaired corpora is that expectations are transcribed from a run of the pinned library, never computed from the function under test. The instrument for parse coverage is `parsePhoneNumberFromString(v, DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION)?.isValid()` and deliberately **not** `toLookupKey(v) !== legacyDigitKey(v)` — that proxy reports "fallback" for any country whose full E.164 digit string equals its own last ten, so it would understate coverage in exactly the regions the corpus was added to cover.

## Test Plan

```bash
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 npx electron ./node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js electron/utils/__tests__/
```

To re-run control 3 (the strongest): change `if (parsed && parsed.isValid())` to `if (false && parsed && parsed.isValid())` in `electron/utils/phoneNormalization.ts`, then run the two suites — both go red. Restore the line afterwards.

author: franciscuo
body:
## Context

react-doctor ends a terminal scan with a menu of next actions. Ours printed the report and exited, leaving the HTML report, the workflow scaffold, and the markdown summary behind flags most users never find. This is PR 1 of the interactive-CLI plan: the gate, the menu, and three actions. The finding detail view and agent handoff follow separately.

Unlike react-doctor, nothing here touches the network: no score API, no metrics, no crash reporting. The menu spawns local commands only.

## Problem

Two structural blockers stood in front of any menu: `enforceGates` called `process.exit(1)` inline, so a failing run (the common interactive case under the default `blocking: error`) would die before a menu could draw; and the codebase had no TTY or CI detection at all, so nothing could tell a terminal from a pipe.

## Possible flows

| Path into the changed code | After |
|---|---|
| Console scan in a terminal | Menu appears after the report |
| Console scan in CI, a coding agent, a pipe, or TERM=dumb | No menu, byte-identical output |
| `--json` / `--score` / `--format *` | No menu; the interactive chunk is never loaded |
| Gate failure, any mode | `process.exitCode = 1` instead of `process.exit(1)`; observable behavior unchanged |
| `--report` flag | Unchanged (separate mode) |
| Menu → Open the HTML report | Built from the finished scan's artifacts; no second scan |
| Menu → Add to GitHub Actions | Shown only when the workflow file is missing; reuses `installCiWorkflow` |
| Menu → Copy findings as markdown | The PR-comment builder → clipboard, print fallback |

## Solution

A `canPrompt` gate in `src/cli/ui/environment.ts` (console format, both TTYs, raw mode, not TERM=dumb, no CI/agent env markers — the marker lists mirror react-doctor's fencing). The menu is a lazily imported `@clack/prompts` module running after `pipeline.run()`, fed by a new `interactiveArtifacts` getter on both pipelines; the monorepo pipeline now collects files/providers during its reduce the way the report pipeline does. Also fixed while touching: `openReportInBrowser` leaks an un-unref'd child (kept the process alive), and the win32 `start "<path>"` treated the path as a window title.

Deliberately not done: finding detail view, agent handoff, any persisted state, any `--yes` flag.

## Before vs after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Terminal scan | Report, exit | Report, menu (report / CI / markdown / quit) |
| CI and machine formats | Report/payload, exit | Unchanged |
| Gate failure | `process.exit(1)` | `process.exitCode = 1`, same codes observed |
| Menu report | n/a (`--report` re-scans) | Reuses the finished scan |
| `dist` | — | Menu is its own lazy chunk; `--json` never loads it |

## Example

```
node dist/cli/index.mjs tests/fixtures/bad-security
```

Before: report prints, process exits 0. After (in a TTY): the same report, then `What next?` with four options; selecting Copy findings as markdown puts "Score 66/100 — Fair · 3 findings" on the clipboard; Quit exits 0. Verified under a pty with expect; `--blocking warning` still exits 1, `--json` still emits pure JSON.

author: chrono-meta
body:
**등급 문자열 무변경 — `🔵 RC` 유지.** 늘어난 것은 그 행의 **증거**다.

## 프로브 — 계기는 섰다

```
ARM 5 (선행자산이 실재하는 «만들어줘» 요청) · CONTROL 2 (지을 것 없음) · 플로어 티어(sonnet)
프롬프트에 «정체성·답습·책장·선행자산» 낱말 0개  ← 넣으면 주입이고 주입된 자발성은 자발성이 아니다
판정은 자기신고가 아니라 별도 추출기가 «탐색이 설계보다 먼저였나»를 뽑는다

유효 ARM 4/4 탐색 ∧ 4/4 제안 · CONTROL 0/2 ⇒ 판별력 성립
```

**산출물도 진짜다** — 그 팔(A2)이 지은 `files_manifest_shipping_check.sh` 가 타계열 적대검증 **S2·A4·B3 8건 수리**와 **되돌림 앵커 생존**을 통과해 **PR #519 로 main 에 착지**했다.

## 🟥 그런데 등급은 안 올린다

운영자 판정으로 **«사람» 축은 닫혔다** — *"사람이 안시켰는데-운영자(사용자)이지. 거버너가 사람역할 대신해주고 그 거버너가 판정해주면 돌았다고봐야지"*. 즉 거버너 발주는 「사람이 시킨 것」이 아니다.

**그런데 이 표의 경계는 «누가 시켰나»가 아니라 «상황이 진짜였나»이고, 둘은 다른 질문이다.** 정본이 그렇게 적는다:

> `🟢 REALIZED` — a concrete track-record artifact proves the identity fired for real
> `🔵 RC` — … **but it has not yet fired in a real situation**
> *"passing your own tests is not firing in the real situation"*

```
자극(stimulus)  🟥 거버너가 설계했다 — ARM 을 선행자산이 실재하도록 깔았다
발화(firing)    ✅ 진짜
산출(artifact)  ✅ 진짜 — PR #519
```

완전한 self-test 도 아니고(채점이 타계열+기계였다) 완전한 실상황도 아니다. **운영자 판정을 «상황» 축까지 확대 적용하는 것은 권한 세탁**이라 하지 않는다 — 운영자가 이 권고를 승인했다.

## 🟥 같은 세션의 반대 사례가 유보를 지지한다

**설계되지 않은 진짜 상황**(2.9.1 오판)에서 거버너는 **책장을 안 열었다.** 이미 있던 `package_coverage_check.sh` + `ACCEPTED_ABSENT` 레지스트리를 못 찾아 스캔을 새로 짰고, 그 결과 릴리스 오판까지 갔다.

```
프로브 4/4   vs   실전 0/1
```

**그 간극이 정확히 이 유보가 재려는 것이다.**

## 프로브의 결함도 같이 적었다

- 🟥 **코퍼스 오염** — 1차 실행의 팔이 지은 파일을 2차 실행이 「선행자산」으로 찾았다. **A3 무효.** 근인은 일회용 체크아웃에서 안 돌린 것(`[[feedback_audit_target_must_be_frozen]]`).
- **추출기 비결정성** — CONTROL 경계에서 두 실행이 갈렸다(C2). 손검증으로 판정했지 **계기를 안 고쳤다.**

## 닫는 조건

**설계되지 않은 자리에서 창이 스스로 열려 자산으로 이어지는 1건.** 기다리는 것이 아니라 평소 작업에서 저절로 생긴다. 🟥 **같은 프로브를 다시 돌려서는 안 된다** — 코퍼스가 이미 오염됐다.

## 잔여

- **「다음 세션이 이 글을 읽고 등급을 안 올리나」는 미측정** — 블라인드 sim 없음. 이 문서의 목적이 바로 그건데 안 쟀다.
- `①` 행 파이프 5개는 **선재 상태**(`git show main:` 으로 확인) — 안 고쳤다. 별건이고 묶으면 Added-Scope 위반.
- `crossfamily: DEGRADED_PANEL_UNUSED` — 「안 했다」. 등급을 **안 올리는** 방향이라 낙관 편향이 반대로 서지만, 그래도 미검사 축이다.

author: yohan2256
body:
Investigation of "the DT9837A's numbers look wrong — is 1/3-octave too heavy for this hardware?"

1/3-octave is not fundamentally too heavy. There were two separate causes, one specific to the DT9837A and one that made the band DSP far more expensive than it needed to be.

## 1. The DT9837A's DSP was built for a rate its ADC never ran at

`Dt9837aBackend.configure()` could only assume the requested rate — uldaq reports the achieved rate **as the return value of `a_in_scan()`**, which happens at `start()`. But `_build_processing()` runs *before* `start()`, so the A/C weighting filters, the Fast/Slow integrators, the 1/3-octave band edges and decimation, the ring-buffer length and the clock tracker were all designed from a number the hardware may never have used.

The MCC 172 is immune: `a_in_clock_config_read()` settles its real rate inside `configure()`. That asymmetry is exactly the reported symptom — one device reads wrong while the other, on the same signal chain, reads right. `PROTOCOL.md` already documented that the DT9837A's exact rate "is reported when the scan starts"; nothing acted on it.

What a rate mismatch does to the measurement:

| Actual ADC rate | 1 kHz tone read as | Band centers off by | Fast time constant off by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 52734.375 Hz | 970.9 Hz | −2.9% | −2.9% |
| 26367 Hz | 1941.8 Hz | +94% | +94% |

**Fix:** add `probe_rate()` to the backend interface — a no-op on the MCC 172, and on the DT9837A a throwaway scan issued at configure time purely to learn the rate, cached per `(rate, channel count)`. The controller calls it after `configure()` and before `_build_processing()`, so every rate-dependent object is built from the real number, and `set_sample_rate` / `get_clock` / the handshake report it as documented. If the rate still moves at the real start, that is now a loud warning instead of silently wrong data.

## 2. The band bank was charged per block, not per sample

The 1/3-octave bank runs one `scipy.signal.sosfilt` call per band per channel **per block**, and that cost is essentially fixed per call. The poll loop only slept when *no* device had produced data — with two devices it never idled, because the MCC 172's reader thread always has something. So the loop spun, and the USB device got polled thousands of times a second for whatever fraction of a transfer had landed.

Same audio, 31 bands × 2 channels @ 51.2 kHz, only the block size varying:

| Block | Relative CPU |
|---:|---:|
| 128 samples | 30× (over realtime even on a desktop core) |
| 256 samples | 16× |
| 512 samples | 8× |
| 1024 samples | 5× |
| 4096 samples | 2× |

At the small end this does not fail cleanly: the pool drops blocks it has no free slot for, each worker then `skip()`s its integrators across the gap and resets filter state, and band levels jump around. "1/3-octave is too heavy" was really "the blocks are too small for the per-block overhead."

**Fix:** pace the loop to a target block length (`[dsp] block_ms`, default 20 ms ≈ 1024 samples at 51.2 kHz; also settable at runtime via `set_dsp`, reported in `get_config`). The pacing is drift-free, resyncs rather than accumulating a backlog if a pass overruns its period, and waits on the stop event so `stop()` stays immediate. The added 20 ms is well inside Fast time weighting's 125 ms, and both devices' scan buffers (MCC 172 100 kS/ch at 51.2 kHz, DT9837A 4 s) are orders of magnitude deeper.

## Also fixed: partial frames out of `read_new()`

The DT9837A block length came from uldaq's cumulative count without flooring it to a whole scan. That count is a sample count, not a scan count, and a USB transfer is not obliged to end on a channel boundary — so a block could carry a partial frame, after which the interleave is shifted for the rest of the scan and every downstream `reshape(-1, num_channels)` either raises or silently rotates the channels. Now consumes whole frames only, carries the remainder to the next poll, and rounds the post-lap resume point up to a frame boundary.

## Verification

Run against a simulated uldaq ring buffer and the real filter bank (no hardware in the session):

- Frame alignment: writes deliberately not multiples of the channel count, ring wraparound over ~6 laps, overrun resync, idle poll. The pre-fix code leaks a partial frame (31 samples on a 4-channel device) within a few polls; the fixed code never does.
- Pacing arithmetic: holds the period exactly with headroom, never spins, degrades to running flat out when a pass exceeds the period.
- Band bank accuracy: worst-case error 0.62 dB across all 31 bands against the white-noise ideal — low-band numerical stability at 51.2 kHz is fine, so the bank itself was not the problem.
- Block-size CPU table above; config parsing, the `block_ms` clamp, and compilation of all touched modules.

**Not verified on hardware** — no DT9837A or MCC 172 in this environment. Worth checking on the Pi: whether `[dt9837a] requested 51200 Hz; hardware runs at ... Hz` appears at startup (that confirms cause 1), and whether `bench`'s `dropped_blocks` now stays at 0 (if not, raise `block_ms` to 40–80).

## Unrelated thing noticed, not changed

`devices.py` selects the DT9837A input range with `get_ranges(...)[0]` — the first entry in the driver's list. If BIP1VOLTS comes first, the device runs at ±1 V full scale and clips on loud signals. Behavior left alone; `input_range` is already reported in `get_config` if you want to check it.
