author: joshuaspence
body:
Fourth of five pull requests fixing the Tier 1 findings from the codebase review. Each lands on its own branch so it can be judged and reverted on its own.

## The bug

A Gmail attachment could not be filed by any route. The organiser's guard held that an identification never overrides a stamp — the recipe that wrote one downloaded the invoice and knew it first-hand, while the agent only ever sees the printed page. But it asked whether a stamp *existed*, not whether it *identified* anything, and a provenance-only stamp identifies nothing on purpose: the engine records source, hash, identifier and timestamp and leaves merchant and filing date honestly empty.

So the two escape routes pointed at each other. Plain `organise` reported the file `unidentified`, detail "provenance only, from gmail", and told the agent to identify it. Running the documented identification, `organise --as <Merchant> --filing-date <date> --apply`, was refused with "already carries a stamp — file it without an identification" — the very branch that had just reported it unidentified. Stripping the XMP by hand with `exiftool` was the only way out, and nothing documents that. Meanwhile `download` still advanced the Gmail watermark, so the attachment accumulated in the staging cache and was never re-fetched.

DESIGN.md's "Provenance-Only Stamps" section describes the organiser identifying exactly these files, so the behaviour was wrong rather than the design.

## The fix

The refusal now keys on `existing?.identified === true`. An identifying stamp is protected exactly as before, and the message says "already carries an identifying stamp" because that is now the only case it covers.

Two subtleties sit behind the guard, and the fix is wrong without either.

`sourceSha256` is the hash of the bytes *as downloaded*, taken before the recipe's own stamp rewrote the file, and it cannot be recomputed afterwards. Replacing the stamp outright with the identification would drop it and leave a re-download of the same attachment unrecognisable as a duplicate. So a new `stampFor` merges instead: merchant, filing date and `identified` come from the agent, while `identifier`, `identifierKind`, `source`, `sourceSha256` and `downloadedAt` are carried through untouched.

The plan's `stamp` field was spread only when the file carried *no* stamp at all. Left alone, the merged stamp would have been planned and reported and then never written on apply — the file would have landed in the archive still saying nobody had identified it. That condition now keys on the identification.

A `--tag`-only re-file needs no separate handling: `Identification` requires a merchant and a filing date, and `cli.ts` rejects `--tag` without `--as`, so every tag arrives inside a full identification and travels the widened path.

## Checks

679 tests pass; `tsc`, ESLint and Prettier are clean. Each of the two guards was validated by reverting its fix individually and watching the corresponding test fail, so neither is load-bearing on the other's coverage. New assertions: the file is planned and applied to the expected archive path, the merged stamp keeps all four provenance fields both in the plan and read back off the archived file, a pre-tool unstamped copy of the same attachment is still recognised by hash (this one fails if the merge drops `sourceSha256`), and the existing "refuses to overrule a stamp a recipe wrote" test still passes.

## Notes for review

The commit message cites `docs/gmail.md`, which #59 has since folded into DESIGN.md. The reasoning is unaffected — DESIGN.md carries the same "Provenance-Only Stamps" description — but the path in the commit body is now stale.

Fixture identifiers are invented, per CLAUDE.md.

body:
Lets a customer be assigned a **preferred team member** who rings first when they call.

## Setting (inbox contact panel)
A **Preferred agent** selector on the contact in the inbox right sidebar. Saved to `contacts.preferred_agent_user_id` (+ name). "No preference — ring everyone" clears it. Migration **V285**.

## Priority ring (Telnyx inbound)
When an inbound call's contact has a preferred agent who is reachable right now:
1. Ring **only that agent first** for a short window (≤15s).
2. On no answer, the `call.hangup` handler **fans out to everyone else** (normal ring), then voicemail as before.

State is carried on `calls.routing_state`. If the preferred agent is unset, offline, or busy, it falls straight through to the existing ring-everyone path — so it's **never worse than today**, and a bug in the priority path can't drop a call (fan-out / voicemail still fire).

## Notes / to verify
- Requires migration **V285** (adds the contact columns + `calls.routing_state`).
- This changes **live inbound call routing**, which can't be exercised in CI — please do a **test call** from a number saved as a contact with a preferred agent set, ideally with a second staffer online, to confirm: preferred rings first → no answer → others ring.

Persistence moves to Neon+pgvector behind the RagStore seam (ADR-0008), owned by #4.

Closes #3 (8 of 10 ACs). Unblocks #4 (RagStore + Neon schema) and #5 (Provider interface).

## What changed

**Packages (6):**
- `packages/contracts` — added the typed trace contract `Trace` / `TraceEvent` / `CostRecord` (ADR-0007 amendment) with a fast-check cost-invariant test.
- `packages/rag-core` — pipeline interfaces: `Router`, `Retriever`, `Assembler`, `Generator`, `Reviewer`.
- `packages/rag-ingest`, `packages/eval` — ingestion/eval seams, domain-agnostic.
- `packages/kajianq-domain` — the domain pack (where Islamic-domain logic is allowed to live).

**Governance/docs:** `AGENTS.md` records the ADR-0009 paid-API amendment to the template's free-tier guardrail (verbatim override). `NOTICES/DATASETS.md` scaffold created with attribution boilerplate. README rewritten for KajianQ. `.gitignore` added.

author: rubenvdlinde
body:
Renames the app id `nldesign` -> `thematiq`.

## The important half is what did NOT move

This app **implements** the NL Design System, so most occurrences of `nldesign` in it are the **external standard**, not this app's id. The standard is owned by the Dutch government, and its names are matched **by string** against stylesheets in every other app in the fleet and in `@conduction/nextcloud-vue`. Renaming one here does not rename it there — the selector simply stops matching and the theme **silently falls back to default styling, with nothing in any log**.

**Frozen:**
- the `nldesign-*` CSS custom properties and class/DOM-id prefixes (`nldesign-color-primary`, `nldesign-font-family`, `nldesign-theme`, …)
- the `nldesign` design-system id in `design-systems.json`, `nldesignsystem.nl`, and the `nl-design-system/themes` upstream
- class names that *name the standard*: `NLDesignEMailTemplate`, `NlDesignThemeShareableConfigType`
- `openspec/changes/archive/**` and every `@spec` capability path

**Moved:** `<id>`, `<namespace>` and `OCA\NLDesign` → `OCA\Thematiq` across 111 files, display name, composer/package names (both lockfiles refreshed), the l10n domain, `/apps/nldesign` routes, `getAppPath('nldesign')`, `APP_ID`, the `occ` prefix, and the two test artifacts named after the app.

## A bug found on the way

**`appinfo/info.xml` did not parse.** The explanatory comment contained `--nldesign-*`, and a double hyphen is illegal inside an XML comment — so the file was malformed and the app could not have installed. Rephrased.

Two docblocks were also damaged by an over-eager rewrap of over-long `@return` lines and are restored; the rewrap now splits type from description on **brace depth**, so a type containing spaces stays whole.

## Local verification
phpcs 0 errors · psalm clean · l10n OK · prettier 0 · no files deleted against `development`. This app has no JS to lint and no JS tests.

phpstan reports 11 `OCA\Theming` `class.notFound` errors — that is **Nextcloud's own Theming app**, absent from a bare clone and present in CI's container. Identical on `development`, so pre-existing and unrelated to this rename.

author: dem-extra1
body:
Post-merge UMS from #2024, where this was a real defect in my own diff that a reviewer caught.

`^\s*>.*$` compiled with `re.S | re.M` deleted every character after the first `>` line,
because `re.M` makes `$` match before any newline while `re.S` makes `.` consume them --
so `.*` runs to the end of the string and `$` is satisfied at the last position.

Two things the entry argues rather than states:

- **The flags are justified by a different alternative than the one they break.**
  `re.S` was there for the triple-backtick fence alternative; the damage landed on the
  blockquote. The line you would scrutinize and the line that is wrong are not the same line.
- **In a stripper it fails toward silence.** Over-removal makes the consumer stop firing,
  which reads as "no findings" rather than as a bug. Twenty-seven positive tests passed.

Filed under `least-flexible-tool` because the remedy is precisely that principle: `.` and
`\s` are the most flexible character constructs available, and `[^\n]` / `[ \t]` say what
is meant and are immune to the flag.

Refs #2024.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Documentation-only addition to a coding rule; no runtime, auth, or data-handling changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a worked example to `least-flexible-tool.md`: compiling `^prefix.*$` with `re.S | re.M` makes the “one line” alternative consume the rest of the string, because `.` eats newlines while `$` is still satisfied at the end.
> 
> The flags are often justified by a different alternative (e.g. a fence), so the broken branch is easy to miss; in a stripper this fails toward silence (over-removal looks like “no findings”). Remedy: `[^\n]*` and `[ \t]` instead of `.` / `\s`, plus a negative test after the stripped region. Drawn from the `hooks/no-unfiled-finding.py` stripper in ai-config#2024.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ca6f10db1903b1721b0a877d3427737605ab595c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

author: ulquiorracode
body:
### Summary

This release introduces comprehensive architectural hardening, an expressive macro system with capability-based authorization, declarative CLI commands with per-command help, resilient epoch-based WASM interruption, full Metamod/AMX Mod X co-existence safety, and live-tested GoldSrc engine hooks.

---

### Changes

#### 1. Architecture & Sandbox Security (Adversarial Audit Rounds 1 & 2)
- **Epoch Interruption Ticker**: Spawned a dedicated background daemon thread (`goldsrc-epoch-timer`) in `goldsrc-wasm-host` ticking `increment_epoch()` every 2ms to ensure fail-safe wall-clock guest timeout enforcement.
- **Resource Constraints (StoreLimits)**: Configured 64MB memory limits, 10,000 table element bounds, and instance limits per Wasmtime store.
- **Metamod ABI & Shared Memory Safety**: Stored `mutil_funcs_t` in atomic pointers without overwriting Metamod's process-global table, preventing co-loaded plugin crashes (AMX Mod X).
- **Network Protocol & SayText Bounding**: Aligned `MessageDest` discriminants with `const.h`, dynamically resolved SayText via `reg_user_msg`, sanitized string payloads to prevent buffer overflows, and set proper server sender IDs.
- **Panic Boundaries & Lifecycle**: Wrapped all entity factories in `catch_ffi_panic` and consolidated asset precaching to run once per map on `ServerActivate`.

#### 2. Macro System & Capability Authorization
- **Typed Command Parameters**: Added `FromArg` trait for automated parameter extraction and validation (`Player`, `Alive<Player>`, primitives, strings).
- **Auto Caller Binding**: When an in-game player runs a command without positional arguments (e.g. `/vip`), the caller index automatically binds to target entity parameters.
- **Fail-Closed Authorization DSL**: Implemented Boolean capability AST expressions (`and`, `or`, `not`, group wildcards) for `#[command(capability = "...")]`.
- **Plugin Metadata**: Extended `#[plugin]` with `url`, `dependencies`, and runtime introspection.

#### 3. CLI & Logging
- **Declarative CLI Specs**: Added structured `CommandSpec` with per-command usage and automated help generation (`grs help <cmd>` and `grs <cmd> --help`).
- **Buffered Logging**: Integrated `BufWriter` in `GoldSrcLogger` with structured, unified formatting across core, plugins, and CLI.

---

### Verification
- **Automated Tests**: 34 unit tests passed across all crates (`goldsrc`, `goldsrc-api`, `goldsrc-macros`, `goldsrc-wasm-host`).
- **Static Analysis & Linting**: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` passed with 0 warnings/errors.
- **Live Server Integration**: Verified on dedicated ReHLDS server running Metamod-r + 9 Metamod plugins + AMX Mod X (59 running plugins) + 4 GoldSrc.rs WASM demo plugins (`admin_system`, `test_suite`, `vip_core`, `vip_menu`).
- **CI Status**: GitHub Actions CI workflow passed with green check.

Two residual holes in scripts/pds-door-census.sh's arg_span/blank_strings pair (filed by the lega-argument-list slice as STATE-not-fix):

body: ## Проблема Аудит всех путей поступления лидов выявил несколько причин, по которым заявки **не попадали в CRM** или **терялись из вида**: 1. **Kill-switch WA Web блокировал Green API** — если у проекта была запись `whatsapp_web_sessions` (даже disconnected), триггер БД отклонял INSERT лидов с `channel=whatsapp, source=whatsapp`. Green API как раз создаёт такие лиды → webhook возвращал 500, лид не создавался. 2. **Заявки с сайта без проекта** — generic URL `/lead-intake` без токена мог создавать лиды с `project_id = null`. Они показывались во **всех** проектах CRM (через `project_id.is.null`), но часть команды их не видела из-за RLS. 3. **Лимит 500 лидов** в CRM — старые лиды просто не загружались в воронку. 4. **Ручное создание** — ошибка insert не показывалась пользователю (toast «Лид добавлен» даже при fail). ## Исправления ### БД (`20260823120000_wa_web_block_greenapi_fix.sql`) - Триггер kill-switch: если Green API настроен (`whatsapp_config.id_instance`), лиды **не блокируются** при offline WA Web - Backfill: восстановить `project_id` у «осиротевших» лидов через pipeline ### Edge `lead-intake` - Обязательный `project_id` — 400 `project_not_resolved`, если проект не определён - Доп. резолв токена через `projects.intake_token` - Назначение `assigned_to` / `created_by` = владелец проекта ### Frontend CRM - Строгий фильтр `.eq('project_id', projectId)` — лиды только своего проекта - Лимит загрузки: 500 → **2000** - Исправлен toast при ручном создании лида ### Настройки подключения - URL формы: `/lead-intake/t/` (привязка к проекту в path) ## Проверка - `npm run ci` ✅ ## Деплой 1. Применить SQL-миграцию в Supabase 2. Redeploy edge function `lead-intake` 3. Обновить URL формы на сайтах (если ещё generic `/lead-intake` без `/t/`) ### SQL для проверки после деплоя ```sql -- Лиды без проекта (должно стремиться к 0): SELECT COUNT(*) FROM leads WHERE project_id IS NULL AND is_personal = false; -- Последние заявки по проектам: SELECT p.name, COUNT(l.id) AS leads FROM projects p LEFT JOIN leads l ON l.project_id = p.id AND l.is_personal = false GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY leads DESC; ```

author: mpgxc
body:
O app estava no repositório sem forma de instalá-lo. Este workflow gera o projeto nativo, constrói o APK e o publica.

## Como dispara

- **Manualmente**, pela aba Actions, com escolha entre `release` e `debug`.
- **Por tag `v*`**, que além do artefato cria a Release e anexa o APK.

Não roda a cada push em `mobile/**` de propósito: um build de APK leva bem mais que os testes, e o gate de qualidade do app já existe no workflow `App mobile`.

## O projeto nativo continua fora do versionamento

`android/` é produzido pelo `expo prebuild` na própria esteira. Assim o APK construído é exatamente o que o repositório descreve — sem projeto nativo ajustado à mão que ninguém consegue reproduzir.

## Três coisas que eu teria errado no escuro

Instalei o SDK do Android e rodei o build **localmente** antes de escrever o workflow. Foi o que revelou:

**1. O release é assinado com a chave de debug.** O template do React Native traz isso, com um `// Caution!` no `build.gradle` gerado. O APK instala e roda — serve para testar e distribuir internamente —, mas não serve para loja.

Em vez de deixar a descoberta para depois, o workflow declara a condição no nome do artefato (`...-debug-signed-...`) e no resumo da execução. Havendo os quatro segredos, a assinatura real entra pela **API de injected signing do AGP** (`-Pandroid.injected.signing.*`), sem editar o arquivo que o prebuild acabou de gerar — que seria justamente o remendo que quebra em silêncio na geração seguinte.

| Segredo | Conteúdo |
|---|---|
| `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64` | keystore em base64 |
| `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` | senha da keystore |
| `ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS` | alias da chave |
| `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD` | senha da chave |

**2. O build baixa ~2,5GB de NDK** para compilar o nativo do VisionCamera e do Nitro. A versão (`27.1.12297006`) entra declarada no setup do SDK — sem isso o Gradle a resolve sozinho a cada execução, e uma eventual falha só apareceria no meio do build.

**3. O prebuild reclamava de duas chaves do `app.json`:** `edgeToEdgeEnabled`, que o Android 16 tornou obsoleta, e `userInterfaceStyle`, que exigiria `expo-system-ui` só para forçar o tema do sistema. As duas saíram — a tela já desenha o próprio fundo escuro.

## Detalhes

- Testes e checagem de worklets rodam **antes** de empacotar: gerar APK de código sabidamente quebrado é desperdício de esteira.
- `gh release create` antes do `upload`: numa tag recém-criada a Release ainda não existe, e o `upload` sozinho falharia.
- Cache de Gradle e npm, para o custo de recompilar o nativo não se repetir inteiro.

## Estado da verificação

O build local que embasou tudo isso **ainda estava compilando o código nativo** quando abri este PR. O que já está confirmado é o que produziu as três decisões acima: prebuild bem-sucedido, SDK/NDK resolvidos, `signingConfig` e versões de SDK lidos do projeto gerado.

O que falta confirmar é o APK saindo ao final. Aviso aqui assim que o build terminar — e, se falhar, corrijo antes de isto sair de draft.

Vale registrar uma limitação: `workflow_dispatch` só fica disponível depois que o arquivo está no branch padrão, então este pipeline **não** pode ser exercitado pela CI antes do merge. É por isso que investi no build local.

author: baadc0de
body:
Nightly run 32625620076's `P2 kill-9 gate` reported **success** while its own evidence read `candidates: 47`, every one `status: error`, every one `qualified: false`, and `selected: None`. Forty-seven candidates enumerated, none qualified, nothing selected, and the job was green.

That is the condition #170 exists to make impossible — its premise, in its own words, is that "an unqualified device and a regression must stop being indistinguishable". Here it was worse: the run returned a **passing** verdict while the qualification produced nothing, so the D16 budget was asserted against whatever ran, with the artifact recording truthfully and in full that no device had been qualified. The evidence was honest; the verdict simply wasn't conditioned on it.

## What it does now

Zero qualified candidates exits non-zero and says why:

> device qualification failed: zero of N candidates qualified; no device was selected. The D16 latency verdict was not evaluated because no device passed fio job A

Three distinctions are kept apart rather than collapsed, which is the substance of the fix:

- **`UNQUALIFIED`** — nothing qualified. Not `SKIPPED`, because a skip says "this did not run" and something did run and returned a verdict; not a latency `FAILED`, because there is no basis to fail on latency without a qualified device. `gate-status.sh` already had the `unqualified` column and it is now populated.
- **`INTERRUPTED`** — all candidates lost to spot interruption stays its own outcome. Environmental, not a retryable test failure and not a pass.
- **A real latency failure** — unchanged, and still the only thing that reports as a D16 miss.

Conflating the first with the last is how this gate spent four nights red with a verdict that named nothing (#137), so keeping them separate is the point rather than a detail.

There is also a second, subtler unqualified case now named separately: candidates that pass `fio` but where no qualified **x86_64** device supports the pinned FoundationDB package. That would previously have looked identical to "nothing qualified".

## Why this had to be fixed independently of its cause

The IAM condition that denied every launch is already fixed and applied (#315 — `ec2:InstanceType` only exists in the request context for the instance, so a statement carrying it could not match `network-interface/*`). Tonight's run will very likely qualify a device, which is exactly the argument for fixing the verdict separately: **the next qualification failure will be silent in the same way and will not announce itself with 47 identical errors.** Spot capacity, a quota, an AMI that stops resolving, a region incident — each produces the same shape, and each would have produced a green gate.

## Verification, re-run independently on the pushed commit

- `p2-kill9-gate.sh --self-test` and `gate-status.sh --self-test` both exit 0.
- `--fast`: **31 gates, 0 failed, 0 unqualified, 0 interrupted, 0 unknown.**
- Unqualified synthetic run **fails**, naming `zero of 3 candidates qualified` and explicitly withholding the D16 verdict.
- Qualified synthetic run still **passes** — the change is not merely stricter.

**Mutation check on the guarded stage rather than the check line:** neutering the qualification branch in the controller so the verdict is no longer conditioned on it fails the self-test with *"unqualified failure did not name its basis"*. Restored, green, tree clean. The agent's own mutation — making the controller call site ignore qualification — failed with *"live controller verdict is not conditioned on device qualification"*.

`#318`'s instance-NVMe telemetry surface and `#317`'s `DISK_TELEMETRY_JOBS` inventory were both left untouched, as the brief required.

## Drifted citations

Reported rather than silently followed: `nightly.yml`'s P2 job `629-692` → `1074-1118`; `p2-kill9-gate.sh:185-195` → definition `98-107`, live call `376`; `:682` → `939-941`; `gate-status.sh:429-442` → `573-585`, `:457+` → `601-640`, `:795` → `1093`; `AGENTS.md:396-402` → `361-367` and `:404-410` → `369-375`. All other normative-document citations from #176 were still at their cited lines.

`./scripts/check.sh` was terminated by the environment at exit 143 during the `p1-swarm` workspace build; fmt, clippy's three feature sets and the static gates passed before that, but no full-check pass is claimed. CI covers it.

Closes #316

author: mwiewior
body:
Annotated output carried no record of how it was produced. This adds two lines after the input's own header, before the `CSQ` declaration:

```
##vepyr="0.3.0" engine="datafusion-bio-function-vep 0.17.0" cache="/caches/116_GRCh38_merged"
  cache_type="merged" backend="parquet" cache_version="116" vep_codebase="116.0" api="116"
  ensembl=116.c0cf13d ensembl-variation=116.2fb834b
##vepyr-command-line='{"input":"...","output":"...","cache":"...","reference_fasta":"...","options":{...}}'
```

The tool name is configurable (`provenance_tool_name` / `provenance_tool_version`) and defaults to this engine's own crate identity, so the label belongs to whoever is calling rather than being hard-coded to one product.

## Three deliberate omissions

**No wall-clock timestamp.** Ensembl VEP writes `time="..."` into its `##VEP=` line, which is why VEP's own output differs byte for byte between two identical runs. Omitting it keeps annotation output byte-reproducible — a property the reference implementation does not have.

**No `##VEP=` line.** Writing one would assert that Ensembl VEP produced the file, at a time it did not run, from a cache path that may not exist on the reading machine. That is a false entry in an audit trail. It would not buy byte parity either, precisely *because* VEP's timestamp differs every run — so the choice was never "parity vs. no parity", only "false provenance vs. true provenance", and both are equally non-identical to a VEP run.

This is a different kind of claim from the `CSQ` description, which reads `"Consequence annotations from Ensembl VEP. Format: ..."`. That describes the format and semantics of a field downstream tools match on by exact prefix; it does not assert a run happened.

**No guessing at the VEP target.** `cache_version`, `vep_codebase`, `api` and the ensembl revisions are stated only when the cache version is known up front. An unpinned run says nothing rather than inferring.

## Re-annotation

Provenance from an earlier annotation is stripped before the new lines are appended — it describes a `CSQ` field that is being replaced. Ensembl VEP does the same with its own `##VEP` lines (`OutputFactory/VCF.pm`). Stale `##VEP` lines from a genuine prior VEP run are stripped for the same reason.

## Known gap

The Ensembl cache's data-source versions — gnomAD, ClinVar, dbSNP, GENCODE, SIFT, PolyPhen — belong in this line too, because they determine what is *inside* `CSQ`. `gnomADe_AF=0.001` is uninterpretable without knowing whether it came from v4.1 or v2.1. They are dropped when a raw cache is converted to Parquet, so they are not available at annotation time. Tracked in #213, which proposes deriving them from the pinned cache version rather than carrying them through the cache.

## Dependencies

Both bio-formats deps move from tag `v1.10.0` to the master revision carrying the header passthrough (biodatageeks/datafusion-bio-formats#242), since that is what makes header injection possible at all. `datafusion-bio-format-core` becomes a direct dependency for the metadata key. Tags to follow once md5 parity is confirmed.

## Tests

Eight cases: identity and cache attributes; no timestamp; byte-identical across runs; never claims to be Ensembl VEP; pinned target present only with a known cache version and absent otherwise; paths and options in the command line; default engine identity.

These were written after the implementation rather than test-first, so I mutation-checked the two that matter most: injecting a timestamp fails `provenance_never_records_a_timestamp`, and changing the prefix to `##VEP=` fails `provenance_never_claims_to_be_ensembl_vep` plus two others. They catch the regressions they exist for.

900 lib tests pass, `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` clean.

author: invierno8
body:
## The comment

> add a profetional user friendly filtering options by date last 24h last week etc ... also by keywords, specific elements on screen and the if the hold ctrl and choose an element he will be a filter and show only comments on marked elements and more.. take that logic make it perfect

- **id:** `jynx-mt5f2ow7dqrw`
- **route:** dashboard
- **targetLabel:** `comments-sidebar`
- **secondaryTargets:** (none)

## Thinking process

This one was mostly unambiguous — the comment names three concrete filter types (date range, keyword, element) and even specifies the interaction for the third one exactly ("hold ctrl and choose an element"). The one place I had to make a judgment call is "and more.. take that logic make it perfect" at the end, which doesn't name anything concrete — I read that as enthusiasm/emphasis on the three named filters, not a fourth hidden requirement, and implemented exactly the three things actually named rather than guessing at a "more" I can't pin down.

For the date filter, I picked plain rolling windows (`now - 24h`, `now - 7d`, `now - 30d`) rather than calendar-aligned buckets ("today", "this calendar week") — this is a QA-feedback triage tool, not a reporting dashboard, and every other date-ish thing in this file (the 5s polling interval, the drag/scroll debounce) is similarly "good enough," not calendar-precise.

For the element filter, I looked at how `DevOverlay.jsx`'s existing hover-highlight + Ctrl/Cmd+click-to-annotate already solves "which element is under the cursor" (`useHoverTarget.js`'s `findTarget`/`labelForElement`) before writing anything new, and reused that exact function pair rather than reimplementing container-detection logic. I did hit one real bug while testing this reuse: `useHoverTarget.js`'s own hover-highlight intentionally ignores anything inside `.jynx-chrome` (Jynx's own UI) unless the caller passes `allowJynxChrome` — my first pass copied that same exclusion into the filter's click handler, which turned out to be wrong for this use case. A filter is picking from an *already-existing* comment list, not creating a new annotation, and a lot of real comments in this queue *already* target Jynx's own chrome (`dev-toolbar-settings-btn`, `jynx-settings-panel`, `comments-sidebar-filters`, etc. — visible in this very queue). Excluding `.jynx-chrome` meant you could never filter by clicking the exact elements this comment itself is about. I removed that exclusion (kept `.dev-overlay-ignore`, the transient highlight/dot layer, excluded — that one's never a meaningful target either way).

I looked at `CommentsPanel.jsx`'s existing `shown` filter chain (status/mine-only) before adding to it, and just extended the same `.filter()` chain rather than introducing a separate mechanism.

## What changed

`client/src/devtools/overlay/CommentsPanel.jsx` only:
- Date-range pills (Any time / 24h / Week / Month) filtering on each comment's `createdAt`.
- A keyword search box, matching against the comment text and its target label (case-insensitive substring).
- An "Element" pick toggle — while active, Ctrl/Cmd+click any element on the page (reusing `useHoverTarget.js`'s `findTarget`/`labelForElement`) to filter the list to comments whose `targetLabel` or `secondaryTargets` match that element; shows as a clearable chip once set.
- All three compose with the existing Open/Done, "Just me", and This-page/All-pages filters — same `.filter()` chain, no new state-management pattern introduced.

## Verification

- `cd client && npx vite build` — clean.
- Live end-to-end check with real `data/` + `client/` dev servers and a headless-browser (Chromium) pass: seeded three throwaway QA-annotation notes (two fresh, one hand-backdated 40 days via direct file edit to test the date boundary), then drove the actual UI:
  - Keyword filter (`unique-marker-A`) narrowed 9 → 1 item, exactly the matching one.
  - "Month" date filter correctly excluded only the 40-day-old backdated item (9 → 8), "Any time" restored all 9.
  - Element-pick mode: Ctrl+click on a real toolbar button (`dev-toolbar-draw-toggle`, inside `.jynx-chrome`) correctly set the filter chip to that exact label and narrowed the list (0 matches, since none of the throwaway test notes targeted that element) — confirms the `.jynx-chrome` fix above actually works, not just that the mechanism runs. Clearing the chip restored all 9.
  - This is also where I initially caught the `.jynx-chrome` bug described above — the first pass silently produced `elementChipText: null` (click didn't register at all) instead of the expected label.
  - All throwaway test notes deleted afterward via the real admin API; `git status` was clean before pushing.
- Not implemented: whatever "and more" in the comment might have meant beyond the three named filter types — left alone rather than guessed at (see Thinking process above).

author: dannyfish-11
body:
**一行外部依赖都没加。** 接的全是仓库里已经躺着、但从来没被走到过的东西。

## 三块拼图一直是齐的，中间断了一根线

`SafeExecutor` 的执行策略写着「优先委托 Node_09_Sandbox，降级到内置」，而：

| 已有 | 状态 |
|---|---|
| `nodes/Node_09_Sandbox/Dockerfile` | 在 —— `python:3.11-slim` + **非 root 用户** |
| `core.node_lifecycle.container_start_node` | 在 —— 能用 Docker/Podman 起任意节点 |
| `core.container_runtime` | 在 —— 运行时探测 / 选择 / 持久化 |

断在这一行：

```python
node09_url = os.environ.get("NODE09_SANDBOX_URL", "")   # 默认空串
if self._node09_url:                                     # → 恒假
```

于是容器那条路**从来没被走到过**；而 `container_start_node` 全仓只有面板上一个 HTTP 端点在调，**要人手动去点**。

也就是说：默认配置下，智能体自己写出来的代码跑在**用户自己的内核、自己的用户身份**下，而那层容器隔离静静躺着没人用。

**与 `--n-cpu-moe` 是同一个形状：能力在、路没接、判据不说实话。**

## `core/execution_isolation.py` —— 判据只此一处

`resolve_isolation()` → `IsolationDecision(tier, endpoint, degraded, reason)`

| 档 | 是什么 |
|---|---|
| `container` | Node_09 在 Docker/Podman 容器内：**非 root、独立命名空间**。默认首选 —— Windows 上 Docker Desktop 同样算 |
| `builtin` | 正则挡 pattern + `setrlimit` + 同内核 `subprocess`。挡得住手滑，挡不住一次不走运的代码生成 |

**刻意只有两档。** microVM（Firecracker / AgentENV / E2B）是真正更硬的第三档，但这里**不给它留一个永远不会被返回的空取值** —— 那就是又一次「看起来接上了，其实没有」。等真接上那条路的那一天再加，加的时候连同它的探测一起加。

## 三件容易做错的事

**① 不在请求里等容器 build。** `container_start_node` 首次要 build 镜像，那个函数自己给的超时上限是 **1800 秒**。在一次用户请求里同步等它是不可接受的。

所以：**探测同步、拉起后台、而且只试一次**（起不来通常是环境问题，每次执行都重试只会把每次执行都拖慢、日志刷满）。代价是**第一次执行拿不到容器边界** —— 这一点写在模块头里，不藏着。

**② 降级必须留痕。** 容器起不来时回落内置是对的（不能让用户的任务因为沙箱抽风直接失败），但**不能悄悄回落**：调用方若不知道这次是在裸机上跑的，就会以为自己有边界。

所以 `ExecutionResult` 新增 `isolation` 一位：

```json
{"tier": "builtin", "is_isolated": false, "degraded": true,
 "reason": "沙箱容器还没就绪(已用 docker 在后台拉起) —— 这一次跑在同一个内核下"}
```

默认值刻意是「内置且已降级」：**拿不到判据时，不能让人以为自己有边界**。降级的形状只有一处定义（`_degraded_from`），否则迟早有一条路径漏掉 `degraded=True`。

**③ `container` 模式真的会拒绝执行。** 那个模式的全部含义就是「宁可不跑，也不在裸机上跑」；降级会把它变成一句没有效力的话。

## 一处我自己写出来又抓到的谎

第一版那份只读报告，在 `allow_start=False` 的路径上照样写「**已在后台拉起**」—— 而它根本没拉。而那句 `reason` 正是给人看着判断该动哪里的：它说谎，人就会去等一个根本没在动的东西。已修，并由 `c03` 钉住。

## 顺带

author: anukuljha
body:
## What changes

Retires the loopback stand-ins in `harness/fake_platform.py` in favour of **real
providers**, and puts the machinery in place to keep using them: one egress
proxy that records and replays, a consent model for the accounts only a person
can connect, and a tenant that keeps those accounts between runs.

```
record   real credentials  →  proxy  →  real Telegram / Google / GitHub / Slack
replay   no credentials    →  proxy  →  what was recorded, and nothing else
```

```bash
make scenarios-record CASSETTE=connectors
make scenarios-replay CASSETTE=connectors
```

Everything below was found by running this against real Telegram, real GitHub,
real Slack, real Composio and real Resend — not by reading the code.

## Why

The suite stood in for other people's servers by running HTTP servers on
`127.0.0.1` and pointing Lemma at them. The reachability problem is the least of
it:

- **~40 scenarios skip against a deployment**, behind `needs(LOOPBACK_REACHABLE)`.
- **It needs `CONNECTOR_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK_TARGETS=true`**, which production
  does not have and should not: that guard exists so an org admin cannot aim a
  connector at the cloud metadata service.
- **It is not what a person does.** Nobody points their Telegram surface at a bot
  API on their laptop.
- **A hand-written stand-in cannot tell you it has drifted.** When Telegram
  changes a response shape, our imitation keeps returning the old one and the
  suite stays green. A recording can — re-record it and the diff is the news.

## The proxy

Two feasibility questions, both answered before anything was built on it:

- **Every outbound client honours the proxy.** No `trust_env=False` anywhere in
  48 `httpx` clients, and `slack_sdk` loads `HTTPS_PROXY` itself — including
  socket mode.
- **Record and replay both work against the real product.** A booted stack
  fetched a real OpenAPI spec from `petstore3.swagger.io`; the scenario read the
  call back out of the proxy; the same scenario with the same assertion passed in
  replay with no network, and an unrecorded request was refused rather than
  forwarded.

Two properties keep it safe, each with a guard that goes red if it is removed:
an unrecorded request is **killed, not forwarded**, and the product is given the
proxy's CA **and no other**, so a client that bypasses the proxy fails on the
certificate rather than succeeding behind the suite's back.

`egress.calls_to("api.telegram.org")` replaces three recorder objects with three
different shapes — `SentMessage`, `ReceivedCall`, `SentEmail` — with one query
that does not care which platform is on the other end.

## Consent, and accounts that survive

GitHub, Slack and Gmail are OAuth2, and the product refuses credential injection
for those outright. That is correct, and this adds no back door: a person
consents in a browser, which is what a real person does.

What makes that usable is that it happens **once**, not once per run:

- The tenant declares its own **standing auth configs** (`github_standing`, …).
  An account belongs to the auth config it was consented against, so a run that
  installed its own discarded every OAuth account when it cleaned up — which
  made consent worth nothing for exactly the connectors that need it.
- Accounts are scoped to **the person who connected them**, so the tenant
  nominates one holder. Without that, provisioning asked the owner while
  scenarios asked whoever they were acting as, and the same tenant answered both
  yes and no to "is GitHub connected?".
- `make scenarios-provision` now prints **the URL to open**, not just a
  description of where to find the button.
- Unmet consent is carried to the end of the run as its own section, and
  `report_scenarios_to_slack.py` says the same in Slack — so an expired grant
  becomes somebody's morning rather than a number that quietly went down.

**Gmail goes through Composio**, which brings its own OAuth app. It is the route
this product's users take today and the only one open to a deployment with no
approved Google client — this one has none.

## Bugs fixed

**In the product:**

- `get_pod_context` converted the `pod_id` path param with an unguarded
  `UUID(...)`, so **every pod-scoped route answered 500** — with a traceback in
  the body wherever debug was on — for a request that was merely malformed. The
  `is None` case right above it was handled; this one was not. Now a 400, with a
  regression test that fails without the fix.

**In the suite, each one hiding a green result that proved nothing:**

- **The live Telegram scenario could never pass.** It sent as the bot and waited
  for an update whose sender `is_bot` — Telegram never delivers a bot its own
  messages, so the filter was unsatisfiable and the only outcome was a 120s
  timeout. It also called `getUpdates` itself, which has exactly one consumer:
  the worker's poller got **409 Conflict forty-five times in one run**. The test
  broke the product it was testing, and had done so for as long as the file
  existed.
- **Three GitHub scenarios skipped against a tenant that had GitHub connected**,
  because the consent lookup asked whichever colleague the scenario happened to
  want first.
- **`GITHUB_REPO` demanded a PAT nothing reads.** Left over from when the
  scenario injected credentials — which that same OAuth2 guard refuses, so it
  never worked. The scenario skipped for a credential it does not use.
- **Two scenarios asserted a *configuration*, not a promise** — both failed
  against a real deployment while the product was right.
  *Installing an OAuth connector with no credentials* named `slack`, which has
  none on a stack we boot and has them on any deployment that uses Slack; it now
  asks the catalogue for a connector with no system default. That hazard was
  written down in `_deployment_settings` and this scenario was the thing it
  described.
  *An unavailable converter does not count against the document* uploaded bytes
  that were not a PDF, so where an extractor is reachable, failing that document
  is correct — and the scenario called the correct answer a bug. It now uploads
  a readable document, and reads the status only once the file is out of
  PROCESSING, since a claimed file answers nothing either way.
- **The stack silently attached to whatever already held `SCENARIOS_PORT`.** A
  stack that fails to bind still waits for health, and the process already on
  the port answers it — so the run tests a stale build with none of its own
  settings. It cost half an hour here, with every symptom pointing at the
  settings. Now it refuses to start.
- **`FakeResend` was deleted.** Nothing pointed Lemma at it, so its one
  assertion passed vacuously — 35 lines of weight and a test that could not fail.
- **`stream_large_bodies=0` enables streaming** rather than disabling it.
  mitmproxy then passes a response through without keeping it and the recording
  replays as `200 OK (content missing)` — satisfying a status assertion while
  containing nothing. A guard asserts the setting stays absent.

## Verified against real providers

Not a green suite — actual round trips, on a stack wired to the real thing:

- **Telegram** — a real bot answered a real message; `sendRichMessage` observed.
- **GitHub** — `users_get_authenticated` returned the connected login; 50
  operations discovered; an agent without the grant is refused.
- **Slack** — a real workspace app installed and connected via OAuth.
- **Composio** — 69 apps and 7,547 operations imported; Gmail's consent URL
  issued.
- **Resend** — real key on a verified domain; each agent gets a real mailbox.

## What is *not* done

Stated plainly, because the point of this PR is to stop the suite overstating
what it proves:

- `fake_platform.py` still has **7 callers**. The ~40 Telegram surface scenarios
  in `surfaces_and_notifications` are not migrated yet — that is the next PR, and
  the biggest one.
- `LOOPBACK_REACHABLE` and `CONNECTOR_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK_TARGETS` are still
  in pla

author: dborup
body:
## Summary

Hardens `default_scope` evidence protection in the ingestor, closing gaps left by the original #7 fix and adding regression coverage plus a benchmarked design decision.

### Bugs fixed

- **Invalid/missing timestamp on a confirmed write was not rejected.** `UpdateNodeDefaultScopeConfirmed` used to fall through to an unconditional write — including a blank `default_scope_confirmed_at` — when `reportedAt` was missing or unparseable. It now rejects the report outright as a complete no-op before any other work, matching `UpdateNodeConfiguredScope`'s existing contract.
- **Last-write-wins only checked `nodes`.** The old guard read only `nodes.default_scope_confirmed_at`, so a node that existed solely in `inactive_nodes` had no ordering protection at all — an older report could silently clobber a newer confirmation. LWW is now enforced independently, per table, via two conditional `UPDATE`s in one transaction.
- **A packet-inferred write could overwrite confirmation held in the sibling table.** `UpdateNodeDefaultScope` only ever checked the row it was about to write. A node can transiently exist in both `nodes` and `inactive_nodes` (retention moves a node to `inactive_nodes`, but a later re-advert resurrects it as a fresh, unconfirmed row in `nodes` — `UpsertNode`'s `INSERT` never sets `default_scope_confirmed_at`, and the old `inactive_nodes` row isn't deleted). Without cross-table protection, the very next inferred ADVERT would silently downgrade confirmed evidence the moment the node resurrected — and this was directly API-visible, since `/api/nodes` reads only the active row. Both `UpdateNodeDefaultScope` and `BackfillDefaultScopeAsync` now refuse to write when a non-empty `default_scope_confirmed_at` exists for the pubkey in **either** table (`NOT EXISTS` against the sibling table).

### Design notes

- `UpdateNodeDefaultScope`'s guarded transaction is preceded by a read-only fast path (a two-row `UNION ALL` over `nodes`/`inactive_nodes`) that short-circuits the dominant no-write cases (unknown pubkey, confirmed anywhere, value already matches) without ever opening a transaction — this is the hottest MQTT-ingest write in the file. The fast path is **an optimization only, never a correctness authority**: the final `UPDATE`s carry the exact same row-local + cross-table `NOT EXISTS` guards regardless of what the read saw, so a race between the read and the write can only ever defer a harmless inferred update, never let one overwrite confirmed evidence. `default_scope_bench_test.go` benchmarks both candidates (always-transactional vs. fast-path-then-tx) and a dedicated correctness test (`TestDefaultScopeBenchCandidates_Correctness`) pins that both reach identical, correct end states before the timing comparison is trusted.
- Both `nodes` and `inactive_nodes` updates in `UpdateNodeDefaultScope` and `UpdateNodeDefaultScopeConfirmed` run inside a single transaction; a failure on the second `UPDATE` rolls back the first.
- `BackfillDefaultScopeAsync` gets the same local-confirmed-at guard plus a cross-table `NOT EXISTS` against `inactive_nodes`, so a confirmed sibling row blocks the one-time backfill from filling in an unconfirmed resurrection row. The migration marker is only written after a successful run (not on query failure). This PR does **not** make the backfill populate `inactive_nodes` itself, and does not change or clean up orphaned `inactive_nodes` rows — only the existing `nodes` backfill path is protected.
- `default_scope == ""` remains a no-op (defense-in-depth, unchanged); `"*"` (firmware's "no default region" sentinel) continues to pass through unchanged; any other non-empty scope is syntactically `#`-prefixed via `regions.Normalize` (no known-region validation exists, so there's no separate "unrecognized region" no-op path — blank/whitespace-only input is the only way `normalizeSingleScope` produces `""`).
- A single report-level log line (`"configured-scope and default-scope evidence ignored"`) fires once per invalid-timestamp `/neighbors` report, regardless of self/neighbor count — not per evidence type, not per neighbor.
- This PR does not change the resurrection logic itself (retention/`UpsertNode` behavior is untouched) — it only ensures inference and backfill respect confirmed evidence that already exists on either side of that resurrection.

### OpenAPI

`default_scope` and `default_scope_confirmed_at` are now explicitly documented as nullable strings (the latter also `format: date-time`) on the `Node` schema, describing the null/empty/wildcard/provenance contract including the cross-table protection guarantee. No route, endpoint, or API shape change beyond documentation.

### Tests & verification

Two commits, kept separate:
1. `fix(ingestor): protect confirmed default-scope evidence` — the guard changes above, plus new/extended tests in `cmd/ingestor/issue1865_test.go`, `cmd/ingestor/backfill_default_scope_test.go` (new), `cmd/server/default_scope_contract_test.go` (new), `cmd/server/openapi_node_schema_test.go`.
2. `test(ingestor): harden default-scope benchmark validation` — comment-only clarifications in `db.go` plus stronger benchmark-correctness fixtures in `default_scope_bench_test.go` (fixtures now fail loudly on any SQL seed error, snapshot both tables before/after, and check confirmed-anywhere fixtures against their live before-write snapshot rather than a hardcoded value).

Independent verification performed on this exact HEAD (`d88d79ce`):
- `gofmt -l`, `go vet ./...`, and `git diff --check` clean across all changed files in both `cmd/ingestor` and `cmd/server` modules.
- Targeted `DefaultScope` tests: 42/42 passed (ingestor), 14/14 passed (server), including under `-race`.
- `TestDefaultScopeBenchCandidates_Correctness` (the benchmark-candidate correctness pin): 20/20 passed at `-count=20`, and 5/5 passed at `-race -count=5` with zero data races.
- All backfill tests: passing (see flake note below).
- Full suite: `cmd/ingestor` 571/571 passed, `cmd/server` 1718/1718 passed.
- Benchmark (`-bench=DefaultScope -benchtime=3000x -count=3`): confirms the fast-path design claim — on no-write scenarios `FastPathThenTx` is ~2.5–3.4x cheaper than always-transactional `CrossTableTx`; on write-triggering scenarios it's ~15–20% more expensive (paying for the read before falling through to the same transaction), consistent with optimizing for the dominant no-write path.

**Pre-existing, unrelated flakes observed during verification (not introduced by this branch):**
- `TestStatsFileWriter_SampledAtMatchesProcIOSampledAt` — the previously-known isolated flake; reproduced independently of this diff.
- `TestBackfillTxLastSeen_ResolvesFromMaxObservationTimestamp` (`cmd/ingestor/tx_last_seen_backfill_test.go`, not part of this branch's diff) — flaky under isolated reruns (3/10 failures), looks like a timing race against an unrelated async migration goroutine. Passed cleanly in the full-suite run. Flagging for visibility, not fixing here.

No migration, routes, frontend, or MeshView Live changes.

body:
## What changed

- fix DS4 vibration/output transport handling on Windows
  - infer USB vs Bluetooth from validated live DS4 reports instead of trusting WMI alone
  - use HID control-output reports for Bluetooth first, interrupt writes for USB first
  - fall back across both output paths and compatible sibling HID interfaces for clone/composite controllers
  - cache the working control path to avoid repeated timeouts during vibration patterns
  - surface detailed output-path diagnostics instead of a generic timeout only
- make vibration cleanup motor-only so a rumble test no longer turns the controller lightbar off
- stop the 50 ms UI refresh from constantly overwriting vibration test status
- bind the Diagnostics Lab to the active live-session device rather than a potentially different picker selection
- add stick jitter and per-stick health status
- add a radial deadzone preview with a “use recommended” action; preview does not remap the device
- add polling stability classification
- add a full Raw HID Inspector with axes, triggers, buttons, battery, motion and exact report bytes
- include the richer diagnostics in JSON export
- expand clean-room open-source research notes

## Open-source research boundary
Protocol/behavior was cross-checked against public DS4 implementations and documentation, including Linux `hid-playstation`, DS4Windows-family material, and small DS4 utilities. GPL implementation code/assets were not copied; the Windows control-output fallback and UI/analyzers are independently implemented for PadScope’s MIT codebase.

## Validation
- automated tests include output transport correction when WMI connection type is wrong
- bad Bluetooth CRC must not change output transport
- motor-only reset behavior is covered
- Windows build and full test suite must pass before merge

Hardware validation is still required for the user’s specific controller/clone because CI cannot physically verify rumble.

author: julienmartel
body:
## What

Every ⌘Space popup that is supposed to be centred has been off-centre, on every display, since it shipped. `recenter` reads the window's real frame over AX after it exists and sets only its position.

## Why

Three popups pass **both** a pixel size and a cell grid, and those disagree:

```
rebuild.sh    --w 750 --h 400  --cols 80 --rows 20
settings.sh   --w 750 --h 400  --cols 80 --rows 20
add-app.sh    --w 800 --h 480  --cols 84 --rows 24
bench-lane.sh --match-focused          ← correct
peek.sh       --match-focused          ← correct
```

The grid wins. Ghostty rounds to whole cells and will not shrink below the grid it was launched with, so `set_frame`'s size half is quietly declined while its position half sticks — the window is planted at the origin that would have centred the size we asked for, and is then a different size. **The only popups that land right are the two that copy another window's frame.**

Measured from the ring in a screenshot of a 2560×1440 Studio Display:

| | |
|---|---|
| asks for | 750 × 400 |
| actually is | **942 × 554** |
| top edge | **518** — centring 750×400 gives `(1440−400)/2 = 520` ✓ |
| miss | **96 pt right, 77 pt down** = exactly half of each difference |

Also struck: the comment above the exact-mode re-plant read *"harmless when we only wanted roughly centered"*. That clause was the bug in prose — the centred modes are the ones where nothing gets the last word, so they are the ones that drift.

**Not a multi-display bug.** The same offset was on the built-in the whole time; a 1512 pt-wide screen has no room to show it. The external revealed it.

## Verify

- `bats test/float-term-recenter.bats` — 13 cases, wired into the Linux job. Arithmetic over two rectangles with AX and the screen probe stubbed, so it runs in CI rather than needing a Mac and a second monitor, which is what it took to find this.
- Mutation matrix, all eight caught — including three that were **0 red** until the assurance read pointed out the stub returned the same rectangle whichever probe point it got:

```
old bug: centre the REQUESTED size            5 red
drop the numeric guard                        3 red
drop the 200pt floor                          2 red
drop the negative-origin clamp                1 red
probe the INTENDED rect, not the window       1 red
drop the rounding tolerance                   1 red
drop the hit=0 fallback                       1 red
drop recenter's pid guard                     1 red
```

- shellcheck 2 warnings, both pre-existing (this file isn't in CI's lint list either way); `nix flake check`'s `desktop-projection` green; the installed copy in the built home-files parses and carries the call.

**👤 The one thing the arithmetic can't do — please feel it:** ⌘Space → Rebuild with the pointer parked on the **other** monitor. All four callers pass `--pin`, so aerospace moves the window to the summoning workspace before `recenter` runs, and with `mouseFollowsFocus` off that workspace is often on a different display than the cursor. That's why this reads the **window's own** frame rather than geom's rectangle. Check where it lands, and that it doesn't vanish on the next workspace switch.

## Watch out

- **Second commit is the assurance read** and changes the design, not just details: `window_size` → `window_frame`, probing the window's centre rather than the cursor's display. Worth reading over the first.
- `raise` now runs **before** `recenter` — its focus claim is a race against a picker tearing down, and an AX round trip in front of it started that race late. Only the ring has to follow the final frame.
- A 20 pt tolerance means agent-peek (`--w 900 --h 560`, no grid flags) skips the correction rather than paying a jump for cell rounding.
- `exact` records what the **caller** asked for, not what geom resolved. A `--frame` caller whose frame was unusable now clears the flag; geom's own degradation of an unreadable `--match-focused` to `--pct 80` is invisible to `spawn` and is written down rather than claimed fixed — those callers pass no grid flags, so the miss there is rounding, not 96 pt.
- Unrelated but blocking your rebuild: `~/.config/nix/hosts/mbp` sets `haus.displays."136A50A4…".uiScale = "slightly-larger-text"`, which doesn't exist on `main` yet — it's in the `haus/nix` lane (`934ac6f`). `bench try` fails on that, not on this.

author: teinhonglo
body:
### Motivation
- Enable evaluation across multiple stress/emphasis corpora (`tinystress`, `stresstest`, `stresspresso`, and `emphassess`) with a single, reproducible pipeline. 
- Canonicalize and validate heterogeneous dataset formats (especially EmphAssess) and ensure consistent audio/label shapes for the existing training/evaluation code. 
- Automate fetching and validation of external corpora and integrate multi-stage evaluation into the existing `run.sh` workflow.

### Description
- Add `corpora.py` which provides adapters and validators for the supported corpora, canonicalizes sample shape, remaps EmphAssess punctuation-based tokens, validates WAV formats, and exposes `load_corpus`, `compute_stress_binary`, and `validate_emphassess_directory`.
- Add `local/download_corpora.py` to download HF-hosted corpora and the official EmphAssess tarball, with safe extraction and strict validation, and to persist a normalized flat layout.
- Update `evaluation_example.py` to accept `--corpus`, `--split`, and `--data_root`, use `load_corpus`, add coverage reporting for skipped samples, and include corpus-level stats in the JSON output.
- Update `test.py` and `run.sh` to support per-corpus Stage 2 (teacher-forced token metrics) and Stage 3 (word-level evaluation) runs, and produce per-corpus result directories and `stage2_metrics.json` files.
- Modify `utils.py` to reuse `compute_stress_binary` from `corpora.py` and to carry `source_dataset` through the dataset items for downstream reporting.
- Add `tests/test_corpora.py` unit tests covering the adapters, EmphAssess remapping/filtering, WAV validation, and canonical sample checks, and update `README.md` with multi-corpus evaluation instructions and output paths.

### Testing
- Ran unit tests with `pytest tests/test_corpora.py`, which exercise adapters, EmphAssess validation/remapping, and WAV format checks, and they passed. 
- Executed the Stage 2 evaluation script to generate token-level metrics for a downloaded corpus using `python test.py` (produces `stage2_metrics.json`) as a smoke check of the pipeline.

author: micheledelliveneri
body:
Stacked originally on #36 (now merged, so this targets `main`). Follows the [SKA SRC DM product streamer](https://gitlab.com/ska-telescope/src/src-dm/ska-src-dm-product-streamer-api) so a client written against one service works against the other.

## Two layers, two defaults

- **Authentication** — with `auth.enabled`, every request needs a verified token (`auth.requireToken`, default true), except the paths below.
- **Authorisation** — #36's gate set decides which of those additionally need a *decision* about the token; still metadata mutation by default.

So a metadata `GET` needs a valid token and nothing more. A metadata `DELETE` needs one the plugin — IAM groups, or PAPI — approves.

## What needs a token

| Requests | Token | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/tap/availability` | no | a Kubernetes probe cannot hold one |
| `/tap/capabilities`, `/tap/tables`, `/tap/registry`, `/tap/examples` | no | a registry harvester or VO client browsing for services cannot hold one |
| `/api/v1/auth`, `/openapi.json`, `/docs` | no | this is where a client learns how to authenticate at all |
| `GET /tap/sync?REQUEST=getCapabilities` | no | TAP 1.0 capability discovery; the handler redirects it to the open `/capabilities` |
| `/tap/sync`, `/tap/async` + sub-resources | **configurable** | `auth.anonymousQueries`, **off by default** |
| everything else — `/api/v1/<mount>` reads and writes, `/api/v1/query`, `/api/v1/jobs` | yes | a JSON client can authenticate, and is expected to |

### This is a breaking default, deliberately

**PyVO, TOPCAT and every other standard VO client get `401` on an auth-enabled deployment unless `auth.anonymousQueries: true` is set.** They cannot obtain or send a bearer token, so this switch decides whether the service serves them at all — and that is a decision about a deployment's audience, so it is taken rather than inherited.

```yaml
auth:
  enabled: true
  anonymousQueries: true    # serve standard VO clients
```

Turning it on opens exactly two things: a synchronous query, and the UWS job that runs one, sub-resources included. It does **not** open `/api/v1/query` or `/api/v1/jobs` — the switch exists for clients that cannot authenticate, and a JSON client can.

With it on, the same metadata is readable anonymously over `/tap/sync` and token-gated as JSON at `/api/v1/<mount>`. The justification is the client population, not the data. Ownership applies either way: an anonymous caller sees jobs with no owner and gets `403` on a job someone claimed.

`auth.requireToken: false` reverts entirely to the previous behaviour — tokens verified when present, demanded only by the gated operations.

## The challenge

```http
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="skao-tap", ivoa_bearer error="invalid_request",
  error_description="Missing access token",
  discovery_url="https://ska-iam.stfc.ac.uk/.well-known/openid-configuration"
```

RFC 6750 `Bearer` first, so a client reading only the first challenge still learns it needs a token; `ivoa_bearer` carries the discovery URL. The same text is repeated in the error body — JSON `message` on `/api/v1/*`, DALI VOTable on `/tap/*` — because that is where the streamer's reference client reads it.

`invalid_request` (no credential → discover the IAM) and `invalid_token` (credential presented, did not verify → get a fresh token) are distinguished, since the remedy differs. `GET /api/v1/auth` advertises `token_required`, `anonymous_queries` and `discovery_url`, so a client need not provoke a 401 to find the IAM.

**No audience check, no exchange step** — SRCNet tokens are not minted per service here, so there is no second "wrong audience" challenge and no AAPI hop. `auth.iam.allowAnyAudience` stays as the explicit record of that trade: any token the IAM issued to any of its clients is accepted here, so it is set deliberately rather than defaulted.

## Verification

321 unit tests. `tests/unit/test_auth_challenge.py` covers the challenge in header and body, `invalid_request` vs `invalid_token` (including malformed `Authorization` headers), every exempt path, the `needs_token` matrix in both switch positions, TAP 1.0 discovery through `/sync`, and two regression tests for discovery-exemption bypass vectors. Existing tests that encoded the old "reads are anonymous" policy were moved to the new one. `ruff`, `mkdocs --strict`, `helm lint` clean; two new CI chart cases. `docs/auth.md`, `docs/deployment.md` (both value tables), `docs/roadmap.md` and `README.md` are reconciled with these defaults.

author: jazzli
body:
## Summary

Adds a commit template, worked examples, a body-wrap check, and a required digest-impact field on pull requests.

## Rationale

The conventions were stated in `AGENTS.md` and enforced by a hook that rejects a message after it is written. Nothing put them in front of the author at the point of writing, which is where a first draft is decided. For agent-drafted messages in particular, abstract instruction is the weakest form of steering — a position this repository already publishes under `do-context-files-pay-off`.

## Changes

- **`.gitmessage`** — commit template, wired through `git config commit.template`.
- **Worked examples in `AGENTS.md`** — one change shown three ways: subject alone, written as a decision, and written as a work log. The distinction is demonstrated rather than asserted.
- **Body wrap check** in `.githooks/commit-msg`. Recent bodies ran to 76 columns against git's 72.
- **Digest impact** on the pull request template.

## Key decisions

**The wrap check only fails a line that could have been wrapped.** A line over 72 with no space before column 72 — an unbroken URL or path — passes, since demanding a wrap there is impossible to satisfy. Verified against all three cases.

**Digest impact is a required field with `none` as a valid answer.** Adopters run a scheduled check against the top-level digest, so a change that moves it interrupts every one of them. That fact has been recorded in prose when remembered; it is now a field.

**Conventional Commits remains declined.** It exists to drive automated semver and changelog generation. This project has no releases and generates its changelog from the source review log, so the structure would have no consumer.

## Validation

140 tests, link check at 0 errors, both hooks pass. This commit was written under the new wrap rule: longest body line 71.

## Digest impact

none — tooling and documentation only.

author: mm-sheng
body:
## Why

Most third-party Agent directories can generate only a stdio command or a bare remote URL. Bare URLs work but cannot preserve `X-404-Agent-ID`, so successful calls remain anonymous and cannot count as de-duplicated external Agent users.

## What

Adds the dependency-free `404-directory-mcp` npm package:

```json
{
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["-y", "404-directory-mcp"]
}
```

The bridge:
- creates one stable random non-personal ID per MCP client
- hashes the client name before using it as a local directory key
- atomically creates identities so concurrent first starts cannot split one installation into duplicates
- refuses to overwrite invalid identity files
- stores identity only in the normal per-user application data directory
- connects only to the fixed public 404.directory endpoint
- sends the existing privacy-safe attribution headers
- has no runtime dependencies or credentials

## Validation

- `npm test` — 100 passed, 1 skipped
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors; 3 pre-existing warnings
- `npm run mcp:proxy:pack` — 4-file, 4.6 kB tarball
- installed the generated tarball into an empty prefix
- npm-installed binary completed production MCP initialize and tools/list
- production returned `404.directory` v0.9.0 and 12 tools
- regression coverage includes npm bin symlinks, concurrent identity creation, invalid-file refusal, and privacy-safe client directory keys

## Publication gate

Keep this PR as draft until `404-directory-mcp@0.9.0` is published to npm. The package name is currently available, but this machine is not authenticated to npm. Documentation should not reach production before the package exists.

author: jeremyandrews
body:
Seven optimisations to the indexing pipeline, one commit each, every one behind a switch that defaults to the new behaviour, and every one measured on the SML-shaped benchmark harness rather than argued for.

Two of the seven did not do what the plan expected. Both are called out below with the measurement that contradicted it, because the numbers are the point of this PR.

## Results

Measured on the `SmlShapedCorpus` harness (`SCOLTA_BENCH_PAGES` selects the size) on Apple silicon, PHP 8.5.9, conservative budget.

### 20,000 pages

| Build | Shipped (`a3bb7ce`) | This branch | Change |
|-|-|-|-|
| Cold | 9.19 s | 7.50 s | 1.23x |
| Warm, nothing changed | 14.43 s | 5.94 s | **2.43x** |
| One page body edit | 0.824 s | 0.289 s | **2.85x** |
| Chunks rewritten by that edit | 34 | 14 | |

The warm build used to be **1.57x slower than a cold one**, and it is now 0.79x of it. That inversion is the headline. Every page was being re-serialised into a chunk file identical to the one already on disk, and the build forced a garbage collection 400 times on the way.

### 109,308 pages (the real corpus shape, `memory_limit=4G`)

| State | Seconds |
|-|-|
| Cold | 51.47 |
| Warm, nothing changed | 46.92 |
| One page edit | 1.44 |
| Edit plus new page plus delete | 3.38 |

110,873 files in the published index. **2187 of 2187 chunks carried forward** on the warm build.

### Where the warm build's time actually goes now

This is the finding worth carrying into the next round. At 109,308 pages, after chunk reuse, the warm build's own chunk work is **1.5 s of 40 s (3.7%)**. The rest is the merge, which this PR does not touch:

| Phase | Seconds | Share |
|-|-|-|
| `merge_pages_start` (fragment write) | 13.0 | 32.4% |
| `writer_complete` | 9.3 | 23.2% |
| `term_merge_start` | 8.9 | 22.1% |
| `premerge_start` | 6.0 | 14.9% |
| `chunk_reused` (2187 calls) | 1.5 | 3.7% |

93% of a warm build is now the merge and the final write. Chunk assembly is done as an optimisation target; the merge is the next one.

## Differential proof

Chunk reuse and fragment reuse both skip reading the data they reproduce, so "the index looks fine" is not evidence. Every state is compared against the same pipeline with every optimisation switched off, over a **copy of the same ledger** (a fresh ledger renumbers the corpus and renames every fragment for reasons unrelated to the optimisations).

At 109,308 pages:

- warm vs cold, whole directory, decompressed: **IDENTICAL** (110,873 files)
- final state (edit + new page + delete) vs reference build with `reuseFragments: false, reuseChunks: false`: fragments **IDENTICAL**, term postings **IDENTICAL**, page table **IDENTICAL** (110,875 reference files)

At 20,000 and 5,000 pages the same comparisons run in the `benchmark` group as `testTheOptimisedBuildEqualsTheReferenceBuildOnEveryState`, and the byte-level codec patch has its own randomised differential: **420 generated cases, zero mismatches**, comparing `patchEntry()` against decode-mutate-`encodeWordEntry()` across delete at head/middle/tail, insert between postings, replace in place, insert past the end, variant add, and all of those mixed.

## The seven items

**1. Stop forcing a garbage collection after every chunk.** Probed before removing, over 800 calls of a cold-then-warm 20,000-page build: the cycle-root buffer sat at a median of **4,092** entries against the engine's own 10,001 trigger, and `gc_collect_cycles()` returned **0 collected on every single call**. The cost was a heap-proportional scan, 0.68 ms per call below the cold run's median heap, 3.27 ms at or above it, 5.25 ms against the warm run's 198 MB heap, which was 2.1 s of a 14.4 s warm build spent finding nothing. `gc_mem_caches()` is kept but runs every 20 chunks rather than every chunk. Warm 14.43 s → 9.48 s; the `gc` sub-timer 4.5 s → 0.2 s.

**2. gzip level 6 for every artifact, as a `MemoryBudget` setting.** A 20 KB index chunk compresses in 6.3 ms at level 9 and 1.5 ms at level 6. Size cost across a 20,000-page index: `index/` +3.09%, `filter/` +0.28%, `pf_meta` +0.18%, `scolta.facets` +0.93%, whole directory **+0.59%**. `fragment/`, 76% of the bytes, is **byte-identical at both levels**, an 823-byte fragment is too small for the level to move. Cold 8.62 s → 7.73 s on this change alone.

**3. Fragment reuse by hard link, and this one does not do what the plan said.** The plan put read-plus-link at about 0.015 ms against about 0.3 ms to write a fragment. Measured here over 20,000 fragments, each variant in a fresh process writing into its own empty directory:

| operation | macOS APFS |
|-|-|
| `gzencode(6)` + write | 0.0595 ms |
| read + gunzip + `link()` | 0.2384 ms |
| `link()` alone | 0.2172 ms |
| `copy()` alone | 0.0809 ms |

`link()` alone costs **3.6x** what creating and writing the whole file costs, and forcing reuse on took the warm build's page phase from 1.8 s to 6.1 s. Two things are going on: hard links are cheap on the ext4/overlayfs container the original figures came from and expensive on APFS, and **item 2 had already cut the write side 5x**, removing most of the headroom item 3 meant to exploit. Items 2 and 3 are not independent.

So the default is measured, not assumed: `beginWrite()` probes the filesystem once (48 writes against 48 links, well under a millisecond) and takes the cheaper path. A wrong guess costs wall clock and never correctness, since both paths emit byte-identical fragments and the differential tests assert it. `setFragmentReuse(true|false)` overrides either way. On the Linux hosts this package actually deploys to, the probe should pick reuse and cut into that 13 s page phase.

**4. Carry unchanged build chunks forward, cut on ordinal ranges.** A chunk used to be "the next N pages in arrival order", which makes its membership a function of the whole corpus: one delete near the front shifts every later chunk. Range k now holds ordinals `[k*chunkSize, (k+1)*chunkSize)`, and an ordinal is durable, so a page's chunk is a property of the page.

**The key is deliberately not the content hash.** `contentHash()` covers language, title, url and body, because that is all tokenization depends on, while a chunk file also carries filters, sortable values, metadata, date, site name and id. A page whose facets changed but whose body did not has an unchanged content hash and a changed chunk, so a content-hash key would carry forward a stale chunk and publish stale facet postings. `pageIdentity()` hashes everything that reaches the chunk plus the ordinal. There is a test for exactly this case.

Identities are stored per ordinal rather than one key per range, so the build can ask "is this page unchanged?" on arrival, drop the body, and defer the token-cache read to flush time, so a reused chunk reads token data for none of its pages. `PageWordCache::touch()` reports whether the cache holds a hash at all, which is what makes dropping a body safe: a corpus past the manifest cap has unchanged pages with no cache entry, and those resolve eagerly instead. Warm 9.20 s → 5.90 s.

**5. Patch index chunks at the byte level.** A common word's entry holds about 100,000 postings and the terms one edit touches are 78% of a touched chunk's bytes, so decoding "only the touched entries" saves nothing, because the work has to stay inside the entry. `splitEntries()` walks CBOR heads and returns raw entry bytes without building an array (1.0 ms for a 47 KB chunk against 4.7 ms to decode it). `patchEntry()` splices the delta-coded run, rewriting a delta head only when the previous emitted page moved and copying the tail as one slice.

It also fixes the rewrite check, which compared decoded arrays, and array identity includes key order, so an `unset` plus a re-add of the same ordinal read as changed even when the bytes were identical. **34 chunks rewritten → 14.** Edit 0.533 s → 0.409 s.

**6. Keep the corpus tables when nothing they describe has moved.** A body-only edit moves no facet posting, so the `.pf_filter` fi

author: aki-joy
body:
単一モジュール `mazegen.py`（768行）を、責務ごとに分けた `mazegen/` パッケージ（10ファイル 933行）に置き換えます。

## 構造

```
MazeBase (共有状態 + 格子操作)
  ├─ PatternMixin        "42" パターンの配置
  ├─ AnalysisMixin       経路探索・ループ数・行き止まり
  │    └─ CarvingMixin   全域木と編み込み
  └─ VerifyMixin         自己検証
MazeGenerator(CarvingMixin, VerifyMixin)
```

| ファイル | 行 | 中身 |
|---|---:|---|
| `constants.py` | 57 | 壁ビット、向き、大きさの上限、`random_seed` |
| `errors.py` | 7 | `MazeError` |
| `glyphs.py` | 67 | `"42"` のビットマップ字形（`self` を使わない純関数） |
| `base.py` | 169 | `MazeBase`: 状態宣言17行 + 格子操作19メソッド |
| `pattern.py` | 103 | `PatternMixin` |
| `analysis.py` | 86 | `AnalysisMixin` |
| `carving.py` | 152 | `CarvingMixin` |
| `verify.py` | 107 | `VerifyMixin` |
| `generator.py` | 122 | `MazeGenerator` の組み立て |
| `__init__.py` | 63 | 公開 API の再エクスポートとモジュール docstring |

状態は `MazeBase` に**1か所だけ**宣言し、層を素直に積んだので **`@abstractmethod` のスタブは1つも要りません**。`mypy --strict` が通ります。

## あわせて解消した重複と入れ子

分割前の `mazegen.py` に残っていたぶんです。

- 幅優先探索が3か所に写経されていた → `_flood` にまとめる
- 四方の隣を求める定型が4か所 → `_steps_from` にまとめる
- **四隅と中央の座標が `_place_pattern` と `_check_playable` に別々に書かれていた** → `_landmarks` に一本化（片方だけ直すと壊れる同期ハザード）
- `_check_borders` の4辺ぶんのコピペ → `_border_walls` の表
- `_glyph_shape` の五重ループを分解（最大ネスト 5 → 4）
- `_braid` の本体を `_open_dead_end` に分離
- `path_to_directions` の線形探索 → 逆引き表
- 大きさの上限/下限を `MIN_SIZE` / `MAX_SIZE` として公開し `amazeing/config.py` と共有

## 互換性

公開 API は変わりません。

- `from mazegen import MazeGenerator, NORTH, EAST, SOUTH, WEST, Coord, ...` そのまま
- `amazeing/` と `a_maze_ing.py` は**無改造**
- `pydoc mazegen` / `help(mazegen)` も `__init__.py` の docstring でこれまでどおり

## パッケージ化にともなう変更

- `pyproject.toml`: `py-modules` → `packages`
- `mazegen-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl` を作り直し（10ファイル入り）
- `README.md` / `README.ja.md` の構成図と「1つのモジュール」という記述を更新

## 検証

- **main の `mazegen.py` と出力がバイト単位で一致**（54MB のスナップショット: アルゴリズム × perfect × pattern × サイズ × seed × テーマ）
- entry/exit と `pattern_text` を振った **1,928ケースでも差分ゼロ**
- `mazegen` を一切使わない**独立検証器**で `maze.txt` を外から検算（出力形式・隣接壁の一致・外周・経路が実際に歩けるか・最短か・行き止まりゼロ/ループゼロ）→ **288通り OK**
- `make lint-strict`（flake8 + mypy --strict）通過
- ホイールをクリーンな venv に `pip install` して動作確認

`check()` が警告を出すのは 2x2 の playable board のみで、これは main でも同じです（2x2 は独立ループが原理的に1本しか作れないため）。

## レビューの前に

分割によって**総行数は 768 → 933 行（+15%）に増えています**。増分は import +49、空行 +39（PEP8 の区切り）、ファイル docstring +16、状態宣言 +17 です。ロジック自体は減っています（文の数 483 → 467、最大ネスト 5 → 4）。

「1ファイルのままのほうがよい」という判断もありえます。その場合は、上の重複解消だけを `mazegen.py` に適用する版を別途出せます。

## Summary
- Follow-up to #466. The overnight day-end clip added in #464 assumed `civilEndTime` was an RFC-3339 string; the real v4 API returns a `google.type.DateTime`-shaped object (`{date:{year,month,day}, time:{hours,minutes}}`). Every parse was silently failing and falling back to "leave the interval alone" — this only became visible once #466's shape-mismatch logging shipped and immediately caught it live: ~9,000 warnings within minutes of that deploy, all for this one field, at essentially every `activity-level` data point.
- Confirmed against a live payload captured through that same logging:
  ```json
  {"startTime":"2026-08-20T22:58:00Z","civilEndTime":{"date":{"year":2026,"month":8,"day":20},"time":{"hours":23,"minutes":59}}}
  ```
- Added `ParseCivilDateTime` to read the actual shape (reusing the existing `ReadInt` shape-safe helper).
- Fixed the existing test fixture (`ActivityLevelPointWithCivil`) — it had been asserting against the same wrong (string) shape, which is exactly why this shipped undetected: the test was "passing" against a fixture that didn't match reality.
- Not a stability issue (thanks to #466, a malformed `civilEndTime` was already degrading gracefully) — this restores the actual clip behavior the feature was meant to have.

## Test plan
- [x] `dotnet build` — full solution, 0 warnings/errors
- [x] `dotnet test` — `GoogleHealthApiClientTests` (83/84 passing; the one failure, `GetGranularDayAsync_PacesPageRequests_AfterTheFirst`, is a pre-existing flaky timing test unrelated to this change — passes in isolation)

## Summary

Adds a Slack Incoming-Webhook alert pipeline so the AGL portal can post operational alerts to the team's Slack channel (`#agl-portal-alerts`). Until now the portal only had Web Push + in-app realtime notifications; there was no Slack integration at all. This is the net-new foundation discussed with the team.

## What's included

- **`supabase/functions/send-slack/index.ts`** — new Deno Edge Function mirroring the existing `send-push` structure (CORS preamble, `Deno.serve`, `json()` helper, secrets via `Deno.env.get`). Posts a Block Kit message to the webhook in the `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` secret. No-ops safely (returns `{ skipped: true }`, never errors) when the secret is unset, so it can be deployed before setup is finished.
- **`src/slackNotify.js`** — pure, unit-tested formatter (`formatLeaveEvent`, `formatOvertimeEvent`) that turns leave/overtime events into `{ text, title, level }`, following the same pure-module pattern as `leaveWorkflow.js`.
- **`sendSlack()`** in `src/supabasePortal.js` — sibling to `sendPush()`, invokes the `send-slack` function.
- **`app.jsx` wiring** — posts **exactly once per event** (outside the per-recipient push loops): new leave request, new overtime request, and final leave/overtime approval or rejection. The intermediate TL-approval and withdrawals are deliberately not posted, to keep the channel quiet.
- **Tests** — `tests/slackNotify.test.js` covering submitted/approved/rejected for both event types plus missing-field cases.
- **Docs** — `docs/SLACK.md` operator guide (create webhook, set `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`, `supabase functions deploy send-slack`) plus a README pointer.

## Validation

- `npm run lint` — clean
- `npm test` — 734 tests pass (includes new suite)
- `npm run build` — succeeds

## Follow-up for the operator

The pipeline is inert until an Incoming Webhook is created for `#agl-portal-alerts` and its URL is set as the `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` Edge Function secret, then `send-slack` is deployed. Steps are in `docs/SLACK.md`.
