author: chenmingwei23
body:
## What is the problem?

Two sibling call sites outside Code Review Sage carry the defects PR #4979 fixed inside it, found by that PR's review lanes and deliberately left out as unrelated scope (#4987):

1. `dashboard/handlers/core.py` rendered the Windows transcribe install command as `& "<sys.executable>" -m pip install "kirocrew[voice]"`. A double-quoted PowerShell string still expands `$name` and honours backtick escapes -- both legal Windows path characters -- so an interpreter under e.g. `C:\tools\$python\...` is silently rewritten into a path that does not exist.
2. Owner-only lockdowns expressed as raw `chmod(0o600)` at ~9 sites. On Windows that call only toggles the read-only attribute and *succeeds*, so the file stays readable through the directory's inherited DACL and nothing surfaces the gap. `platform_compat.restrict_to_owner` is the existing helper that applies a real owner-only DACL there -- but it spawns `icacls` (a blocking subprocess), so it must never run on the asyncio event loop.

## Why this issue matters to the user

Both defects are latent on POSIX and live on Windows. The copy-paste install command is the one user-visible surface for enabling Transcribe on Windows; when it silently corrupts the interpreter path the user gets an unexplained failure on a command the product told them to run. The chmod sites are worse than an absent guard: the source reads as if Slack tokens in `.env` and inline credentials in `config.json` are protected, and on Windows they are not.

## How our fix solves it

**Shell quoting** (`dashboard/handlers/core.py`): the user's shell is unknowable (PowerShell or cmd), so the emitted form must be free of *silent* corruption in both. PowerShell is the harder shell: a double-quoted string AND a bare unquoted token both expand `$names` and honour backticks. The command now uses PowerShell's literal form -- `& '<exe>' -m pip install kirocrew[voice]`, with a quote in the path escaped by doubling. Single quotes expand nothing and carry spaces (so the all-users `C:\Program Files\...` layout works); cmd performs no `$`/backtick processing and rejects the leading `&` loudly, so a cmd user gets a clear re-quote error, never a corrupted install. (A truly shell-neutral unquoted form was considered and rejected: unquoted tokens are still `$`-expanded by PowerShell, and spaces would break both shells.)

**Owner-only lockdown**, adjudicated per site as the issue asks ("this list is a starting point, not a verdict"):

| Site | Verdict | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `cli_setup.py` (.env Slack tokens) | converted | now `atomic_write(restrict_to_owner=True, restrict_on_error="warn")`: the unique temp is locked BEFORE any token byte reaches it, a lockdown refusal logs a warning instead of aborting the wizard after the user typed their tokens (the `.env` doctrine, matching the dashboard credential writers), and a failure leaves the previous `.env` untouched. Was the last `.env` writer not on the helper. |
| `apps/routes.py` `_sync_builtin_config` (config.json) | converted | hand-rolled fixed-name tmp+chmod+replace replaced by `update_config_locked`, the required path for new config.json mutations: the whole read-modify-write runs under an advisory sidecar FILE lock (serialized against every other converted writer and other processes, which an in-process lock could not offer), the write is mode-preserving and symlink-safe, and a corrupt config fails closed. Followed off-loop by the Windows `restrict_to_owner` lockdown the shared helpers deliberately leave to their callers (warn on refusal). Both async call sites offload via `asyncio.to_thread` (file I/O + icacls must not run on the loop). Known residual, stated plainly: the DACL lasts until any OTHER config.json writer replaces the inode -- the legacy `write_config_atomically` call sites apply no DACL, so on Windows the file periodically reverts to the directory-inherited ACL (the pre-PR posture for every writer); a systemic fix belongs in the shared helper, not this PR. |
| `config/loader.py` `load_credentials` | gated to POSIX | loop-reachable reader (async request handlers): the icacls spawn is forbidden there and the chmod was already a Windows no-op. Windows enforcement lives at the writers, all off the loop. |
| `workflows/store.py`, `sel.py:568` | documented keep | both loop-reachable (registry persist hooks; the critical audit-or-deny SEL write); workflow payload is redacted before serialization. |
| `mcp_gateway/apps.py:175` | no change | already applies `restrict_to_owner` on non-POSIX. |
| `sel.py:966` (rotation lock) | no change | the file holds no data (existing comment says so). |
| `pod/runtime.py` | no change | pod runtime is systemd-only, unreachable on Windows. |
| `metrics/local_exporter.py` | no change | aggregate telemetry with no content; its chmod runs on every export, where a per-export subprocess spawn is not worth a non-secret file. |

## What tests we did

- New/updated regression tests: PowerShell-literal command shape (exact match with a spaced `C:\Program Files` path; `$`-path and quote-doubling survival), lock-before-content ordering and warn-on-refusal wizard survival in `cli_setup`, `update_config_locked` routing with mode preservation, the Windows off-loop lockdown branch, and failure propagation in `_sync_builtin_config`, a source ratchet that both call sites stay on `asyncio.to_thread`, and the POSIX-only gate in `load_credentials`.
- All eight fix mechanisms mutation-verified: reverting each one (quoted form back, chmod back, lock removed, ordering swapped, POSIX gate dropped, warn flipped to raise, quote-doubling dropped, to_thread removed) turns its test red.
- Local gates: isort, flake8, black (touched non-baseline files), mypy clean on touched files; full pytest with failures confirmed host-environment-only by a pristine-main control run on the same host.
- Two model-pinned pre-push review lanes (GPT + Opus); every finding verified against code and fixed forward: the `.env` lockdown-failure exposure window, the wizard abort on ACL-refusing hosts, the fixed-temp-name race introduced by the to_thread offload, and the spaces regression in the first quoting attempt.

## Any other suggestions on the work

`workflows/store.py` and `sel.py`'s append path remain POSIX-tightening-only because they are loop-reachable; if a hard Windows owner-only guarantee is later wanted there, the write paths would need the same split-and-offload treatment #4979 applied (snapshot on the loop, write+lockdown in a thread) -- a larger change than this fix should carry.

Closes #4987

author: youssefegabi
body:
Calls that are never answered produce no ElevenLabs conversation, so the post-call webhook that normally delivers a result to Tamweely never fires and those calls reach Tamweely with no outcome at all. This middleware is the only component that knows about them, so it now pushes them itself via POST /v1/data/add-call-result/by-tracking-id/{trackingId}?status=

Off by default: ADD_CALL_RESULT_ENABLED plus a base URL and API key are all required before anything is sent.

The push set is deliberately narrower than the Status values written to BatchCallDetails, because a pushed Cancelled/Timeout permanently overwrites FinalOutcome and SummaryArabic on Tamweely's side:

  ring timeout                  -> Timeout
  SIP 486 Busy                  -> Cancelled
  client hangup before answer   -> Cancelled

  SIP 503                       -> NOT pushed (PBX/trunk failure, not the
                                   customer declining)
  shutdown-initiated hangup     -> NOT pushed (a deploy, not customer
                                   behaviour)
  answered / Transfer / TranFail -> NOT pushed (ElevenLabs path owns those)

Delivery mirrors WebhookSender (F-18): no pool thread ever sleeps, retries run on daemon Timers with jittered backoff, and anything undeliverable is dead-lettered for manual re-push. HTTP 200 does not mean success -- the endpoint returns 200 for both not-found and Tamweely-side failures, so the isSuccess field is what decides, checked with `is True` rather than truthiness. isSuccess:false is retried because it is usually the row-arrives-late race in CALL_STATUS_TRACKING.md; validationErrors and 401 are treated as permanent.

A pending retry is claimed by whichever of its timer or shutdown() first pops its entry, so each record is either submitted or dead-lettered, never both and never neither. Timer.is_alive() cannot make that call: a Timer stays alive while its callback runs, so shutdown would read an executing retry as pending and dead-letter a result that then succeeds.

request_hangup() gains a reason and is first-writer-wins under the status lock, so a shutdown drain racing an API hangup cannot be relabelled "api" and pushed as customer no-answer.

Verified against live calls on 2026-08-23: a busy extension pushed Cancelled 34 ms after 486, an unanswered extension pushed Timeout after a 45 s ring-out, three pushes accepted first attempt with no dead letters, and push_async measured 0.6 ms on the SIP thread.

Delivery is at-least-once and the endpoint gives no idempotency guarantee; ADD_CALL_RESULT.md records that as the remaining question for Tamweely before this is enabled in production.

body:
## Description

Follow-up from an agent-ergonomics review of CONTINUUM: "the contract is the instruction set, make it executable." Resume/validate named blocked items (`reconcile_action:action_abc`) without saying what to do about them.

`RecoveryDecision` now renders `human_steps`: executable next steps derived from the plan plus whatever automation this project registered:

- Reconcile step + registered probe (#218) -> one command: `continuum reconcile <run>`
- Reconcile step, no probe -> the external check to perform plus the exact `continuum_reconcile_action(run_id=..., action_key=..., occurred=true|false)` call, with the reason it is manual stated
- `human_review` -> verify yourself, then `continuum confirm <run>`
- Dependency/evidence/model steps -> their concrete re-pin or re-validation action
- Gate configured (#217) -> routing reminder so new side effects go through claims

Surfaced identically in CLI text ("Next steps:"), CLI JSON (`human_steps`), MCP `continuum_resume`, and the sidecar's mirrored payload (parity test extended). Guidance is strictly rendering over existing state and config files: nothing is executed by CONTINUUM, and `requires_human` steps remain human-gated.

## Related issues

Advances #213 (agent ergonomics follow-up); no single tracking issue.

## Types of changes

- Type: `feature`

## Breaking changes

No

## How has this been tested?

```
python -m pytest            # 1192 passed, 12 skipped
ruff check src tests        # clean
ruff format --check         # clean
mypy src                    # Success: no issues found in 91 source files
```

Eight new tests in `tests/test_recovery_guidance.py`: derivation rules (probe vs no-probe wording, confirm mapping), CLI JSON/text carriage, validate parity, gate-presence surfacing, and a real stdio MCP round trip asserting `human_steps` arrives through the wire. The sidecar resume-parity test was extended to cover the new field, which caught that `serve` needed the same projection.

Verified live: an uncertain `send_invoice` run renders step 1 as "check whether 'send_invoice' actually reached the outside world, then call continuum_reconcile_action(...)"; after registering a probe the same run renders "run `continuum reconcile inv` to settle it automatically".

## Checklist

Tests added or updated for the changed behaviour. Documentation updated where the change affects user-facing behaviour. CI passes on the latest commit. Security-relevant changes state known limitations explicitly in this description.

## Additional context

Inspired by an LLM-agent critique asking CONTINUUM to make contracts executable rather than descriptive. Deliberately not adopted from the same critique: an orchestrating `continuum run` command (contradicts the documented non-orchestrator scope refusal) and trusting MCP provenance without confirm (that gate is the anti-self-certification fix).

  * Added actionable recovery guidance to resume and validation results.

  * Next steps are available in CLI text and JSON output, MCP responses, and sidecar payloads.
  * Guidance is informational only and does not execute actions.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for recovery guidance and its CLI, MCP, and sidecar integrations.

author: hydrapse
body:
Harness prerequisites for the v1.0.2 filter campaigns (#25, #26), per `docs/maintainers/v1.0.2-release-plan.md` §2 (PR #41). No scoring formula, classification, image or test-byte change.

## R1: filter lists are validated, the P2P subtraction is an intersection
- `evaluator.validate_filter_list(filter_list, classification, milestone_id)`: every `invalid_pass_to_pass` id must be in `stable_classification.pass_to_pass`, every `invalid_fail_to_pass` / `invalid_none_to_pass` id in `fail_to_pass ∪ none_to_pass` (the filter merges those keys); no duplicate within or across buckets; `version` absent or 1; no `condition` on an entry. `validate_workspace_filter_lists(workspace_root)` runs it over every `test_results/<MID>/<MID>_filter_list.json`.
- `run_e2e` refuses to start or resume a trial on an invalid list (before any trial state exists).
- `generate_filtered_evaluation` fails closed on an invalid list: no derivative written, an existing one moved to `.stale`, the raw result stamped `filter_list_error` + `scoring_blocked: true`.
- `filter_evaluation_result(..., p2p_universe=...)`: with the classification at hand the P2P requirement is reduced by `len(invalid_p2p ∩ universe)`, not by the raw count; `None` keeps today's bytes (all 93 shipped lists are unaffected; the defect was an id outside the bucket lowering `pass_to_pass_required` without removing an obligation).
- `collect_ran_test_ids(cell_dir)`: the one `ran_test_ids` rule (union over `artifacts/*/eval.json`), used by the evaluator, the re-tally and the gate.

## R2: `rescore.py --mode filter-only`
- Inputs per cell: the stored raw `evaluation_result.json` (never a filtered file), the pinned classification (drift = non-promotable), the validated filter list, `ran_test_ids` by the union rule. No replay selection: a non-replayable or frozen pass-wins cell has a derivative exactly as stale as any other (`--mode mirror` would strand 368 + 288 published cells).
- The derivative is regenerated with the envelope's resolution locks re-applied (a waiver never un-locks a cell) and N2P missing adjusted for waived ids that never ran.
- Mirror per cell: byte-identical copy of the raw result (so `promote_cells.py` leaves it alone), the derivative, or none when the milestone has no filter list and a stale derivative must be deleted; `rescore_manifest.json` (mode, `--campaign`, filter-list sha256 + entry counts, classification sha256 + pin, ran count, locks; a previous manifest is kept under `supersedes`); `PROMOTION_NOTES.md`. No artifacts.
- Statuses: `filter-regenerated`, `filter-identity` (verified no-op on re-run), `stale-derivative`, `no-filter`, `non-promotable:<reason>`, `error:<reason>`; any error exits 1. Every mode now refuses to start on an invalid filter list (exit 2). `promote_cells.py` needs no change.

## R3: release gate checks derivatives
- `scripts/check_record_consistency.py`: a served cell in a universe with a non-empty filter list and no `evaluation_result_filtered.json` fails (`derivative missing`: the collector would serve the raw result, so a half-finished campaign would pass); a derivative is compared against the shared regeneration (union rule, locks re-applied, `resolved` included); an invalid filter list fails every served cell of the repo as rows, not as a crash.

## Docs and tests
- `docs/maintainers/re-evaluation.md`: "Filter-list campaigns (filter-only re-tally, v1.0.2)".
- `tests/e2e/test_evaluator_filter.py` (+13), `tests/e2e/test_rescore_filter_only.py` (new, 16), `tests/e2e/test_check_record_consistency.py` (+4), `tests/e2e/test_scikit_collection_death_golden_replay.py` (new, 6: golden replay of the published scikit `_claude-code_glm-5.2_run_002/M12.1` cell under the v1.0.2 M12.1 list, fixture 23 KB trimmed to what the filter arithmetic reads; re-checks against the full inputs when present). Full suite: 1,176 passed.

## Run against the published record (this machine)
- Baseline gate with this branch over the published record before any data change: every repo ok/accepted except dubbo, 260 cells `filter list invalid` (the M024 wrong-bucket `invalid_fail_to_pass` entries, 8 errors; the v1.0.2 data branch deletes them).
- Filter-only campaign `v102-filters` on the v1.0.2 data branch (working copy), 2,892 served cells: 2,031 derivatives regenerated, 0 errors, 46 resolved F→T / 0 T→F, per-cell identical to the dry-runs; `promote_cells.py` dry-run: every cell `result=same artifacts=unchanged filtered=copy`; gate simulation with the mirror derivatives in place: 2,891 ok + 1 accepted (classification drift), 0 failures. Details in PR #41 §10 and `SWE-Milestone-data/reeval/v102-filters/SCORE_DELTA_v102-filters.md`. Promotion and publication await the maintainer.

The same drift as #166, two PRs later. AUDIT-143 is a **security fix** and AUDIT-145 documents where an authority guarantee stops; both landed after `0.14.0`'s section was written and sat under `Unreleased`.

Tagging with them there would publish a version whose changelog omits a security fix that is present in the tree. `0.14.0` is still untagged, so it is still a draft.

Bullets asserted rather than eyeballed: 21 before, 21 after, identical set, and `Unreleased` is empty.

That this has now happened twice says the fold belongs in the release procedure rather than in somebody's memory. Noted for the runbook — not fixed in the commit that immediately precedes a tag.

## Summary

- honor Claude bypassPermissions for ordinary tool callbacks so Write and Bash do not surface blocking permission cards
- coalesce concurrent permission responses and replay recent resolutions to dismiss stale client cards safely
- reset failed permission actions and show a visible toast instead of leaving the card in a silent spinner state
- forward-integrate the fix with Paseo 0.5.1 main

## Current 0.5.1 reproduction

The official 0.5.1 desktop-managed daemon reproduced this across multiple Claude bypass sessions. Permission cards accumulated even though the provider no longer had matching pending requests, so responses failed with `No pending permission request`. Reloading affected sessions cleared the old cards, but new Bash/Write/Edit cards appeared again as the active bypass turn continued.

## Verification

- Claude provider + AgentManager focused tests: 242 passed
- full workspace typecheck passed on 0.5.1 main

- isolated 0.5.1 daemon real Claude bypass smoke created `PASEO_BYPASS_OK\n` (16 bytes) with zero pending permissions

### Changes

author: yukon-autoresearch[bot]
body:
Yukon submission `ac3ef103-befe-4619-a893-93d222d78eb8` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/flock-challenge-multi at `7791f7e0c80def15d6607dd4d4b75e1bd2d234ca`.

Current best score: 1432042.75922438. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Grok 4.6

# 16-wide AVX-512 G-function with two 8-block drains

Effort: high
Agent: Grok
Harness: Grok Build / Yukon CLI

## Goal

Raise `262144 / median(100 verified seconds)` on the c7i.4xlarge Sapphire Rapids runner. Crown at submit: **1,432,042.76 cps** (`9d3dcaa` / `7791f7e`). Editable paths only. This archive is the promoted tree plus one mechanism in the BLAKE3 witness builder.

Prior rows from this account, both reverted before this work:

- `dd97c9a`: xmm-resident Karatsuba `F128::Mul`. Verified, **1,429,697.84 cps**, not promoted.
- `de20b87`: `POOL_MODE = phys8` (8 rayon workers on 8 physical cores). Verified, **1,224,003.46 cps**, not promoted. Topology is restored to `pin16`.

This row does not restack either of those.

## What changed

The ranked witness builder already walks compressions in groups of 16, but the G-function is 8×u32 in YMM (`build_octa_witness_ab_stream_elide`). Each group is two sequential octa dumps. Sapphire Rapids has 512-bit `vpaddd`, `vprold`, and `vpternlogd` with the same port layout as the 256-bit forms, so the 8-wide loop leaves half of each of those instructions unused.

This submission runs the **G-function, carry-part algebra, and rotates on ZMM (16×u32)**. After each vector result the ZMM is split to two YMM and fed to **two existing 8-block `Drain8` / `W8` paths**. Packed z/a/b stay 8-block-major. Round-1 streaming projection stays one `StreamProj` per eight blocks. Lincheck, NTT, PCS, and zerocheck readers are untouched.

Files:

- `crates/flock-prover/src/r1cs_hashes/blake3_witgen8.rs` — ZMM helpers, `build_hex_witness_ab_stream_elide`, `witgen16_enabled`, shared `prepare_octa_inputs`.
- `crates/flock-prover/src/r1cs_hashes/blake3.rs` — rayon group of 16 on the streaming path dispatches one hex dump instead of two octa dumps when AVX-512F is present.

Kill switch: `FLOCK_NO_WITGEN16=1` restores the two-octa loop in the same binary. The ranked worker env is cleared, so the 16-wide arm is what scores on SPR. AVX2 hosts never enter it (`is_x86_feature_detected!("avx512f")`).

## Why this shape

The drain is the part that knows 8-block row-major layout, NT store pairing, spread publication, and the fused round-1 window transform. Duplicating that for 16-block rows would touch every packed-row reader. Splitting ZMM → two YMM after the ALU, then reusing `Drain8`, keeps the published bytes equal to two octa dumps of the same 16 compressions.

Carry packing still runs in `W8::push` / `vsli_v8` after the split, so the 8-wide `VPTERNLOGD` 0xF8 path and the AVX2 fallback stay on the drain side. The new ZMM path uses `_mm512_ternarylogic_epi32::<0xF8>` and `_mm512_ror_epi32` for the G-function itself — the same boolean and the same rotate counts (16/12/8/7) as the 8-wide G.

`add_carry_parts_v16` is the same algebra as `add_carry_parts_v8`: `sum = x+y`, `left = sum^y`, `right = sum^x`. The unused AND carry is still computed so LLVM's DCE decision matches the 8-wide form.

Closed-form inputs are two `prepare_closed_inputs` results merged with `_mm512_inserti64x4`. That reuses the existing AVX2 and AVX-512DQ generators; lanes 0..7 and 8..15 are exactly octa `base` and `base+8`.

## Exactness

For seeds where the 16-wide arm runs, the 16 compressions are the same `OctaInputs` the two-octa loop would have built. G-function lanes are independent. Splitting a ZMM to two YMM is a register partition, not a shuffle of values across the 8+8 boundary. Each `Drain8` then sees the same 8 YMM streams the octa builder would have produced.

A unit test `hex_dump_matches_two_octas` fills z/a/b two ways (two octa dumps vs one hex dump) on closed-form inputs and asserts equality. It is compiled into the crate; it returns immediately on hosts without AVX-512F.

The streaming projection is two `StreamProj` values with disjoint `out` ranges and disjoint staging (`STREAM_STAGE_WORDS` apart). `live` bits follow the same `skip_blocks` rule as the octa loop. Task scratch allocation is doubled for staging when the 16-wide switch is on (~3 KiB extra per rayon task).

## Dispatch

Inside `generate_round1_inner_octa`, a group of 16 on the streaming fused path (`ab_nt && winstream`, the ranked default) calls `build_hex_witness_ab_stream_elide` when:

- `n_here >= 16` (last rayon chunk of 8 stays on the octa loop),
- `witgen16_enabled()` (no `FLOCK_NO_WITGEN16`),
- `std::is_x86_feature_detected!("avx512f")`.

The fused whole-block window path (`ab_nt` without winstream) is unchanged: it still reuses one 8-block window across two sequential octas. Hex is streaming-only so that window geometry is not widened.

The hex function is `#[target_feature(enable = "avx512f")]` without `#[inline(always)]`. It is present in the challenge binary even when the compile host is AVX2 (confirmed: `nm` shows `build_hex_witness_ab_stream_elide` in `flock-benchmark-worker` built with this machine's `target-cpu=native`). SPR `-C target-cpu=native` enables AVX-512F, so the runtime detect is true there.

## Commands

```
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native" \
  cargo +1.97.0 build --locked --offline --profile challenge \
    --target-dir target/challenge-candidate -p flock-benchmark-worker

nm -C target/challenge-candidate/challenge/flock-benchmark-worker | grep build_hex

BLAKE3_LOG2=10 BLAKE3_WARMUP_RUNS=0 BLAKE3_RUNS=2 ./benchmark.sh
```

Local trusted smoke (this AVX2 VM, 16-wide arm not entered): both measured trials `verified=true`. Tiny-batch cps is not a ranked estimate.

`cargo +1.97.0 test --locked --offline --lib -p flock-prover hex_dump_matches_two_octas` skips here (`avx512f` false) and compares dumps on SPR.

## Local measurement limits

This development box is AMD EPYC without AVX-512. The 16-wide function is linked but never called. Local seed→proof times therefore measure the 8-wide octa path only and are not a price of this change. Official scoring rebuilds with `-C target-cpu=native` on Sapphire Rapids, where AVX-512F is present and the dispatch condition is true.

## Implementation notes that matter for the emitted code

ZMM helpers use `#[target_feature(enable = "avx512f")]` and not `#[inline(always)]` (that pairing is a compile error). Shift immediates on `_mm512_srli_epi32` / `_mm512_slli_epi32` are `u32` const generics; rotate immediates on `_mm512_ror_epi32` stay `i32` to match the 8-wide G call sites (16, 12, 8, 7).

`prepare_octa_inputs` is shared so the hex merge cannot drift from the octa generator. Slice input still transposes 8×8 then merges; closed input skips the transpose and uses the existing word-major SIMD generator twice.

Prologue words 16..35, rolling `W8` epochs, zero tail from `USEFUL_BITS`, and the deferred CV/out_hi band 0 are all issued twice, once per drain, in the same order as two octa calls. B-side `MAX` fills use the split of a 16-wide all-ones vector.

Rayon grain is still `GROUP = 16`. The change is inside one task: one 16-wide G instead of two 8-wide G calls, not a coarser parallel split.

## Caveats

- If AVX-512F is absent, this binary is the crown witness builder. That is the AVX2 fallback, not a second algorithm.
- Register file: 16 state ZMM + 16 message ZMM fills the architectural 32 ZMM. Temps spill to L1. The bet is that 512-bit G-function ops still pay for that spill on SPR.
- Two `Drain8` in one task double the in-flight NT-store set versus one octa. Spread publication (`drain_range_spread`) still spaces stores per block inside each drain. Both drains run the same spread schedule.
- Proof size is unchanged (same witn

author: fabkho
body:
The architecture page still rendered its opening line twice:

> There is one engine. Everything else is a way of reaching it.
> There is one engine. Everything else is a way of reaching it.

## Cause

Moving `description` under `seo:` was not sufficient. **Nuxt Content derives a description from a page's first paragraph when the frontmatter omits one**, and Docus renders `page.description` under the heading — so removing the key just swapped one subtitle for a copy of the opening line.

Pages opening with a **heading** were unaffected. That is exactly why it survived my check: I verified `/introduction/why`, which opens on `## The Problem`, saw no subtitle, and concluded the sweep was clean. It opens with a heading, so there was no first paragraph to derive from.

## Fix

An explicit `description: ''` stops the derivation. `seo.description` still feeds the meta tag and the OG image.

The generator emits the same pair, so the ~40 reference pages hold the line without anyone maintaining them.

Swept all **289 rendered routes** for a sentence repeated immediately after the title. Zero remain.

## Regression test

The failure is invisible on more than half the pages — any page opening with a heading looks fine — and the fix is one line of frontmatter, so this is precisely the kind of thing that comes back.

The test fails if a page omits the key, or gives it a value. **Verified in both directions**: removed the key from the architecture page and watched two assertions fail, restored it and watched them pass.

Fallow flagged that the two content tests walked the tree with identical code; that walk is now shared.

## Verified

289 routes, exit 0. 1058 CLI + 37 MCP + 35 nuxt + 83 docs tests. Lint, typecheck, fallow clean. Reference regeneration leaves no drift.

author: chefboyrdave21
body:
## What broke

`embed_url` moved to the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` endpoint on the .100 Arc iGPU during the mxbai-arc cutover, but `reconcile.embed()` only recognised Ollama's native `{"embeddings": [...]}` shape.

Every batch therefore read as a failure: the recursion halved the batch, truncated the last text, burned four attempts and raised `embed failed`. The `skmemory-sync@` cron has been red and **983 memories sat unvectorised** in skmem-pg, with no signal louder than one line of output.

`PGVectorBackend._embed` already handled both shapes, which is why search kept working and this stayed quiet.

## Fix

`_embeddings_from_response()` handles both wire shapes and sorts OpenAI `data` rows by `index` so vectors come back in request order.

## Verification

- 4 new unit tests over both shapes, reordering, and error payloads
- `pytest -k "reconcile or sync or embed"` → 112 passed, 1 skipped
- Live `skmemory sync --vector`: `backfilled=986 pruned=1019 embedded=13680/13680`

## Summary

Follow-up to #52. The user tested the redesigned expense form on a real iPhone and sent screenshots showing the "طريقة الدفع" (payment method) `<select>`, in the collapsed-defaults expanded state, rendering with Safari's native up/down-arrow select chrome instead of the flat custom-chevron style used everywhere else in the redesign.

Root cause: this one `<select>` was missing `appearance-none` — unlike the currency and category selects added in #52, which already had it and render correctly (confirmed in the same screenshots). Chromium-based e2e tests never caught this because Chromium doesn't replicate WebKit's native form control rendering; this is purely a Safari-on-real-device issue.

## Fix

Added `appearance-none` plus a custom `ChevronDown` icon overlay to the payment-method select, matching the exact treatment already used for currency/category.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run lint && npm run typecheck` clean.
- [x] e2e: `balances-math.spec.ts`, `critical-flow.spec.ts`, `delete-empty-trip.spec.ts`, `soft-delete-trash.spec.ts` — all green (functional confirmation that the select still works).
- [ ] **Not verified in this environment**: actual visual rendering on Safari/iOS. This machine has no full Xcode install (only CLI tools), so the iOS Simulator tooling isn't available, and Chromium can't reproduce WebKit's native `<select>` chrome either way. `appearance: none` on `<select>` is a well-established, standard fix across all evergreen browsers including Safari, so confidence is high, but the user should re-test on their iPhone once this merges.

author: jeremiah-k
body:
## Overview

While a radio is disconnected, the periodic heartbeat tick rejects every send. Both the heartbeat sender and the BLE transport logged each rejected handoff at warn severity with no bound, so an out-of-range or powered-off node produced roughly one hundred twenty warn lines per hour — observed directly in a captured field log.

This keeps the first two consecutive heartbeat rejections at warn and demotes subsequent consecutive rejections to debug until a successful send resets the streak. It also suppresses the duplicate transport-unavailable warning only for heartbeat handoffs, while ordinary sends and BLE backlog rejection retain their warnings. Reconnection after an absence still surfaces at full severity because any successful heartbeat resets the counter.

## Key Changes

* Add `HeartbeatRejectionLogPolicy`, a small internal policy that tracks consecutive rejected handoffs and returns the severity to log.
* Keep rejection logging outside the nonce mutex so logging work never extends the critical section.
* Demote rejections beyond the two-rejection warn limit to debug; reset the streak on any accepted send.
* Route BLE and Android serial heartbeat callbacks through a quiet transport-unavailable path without changing admission decisions for ordinary sends or BLE backlog rejection.
* Keep touched transport diagnostics free of raw device identifiers.
* Keep the policy decoupled from Kermit so tests exercise it without process-wide logger configuration.

## Testing

* Added sender-level coverage proving the first rejections use warn severity and later consecutive rejections demote to debug.
* Added sender-level coverage proving a successful send resets the streak so the next rejection warns again.
* Added BLE and Android serial transport coverage proving offline heartbeats suppress the generic transport warning while ordinary sends retain it, and that BLE backlog rejection still warns.

## Scope

* Heartbeat cadence, encoding, and transport admission decisions are unchanged.
* Accepted-heartbeat handling and post-send drain scheduling are unchanged.
* No protocol or persistence changes are introduced.

author: firatcand
body:
**Part of #364** — deliberately NOT "Closes". Two acceptance criteria ship partial with tracked owners (see Governance below).

## What

A consolidate-and-prove ticket: most of what #364 asks for was built incrementally across earlier work, so this branch's job was to **prove it adversarially**, fix what the proofs exposed, and map what remains.

**Five disclosed product hardenings** (each with regression tests):
- `brain fs put` — raw `readFileSync` → bounded capped read (64 MiB).
- `brain fs get` — output through an `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK` open with an `fstat` regular-file re-proof before any write (a reader-less FIFO fails `ENXIO`; a FIFO *with* a reader is refused with zero bytes diverted), plus a looping writer with a zero-progress guard.
- `brain mount` — bounded read.
- `doctor` `.env` — hardened bounded reader + atomic write with the mode applied **before** rename (closing a permission window).
- `createVerifiedPool` seam on the brain executors (behaviour-identical when absent) so ordering can be observed.

**Adversarial proof suites**: `T-AC3-CHAR` pins the runtime's effective privilege surface via `has_table_privilege`/`has_any_column_privilege`/`has_sequence_privilege` over every relation (covering `PUBLIC` and inherited paths, with a zero-foreign-table pin and the full USAGE/SELECT/UPDATE sequence triple); `T-ORD` proves cross-workspace mismatch rejection happens after only the protected-metadata handshake and before any content read, S3 access or mutation, using an all-statement classifying spy with a vacuity guard; `T-DECIDE` proves forged/stale/wrong-action/digest-mismatched decisions cannot authorize promotion; `T-CAN` sweeps planted canaries across every output channel including **tarball contents** (previously membership-only), with exact path containment, JSONL tracing, all-matches scanning, and name-checks-before-skip.

**T-INV file-access audit — claim descoped by owner decision.** Five review rounds of heuristic tightening each fell to a new bypass, so rather than build a whole-file AST scanner the audit now claims what it proves: an enumerated-rule audit producing a classified inventory, **fail-closed within the recognized shape** (a new unclassified recognized-shape mutation still fails loudly by name), with the seven known-unrecognized syntax classes enumerated in the test header and plan §14. 20 planted controls prove each rule fires. No coverage was removed — round 6 *added* namespace/default dead-import enforcement and two controls.

## Governance / residuals

- **AC-3 partial** — the runtime still holds direct `INSERT` on some Brain tables. Mapped and owned: `entities`/`facts`/`events` → #383-PR-B (measured and confirmed), `edges` → #397, `documents`/`files`/`mounts` → **#408** (filed from this branch's privilege sweep).
- **AC-6 partial** — resolved by owner decision, tracked as **#410** (`roster run show` will sanitize by default with verbatim readback behind an explicit flag). This branch characterizes the shipped behaviour rather than implementing the change.

## Review

Codex adversarial gate over seven rounds: 5 → 6 → 7 → 7 → 5 → 7 → **9/10, no blockers**. Gate: typecheck, build, **3627 tests (0 fail)**, scaffold-scripts, smoke, `npm pack --dry-run` (86 files), gitleaks (baseline unchanged, zero from this branch). DB tier genuinely exercised.

author: padelvillage
body:
Chiusa dal committente il 23/08 mattina: *«chiudi pure»*.

Gli inviti non restano più attaccati a una partita che non c'è più. Provata su un invito **vero** a una persona **vera** e su una partita **vera** spostata **dal gestionale** — non dal bot, che è la differenza fra provare la 63 e provare la cura del 20/08 (dal bot gli inviti li ritira subito un'altra strada; la 63 esiste per il caso in cui **il bot non lo sa**).

## L'orario è stato previsto PRIMA, leggendo il codice

Bot riavviato alle 11:42:19 ⇒ giri agganciati a quell'istante (`RITARDO_AVVIO_MS` 60″, poi `PERIODO_MS` 15′) ⇒ **11:57:19 · 12:12:19 · 12:27:19**.

**Successo alle 12:27:20.** Un secondo di scarto.

## La catena

| ora | cosa | fonte |
|---|---|---|
| 11:52:20 | invito in sospeso | `telegram_inviti_partita` |
| 11:55:22 | lo spostamento è registrato dalla copia locale | `pmo_cloud_records` |
| 12:00:08 | il sync atterra, lo slot vecchio sparisce ⇒ **orfano** | `pmo_cloud_records` |
| 12:12:19 | primo giro — verificato alle 12:14:26 che è **ancora vivo** | DB |
| 12:27:20 | 🧹 ritirato | registro del bot **+** DB |

⭐ **La regola delle due conferme è dimostrata, e la dimostrazione è indiretta**: il ritiro al secondo giro prova **retroattivamente** che il primo l'aveva visto e si era trattenuto, perché il codice ritira solo ciò che era già orfano al giro prima. Serve saperlo perché **il primo giro non scrive nulla**: da solo, un giro muto e un giro mai passato si assomigliano.

📏 Due fonti indipendenti concordano — il database su `ayly…` e il registro del bot sulla VM. Nessuna delle due da sola sarebbe bastata.

## Residuo aperto, dichiarato e NON promosso

**L'invitata non viene avvisata** che il suo invito non vale più. La scheda lo diceva già (*«se il socio debba anche leggere che quegli inviti non valgono più è una decisione sua»*), e quella decisione non è ancora stata presa ⇒ **non ne ho fatto una voce numerata**: promuoverla spetta al committente.

## Emerse per strada, e non erano la prova

① Il messaggio *«è stata annullata dal circolo»* arrivato all'organizzatore per uno **spostamento** è la **voce 74**, vista qui per intero sul ramo delle **partite**: un solo fatto in coda, e la metà buona soppressa dal salto del primo dell'elenco, che su una partita di un socio solo toglie l'unica persona da avvisare. Gesto → messaggio **~4′40″**.

② Il sync ha avuto un buco di **6′47″** fra le 11:52:02 e le 12:00:08, sopra la mediana misurata di ~2′. Non ha rotto niente: la cura è paziente per costruzione.

## Conti

Urgenti da **3 a 2**, chiuse da **60 a 61**. Otto controlli su otto di `guard-docs-truth` tornano — verificati in locale con lo stesso `awk` della guardia, compresa la riga della tabella riassuntiva che al primo giro era rimasta indietro.

author: kanchan78
body:
<!-- ignore-task-list-start -->
- [ ] **Breaking change?** (if so, please describe the impact and migration path for existing application instances)

<!-- ignore-task-list-end -->
**What changes did you make?** (Give an overview)

Fixes #1454.

`McpSpecificationGenerator.toCallResult()` already handles a bare `Flux<?>` correctly by calling `.collectList()` before serializing. But controllers like `ClustersController#getClusters`, `AclsController#listAcls`, `KafkaConnectController#getAllConnectors`, and `MessagesController#getTopicMessagesV2` return `Mono<ResponseEntity<Flux<T>>>` — the `Flux` is nested *inside* the `ResponseEntity` body.

`reponseToCallResult()` unwraps the `ResponseEntity` and passes its body straight to `callToolResult()`, skipping the `Flux`-aware branch in `toCallResult()` entirely. Jackson then introspects the live, unresolved `Flux` object graph and serializes its internal Reactor fields instead of its contents, e.g. `{"scanAvailable":true,"prefetch":-1}` instead of the actual list of clusters/ACLs/connectors/messages. The tool call reports `isError:false`, so an MCP client gets silently wrong data rather than a visible failure.

Fix: `reponseToCallResult()` now delegates the response body to `toCallResult()` instead of calling `callToolResult()` directly, so the existing `Flux` branch (`flux.collectList()`) applies uniformly whether the `Flux` is top-level or nested inside a `ResponseEntity`.

**Is there anything you'd like reviewers to focus on?**

None — it's a one-line change (see diff), the risk is in the surrounding reasoning rather than the code itself, which the added regression test should make easy to check.

**How Has This Been Tested?** (put an "x" (case-sensitive!) next to an item)
<!-- ignore-task-list-start -->
- [ ] No need to
- [ ] Manually (please, describe, if necessary)
- [x] Unit checks
- [ ] Integration checks
- [ ] Covered by existing automation
<!-- ignore-task-list-end -->

Added `toolBackedByResponseEntityOfFluxReturnsCollectedDataNotReactorInternals`, exercising `ClustersController#getClusters` through the real `McpSpecificationGenerator`. Verified it fails on unpatched code (reproduces `{"scanAvailable":...}`) and passes after the fix. Also manually reproduced the bug against a live deployment across `getClusters`, `listAcls`, `getAllConnectors`, and `getTopicMessagesV2` (all `ResponseEntity<Flux<T>>>`-shaped, all affected) before the fix, and confirmed `getTopics`/`getConsumerGroupsPage`/`getSchemas`/`getLatestSchema` (which return `Page<T>`/plain DTOs, not `Flux`) were unaffected — confirming the bug is specific to the `ResponseEntity<Flux<T>>` shape. After the fix, built the full application (including frontend) and smoke-tested the resulting image standalone: opened a real MCP SSE session and called `getClusters`, which returned `[]` (correct, no clusters configured) instead of the Reactor-internals payload.

## Summary

Two places let an admin author an email that gets sent to a lead — Form Builder's Confirmation Email and Settings → Email Rules. Both were plain textareas with no way to paste real designed HTML (banners, buttons, brand colors), even though both already send the body as HTML via Resend.

- New shared `HtmlSourceEditor` (Source/Preview tabs, sandboxed iframe preview, cursor-aware `{{token}}` insertion) replaces the plain textarea in both surfaces, matching the ref+`insertText` pattern already used by `sequence-editor-dialog.tsx`.
- **Auto-detects plain text vs. HTML** on both surfaces: a body with no HTML tags still sends as a normal email with line breaks preserved (matches today's behavior exactly); real pasted HTML is sent exactly as written. Admins don't pick a mode — it's detected automatically (`looksLikeHtml()` in `render-template.ts`).
- **Fixed a real escaping gap** in `email-forward.ts`: `rule.body` was rendered without `{ escape: true }`, so a lead's own submitted field value could inject unescaped HTML into the admin's email template. Now matches the already-correct pattern in `form-autoresponder.ts`.
- Added a `maxLength` cap (100k, matching `form_configs`) on `email_forward_rules.body` in both POST and PATCH validation, now that it's an intended full-HTML-document field.

No schema/migration changes — both fields were already free-text columns.

author: niyaznigmatullin
body:
Two MCP tools passed arguments that did not line up with the `polygon_api` client, plus a test that catches this class of bug in general.

## `problem_save_solution` — `tag` and `source_type` swapped

The client signature is:

```python
problem_save_solution(problem_id, name, file, tag, source_type=None, check_existing=None)
```

but the call passed `(problem_id, name, file_value, source_type, tag)` positionally, so a call with `tag="MA"` and `source_type="cpp.g++17"` reached Polygon as `sourceType=MA`, `tag=cpp.g++17`. `tag` now fills its own positional slot and `source_type` goes by keyword.

## `problem_view_test_group` — missing `problem_id`

The client signature is `problem_view_test_group(problem_id, testset, group=None)`, but the tool was declared as `(testset, group)` and forwarded both positionally, so `problemId` got the testset, `testset` got the group and `group` stayed unset. The tool could never return the requested group. It now takes `problem_id`, and `group` is optional as the API allows.

The remaining ~50 `_call_polygon` sites were checked and are correct.

## Test

`tests/test_api_signature_conformance.py` parses every `_call_polygon(polygon.<method>, ...)` site out of `server.py` with `ast` and checks it against the real `Polygon` signature:

- the method exists on `Polygon`;
- the arguments bind (arity, unknown keywords);
- an argument passed as a bare identifier fills the API parameter of the **same name**.

That last check is the one that matters here — both bugs bind cleanly, so only name matching catches them. Deliberate renames (`file_value` → `file`, `verdict` → `test_verdict`, `info` → `problem_info`, …) are listed in `ALLOWED_ALIASES`; adding a tool that renames an argument means adding a line there.

The two fixed tools also get focused regression tests in the style of `test_problem_build_package.py`. They resolve the forwarded arguments back to API parameter names via `inspect.signature(...).bind()`, so they assert behaviour rather than call shape and keep holding if the calls are later rewritten to use keywords.

Both regression tests were run against the unfixed code to confirm they fail on the bug — `problem_save_solution` fails with `'cpp.g++17' != 'MA'`.

## Verification

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
Ran 83 tests in 0.037s

OK
```

79 before, 83 after.

Closes #95

## Summary
- **Backend**: `GET /v1/analysis/{id}` now honors `If-None-Match`. When the header matches the current revision ETag, it returns `304 Not Modified` with the ETag and skips building the full response payload. Matching is lenient about quoting and weak (`W/`) validators, consistent with the existing `If-Match` validation.
- **Frontend**: analysis detail fetches send `If-None-Match` with the stored ETag. A `304` is treated as success: TanStack Query serves its cached data and local editor edits are preserved (no store clobber on background refetch). Added a shared `analysisQueryKey` / `fetchAnalysis` helper module, and gallery cards prefetch the analysis on hover so navigating into the editor usually hits an already-warm (and 304-revalidated) cache.

- Backend: new `TestAnalysisGet` cases — 304 on matching ETag (empty body), 200 after a revision bump with stale ETag, lenient unquoted/weak validator handling, mismatch ignored.
- Frontend: client tests for 304 passthrough, normal 200, and HTTP-error propagation through the conditional path.

body:
This pull request updates the song identification and sorting logic in `scanner.js` to address issues with incorrect pack names and duplicate song entries. The changes ensure that:

- Only immediate children of `SONGS_DIR` are scanned as packs.
- Only immediate child folders of each pack are scanned as song folders.
- The `.ssc` file is preferred over the `.sm` file when both are present in a song folder.
- Folders deeper than depth 2 are ignored to prevent incorrect indexing.
- If a pack folder contains a `pack.ini` or `Pack.ini` file with a non-empty `DisplayTitle`, that value is used as the pack name instead of the folder name.

Validation was performed using a Node-based check against a synthetic Songs tree, confirming that the new logic correctly indexes songs and handles pack names as intended.

author: orenyomtov
body:
The Deny matches the six tag keys through aws:TagKeys, which compares the key case-sensitively. Policies read the same tags back through aws:PrincipalTag/<key>, which folds case. So a request that sets KUBERNETES-NAMESPACE is not denied, and the tag it leaves behind still answers the aws:PrincipalTag/kubernetes-namespace read.

To fix each key moves to its own statement with a Null aws:RequestTag/<key> test. That means "this key is present in the request", and it folds case the same way the read does, so the two sides cannot drift apart. One statement per key, because two keys in one condition block are ANDed and would only fire when a request carried both at once.

author: slachiewicz
body:
`AbstractArchiver.addFileSet` hardcoded `collection.setFollowingSymLinks(false)`, and neither `Archiver` nor `FileSet` exposed the flag, so no caller could reach it. `FileSet.isFollowingSymLinks()` now drives it.

The default stays false. Preserving links is pinned behaviour downstream — maven-assembly-plugin has an IT asserting `Files.isSymbolicLink` on its output, and MASSEMBLY-785 ("copy symlink target instead of symlink") was closed as not planned. Only a caller that asks gets the resolved tree, so `addDirectory` and every existing `FileSet` behave exactly as before.

This is the archiver half of #160. The consumer end is [MASSEMBLY-1002](https://github.com/apache/maven-assembly-plugin/issues/1213): today an assembly whose fileSet contains a symlinked directory silently loses that directory's contents in every format — `tar.gz` gets a dangling link entry, `zip` gets a regular file holding the link text.

It depends on plexus-io 3.7.0 (codehaus-plexus/plexus-io#187), already in 4.13.0. Before that release, following also left attributes unresolved, so a followed directory arrived as a `PlexusIoSymlinkResource` *and* its contents were added alongside it.

`@since 4.14.0` on the new methods — the getter is a `default` method and the setter is new, so this is source and binary compatible, but it is API and wants a minor.

Verified: `mvn clean verify` → 342 tests, 0 failures. The new `followingSymLinksResolvesLinkedDirectories` test fails with `expected: <false> but was: <true>` when the one-line wiring is reverted.

*This change was created with AI assistance.*

## Kỹ năng — kế thừa nguyên flow Multica

Người chủ chốt 2026-08-23. Trước đó có **hai đường đá nhau**: agent tự gọi `GET /agent/skills` rồi tự ghi (đường đang có, còn dở dang), hay daemon ghi (đường contract mới ghi). Giờ chốt một đường.

author: h0x91b
body:
Hi, this is Claude (the AI assistant that made this change).

Two commits, one problem: **modifier+arrow word motion did not work in dev3 terminals**, and one half of the cause was ours.

**1. tmux was eating Alt+arrow.** `src/bun/tmux/config.ts` bound `M-Left/Right/Up/Down` in tmux's **root** table, so Alt+arrow switched panes with no prefix. A root-table binding is swallowed by tmux and never reaches the pane. Prefix-free pane navigation now sits on **Alt+Shift+arrow** (`M-S-<arrow>`), and the four `M-<arrow>` keys are explicitly unbound — the unbinds are load-bearing, since `configureTmux` calls `source-file` on every session spawn and a merely deleted `bind` line stays in effect on a live server. `⌃B` + arrows is tmux's default and is unchanged.

**2. Freeing the key was not enough — nothing bound it.** Measured: `zsh -f` binds neither `^[[1;3x` (Alt+arrow) nor `^[[1;5x` (Ctrl+arrow); and macOS claims Ctrl+arrow system-wide (`com.apple.symbolichotkeys` IDs 79/81, "move left/right a space", enabled by default), so that form never reaches any app. tmux itself is innocent for the Ctrl form — fed `CSI 1;5 D` through a real PTY into tmux running this config, the inner app receives `^[[1;5D` intact. So `src/bun/shell-init.ts` now binds both forms to `backward-word` / `forward-word` for zsh and bash, after sourcing the user's own config.

Verified end to end through a real PTY into tmux 3.6a with this config: `CSI 1;4 D` / `CSI 1;4 C` move the active pane, and plain Alt+Left now arrives in the pane as literal `^[[1;3D`. The generated `.zshrc` / `.bashrc` were checked in real interactive shells (`bindkey` and `bind -q` both report the new bindings). Ctrl+Alt+arrow was rejected as the pane-nav replacement — GNOME uses it for workspace switching and some Windows graphics drivers rotate the screen with it.

Also updated: the Keyboard Shortcuts overlay's Terminal tab (new `⌥⇧` + arrows row, all three locales), `docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md`, the UX manifest note, a decision record, and guard tests for both the tmux config and the generated shell init.

---

author: elitetk
body:
This is a new take on #4630.

I noticed there is now a `mode` thing in embassy-stm32 itself. The way I use it here is not quite how it's used elsewhere. I was trying to avoid a disruptive change to the low level timer constructor and to avoid requiring every user of this to pass every relevant IRQ binding.

You call `with_update_interrupt` on a `Timer` and this gives you a new `Timer` with a slightly different time indicating that the binding was passed. This unlocks `wait_for_update`. The idea is that capture compare and all the other timer specific interrupts could be added this way in the future without disrupting each other.

I believe this would eventually make the low-level timer driver powerful enough to implement _any_ of the high level drivers from normal code without necessarily needing direct support from embassy-stm32.

I think this does a good job of addressing some of the comments from the previous PR discussion while staying relatively small as a change.

But I understand that the `with_update_interrupt` approach is somewhat unusual here... Interested to hear opinions.

author: jackwener
body:
## Summary

- revoke the Windows pre-upgrade backup completeness marker before best-effort successful-install cleanup
- prevent a residual old-version marker from blocking later upgrades when `RMDir /r` is interrupted by a held file
- pin the authority-before-cleanup ordering with a product release policy test

## Why

The successful upgrade tail intentionally treats backup removal as best effort. On Windows, antivirus or indexing can keep an application file open, so `RMDir /r` may partially delete the backup and leave its completeness marker behind. After the successful install, the registry identifies the new version, while that marker still identifies the old backup version. The next installer sees the stale authority, detects the version mismatch, and refuses an otherwise healthy upgrade with exit 101.

Deleting the marker first makes any cleanup residue inert before recursive tree removal begins. The completed install remains successful even when cleanup cannot finish.

## Verification

- `npm run build`
- `npm run test:product-release` (32/32)
- `npx biome check scripts/product-release.test.mjs`
- `git diff --check`
- mutation: deleting the production marker invalidation makes the new targeted test fail

## 概要
[Issue #45: 終了が2つ連続するところの線の位置修正](https://github.com/shota4327/TraceApp/issues/45) の対応として、while / for ループ内の末尾に if 条件分岐がある場合の流れ図の合流線の位置修正、および No 側迂回線のコメント余白ロジック共通化を実施しました。

## 主な変更点

1. **ブロックスタック巻き戻し処理の親子階層解決 (`src/services/flowchartGenerator.ts`)**:
   - `unwindBlocksWithHierarchy` を導入し、インデント減少時およびコード末尾において、親ブロックが `loop` の場合は内側の `if` の合流先ターゲットを親ループの `loopEndNode`（ループ終了記号）に正しく解決。
   - ループ終了記号を飛び越えて外側のノードへ直接接続される不具合を解消。

2. **合流位置の縦の隙間（`mergeGap` 45px）の適用 (`src/services/flowchartLayout.ts`)**:
   - `loop-end` ノードへの合流時も、通常の条件分岐ブロックと同様に `isMerge = true` と判定して `mergeGap`（45px）を適用し、直前ブロックとの間に十分な縦の隙間を確保。

3. **No 側迂回線のコメント余白ロジック共通化 (`src/services/flowchartLayout.ts`)**:

   - Yes 側にコメント（例: `#(ア)` や `#(アaa)`）がある場合でも、コメントの文字幅を考慮して外側を綺麗に迂回するよう修正。

4. **テストの追加 (`src/__tests__/flowchart.test.tsx`)**:

author: dvjn
body:
## Problem

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` filtered the `pull_request` trigger to `branches: [main]`. A pull request that targets any other branch was never dispatched. Nothing failed and nothing reported why — the checks were simply absent, which reads as "CI passed" at a glance.

## Change

Removed the branch filter from `pull_request`. Every pull request now runs the checks, whatever it targets.

The `push` trigger keeps `branches: [main]`, so a branch push does not duplicate the run that its pull request already triggers.

## Validation

The workflow itself is the validation. A pull request targeting a branch other than `main` previously ran nothing and now reports both jobs.

## Not included

Running checks on every pull request means a force-push can leave a superseded run going. A `concurrency` group keyed on `github.ref`, cancelling only for `pull_request` events so a run on `main` is never cancelled, would fix that. I left it out to keep this change to the one trigger — happy to add it here or separately.

author: jvsena42
body:
## Problem

The Speak pronunciation sheet was rendered with `targetWord = state.backText` unconditionally (`StudySessionScreen.kt`), so tapping Speak while the **front** was facing prompted with the back-side text. The ViewModel graded correctly against the front (`targetFor` follows `revealed`), so the sheet asked for the answer and then marked the correctly-spoken prompt wrong.

## Fix

`SpeakPhase.Listening` now carries the captured `expected` text, and the sheet prompts from it. The prompt and `onSpeechResult`'s grading read the same value, so they can't disagree about which side the attempt is for — including across a mid-listen flip, which the target capture already guarded.

## Test

New `theListeningPromptShowsTheSideBeingGraded` asserts `Listening("hola")` on the front and `Listening("hello")` after reveal. `./gradlew :shared:allTests`, `:composeApp:assembleDebug` and `detektAll` are green. Not driven on a device — no emulator/device was attached, and emulator speech recognition doesn't run the flow end to end anyway.

## Object and proof

- Checked commit and tree: b6f044e6953d3684025e787702e18918db78e25e on `claude/issue-553-decision-buttons`, worktree clean
- Acceptance sentence → proof, and what the test shows beyond the link the gate checks:
  - `a-waiting-v3-run-is-answerable-on-its-run-page`: `test_a_published_wait_schema_reads_back_classified_over_the_real_route` (tests/integration/test_workflow_v3_publication.py) publishes a real boolean and a real enum schema and proves `GET /workflow-revisions/{hash}` reads them back correctly classified (`kind: "boolean"` / `kind: "enum"` with its exact `values`) over the real route, no intercept. `frontend/tests/app/v3RunCockpit.test.ts` adds three tests: a boolean schema renders two decision buttons and sends the exact `true`/`false` click, an enum schema renders one button per value and sends its exact JSON, and an unclassified (`free`) schema keeps the textarea unchanged -- the "answer field" the acceptance sentence names is still there for every schema this build cannot classify. `frontend/tests/e2e/cockpit.spec.ts` drives the same three behaviors against a real running V3 app and captures screenshots (its graph-read intercept is now optional plumbing kept deliberately, to isolate the UI assertion from the read route's timing -- documented in the test itself).
  - `a-node-carries-how-long-it-ran` / `a-run-carries-when-it-started-and-ended`: the node panel's and run head's facts lines (`whenFacts` in `runProjection.ts`) are pinned structurally in `v3RunCockpit.test.ts` (state word · started · ended · duration, honestly omitting an absent timestamp) and visually in the attached screenshots. `acceptance/350-runs-and-nodes-carry-their-time.toml`'s `a-run-carries-when-it-started-and-ended` text is sharpened to match: the exact stamp now "stand[s] in their own facts line, visible without a reveal a person has to find first" rather than sitting "behind the info affordance" -- identifier unchanged. The vitest test proving it now carries `proves(a-run-carries-when-it-started-and-ended)`.
- External effects and authorization, or `none`: none

## Architecture note

Classifying a wait node's answer schema needs reading the schema's own published bytes. `scripts/check_architecture.py`'s `api-port-record-problems` check refuses the API/wire projection layer from matching a `PublishedRevisionResolver`'s own result record directly, and `route-port-problems` refuses a route reaching `context.ports.*`. The classification (`WaitAnswerClassification`) is therefore computed in `atelier2/application/read_workflow_revisions.py` -- the use case that already owns `get_workflow_revision` -- which names each of its four failure modes explicitly (malformed hash, not yet published, wrong published kind, unreadable document) rather than falling through to `free` silently. The wire projection (`api/projection/workflows.py`) receives the plain, portless verdict as a parameter and never touches a resolver. Composition wiring stayed to two one-line, zero-decision pass-throughs: `bound_use_cases` (`api/app.py`) closes the `get_workflow_revision` lambda over `ports.published_revision_registry`, and the GET route (`api/routes/revisions.py`) destructures the use case's second result field through to `workflow_revision_detail_resource`. The publish route (`POST /workflow-revisions`) still answers `kind: "free"` for a freshly published document, since `publish_workflow_revision`'s own use case doesn't classify and wasn't in this claim's fence -- a freshly published wait's schema is often not yet published itself, so `free` there is an honest default, not a regression.

Loop round numbers (`round N of M`) remain a named gap in the node facts line: `RunResourceV3` carries no round datum on the wire at all, so the line never guesses one; only a retried attempt's ordinal (already on the rail) is shown, and only past the first.

author: buhenxihuan
body:
## Problem

An axvisor+starry guest on OrangePi 5 Plus ran a SenseVoice NPU
workload several times slower than native Linux (inference 2.96s vs
1.07s, model load 41.2s vs 0.58s). Instrumentation added along the way
attributed the gap to four removable costs.

## What changed

1. **Pin the guest vCPU to a big A76 core** (`phys_cpu_ids` 0x00 ->
   0x400): the guest was running on the A55 little core (~1175 MHz
   delivered) while the big pair idles at its 1200 MHz ring. Measured:
   model load 41.2s -> 27.1s, inference 2.96s -> 2.60s.
2. **Quiet the board log to Warn**: the per-ioctl info! lines in card1
   (cmd/is_driver_ioctl/op plus a full RknpuSubmit debug dump per
   submit) cost ~100KB of serial traffic per workload round at
   1.5Mbaud. Measured at the quietest level: inference 2.60s -> 1.72s,
   model init 1.22s -> 0.66s. Warn keeps the [perf] aggregates and
   warnings visible.
3. **card1 ioctl timing aggregates**: per-kind cumulative/windowed
   count/total/avg/max reported at power-of-two counts past the
   per-call log limit and on device close — the instrument that
   attributed items 1, 2 and 4. Action ioctls are now timed as well.
4. **Enlarge the cached-file readahead window to 1 MiB**: the window
   becomes ONE block request, so the cap directly sizes the largest
   request. At 32 pages a 490 MB sequential read issued ~3,800 requests
   whose completion->resubmission gap cost ~22% of the SD HighSpeed bus
   ceiling (19.2 of 24.75 MB/s measured). 1 MiB windows amortize the
   gap across 8x more bytes and exactly match the dwmmc IDMAC
   descriptor-chain limit.

## Validation

- `cargo xtask clippy --package ax-driver`, `--package ax-fs-ng` pass;
  StarryOS board build succeeds.
- On-board numbers cited above; after all four, inference sits at
  native parity for the NPU submit path (7.78ms avg per submit vs
  ~7.5ms native) and the remaining load gap is bounded by the SD bus.

Companion fix: the governor busy-attribution bug that made dynamic
DVFS counterproductive for a pinned small guest is fixed separately in
"attribute RK3588 governor busy by FDT cpu topology".

author: anthonydarmon213-ux
body:
## Système uniforme
Le composant traite **tous les exercices de la même façon** : il demande une animation pour un nom, l'affiche si elle existe, retombe sinon sur le lien de démonstration.

**Ajouter un mouvement = déposer un MP4 dans `public/animations/` + une ligne dans `animations.ts`.** Aucun composant à modifier.

Câblé sur la fiche d'exercice **et** le lecteur de séance, où la boucle passe devant la photo de stock.

## Clips disponibles
Trois segments découpés dans la vidéo fournie (squat, soulevé de terre haltères, pompe), rognés en bas pour retirer les sous-titres de marque. **30 à 71 Ko** chacun.

## ⚠️ Couverture réelle : 14 exercices sur 48
Les motifs élargissent chaque clip à sa famille (le squat couvre fentes/presse/chaise, la pompe couvre développé couché/dips).

**Restent sans animation** : dos, épaules, bras, abdominaux, mollets — **34 exercices**, qui gardent le lien de démonstration.

Un mouvement non reconnu n'affiche **aucune** animation, jamais un clip approchant : montrer un squat sur un curl biceps serait pire qu'un lien externe — un mauvais geste avec l'apparence de l'exactitude.

## Note technique
`preload="metadata"` ici — et non `"none"` comme la vidéo de la landing qui restait noire. Les clips pèsent quelques dizaines de Ko, et c'est ce qui permet à la boucle de réellement démarrer.

author: raviprakash-26
body:
The first thing this file's own tests assert is that **the trend cannot disagree with the statements**. It holds, and for a good reason: the trend is read from the ledger, where a sales return debits Sales Returns — an income account of debit nature in the trading section — so it comes off revenue without anybody arranging it.

The three breakdowns underneath it are read from the documents instead: sale items for products and categories, sale headers for customers. A void is excluded by the sale's status, so that much was handled. **A return is not a status.** It is a separate document, and none of the three subtracted it.

## What a shop saw

Sell ten bags at ₹1,000, take four back:

```
AssertionError: expected 10 to be 6                 ← bags the product table says sold
AssertionError: expected 10000 to be close to 6000  ← product revenue against the trend
```

₹6,000 in the chart at the top of the page, ₹10,000 in the tables underneath, for the same period. The tables were reporting what went out of the door rather than what the business kept — and the product returned most often looked like the one selling best, which is the opposite of what that table is read for.

## What changed

Returns are netted rather than filtered: each query unions the sale rows with the return rows negated.

Negating rather than excluding is what makes a partly returned line come out right. Four bags back off a line of ten is **six sold**, not a sale that never happened — and dropping the whole line, which is the tempting shortcut, would have been wrong in the other direction.

The **bill count is deliberately not netted**. The customer was invoiced, and a count that fell when the goods came back would say a shop had served somebody fewer times than it did.

## Tests

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Product query stops netting | *takes a return off what the product earned* · *adds the products up to the revenue the trend reports* |
| Customer query stops netting | *takes it off the customer and the category as well* |
| Category query stops netting | same case |
| A return also decrements the **bill count** | **passed** until the last assertion was added |

That final row is a decision this change makes rather than a bug it fixes, which is exactly why it needed pinning — the same gap shape as the cess sweep in #66, where a deliberate choice sat untested until a mutation walked through it.

The middle case is the one carrying the argument: it asserts the product table adds up to the trend, which is the invariant the top of this file already demands of the trend itself. Two revenues on one page for one period is one revenue too many.

The 22 existing analytics cases pass unchanged — none of them creates a return, which is why this never showed.

Full verification on top of the merged #68: **1831 passed, 6 skipped across 118 files** — the baseline was 1828 with the same skip count, so exactly the three added. `tsc --noEmit`, eslint, prettier.

author: matze4u
body:
Phase 0 of `road-to-frontend-fidelity-calibration` — the calibration pins and the
discriminator they measure. **3 of 36 steps; the roadmap stays open** and is not archived.

## What this establishes

`design.fidelity_mode: strict` was doing two jobs at once. It correctly forbids redesign,
and it was also being read as *reproduce every pixel* — including a wireframe's placeholder
greys, which are **non-decisions**. A non-decision reproduced 1:1 is a decision nobody made,
and the skill that produces those artefacts already says so ([`wireframe`](../src/skills/wireframe/SKILL.md)
§ Gotchas: *"the wireframe's greyscale skeleton hard-codes non-decisions"*). The rule now
splits the two axes: **maturity is a property of the artefact, mandate is a property of the
instruction.**

## Step-by-step evidence

| Step | Verify as written | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 0.1 fixtures | id resolves across `tests src docs`; pre-state `grep -c wireframe` on the rule | **discharged** — id resolves, pre-state count is `1` |
| 0.2 discriminator | `check_references` green; the trigger no longer stands alone | **discharged** — green; trigger `:8` now joined by § Two axes `:92` |
| 0.3 matrix pin | the routing test passes with both rows | **discharged** — 29/29, up from 25 |

Two things the steps did not ask for and that are in anyway, because leaving them implicit
is how a maturity trigger goes wrong:

- **the discriminator reads the ARTEFACT, never the prose** — a finished full-colour comp
  whose description says *"this replaces the wireframe we reviewed last week"* still routes
  **strictly**; that is a reference to a previous artefact, not a declaration about this one;
- **an artefact that does not declare its maturity is treated as FINISHED** — the safe
  direction, since guessing *low fidelity* would authorise exactly the redesign the rule
  exists to prevent.

## Two self-caught defects, recorded rather than quietly fixed

**The two new matrix rows were a hollow pass.** `mandate` was optional and unasserted, so
adding the rows made the suite green while measuring nothing — the field was data no test
read. Four assertions now carry it: the rows **disagree on mandate while agreeing on
`routes`** (two rows agreeing on both would measure nothing new); absent mandate means
`pixel`, so no pre-existing row was silently downgraded; the rule carries both clauses; and
— the one that makes the near-miss mean something — **a naive `includes('wireframe')` DOES
misfire on the near-miss prompt**, so the row guards a measured failure mode rather than a
hypothetical one. Sabotage-proven: softening the artefact-not-prose clause takes the
discriminator assertion RED.

**The rule's first draft was 218 lines and reddened `lint_regression`** (`rule_too_large`,
hard limit 200). Fixed by migration, not by weakening a gate: the maturity→spec table, the
full quotation and the near-miss rationale moved to `design-fidelity-mechanics § Artefact
maturity`, this rule's established P4 pattern. It now sits **at** 200 — recorded in the
roadmap because it constrains the next step: further maturity prose goes to the mechanics
guideline, not to the rule. One trap fell out of the trimming and is written down — a
reflow moved *"it is treated as finished"* across a line break and took the assertion RED;
a `toContain` over a hand-wrapped rule is whitespace-sensitive.

## Council decisions — both blockers, both closed

AI council 2026-08-23, 2/2 quorum (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 + openai/codex-default),
convergent on both. The maintainer delegated owner-reserved blockers to the council for this
autonomous drain run; the council decides *how*, not *whether*.

**`b-detector-license-verification` → (b)** derive the detector independently from this
tree's own token model, with an own-analysis label and no external shape taken. Independent
derivation **removes** the licensing question rather than answering it, and is executable
here with no external evidence to fetch. Option (a) — the borrow-check skill plus a
`provenance/borrows.jsonl` row — stays available if a future implementation does take an
external shape. Consequence pinned at step 3.1 so it is not rediscovered: **nothing is added
to the ledger, and that absence is the decision.**

**`b-page-capture-primitive` → (b)** the render-dependent dimensions ship as recorded nulls
and are cut from the Phase 2 matrix in step 3.3. This environment has no verified
page-reaching capture primitive wired to the fixture harness, so measuring them is not
decidable here. The null carries this run's four parts — *unavailable capability*: a
page-reaching capture primitive on the fixture host · *affected claims*: every dimension
whose measurement requires reaching a rendered page · *evidence boundary*: the static-scoped
dimensions are unaffected and measurable · *reopening condition*: a primitive is confirmed,
the fixtures un-skip against it, the cut dimensions return. Step 7.2's obligation follows
from this and is **not** discharged by it: 3.3 must **name every dimension it cut**, because
a null that does not enumerate its coverage is indistinguishable from a matrix that never
had those rows.

## Honest nulls and what is NOT done

- **No render-dependent measurement exists on this branch**, by the decision above — not
  deferred silently, recorded as a null with a reopening condition.
- **Phases 1–7 are untouched** (33 steps). The roadmap is not archived and
  `archive_completed_roadmaps` was not run: `count_open > 0`.
- The two fixtures score **routing**, not rendered output. Nothing here claims a rendered
  artefact was compared against anything.

## Gates

Full roadmap battery green — `lint_roadmap_blockers`, `lint_roadmap_complexity`,
`lint_roadmap_ci_steps`, `check_roadmap_trackable`, `check_no_roadmap_refs`,
`lint_empty_roadmaps`, `lint_roadmap_later_disposition`, `check_estate_count`,
`check_references` — plus `task preflight` (**No regressions detected**) and the routing
suite at 29/29. No gate was skipped, weakened, or baselined around.

body:
Closes #867 `schedule/blowout/[tripId]` renders two quite different bodies off one `if (!blowout)`: - **confirm** — header, then one `SectionCard` at `max-w-2xl` (lead, money note, roster list, danger submit); - **record** — header, then a full-width `sm:grid-cols-3` row of stat tiles above a five-column table. `loading.tsx` was shaped like the record state, down to the grid class and its own doc comment. So the common navigation painted three wide tiles and a table and then replaced them with one narrow card — the sideways jump design principle 10 is about. ## What changed One file: `src/app/shop/[shopSlug]/schedule/blowout/[tripId]/loading.tsx`, reshaped for the **confirm** state. - The card shell at the page's own `max-w-2xl`, `padding="lg"`, via `sectionCardClass()`. - Bars for what is inside it rather than one empty block: the lead (three `text-sm` lines), the money note (two), the "N divers will be messaged" heading and three roster rows at the list's own `gap-1`, then the `min-h-11` danger submit at `mt-6`. An empty `h-*` shell at the right width would have traded a horizontal jump for a vertical one. - The header bars now stand in for `meta` (`description={false}`), which is what **both** states render — two `text-sm` rows at `gap-1` under the component's `mt-3`, the exact height the real header takes. It was drawing a `description` bar the page has never had. - The doc comment now describes the confirm state and says why, so the next reader does not inherit the same wrong picture from the other direction. ## Why confirm is the arrival Every in-app door maps 1:1 to a state, and there are only two, both in `trips/[id]/page.tsx`: the danger `weatherBlowout` button renders only while the trip is live, so it always lands on confirm; the `viewBlowout` link is gated on `blowoutCalled`, so it always lands on record. Confirm is also the slower branch — it awaits `getTripRoster` *after* the page's `Promise.all` resolves — so its skeleton is the one on screen longest. And the tie-break in the issue points the same way: the card is the narrower of the two bodies, so a skeleton shaped for it commits to nothing wider than what replaces it. ## Two notes for review - **The banner slot is deliberately not reproduced.** Both states render `
{banner ?? null}
` between the header and the body, and the triage comment flagged its absence as a rhythm gap. On any arrival carrying no `?notice=` that div is empty, and an empty block's margins collapse through — the header's `mb-8` is the whole gap above the card in the real page too, which is what the skeleton already renders. Adding a permanently-empty div would change no pixel. The reasoning is written into the file so it is not re-litigated. - **No visual capture can catch this**, since a skeleton has no steady state to photograph; `capture()` waits for the last `animate-pulse` to leave, and both blow-out captures already wait on real destination elements (`heading "Call a blow-out?"`, `heading "Blow-out cascade"` + the `Diver` columnheader). Checked, unchanged, no e2e edit needed — so a clean visual run here is not evidence the change did nothing. Scope held to the one file, per the issue: no two-state sweep, and nothing stacked on #866 (that check does not exist on `main`). ## Verification `pnpm check` green — repo safeguards, lint, typecheck, 6691 unit tests passing. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01L1RZawcSXS6AAEgmDiSuQk)_ ## Summary by Sourcery Align the blow-out loading experience with its confirmation page and stabilize the related boat-change end-to-end test. Bug Fixes: - Prevent the schedule-trip end-to-end test from racing navigation against the boat-save action by waiting for the saved confirmation. Enhancements: - Reshape the blow-out loading skeleton to match the narrower confirmation state users reach when initiating a blow-out, avoiding a layout shift from record-style tiles and tables to the confirmation card. Tests: - Strengthen the schedule-trip end-to-end test with an explicit assertion that boat changes have been saved before reading them back.
