author: mbastian
body:
## Description

`AsynchronousTest` has been failing intermittently on CI in two different ways. Commit 85af31566 raised the Awaitility timeouts from 10s to 30s to fight it, but both recent failures happened on commits that already had the 30s timeouts, so the bump only changed which failure surfaces. Both are races in `LongTaskExecutor` itself.

## Race 1: `currentTask` is published without any happens-before edge

`currentTask` is written by the pool worker thread in `RunningLongTask.call()` and read by `isRunning()` from any other thread, with no synchronization on either side. Nothing guarantees a poller ever observes the write.

That is the macOS failure mode: `testCancel` timed out after 30s waiting for `isRunning()` to become `true`, which no amount of extra timeout can fix.

Fix: `currentTask` is now `volatile`.

## Race 2: the failure path completed the task without notifying the listener

`RunningLongTask.call()` only called `finished()` on the success path. The `catch (Throwable)` block nulled `currentTask` directly and returned, so:

- `cancel()` schedules an `InterruptTimerTask`, which calls `future.cancel(true)` and then, separately, `finished(task)` — which is what notifies the listener.
- The interrupt makes the task throw, and the pool thread's catch block nulls `currentTask` **without** notifying the listener.
- `isRunning()` flips to `false` as a side effect of that write, so the test's `await(...).until(isRunning, t -> !t)` returns immediately.
- `verify(listener).taskFinished(...)` then runs before the Timer thread got to its own `finished()` call.

That is the Windows failure mode: `testCancelRunnableInterrupt` failed with "Wanted but not invoked: listener.taskFinished(<any>) ... there were zero interactions with this mock", not with a timeout.

Simply calling `finished()` from the catch block would swap this for the opposite bug: in the interrupt scenario the listener would be notified twice (once by the pool thread, once by `InterruptTimerTask`) and the same `verify()` would fail with `TooManyActualInvocations`.

Fix: each `RunningLongTask` now carries an `AtomicBoolean` claimed with a CAS. Only the first of {success path, failure path, `InterruptTimerTask`} performs the completion work (cancelling the cancel timer, clearing `currentTask`, notifying the listener); the others are no-ops. `InterruptTimerTask` claims the completion *before* interrupting the task thread, so the interrupted thread can never end the task ahead of the listener notification. The catch block now reaches the shared completion code instead of bypassing it, which is also what stops a pending interrupt timer from firing after a task already failed.

The error-handling contract is unchanged: failures are still reported to the error handler only, never to the listener (`testExecuteCallableException` still asserts `verify(listener, never())`). The completion in the catch block was moved after the error handler is invoked, in a `finally`, so `isRunning() == false` now also implies the error has already been reported.

## Tests

- New `testCancelRunnableIgnoresInterrupt`: the task swallows the interrupt and completes normally, so both the interrupt timer and the task thread reach the completion code. It asserts the listener is invoked exactly once. Verified it catches the double-notification regression: removing the CAS guard from the success path makes it fail with `TooManyActualInvocations`.
- `testCancel` no longer depends on a 200ms mock delay that the 100ms Awaitility polling can miss entirely; the task blocks on a latch released by the test, so it is guaranteed to be observed running. No assertion or timeout was relaxed.

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduced the Windows failure deterministically by injecting a 500ms sleep in `InterruptTimerTask.run()` before `finished(task)`: identical "zero interactions with this mock" failure on master, passing after the fix, which shows the window is closed rather than narrowed (instrumentation removed before committing)
- [x] Verified the new test catches the double-notification regression
- [x] `mvn -pl modules/LongTaskAPI test` run 25x consecutively on the final code (65 runs total across iterations), no failures
- [x] `mvn -pl modules/LongTaskAPI -P enableCheckStyle checkstyle:check`: 0 violations

## Checklist

- [x] Merged with master beforehand

## Added tests?

- [x] 👍 yes

## Added to documentation?

- [x] 👍 Relevant code documentation

## Summary

Introduces a global 3/2/1 card-density contract for the CAPTAiNFiN admin instead of letting every page invent its own card width.

### Shared rule
- 3-up: ordinary compact settings/configuration cards
- 2-up: medium editors that need more horizontal room
- 1-up: deliberate exceptions only (tables, permission/source matrices, wide operational editors, charts/timelines)
- six-column foundation so 3-up = 2/6, 2-up = 3/6 and 1-up = 6/6
- short cards stop stretching to match taller neighbours
- tablet collapses to 2-up; mobile collapses to 1-up

### Global families
- `settings-grid` now defaults to 3-up and balances 2-card and 4-card pages automatically
- table/matrix settings cards escape to full width automatically
- `serverGrid` uses the same balanced density contract for customer/server/settings cards
- personal notification/connection cards cap at 3 across
- KPI/overview strips remain compact informational surfaces and are not forced into this settings-card model
- analytics and complex capability/source editors intentionally retain their wider layouts

### Jellyfin plan editor
- Product & storefront: 2-up
- Access specification: 2-up
- Availability: 3-up
- Delivery & server placement: 3-up (advanced server list remains collapsed)
- Library access: 3-up
- Requests / Jellyseerr: 2-up
- Commercial schedule / payment options: 2-up

### Stremio plan editor
The four primary plan cards remain 2-up because household/replacement controls need more width. Request permissions and source-management matrices remain wide exceptions.

### Card chrome
Tightens shared settings-card header/body/form spacing without reducing control minimum sizes or typography.

### Regression coverage
Extends the semantic surface smoke test to pin the six-column density contract, balanced shared grids, wide-table escape rule, plan-editor classifications and responsive collapse.

body:
💡 **What:** 
- Disabled the main prompt `<textarea>` while `isLoading` is true.
- Disabled the "Generate component" button when the prompt input is entirely empty.
- Added a helpful tooltip (`title="Enter a prompt to generate a component"`) to the disabled button.
- Updated the `.Jules/palette.md` journal with this pattern learning.

🎯 **Why:** 
Users could previously attempt to edit the prompt while an async generation request was in progress, which could lead to confusion or lost text if the UI reset. Furthermore, clicking submit on an empty input does nothing useful, so disabling the button clarifies the state requirements. The tooltip explains the disabled state rather than leaving the user guessing.

📸 **Before/After:** 
- **Before:** Textarea remained active and clickable during generation. The submit button remained active even when the prompt input was entirely empty.
- **After:** Textarea dims and prevents input during generation. Submit button dims and prevents clicks when empty, showing a native tooltip on hover.

♿ **Accessibility:** 
The disabled attributes are fully semantic (`disabled={isLoading}`), tying directly into standard screen reader behavior and automatically applying the existing Tailwind `disabled:` visual cues (like `cursor-not-allowed` and dimming) for sighted users without requiring custom CSS. The `title` attribute on the button provides crucial context for screen readers and mouse users as to *why* the button is unavailable.

author: quixthe2nd
body:
## Summary
`/restart` currently refuses new work and waits for every live turn to finish. With a few long Discord threads that blocks new threads until those sessions die.

This change asks other live chat sessions to park themselves, then auto-continues them after the bounce:

1. On in-band restart, steer every *other* live chat agent once: reach a pausable state, do not start new long work, end the turn.
2. Mark those sessions `resume_pending` with `cooperative_restart`.
3. Startup auto-resume continues the parked work instead of asking "what next?".
4. New turns still stay refused while the drain runs. Cron and API-server work are not steered.

author: jhanvi857
body:
## Summary

Adds a **local, dependency-free, deterministic, rule-based escalation layer** to `gitresolve`. 

Before performing conflict resolution, `gitresolve` now inspects repository Git history and AST structure to detect *why* a conflict occurred (e.g. stale branch divergence) and scores structural risk (blast radius, historical file coupling, import cycles). 

When structural risk is detected, `gitresolve` escalates with a plain-English explanation and a concrete suggested command rendered from parameterized templates filled with real repo facts—**100% deterministic with zero ML/LLM dependencies**.

---

## Key Changes

### 1. In-Memory History Index & Divergence (`internal/history`)
- **`SymbolCallers`**: Cross-file call-site index extracted via AST inspection for blast radius detection.
- **`FileCoChanges`**: Co-occurrence matrix built from `git log --name-only` over the last $N$ commits (default 500), normalized to $[0.0, 1.0]$ strength.
- **`FileAuthors`**: Exponential recency-weighted author contributions per file ($e^{-\text{days}/90}$).
- **`ImportCycles`**: Go package import cycle detection using Tarjan's Strongly Connected Components (SCC) algorithm.
- **Pre-Resolve Divergence (`divergence.go`)**: Runs `git rev-list --left-right --count` to detect behind-commit threshold breaches and cross-references affected file authors.
- **Incremental Sync (`persist.go`)**: Persists `last_processed_sha` in SQLite to make subsequent runs instantaneous (~10–50ms).

### 2. Parameterized Message Templates & Reason Codes (`internal/conflict`)
Registered 5 new stable reason codes:
- `semantic.high_blast_radius`: Modified symbol called from $> 10$ locations.
- `semantic.missing_coupled_file`: Strongly coupled partner file ($\ge 0.60$) was not modified in the branch.
- `semantic.import_cycle`: Conflict block resides inside a dependency cycle.
- `strategy.stale_branch_divergence`: Branch is $> 10$ commits behind remote default branch.
- `strategy.multi_author_conflict`: Conflicted sides authored by different contributors (informational).

All escalation messages and suggested commands use fixed Go templates with `{placeholders}` filled strictly from verified struct data (no hallucinations or dynamic free-form text).

### 3. Policy Configuration Extension (`internal/ownership`)
Extended `.gitresolve/policy.json` schema with configurable thresholds:
```json
{
  "default": "balanced",
  "max_divergence_commits": 10,
  "max_callers": 10,
  "co_change_min_strength": 0.6,
  "history_max_commits": 500
}
```
- Removed strict `DisallowUnknownFields` for forward compatibility, adding warning-level typo detection.

### 4. Database Migrations (`internal/store`)
- Migrations 5–8 in `migrate.go` adding `co_changes`, `file_authors`, and `history_sync_state` tables.
- Added `escalation_message` and `suggested_command` columns to `decision_logs`.
- Added shared connection accessor `db.Conn() *sql.DB`.

### 5. CLI Integration (`cmd/gitresolve`)
- Added `--skip-sync-check` flag to `resolve` command.
- Pre-resolve divergence warning + suggested pull/rebase command before resolution begins.
- **Default tier**: 1-line reason + 1-line suggested command.
- **Verbose tier (`--verbose` / `-v`)**: Full evidence details (AST diff, co-change coupling facts, author weights, decision log row).

### 6. Tiered Test Fixtures & Golden-File Assertions (`tests/testdata`)
- Added fixtures `S6_blast_radius`, `S7_co_change`, `S8_import_cycle`, `S9_stale_branch`, `S10_multi_author`.
- Dynamic golden-file test runner verifying exact reason codes, messages, and suggested commands on real parsed conflict blocks.

### 7. Documentation (`README.md`)
- Updated command reference table with `--skip-sync-check` and updated `--verbose`.
- Updated architecture Mermaid diagram showing divergence check and history index.
- Added dedicated section explaining deterministic rule-based escalation.

Follow-up to #25. Dispatch run [32634051113](https://github.com/GuangDai/Clipy/actions/runs/32634051113) refused every seed capture on the dedicated mounted probe volume (254 MiB free): the `volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage` fact returned **zero** there — the OS maintains purgeable-space accounting only on the boot volume (same zero documented in [SO 56474397](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56474397/why-is-volumeavailablecapacityforimportantusage-zero)).

The admission reader now reads the raw `volumeAvailableCapacity` fact: the same accounting `df` and the workflow's own volume-facts breadcrumbs use, valid on every volume; on the boot volume it ignores purgeable space and errs conservative, which a typed retryable refusal already governs. Spec §16 bullet and the AUDIT §3 row record the observed zero and the corrected choice.

Traceability: docs/05-authority-kernel.md §16; docs/AUDIT.md §3; Review Card 6B (ledger §20).

author: latinmaestro
body:
## Summary
- let the deferred bounded NDJSON writer abort without flushing its remaining in-memory partition
- return receipts for every partition already stored before the abort
- preserve earlier receipts even when a later R2 partition write fails
- reject finish/append after abort while keeping abort replay-safe

## Why
Durable Preview staging must be able to clean up newly created R2 objects when CSV processing or integrity verification fails before the Neon import-batch commit. Flushing buffered rows during abort would create unnecessary objects; hiding earlier receipts would strand them.

## Safety
Code-only recovery prerequisite. No schema, migration, provider, Preview data, Production data, Vercel deployment, real upload, paid action or game action.

## Validation
Exact-head GitHub Actions must pass the complete CI and migration chain.

author: szatmary
body:
Phase 2 of the keyed-mode design: records addressed by a caller-supplied key
instead of an auto-increment id, sharing the record layer Phase 1 extracted.

A db is autoinc **or** keyed for life. The mode is recorded in every record file
header, and both constructors refuse the other mode's directory.

```go
kdb, err := gitdb.OpenKeyed("data", "events")
err = kdb.Put(key, value)      // insert or replace
value, err := kdb.Get(key)     // wraps ErrNotFound
err = kdb.Delete(key)
err = kdb.Compact()
for rec, err := range kdb.All() { /* rec.Key, rec.Value */ }
```

## How it works

A key's location lives in an open-addressed hash table, sharded like everything
else. A slot is 21 bytes: the key's **full 64-bit hash** and the record's packed
location, each as ten base-94 digits.

Storing the whole hash rather than a short tag is the load-bearing decision. A
rehash has to recompute every home slot as `hash & (newSlots-1)`; with only a
tag the hash is unrecoverable, so a rehash would have to re-read and decompress
every record — an operational cliff, and an inversion of the layering Phase 1
built, since the table would have to call back into the record layer. It costs
seven bytes a slot and buys a rehash that reads nothing but the table.

A keyed record carries its key with its value, so a probe hit can be checked
against the real key. `All` walks record file order rather than table order:
stable, sequential, and unaffected by a rehash. A line is live only when the
table's entry for its key names that exact location, which skips deleted records
and superseded versions without a second structure.

## Also lands the three carry-overs from Phase 1's review

The record header is parsed rather than string-compared, so a mismatch names the
field that differs. Record-file rewriting moved into the record layer, where
keyed compaction reuses it. And the record layer gained a sequential line scan.

## Honest costs

Keyed mode costs more than autoinc, and the README now says so rather than
implying otherwise. A table costs roughly 28 bytes per live key just before a
rehash, up to about 112 just after a `Compact` that rounds its size up to a
power of two — against 11 bytes for an autoinc id. Any keyed db, however small,
starts at ~21 KB because the table has a 1,024-slot floor.

The key shards are also the one file family in this format whose diff is not
worth reading: hashing scatters writes, so a batch produces many isolated hunks
rather than a contiguous block. Storage is unaffected — delta compression works
on bytes, not hunks.

## API note

`Option`'s underlying type changed from `func(*DB)` to `func(*recordStore)`.
`Open`, `OpenKeyed`, and the four `With*` functions are unchanged, but code
outside the package that declared its own `gitdb.Option` as `func(db *gitdb.DB)`
will no longer compile. The change makes `Option` opaque, which is the right
shape, but it is a break.

## Review notes

Eleven tasks, each TDD'd by a fresh implementer and gated by its own review,
then a whole-branch review and one fix wave. Format version stays 6.

The whole-branch review found a reachable state where a directory ended up
holding **both** an index and a key table, and was then unopenable in either
mode with the two errors pointing at each other — because `OpenKeyed` claimed
the mode eagerly while `Open` wrote nothing until the first `Insert`. Fixed by
making the claim symmetric: `Open` now lays down a header-only index shard, so
the mode boundary is an invariant of the directory rather than of write order.

Also fixed in that wave: the README's per-key cost was optimistic by 2× in the
state `Compact` actually produces, `openShard` reported an I/O error as a header
mismatch and sent a torn shard down the wrong recovery path, and autoinc
compaction had a second definition of "this file holds dead bytes".

Five defects in the plan itself surfaced during execution and were fixed against
their briefs: a `uint64` overflow that panicked on a hostile length prefix, a
fixed-length header read, an unsatisfiable test fixture, a `lookup` that would
have reported "table is full" for an absent key, and a growth check that made
bulk loading O(N²).

## Known and deliberate

`All` opens and header-verifies a key shard once per probe step, so a walk is
only about 1.5× faster than the equivalent point lookups despite reading records
sequentially. Caching an open shard handle across a walk would fix it; that has
concurrency implications and was deliberately not done in a fix wave.

## Verification

208 tests, `gofmt` clean, `go vet` clean, `go test -race` green. Autoinc
behaviour is unchanged apart from `Open` claiming its mode; its suite passes
untouched.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body: **User story** > As a kid, I want to tap my own face to sign in, and see the proper Hero Tasks artwork when I open the app — not a generic emoji. ## ⚠️ One thing to check: which boy is which I mapped **curly brown hair → Toby**, **blond in the soccer kit → Ollie**, from the 3D printer sitting beside the curly-haired boy in both images — matching Toby's existing `3d-printer` icon. If that's the wrong way round it's two lines in `api/src/lib/seed.js` (the migration `to:` values). Worth a look before this reaches the kids. ## What was extracted | Asset | From | Size | |---|---|---| | `hero-splash.webp` | image 1, whole | 720×1604, 182KB | | `avatar-toby.webp` / `avatar-ollie.webp` | the two rounded tiles, cropped inside their rings | 320px, ~28KB each | | `head-toby.webp` / `head-ollie.webp` | the two small circles at the bottom | 96px, ~3.5KB each | 256KB total. The tiles are cropped *inside* the supplied teal/orange rings so the app draws its own `--kid-color` ring instead — which is why Toby still comes out teal and Ollie orange. **Two crops per kid, not one scaled down.** `tile` is chest-up for the picker; `head` is the tighter face crop, because at ~40px in the header a chest-up shot is an unreadable smudge. That's exactly what the small circles in your second image are for. ## How avatars work now A third prefix alongside the existing two: | Value | Renders as | |---|---| | `img:` | a photo, via `IMG_AVATARS` | | `svg:` | inline SVG tinted with the kid's colour | | anything else | the string itself (emoji) | Each photo also declares a `fallback` emoji, because plenty of places can only hold text — `

author: seantalts
body:
One page answering the two questions that kept being answered from memory: what guards against wrong numbers, and how coverage is determined. The material lived in six places -- ctest conventions, `verify_refs`, the conformance README, `policy.toml`, the ratchet's commit messages, `gen_docs` -- and the connecting tissue was oral tradition.

What it covers:

- **The layers**, as a table with their exact commands: kernel tests, the corpus oracle, the conformance sweep, the coverage ratchet, doc consistency, formatting.
- **The numeric standards in one place**: bitwise wherever the sides share arithmetic; 2 ULP as the outer budget, usable only with the divergence mechanism named in a comment; policy gates for identified cross-implementation causes; and the rule that a tolerance chosen before the error was measured is a defect (with the 1e-13-that-measured-zero story).
- **What blocks a run and why coverage gaps do not** -- the gate-on-disagreement framing, stated where a new contributor will find it.
- **How support is determined without trusting stanli's own tables** -- a name is covered when the sweep reports no `unexpected_unsupported` row for it, full stop.
- **What each layer cannot see**, with the bug that proved each blind spot: the corpus and the single evaluation point, conformance and operator-reached behavior (`B / A`), kernel tests and whole-path divergence.
- **Practices that exist because something went wrong**: verify merges landed what you think, a green nightly covers its dispatch SHA not the merges since, crashes hiding behind the recorded point, numbers nothing recomputes.
- **In progress**, clearly marked as such: multi-point corpus replay, ASan, and the cross-path harness.

Also corrects the README's coverage line, which still said 69/72 densities and 90/105 distribution functions immediately beside a link to the regenerated table saying 71/72 and 105/105, and adds the TESTING.md pointer.

`gen_docs.py --check` clean -- the gen-marked numbers were not touched, and TESTING.md deliberately carries almost no volatile numbers, pointing at the regenerating commands instead.

Self-applies the Copier payload to this repository, so the publisher exercises
the same Layer 0, Claude, and Codex process it distributes. The source keeps
its root-only reusable workflows, while ordinary rendered consumers retain
immutable workflow SHA references.

The self-application bootstrap is executable before its own merge: local
callers use the root-only reusable workflows, which use the PR driver only if
the default branch does not yet contain that driver. Once this PR merges, they
return to the trusted default-branch driver.

author: jonbj
body:
## Cosa cambia e perché

Questa PR rende osservabile point-in-time l’intero funnel degli ingressi S4 senza intervenire sulle decisioni live. Ogni segnale letto dal ciclo viene registrato prima dei guard con identificatori deterministici di intento ed evento causale, i quattro timestamp richiesti, provenance della notizia e del resolver, snapshot versionati dei componenti decisionali e missingness esplicita. Il ranking produce inoltre una disposizione per ogni input, compresi deduplicati, scarti, candidati fuori top-N e selezionati.

Il ciclo completa poi lo stesso intento con rango, concorrenti, stato S1, risultato anti-pyramiding e reason code fino al broker boundary. La popolazione candidata e quella tradabile post-gate restano separate ma riconciliabili per `intent_id`: “tradabile” descrive il superamento di gate e ranking, mentre la disposizione conserva separatamente eventuale censura successiva o rifiuto del broker. Le scritture sono append-only e gli UUID deterministici, insieme al vincolo semantico e a `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, rendono retry e restart idempotenti.

La strumentazione è fail-open: errori di inizializzazione, callback o persistenza vengono osservati ma non modificano il percorso degli ordini. I test di parità confrontano esattamente l’output della submission con e senza ledger, compreso il caso di callback guasta.

## Come verificare

Eseguire:

```bash
UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/alembic-294-uv-cache uv run pytest tests/strategies/test_s4_intent_ledger.py tests/strategies/test_s4_ranking_diagnostics.py tests/strategies/test_s4_ranking.py tests/strategies/test_s4_strategy.py tests/store/test_s4_intent_ledger_store.py tests/test_pg_store.py tests/workers/test_s4_intent_wiring.py tests/workers/test_portfolio_scheduler.py tests/workers/test_p2_05_execution_edge_cases.py tests/portfolio/test_orchestrator.py tests/portfolio/test_orchestrator_allocation.py tests/portfolio/test_orchestrator_bug4.py tests/portfolio/test_orchestrator_rebalance.py tests/workers/test_day2_fixes.py tests/workers/test_exit_mechanism_observed.py tests/workers/test_s4_signals_df_provenance.py tests/test_p1_s4_freshness_idempotency.py -q --tb=short
```

Il risultato atteso è `422 passed`; restano soltanto 34 warning di deprecazione già presenti. I controlli statici mirati su ledger, ranking, modello e relativi test passano, così come mypy sui nuovi tipi centrali.

## Freeze osservazionale

Non sono state cambiate soglie, pesi, flag, cooldown o policy di strategia. Non è stato necessario lasciare fuori alcun requisito della issue per effetto del freeze: l’intervento è interamente additivo e di strumentazione/misura.

Closes #294

author: gemisis
body:
## Two fixes, both measured on the finished v10 runs

### The researcher agents stopped filling the regions their own later stages read

Measured over two completed runs, across every context snapshot each took (225
and 251):

| | region | peak | budget | fill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| deep | `claims` | **0** | 40,000 | 0% |
| deep | `contradictions` | **0** | 15,000 | 0% |
| deep | `analysis` | **0** | 150,000 | 0% |
| deep | `sources` | 149,066 | 150,000 | **99%** |
| wide | `comparisons` | 2,560 | 125,000 | **2%** |
| wide | `challenges` | **0** | 20,000 | 0% |
| wide | `landscape` | 125,247 | 150,000 | **83%** |

High-water marks across all snapshots, not the end state, so nothing reads as
unused merely because a transform cleared it on the way out.

This is not cosmetic. `challenge` is told to *"go through `claims`,
`contradictions` and `analysis`"* and was handed three empty regions, so the
adversarial pass had nothing to attack. `synthesize` is told to build the report
*"from `claims`"* and pull disagreements *"straight from `contradictions`"*, and
had neither. `sources` sits at 99% because it absorbed all four jobs.

The instruction to write them lived only in `system_prompt`. The decision is made
against `transition_prompt`, which never mentioned those regions, and nothing
checked afterwards, so the model did what it was told about at the moment of
choosing and skipped what it was told about at the start.

Both halves of the pair that has worked before: name it where the decision is
made, and gate the edge on the region having changed during the pass. The gate
allows three attempts and then lets the run through with a warning, so a model
with genuinely nothing to record cannot strand a run.

### A cancelled run is stopped, not finished

Closes #576.

Everything needed to carry on is already on disk, and the machinery that rebuilds
a run from it runs on every daemon restart. A status check grouped `Cancelled`
with `Complete` and `Error`, so `reload_run` refused to page it back in and
`lev resume` had nothing to reach.

`Complete` and `Error` stay finished. Startup recovery is untouched and still
leaves cancelled runs alone: somebody stopped that run on purpose, and restarting
the daemon is not them changing their mind.

## Guards, both checked by mutation

- a declared `gate` must parse into one that checks something. Its fields are
  read key by key, so a misspelt condition leaves them at their defaults and the
  edge ships with a gate that passes every time. Verified by misspelling
  `require_region_updated` and watching the guard catch it.
- the #576 tests were run against the unfixed code first and fail there.

## Gates

`cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `cargo xtask coverage` (100%, 13
packages), `cargo xtask docs`, `cargo xtask structure`, clippy clean.

author: gabrielguerrero
body:
Refs #338

## Problem

Features declare their dependencies in the `Input` half of
`SignalStoreFeature<Input & Requirement, Output>`, so forgetting one surfaced as a
structural mismatch of `InnerSignalStore<...>` ending in
`Property 'productEntitiesCallStatus' is missing in type ...`, which never names
the feature to add.

## Solution

New `feature-requirements.model.ts`. `RequireFeature` returns the real requirement
when the required feature's state key is already in `Input`, otherwise a
`MissingFeatureError` whose only method is named after the message, so ts reports:

```
Property 'Missing store feature: withEntitiesLoadingCall requires
withCallStatus({ collection: 'product' }) to be present in the store before it'
is missing in type ...
```

The message also shows early in the error as `MissingFeatureError<"...">`, and the
collection is interpolated when set. Wrappers per dependency: `RequireEntities`,
`RequireEntitiesCallStatus`, `RequireEntitiesFilter`, `RequireEntitiesSort`,
`RequireEntitiesSingleSelection`, `RequireEntitiesMultiSelection`.

Applied to the 17 features that have requirements, including the
`withLinkEntities*`, which report the filter/sort/selection feature they link to.

## Edge cases

- inside `withFeatureFactory` (or any generic feature) `Input['state']` is still
  the `SignalStoreFeatureResult` constraint, there is no store to check yet, so
  the check is skipped instead of reporting a false missing feature
- a non literal collection makes the message stop being a literal and the mapped
  type would degenerate into an index signature that `{}` satisfies, a fixed
  `__missingStoreFeature` key keeps the requirement unsatisfiable
- presence is checked by state key only, so a genuine type mismatch (wrong
  `errorType`) still produces the real structural error

## fetchEntities result

`withEntitiesLoadingCall` has the same kind of hidden requirement: the result
`fetchEntities` returns is `Entity[] | { entities: Entity[] }`, unless the store
has an entities pagination feature, in which case it is whatever that feature's
`set[Collection]EntitiesPagedResult` accepts, which differs per pagination
feature. A wrong result only listed the properties that were missing.

The conditional, inlined three times before, moves to `FetchEntitiesResult` in the
new `with-entities-loading-call.model.ts`, and what `fetchEntities` returns is
expected through `PagedFetchEntitiesResult<ResultParam, Explanation>`, which adds
an unconstructible `{ [K in Explanation]: never }` member. Nothing extra is
accepted, but ts keeps alias names in errors, so the explanation is printed:

```
Type 'Observable<Product[]>' is not assignable to type
'Observable<PagedFetchEntitiesResult<{ entities: Product[]; total: number; },
"the store has an entities pagination feature, fetchEntities must return the
result setProductEntitiesPagedResult accepts">>'
```

With `withEntitiesRemoteScrollPagination` the union of shapes it accepts is
printed too. `onSuccess` keeps the plain `FetchEntitiesResult`, an explanation
member there would have to be narrowed away by the user.

## Testing

654 tests pass; `tsconfig.lib.json`, `tsconfig.spec.json` and the example app
typecheck clean. New type only spec `feature-requirements.spec.ts` covers the 20
missing feature cases, the `withFeatureFactory` case and a store combining 12
features, and `with-entities-loading-call.spec.ts` covers the fetchEntities result
shapes; both are enforced by the `typecheck` CI target.

author: aswinsam
body:
Second slice of ADR-0024, closing [#135](https://github.com/meshpnet/meshp/issues/135).

Four subsystems have written audit events since migration 0001. Every administrative one landed as `actor_kind = 'api_token'` with **no id and no label** — the record could say what happened and never who, which is half of what an audit trail is for.

## The design question, answered differently than the issue framed it

[#135](https://github.com/meshpnet/meshp/issues/135) posed it as explicit request fields versus request context. It turned out to be neither.

There is now a `store.Actor` — one value rather than three loose fields — and a `WriteAudit` that **refuses a zero one**. Context would have made the omission invisible again, exactly as it is today. Explicit fields make it forgettable, which is how four subsystems ended up anonymous. A required value that fails loudly makes it neither: forgetting is a test failure at the first run rather than a blank column somebody notices in six months.

**The refusal immediately found five call sites in the existing tests that had never said who was acting** — the same silence the production code had been keeping, and a fair demonstration that the guard is the part worth having.

## What changes in the trail

A signed-in person: `actor_kind = 'user'`, a real id, and their **email** as the label — an audit line is read months later by somebody trying to reach whoever did it, and a display name is not a way to reach anyone.

The bootstrap token now names itself. It still cannot name a person — a shared secret has no identity, which is ADR-0024's whole argument — but *"somebody used the root credential"* becomes something an operator reads rather than infers from an empty column.

## The warning, and why it is throttled to an hour

ADR-0024 §5 keeps the token working and asks that using it stop being invisible. Once the deployment has accounts, reaching for the shared secret means somebody is using it *instead of* one.

Throttled for two reasons rather than one. The obvious: the commercial layer polls with a bearer token and would write a line per request. The less obvious: the query behind it is a count of the users table, and asking per request would put a scan in front of every administrative call to produce a message nobody reads twice.

Full suite against a local PostgreSQL, lint, reachability, `make sqlc` clean.

author: jimisola
body:
## Description

Companion to [reqstool/.github#94](https://github.com/reqstool/.github/pull/94) — see
[reqstool/.github#95](https://github.com/reqstool/.github/issues/95), **including the
corrections in the second comment**.

Today's real release run failed at `publish-to-pypi`:

```
docker run ... ghcr.io/reqstool/.github:b10b898cd5a1d552a578dbe4f170f84fb8f98b6c
docker: invalid reference format
```

`pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` is a Docker container action, and nesting one inside a
composite action makes GitHub resolve its image against the wrapping action's repository
rather than its own. Its own maintainer
[describes the same breakage](https://github.com/pypi/warehouse/issues/11096#issuecomment-2871981512).

The composite action itself was fine — it creates no new workflow context, so the job keeps
this repo's own OIDC identity, which is why it works where a cross-repo reusable workflow
does not. So only the publish step comes out.

## What changes

```yaml
      - uses: reqstool/.github/.github/actions/download-dists@main
        with:
          artifact: dist-tagged
      # Inline, not inside download-dists: nesting this Docker action in a
      # composite action makes GitHub resolve its image against the wrapper's repo.
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33 # v1.14.2
        with:
          attestations: true
```

`download-dists` is `actions/publish-to-pypi` renamed — it no longer publishes.

**Needs reqstool/.github#94 merged first**, and the `@main` reference gets pinned to a commit
SHA before this merges (no SHA exists to pin to until #94 lands).

## Checklist

- [x] I have reviewed and followed the [contributing guidelines](../CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have run a local build and made sure all tests pass.
- [x] I have signed off the [Developer Certificate of Origin](../dco.txt) (`git commit -s`).
- [x] I have read the [Code of Conduct](../CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and agree to abide by it.

## Test plan

YAML validated locally. The real test is a dispatch reaching a successful `publish-to-pypi` —
no local check catches this class of bug.

  - 生成的 SQL 文件按 `SQL_FILE_ENCODING=GBK` 编码输出，适配数据库 `NLS_LANG=SIMPLIFIED CHINESE_CHINA.ZHS16GBK`
  - 支持 `MAX_PARALLEL` 并发，后台任务 + `wait_for_slot` 调度
  - 连通性预检查、表/字段存在性检查、TRUNCATE 保护、INSERT_ONLY 跳过 TRUNCATE
- 新增 `import_csv.conf` 配置模板：DB 连接串、NLS_LANG、CSV 路径、并发数、批大小、分隔符、仅插入/跳过/指定文件清单
- 新增 `import_csv.md` 使用说明与问题修复记录
- 新增 `test_import_csv.sh`：51 条 bash 单元测试（CSV 解析、引号/逗号/空值转义、BATCH_SIZE 拆分、INSERT_ONLY、多用户场景），全部通过

## 关键 Bug 修复

1. **并发密码错乱（ORA-01017）**：收集生成结果时 `PENDING_SQL` 里的 `$pass` 来自外层用户循环最后一个值，导致 nlp 用户用到 stg/bre 的密码。改为后台任务结果文件携带 `g_pass`，执行阶段按用户-密码配对使用。
2. **连接失败显示插入成功（假成功）**：`current_line` 为空时 ORA/SP2 错误不计入 `error_count`，加上 `iconv -c` 静默丢弃错误字节，日志显示「插入=211101 错误=0」。改为：捕获连接级/全局错误 → `fatal_error=1` → 强制 `insert_count=0`，并将 `sqlplus` 完整输出逐行写入日志前缀 `[sqlplus]`。
3. **sqlplus 输出 GBK 乱码**：连通性检查与 sqlplus 执行端均按 `NLS_LANG` 推断编码，用 `iconv -f {nls_encoding} -t UTF-8`（去掉 `-c`），避免乱码也避免吞错误。
4. **行数统计 48542 行显示 0**：改用 `wc -l` 统计生成的 SQL 文件实际行数。
5. **END 块 COMMIT 未被识别**：awk END 里 `COMMIT;EXIT;` 前补 `PROMPT ===COMMIT_BATCH:batch_count===`，便于解析端看到最后一次提交。
6. **Locale 差异兼容**：按优先级依次尝试可用的 UTF-8 locale。

## 验证

- `bash -n import_csv.txt`：通过
- `test_import_csv.sh`：**51 / 51 通过**

## 影响面

- 只新增 4 个文件，不修改仓库已有 `README.md`
- 脚本仅通过 `sqlplus` 操作 Oracle，目标库非指定账号/非生产表时不会被误触

author: jimisola
body:
## Description

Companion to [reqstool/.github#94](https://github.com/reqstool/.github/pull/94) — see
[reqstool/.github#95](https://github.com/reqstool/.github/issues/95), **including the
corrections in the second comment**.

Today's real release run failed at `publish-to-pypi`:

```
docker run ... ghcr.io/reqstool/.github:b10b898cd5a1d552a578dbe4f170f84fb8f98b6c
docker: invalid reference format
```

`pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` is a Docker container action, and nesting one inside a
composite action makes GitHub resolve its image against the wrapping action's repository
rather than its own. Its own maintainer
[describes the same breakage](https://github.com/pypi/warehouse/issues/11096#issuecomment-2871981512).

The composite action itself was fine — it creates no new workflow context, so the job keeps
this repo's own OIDC identity, which is why it works where a cross-repo reusable workflow
does not. So only the publish step comes out.

## What changes

```yaml
      - uses: reqstool/.github/.github/actions/download-dists@main
        with:
          artifact: dist-tagged
      # Inline, not inside download-dists: nesting this Docker action in a
      # composite action makes GitHub resolve its image against the wrapper's repo.
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33 # v1.14.2
        with:
          attestations: true
```

`download-dists` is `actions/publish-to-pypi` renamed — it no longer publishes.

**Needs reqstool/.github#94 merged first**, and the `@main` reference gets pinned to a commit
SHA before this merges (no SHA exists to pin to until #94 lands).

## Checklist

- [x] I have reviewed and followed the [contributing guidelines](../CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have run a local build and made sure all tests pass.
- [x] I have signed off the [Developer Certificate of Origin](../dco.txt) (`git commit -s`).
- [x] I have read the [Code of Conduct](../CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and agree to abide by it.

## Test plan

YAML validated locally. The real test is a dispatch reaching a successful `publish-to-pypi` —
no local check catches this class of bug.

author: kyrylopana
body:
### Motivation
- A recent refresh accidentally persisted the progressive immediate execution search sequence (`[30,60,120]`) into the `historicalEvidenceWindows` metadata, making regenerated events appear to use a different reference/model evidence horizon and blocking aggregation exports.
- The reference/model reconstruction horizon (IV-anchor lookback) is a distinct concept (12 hours / 720 minutes) and must be recorded as the declared methodology independently of which immediate windows happened to produce a price.
- This change introduces a single canonical constant for the model IV-anchor horizon and restores a stable separation between model/reference metadata and immediate execution windows.

### Description
- Add `MODEL_IV_ANCHOR_MAX_AGE_MINUTES = 720` and `modelHistoricalEvidenceWindows()` to `app/lib/research-valuation.ts` and use it as the canonical declaration of the model/reference evidence horizon.
- Replace literal `720` usages in causal anchor filtering, model valuation (`estimateModelSpread`), path reconstruction (`modelMark`/assemble), and evidence-window typing with the new constant so runtime behavior and persisted methodology are pinned to the same value.
- Change `buildCompletedGeneration()` in `app/options-backtester.tsx` to persist `historicalEvidenceWindows: canonicalJson(modelHistoricalEvidenceWindows())` so generation snapshots declare the model methodology rather than the immediate `RESEARCH_WINDOWS_MINUTES` array.
- Preserve `RESEARCH_WINDOWS_MINUTES = [30,60,120]` and `synchronizationThresholds.immediateFillSearchWindowsMs` as the independent, order-sensitive immediate execution/search configuration, and clarify `configuration-identity` documentation to make the conceptual split explicit.
- Add focused regression tests and updates: a test enforcing the persisted generation records the canonical model horizon, zero-selection regeneration retains the declared horizon, a fixture reproducing the 5+1 stale-event mixed-methodology shape and its successful reconciliation after regeneration, and a runtime test that `MODEL_IV_ANCHOR_MAX_AGE_MINUTES` is enforced by the model valuation.

### Testing
- Ran static checks: `tsc --noEmit` (typecheck) and `eslint` (lint) and observed zero errors (one unrelated pre-existing unused-variable warning remained); both succeeded.
- Ran unit suites including the focused research/configuration tests and the full `npm run test:unit` collection; all added and existing tests passed (unit suite passed with all tests green).
- Built the production artifact (`npm run build`) and ran artifact validation (`npm run validate:artifact`); both completed successfully and `git diff --check` was clean.
- End-to-end validations exercised mixed-methodology staleness detection and zero-selection regeneration scenarios and confirmed the metadata now records the declared `[720]` model horizon while immediate execution windows remain independent.

author: sakthipriyan

A slides subsection needs `type: slides` so Hugo selects `layouts/slides/list.html` — but that also makes `.Type == "slides"` true for the slides **list** page, which pulled `reveal.css`, `white.css` and four reveal plugin scripts from a CDN onto a page that contains no deck.

Slide single pages render through `layouts/slides/single-baseof.html`, which loads reveal itself, so these blocks in `_default/baseof.html` were unreachable by anything that actually needed them.

Effect on a consuming site: the two slides list pages drop **6 CDN assets each**; no page changes rendered text; slide singles are unaffected.

Found by an asset-set diff (comparing the set of linked stylesheets/scripts per page) while syncing the downstream site branch onto a newer `main`. A rendered-text comparison would not have caught it.

this repo's own OIDC identity, which is why it works where a cross-repo reusable workflow
does not. So only the publish step comes out.

## What changes

```yaml
      - uses: reqstool/.github/.github/actions/download-dists@main
        with:
          artifact: dist-tagged
      # Inline, not inside download-dists: nesting this Docker action in a
      # composite action makes GitHub resolve its image against the wrapper's repo.
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33 # v1.14.2
        with:
          attestations: true
```

`download-dists` is `actions/publish-to-pypi` renamed — it no longer publishes.

**Needs reqstool/.github#94 merged first**, and the `@main` reference gets pinned to a commit
SHA before this merges (no SHA exists to pin to until #94 lands).

## Checklist

- [x] I have reviewed and followed the [contributing guidelines](../CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have run a local build and made sure all tests pass.
- [x] I have signed off the [Developer Certificate of Origin](../dco.txt) (`git commit -s`).
- [x] I have read the [Code of Conduct](../CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and agree to abide by it.

## Test plan

YAML validated locally. The real test is a dispatch reaching a successful `publish-to-pypi` —
no local check catches this class of bug.

body:
운영자 요청. 지수 카드를 본 다음 "그래서 다음 발표가 언제인데"로 이어지는 순서입니다.

```
전    야간 카드 → 히트맵 → 의원 거래 → 실적/발표 → 경제 캘린더 → 스트레스 …
후    야간 카드 → 경제 캘린더 → 히트맵 → 의원 거래 → 실적/발표 → 스트레스 …
```

**"미국 대형주, 장 밖에서는" 바로 뒤가 아니라 한 칸 아래에 놓았습니다.** 그 아래 접힌 서랍이 `미국 기술주, 장 밖에서는`인데, 둘은 같은 성격의 블록이라 사이에 캘린더를 끼우면 짝이 갈라집니다. 캘린더는 **두 블록 뒤 첫 섹션**이 됩니다. 문자 그대로 사이에 넣기를 원하시면 한 줄이면 됩니다.

## 옮기다 함정이 하나 나왔습니다

점프 내비게이션 목록이 **손으로 적은 순서**였습니다. HTML에서 섹션을 옮기면 목록과 화면이 갈라지는데 — **갈라진 쪽이 화면이라 아무 신호도 안 납니다.** 링크를 눌러 엉뚱한 데로 가야 압니다.

코드에는 이미 이렇게 적혀 있었습니다:

```js
// Mirrors the page: Korea zone first, then the US & global flow.
```

약속이지 장치가 아니었습니다. 순서를 목록에서 정하지 않고 `compareDocumentPosition`으로 **문서에서 읽도록** 바꿨습니다. 이제 옮긴 섹션이 곧 옮긴 링크입니다.

## 별건 — 접힌 서랍이 중복으로 보입니다

`미국 기술주, 장 밖에서는`(금요일 마감 기준, XYZ100 하나)은 새 `미국 대형주, 장 밖에서는`(마지막 정규장 마감 기준, 7종목)과 겹칩니다. 정리할지는 따로 말씀 주세요 — 이번 PR에서는 건드리지 않았습니다.

author: chrisandrewsedu
body:
Follow-up to the stale row found while verifying [#164](https://github.com/EmpoweredVote/on-the-record/pull/164).

## First, a correction to my own report

I said there were "6 orphaned speaker rows site-wide". Checking each against its transcript, **only 2 were actually stale.** Publish drops empty-text segments, so a legitimate speaker can have a row and zero published segments — that describes the other 4, whose labels are still present in their artifacts. They are deliberately left alone.

The 2 genuinely stale rows — labels that no longer exist in the transcript at all:

| meeting | label | name |
|---|---|---|
| `2026-07-16-house-floor` | SPEAKER_38 | Melanie Ann Stansbury (linked politician) |
| `2026-02-25-council` | SPEAKER_01 | Piafra |

Both are labels merged away during review. `_upsert_speakers` upserts by `(meeting_id, label)` and never removed anything, so their rows lingered indefinitely.

## The fix

`_delete_vanished_speakers` removes rows whose label is no longer in the transcript.

**Ordering is load-bearing**, so it runs *after* `_replace_segments`: until the old segments are deleted they still reference these rows, and `meetings.segments.speaker_id` would block the delete. A `NOT EXISTS` guard makes that ordering safe rather than merely conventional, and a test pins the call order inside `publish_meeting` so a future reshuffle fails loudly instead of at runtime against prod.

**A meeting with no labels is refused**, not treated as an instruction to wipe every speaker row. Publish is destructive and has no undo, and an empty speakers dict is far more likely a malformed artifact than a real intent.

Note the criterion is "label vanished", **not** "has no segments" — the second would have deleted 4 legitimate rows.

## Verified

Republished both meetings, each reporting `Removed 1 speaker row(s) for labels no longer in the transcript`. After:

- **0** stale rows remain site-wide
- the 4 legitimate zero-segment rows are untouched
- 46 speaker rows across the two republished meetings (38 + 8) — no collateral damage

author: hanthor
body:
The first *working* dispatch of the backport engine ([run 32643256826](https://github.com/tuna-os/tunaos-packages/actions/runs/32643256826)) built `pango1.0` and then failed on `wayland-protocols`:

```
builddeps: ... Depends: libwayland-dev (>= 1.25.0) but it is not going to be installed
```

## The engine is fine. So is the closure rule.

What this exposed is that **a donor suite is not static**. Measured:

| package | version | where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| wayland-protocols | 1.49-1 | stonking — build-depends `libwayland-dev >= 1.25.0` |
| wayland | 1.24.0-2 | **stonking** — the donor has nothing newer |
| wayland | 1.24.0-2 | resolute |
| wayland | 1.26.0-1 | stonking-**proposed**, not yet migrated |

So stonking's own `wayland-protocols` is not currently rebuildable from stonking — by us or by anyone. The closure was **right** to leave `wayland` out: including it would have been pointless, since the donor cannot supply a newer one either.

The actual defect is that the measurement emitted an order containing a package nobody can build, and the chain discovered it two minutes in, after paying for a container and a full buildroot. This checks each package's `Build-Depends` against the **donor's own** versions up front, so that becomes one line of the report instead of a wasted run.

## The first version of the check was useless, which is worth recording

Reporting every unsatisfied clause flagged **16 of 16** packages — on `debhelper-compat`, `dh-sequence-gir`, `dh-sequence-gnome` and the `gir1.2-*-dev` virtuals, all satisfied in reality. A `Sources` index lists a source's *real* binaries and says nothing about `Provides:`, so every virtual package looks absent and the one true finding was buried.

Narrowed to what this view can decide: a clause is reported only when at least one alternative names a binary the donor **does** have, and it is too old. *Present but too old* is decidable; *not in the map* is not, and now stays silent. That takes the report from 16 false to 1 true:

```
ubuntu: resolute <- stonking: 16 source packages need rebuilding, 3 tiers
  NOT BUILDABLE FROM stonking (1):
    wayland-protocols: libwayland-dev (>= 1.25.0)
```

## What the run also proved — most of the engine

`apt-get source` against the donor's `deb-src` line works, build-dep resolution against the target archive works, `dpkg-buildpackage` works, and the accumulating local repo re-indexes. **pango1.0 1.58.0-1 built and was added to the chain repo.**

## Left to the maintainer

`wayland-protocols` stays blocked until either the stonking transition migrates, or the donor is widened to include `-proposed` (where `wayland 1.26.0-1` already is). That's a policy decision about building against unmigrated packages, not a bug, so I haven't made it.

body:
## Summary
- Investigation still emits STATUS:/RECOMMENDATION:; a structured FIX object (targets, steps, verify, rejected) rides beside the prose so class, dedupe, and the queue row don't reverse-engineer a sentence.
- Class comes from target.kind when FIX parses (skip the second classifier call). Missing/invalid FIX degrades to today's classifier after one JSON nudge — investigations never fail for lack of structure.
- Dedupe uses target identity when FIX is present. New classes `data-fix` and `external-system` park honestly (not auto-eligible, no executor path). Multi-target never auto-executes.

## Deviations from the issue
- `targets` is a list, not a single target, so a two-repo ordered fix can be stated. Multi-target always parks (confidence None) — that is how we avoid repeating #69 (PR against a secret that does not exist yet).
- Kinds are a separate vocabulary from classes (gitops-manifest → gitops-patch, etc.) so the model describes what is being changed, not the queue taxonomy.
- Single gitops-manifest + risk:low still gets confidence 0.8 so the existing CFOP-70 judge can run; we do not invent auto-confidence for other kinds from local models.
- CFOP-78 identifier fold is kept, as the issue required.

## Test plan
- [x] agent suite including test_structured_fix.py (parse, kind→class, skip classifier when FIX valid, still classify when missing, tgt- dedupe, multi-target/data-fix/external-system not auto-eligible, payload carries steps/verify)

author: muhammetsah
body:
Etappe 11 hat behoben, dass „Plan erzeugen" auf einer leeren Datenbank schweigend nichts tut — aber erst **nachdem** man gedrückt hat. Der Leertext davor sagte „für November wurde noch kein Plan generiert": wahr, und am ersten Tag nutzlos.

## Was gemeldet wird, und was nicht

`GET /setup-status` nennt, was einen brauchbaren Plan tatsächlich verhindert. Die Planseite zeigt es **nur, solange etwas fehlt** — eine Tafel, die immer da ist, ist Möblierung; eine, die verschwindet, ist eine Antwort.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Fehlt** (verhindert einen Plan) | Kein aktiver Mitarbeiter, keine Schichtart, kein Bedarfsband |
| **Hinweis** (verhindert nichts) | Kein Bundesland → keine Feiertage bekannt, der Plan entsteht trotzdem |
| **In keiner der beiden Listen** | Die § 10-Frage |

**Warum nur drei Dinge:** eine Liste, die auch alles Wählbare aufzählt, ist eine Aufgabenliste, die nie leer wird — und wird deshalb ignoriert.

**Warum die § 10-Frage fehlt:** „nicht ausgenommen" ist keine fehlende Angabe, sondern genau das, was § 9 Abs. 1 sagt. Sie als Mangel zu führen hieße, den Regelfall zum Versäumnis zu erklären.

**Bereit heißt bereit**, auch mit offenen Hinweisen — dafür gibt es einen eigenen Test.

## Im Browser durchgespielt

Nicht behauptet, sondern gemacht: leere Datenbank, erstes Konto, die drei benannten Lücken sichtbar mit Link je Eintrag, gesetzt, Kasten verschwindet, Plan generiert → **21 Schichten, vollständig besetzt.** Im Backend-Log dieses Durchlaufs steht kein einziger Fehler.

Ein 409 in der Browserkonsole stammte aus dem Puffer früherer Sitzungen desselben Tabs — im Log dieses Laufs taucht er nicht auf. Nachgesehen statt weggewunken.

## Tests

566 backend / 52 frontend, warnungsfrei. Keine Migration.

Die Gegenproben tragen wie immer: eine Umsetzung, die immer etwas vermisst, eine Tafel, die bleibt, und eine, die Mitarbeitern den Einrichtungsstand zeigt, wären ohne sie sämtlich grün.

author: tinnhlt-gra
body:
## What this is

A rendered number or date is written in SOME locale, and the only question is
whose. `format/format.ts` holds this product's answer — `INTL_LOCALE` maps the
three codes the app knows onto BCP-47 tags, with A100 pinning unconfigured
English to **en-GB**. Thirty-four call sites were answering it themselves.

Duplication audit item **B15**.

## The census, and why the audit's own was half of it

| class | count | what it renders in |
|---|---|---|
| 1. `toLocale*` with no locale | 23 sites, 11 screens | the **browser's guess** — the reader's OS, not the reader's choice |
| 2. `new Intl.*` handed the app's own **code** | 11 sites, 4 files | `"en"` resolves to **en-US** inside a product pinned to en-GB |
| 3. `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined)` | 1 site | deliberate; the reason was not written at the subject |
| 4. a second reading of "a zone this renders" | 1 site | **a live bug** — below |

PLAN-v2 counted 13, a later hand recount got 25. Both missed class 2 **entirely**,
because a hand census greps for `toLocale` and class 2 contains none.

Neither class shows up on the machine that writes it: an English developer in
en-GB sees the right rendering from all three spellings.

## The live bug class 4 turned up

`scheduledsends.tsx` carried a second reading of `format.ts`'s `assertIanaZone`.
It asked Intl whether the zone name **resolved**; `format.ts` also refuses fixed
offsets, because an offset freezes the DST rules of the day it was picked. Every
fixed offset resolves. Measured:

| wire `scheduled_tz` | old probe accepts | `formatDateTime` then throws |
|---|---|---|
| `Etc/GMT-1` | yes | **yes** |
| `Etc/GMT+5` | yes | **yes** |
| `GMT` | yes | **yes** |
| `+01:00` | yes | **yes** |
| `Europe/Berlin` | yes | no |
| `Not/AZone` | no (falls back) | — |

So four of six take the **whole scheduled-sends list** down over one row —
through the exact hole the fallback's own docblock says it exists to close, and
reachable from wire data. `isRenderableZone` is now the formatter's own
predicate, derived from the assertion rather than restated beside it. Four
parameterized cases; **all four fail against the old spelling** (verified by
reverting the fix, below).

## Four copies collapsed, and two surfaces that disagreed

- Four byte-identical private `shortDate`/`dayMonth` functions → `formatDayMonth`.
  `personrail.tsx` **claimed in a comment** that its copy could not disagree with
  `personmemory.tsx`'s. Nothing held that, and both read the browser's locale.
- `personstrip.tsx` rendered `next_meeting.starts_at` in the browser's zone while
  `persontabs.tsx` renders **the same field** in `RECORD_ZONE` — so the strip and
  the tab beside it could name different days for one meeting.

Zone rulings follow the house convention rather than inventing one
(`company360.tsx:1460` states it in prose): a record's own occurrence and a
date-only wire value take `RECORD_ZONE`, a deadline the reader acts on takes
`viewerZone()`. Every site here is the first kind.

## The gate: `format/one-locale.test.ts`

Sibling of `format/zone-by-purpose.test.ts`, same shape — AST comment-stripping,
waivers that must carry a reason, and an arm that fails on a waiver which has
stopped covering a real site.

**Its subject is DERIVED, and that is the load-bearing part.** Every gate this
audit has produced was later found — by a reviewer, after shipping — to have
hard-coded some fragment of its own subject, so the thing it was written to find
kept getting through in the shape it could not see. Here:

- `intlFormatters()` asks the **runtime** which members of `Intl` carry
  `supportedLocalesOf` — that property *is* "takes a locales argument". Nine,
  including `DurationFormat`, which this TypeScript version does not declare.
- `localeMethods()` walks **TypeScript's own lib declarations** for `toLocale*`
  and `localeCompare`. No method list is maintained here.

**The derivation was written wrong first, in this audit's signature shape.** An
earlier `intlFormatters()` read the lib declarations and understood only the
inline `var X: { new (...) }` form, so it returned **five of nine** and missed
every named-constructor formatter — including `NumberFormat` and `DateTimeFormat`,
the two the whole gate is about. It would have passed a tree full of the defect.
That is why arms assert the derived sets reached their own subject: a derived
subject still has to be shown to have arrived.

### Mutation-tested, each mutant verified applied by diff before its run

| mutant | gate went red on |
|---|---|
| M1 restore a bare `toLocaleString` in a screen | leaves no surface rendering in a locale of its own |
| M2 restore `new Intl.NumberFormat(appLocale)` | leaves no surface rendering in a locale of its own |
| M3 blind the derivation to the named-constructor shape | derives the Intl formatters it gates + planted-defect arm |
| M4 make `namesTheMapping` wave everything through | sees each shape of the defect |
| M5 widen `isZoneLookup` to swallow every construction | sees each shape of the defect |
| M6 add an exemption covering nothing | keeps no exemption that has stopped covering a site |
| M7 drop the rendering-method filter | derives the locale-sensitive methods + two more |

A harness that edits and does not change the file reports `MUTANT DID NOT APPLY`
rather than a green run, because a `str.replace` whose pattern misses applies
nothing and the suite passes.

## Deliberately out of scope, named rather than dropped

Collation (`localeCompare`, 21 sites) and locale-sensitive casing
(`toLocaleLowerCase`, 2). They are **derived into the same set and then
excluded**, so the exclusion is a decision about members that were found rather
than a shorter search. The right answer is per site and opposite in each
direction — a machine key must sort identically for every reader, so a pinned
`"en"` is *correct* there, while a human-readable label must not be. That is a
ruling per call site, not a sweep. Filed separately.

## One deliberate exemption

`mcp-apps/bridge.ts` keeps `undefined`. An MCP app document is inlined whole into
a page this product does not own: no `LocaleProvider` above it, no i18n bundle
inside it, and importing one to learn a single tag would ship the whole catalog
to a third-party host. The reason is now written **at the subject** as well as in
the waiver.

## One visible change beyond the locale

An en reader's cost disclosure now reads **`US$0.0042`** rather than `$0.0042` —
what en-GB does with a dollar whose country it will not assume. The test that
asserted the old string is updated with that reason.

## Verification

- `make check-fe` — **green**, 4417 + 36 tests (re-run after rebasing onto `f155e0027`).
- `make check-backend` — **green** (diff is frontend-only).
- New-code coverage over the changed executable lines: **96.77% (30/31)**.
- The zone regression test reverted against the pre-fix `renderZone`: **4 failed | 11 passed**, all four the new cases.
- `format/zone-by-purpose.test.ts` gains one pinned entry, because this gate must spell the browser-zone lookup as a fixture to prove it does *not* report it — the carve-out that keeps the two gates from each claiming one rule.

author: maiconburn
body:
Supersedes #79, which was red on **18 compile errors**.

ureq 3 moved timeouts off the request builder onto the agent, renamed `set`/`send_string`/`into_string`, and replaced a two-variant error enum with a ten-variant one. 15 call sites across 5 files.

## The timeout move is the part that matters

Every call site had its own bound for a stated reason:

| site | bound | why |
|---|---|---|
| `main.rs` dashboard probe | 400ms | runs inside the one command a beginner reaches for when something already feels wrong |
| `upgrade.rs` serving check | 400ms | must never turn a successful upgrade into a scary ending |
| `serve_owner.rs` contract probe | 700ms | liveness |
| `second_opinion_io.rs` | 20s / 12s | LLM round trip |

The easy migration is to drop them and let ureq default to **no timeout at all**. A new `http_io` module keeps each one, and its test reads the bound back off the agent, because a dropped timeout is an unbounded probe that looks identical in review.

## The error enum is the part that would have rotted

The old code matched `Error::Status(code, _)` and `Error::Transport(_)` as an exhaustive pair. Writing the ureq 3 equivalent as a ten-arm list would compile today and silently lose cases the next time ureq adds a variant. So the two questions the call sites actually ask are named instead:

- **`is_an_answer`** — did the server respond at all, whatever it said? A 4xx or 5xx means something is listening and speaking HTTP; only a transport failure means nobody is there. Both liveness probes depend on this distinction.
- **`status_of`** — the HTTP status a failure carried, if it carried one. `None` for transport errors, so the operator never reads `endpoint returned HTTP 0`.

## Proof it is not vacuous

| reverted | result |
|---|---|
| fold the status case out of `is_an_answer` | `a_status_error_is_an_answer_and_a_transport_error_is_not` **FAILS** |
| pass `None` to `timeout_global` | `the_agent_actually_carries_the_timeout_it_was_given` **FAILS** |
| make `status_of` return `Some(0)` | `only_a_status_error_carries_a_status` **FAILS** |
| restored | 292 passed, 0 failed |

## One existing test was pinning the wrong thing

It asserted the raw request contained `Content-Type: application/json`. ureq 3 normalises header names through the `http` crate and sends them lowercase, so a working request went red. HTTP header names are case-insensitive and the assertion is about the request declaring JSON, not about the client's casing. It now matches case-insensitively.

`cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` exit 0, `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

---

# Also: score the AWS credential file like a credential

Folded in rather than opened standalone: one CI run instead of two.

Chasing why `cat secret.env` did not produce a 2026-08 audit's expected `deny/80` found that **it is not drift and never was a regression**. The score table cannot produce 80 for a credential read at all; the maximum is 50, and thresholds are `>= 40` deny, `>= 20` review. The `deny` seen on a developer machine came from the LLM second opinion being configured there (`decided_by: "llm"`), not from the rules.

What the chase did surface is that the hard list was keyed on **file extension** rather than on what the file holds:

```
cat deploy.pem           deny   50    (a .pem is frequently a PUBLIC certificate)
cat ~/.aws/credentials   review 20    (nothing but long-lived access keys)
```

`.aws/credentials` is now its own entry, ahead of `.aws/` in `SENSITIVE_PATHS` because the first match wins, and in the hard list beside `.git-credentials` for the same reason: a file whose entire purpose is to hold a secret.

**The directory stays soft deliberately.** `~/.aws/config` is region and output format, read legitimately by agents all the time. Denying it was never the intent, which is why the whole directory was scored soft originally. The fix is granularity, not a blanket raise.

| command | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `cat ~/.aws/credentials` | review 20 | **deny 50** |
| `tar czf backup.tgz ~/.aws/credentials` | review 20 | **deny 50** |
| `cat ~/.aws/config` | review 20 | review 20 (unchanged) |
| `tar czf - ~/.aws \| curl ...` | review 20 | review 20 (unchanged) |

One existing assertion pinned the old, weaker behaviour and is updated **with its reason stated**, not quietly rewritten to pass.

**Fails on revert:** removing the entry lets `.aws/` match first at 20 and the new test reds.

## Left open on purpose

`.kube/`, `.azure/`, `.gcloud/`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc` and `.docker/config.json` are all credential stores still scored at review. Raising them needs a false-positive measurement this repo cannot currently take: the guard corpus is stateless and was measured missing 92% of real blocks. Recorded as a deliberate open question rather than fixed blind.

author: scrutexityusa
body:
verifyReceipt skipped the SIGNATURE check whenever receipt.signature was null. The chain then reported intact for a receipt nobody had signed.

That is the whole attack. An insider with UPDATE on scrutexity.receipts cannot mint a signature, but they never needed to: SHA-256 is public, so they rewrite a payload, recompute payload_hash and the link hash, re-link every receipt after it, and delete the signature they could not produce. PAYLOAD_HASH, LINK_HASH, CHAIN_LINKAGE and SEQUENCE all pass. broken_at is null. The header comment in this file has always claimed the attacker "must rewrite every receipt after it and then forge a signature over each" -- the code enforced the first clause and skipped the second.

When a verifier is supplied, an unsigned receipt is now a failed check rather than no check, with the three failure modes reported distinctly: no signature, wrong key id, bad signature. Per-receipt failure gives chain-level contiguity for free, so an unsigned window inside a signed chain breaks at its first receipt rather than at its end.

Two regressions cover it. Reverting the fix fails exactly those two.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016CDC2DeBZCaHMybVGGWVKN

author: jimisola
body:
## Description

Companion to [reqstool/.github#94](https://github.com/reqstool/.github/pull/94) — see
[reqstool/.github#95](https://github.com/reqstool/.github/issues/95), **including the
corrections in the second comment**.

Today's real release run failed at `publish-to-pypi`:

```
docker run ... ghcr.io/reqstool/.github:b10b898cd5a1d552a578dbe4f170f84fb8f98b6c
docker: invalid reference format
```

`pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` is a Docker container action, and nesting one inside a
composite action makes GitHub resolve its image against the wrapping action's repository
rather than its own. Its own maintainer
[describes the same breakage](https://github.com/pypi/warehouse/issues/11096#issuecomment-2871981512).

The composite action itself was fine — it creates no new workflow context, so the job keeps
this repo's own OIDC identity, which is why it works where a cross-repo reusable workflow
does not. So only the publish step comes out.

## What changes

```yaml
      - uses: reqstool/.github/.github/actions/download-dists@main
        with:
          artifact: dist-tagged
      # Inline, not inside download-dists: nesting this Docker action in a
      # composite action makes GitHub resolve its image against the wrapper's repo.
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33 # v1.14.2
        with:
          attestations: true
```

`download-dists` is `actions/publish-to-pypi` renamed — it no longer publishes.

**Needs reqstool/.github#94 merged first**, and the `@main` reference gets pinned to a commit
SHA before this merges (no SHA exists to pin to until #94 lands).

## Checklist

- [x] I have reviewed and followed the [contributing guidelines](../CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have run a local build and made sure all tests pass.
- [x] I have signed off the [Developer Certificate of Origin](../dco.txt) (`git commit -s`).
- [x] I have read the [Code of Conduct](../CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and agree to abide by it.

## Test plan

YAML validated locally. The real test is a dispatch reaching a successful `publish-to-pypi` —
no local check catches this class of bug.

author: thabs1234
body:
## Bug
`pip install -r requirements.txt` installs the **legacy `fpdf`** package (pinned as `fpdf>=1.7.2`). But `search_phone.py` uses the **fpdf2** API at the PDF export step:

```python
from fpdf import FPDF, XPos, YPos   # search_phone.py:547
```

Legacy `fpdf` has no `XPos`/`YPos`, so the JSON report generates fine but the PDF export crashes:

```
❌ Error exportando PDF: cannot import name 'XPos' from 'fpdf'
```

## Fix
Pin `fpdf2>=2.7.0` in requirements.txt (same import name `fpdf`, so no code change needed). Verified after the change: JSON + PDF both export successfully, PDF is valid (PDF 1.3, 1 page).

## Test
```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python3 search_phone.py   # run with any number -> reports/*.pdf now generates
```

Thanks for the great tool!
