## 背景

Dockerfile の最終段が `FROM --platform=linux/arm64` と定数を指定しており、Docker のビルドチェック `FromPlatformFlagConstDisallowed` に引っかかっていました。ビルド段も `GOARCH=arm64` を直書きしていたため、アーキテクチャの指定が Dockerfile とワークフローの二か所に散っている状態でした。

実際の真実の源はワークフロー側で、`build-push-action` に `platforms: linux/arm64` を渡しています。

## 変更内容

- 最終段の `--platform=linux/arm64` を削除し、ターゲットプラットフォームは buildx の `--platform` に委ねる
- ビルド段で `ARG TARGETOS` / `ARG TARGETARCH` を受け取り、`GOARCH` に渡す。buildx が自動で注入するため、バイナリとランタイムイメージのアーキテクチャが食い違うことがなくなる
- ビルド段の `--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM` は維持。Go のツールチェインは従来どおりランナーのネイティブアーキテクチャで動き、QEMU エミュレーションは走らない

CI 経由のビルド結果は変更前と同一（`linux/arm64`）です。

author: rambaarde
body:
## Summary

A different **source** from every other screen. Everything else reads agent transcripts or git history — records of what already happened. This reads the OS, right now.

```
PROJECT       BRANCH   WORKTREES  VERSION   TAG      CPU    RUNNING
skeins        develop       none  0.36.0    0.36.0   11.5%  claude
```

- **WORKTREES** counts *other* checkouts, never a raw total that would count this one as one of its own others.
- **VERSION / TAG** is the gap that matters: `package.json` is a number someone typed and can go stale; the tag is what a release process actually pointed at.
- **CPU** is sampled from the OS, batched into one `ps` call and one cwd lookup rather than one per process. Measured on a machine with eight running agents: **178ms** for eight per-process `lsof -p <pid>` calls against **52ms** for one batched call.
- CPU with no resolvable project is folded into `unattributed`, not dropped.

Sampled only while this screen is on screen — never on the 1s paint tick, only the slow poll cadence, plus once immediately when you switch to it. `skeins estate` is the same table in the CLI door.

## Three bugs, each found by driving the real thing

1. **`lsof` exits 1 whenever it can't fully introspect one process**, while still printing everything it could read. `execFileSync` throws on that exit code and discards the good output on `.stdout` — this returned *nothing* on any machine with a process it couldn't fully see, which in practice was every real run.
2. **`pollMachine()` updated a closure variable and `sync()` never picked it up** — the same `sync()`/`reload()` split this file already hit once for `menu`, now for `machine`. `render()` alone couldn't catch it; only a keypress through the real `start()` loop found the gap.
3. **The "no git history" row was `fit()` into the BRANCH column** and truncated to `no git his…`. Every other empty row in this codebase prints the message raw, spanning the row.

## And the sampler is injectable

`start({ sampleMachine })`, the same discipline every git/OS read here already keeps. A test that hit the real process table would pass on a machine running an agent and fail on CI with none — caught before it shipped.

## Housekeeping

- The "will not do" promise is corrected, not silently broken: *"Process trees and CPU gauges"* is narrowed to what's actually ruled out (trees, per-core, memory, disk), and says what preset 6 is instead — one number per project, sampled on request.
- The README's preset table still described preset 5 as session-vs-file contention, which it stopped being when it became change coupling earlier today. Fixed alongside.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 239 passing, 0 failing
- [x] Driven through the real `start()` loop with an injected sampler, asserting the *exact* injected number reaches the screen
- [x] `byRoot()` unattributed-CPU and empty-sample cases
- [x] `worktrees()`/`versionOf()`: porcelain parsing, detached HEAD, no-root, no-tag-and-no-package.json all null (never `0.0.0`)
- [x] Column widths shared between header and rows via one plan — RUNNING widened after `claude+codex` truncated to `claude+c…`
- [x] Verified against the real repo/OS: alignment, gap coloring, worktree wording
- [x] Confirmed no new dependency (checked against the actual `no-dependencies` CI script) and no write outside `install.js`/`cache.js` (checked against the actual `reads-only` CI script)

## Summary

Brand kit v3.1 for the mobile app. Pairs with the main-repo brand PR (desmotech/taikan#288) — the generator lives there: `TAIKAN_MOBILE_ROOT=… pnpm brand:assets:all`.

## What's in it

**Native assets (need a rebuild, not an OTA)**
- `icon.png` (1024, no alpha), `adaptive-icon.png` (inside the 66/108 safe circle), `splash.png`, `notification-icon.png` (white **flat** mark — Android discards gradients here). Sizes: splash 3.2MB → 14KB, icon 910KB → 39KB.
- iOS 18 appearance variants: `ios.icon.{light,dark,tinted}`. Android 13 themed icon: `adaptiveIcon.monochromeImage`.
- `expo-notifications.icon` was never set → wired.
- Android `colorPrimary` was Expo's default navy `#023c69` → `#0E8C8C` (tints the task-switcher header + native dialog accents).

**Store listing art** (`store-assets/`, Console uploads — EAS never derives these)
- Play feature graphic regenerated to kit §08 (the previous one was **FitKit-branded**: old name, old globe). `.jpg` for upload, `.png` alongside.
- `play/icon-512.png`, `appstore/icon-1024.png`. README updated; marks which assets are generated vs captured.
- App Store screenshots are already Taikan-branded and current (separate, non-repo asset set). Play screenshots still show FitKit and aren't touched by this PR — captured from a running app.

**Code**
- `FKBrandMark` redrawn in `react-native-svg` — one source for the 20px tab bar and the 160px splash; picks gradient/flat from `size`. Old API (`size`, `style`) unchanged.
- `colors.ts`: `primary` light `#0E8C8C → #0B7575` (white on the raw teal is 4.08:1 — fails AA on buttons and own-message bubbles); `brandTeal` keeps the raw value for graphics. Violet tokens added (`violet`, `violetText`, `violetPress`, `onViolet`, `violetSoft`, `violetEdge`) — no call site yet, there is no Spotter/AI surface in the app. Dead `mauve` removed.
- Animated splash now matches the kit: tagline **"Train. Track. Thrive."** (was "Train · Track · Progress" — the app and the website disagreed), one ramp colour per word in en/he/ru; wordmark Rubik SemiBold at −18/1000; violet halo on dark (kit lights the mark from violet on dark grounds); non-brand `#36D6C6` → `#2AB8B8`.

## Verified

`tsc` clean · `app.config.ts` asset paths all resolve · ran `expo prebuild` and inspected the output directly: iOS `AppIcon.appiconset` has all three appearances with correct alpha per appearance (light opaque, dark transparent, tinted flattened opaque grayscale), Android adaptive icon has `<foreground>` + `<monochrome>`, notification icon registered for both FCM and Expo notifications, `colorPrimary` confirmed in `colors.xml`.

## Follow-ups

- Native rebuild (`eas build`) to actually see icon/splash/notification icon — Expo Go only shows the manifest icon and won't reflect this until a new build.
- Re-capture Play store screenshots on a Taikan build (only if/when Play submission is active).
- Play Console: upload the new icon-512 + feature graphic (one-time manual upload, not a build input).

body:
## Summary

PR 2 of 3 for #1361 (saved conversations on `/ai`). Frontend only, on top of PR 1's backend (#1365). `/ai` gets a **per-conversation URL** (`/ai/c/:id`), a **conversations pane** in the left rail replacing the Pages tree on AI routes, reopenable history with rename/delete, and a simplified `/ai` page. Design of record: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-17-ai-conversation-history-design.md` — **read its `Amendment (2026-08-18, dev drift before PR 2)` block first; it supersedes three sentences of the body**. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-ai-conversation-history-pr2-frontend.md` (18 tasks, executed one implementer + one independent reviewer each, then a whole-branch review).

Sequencing (spec): PR 3 (auto-title + pending-title polling) comes after this. Squash-merge; not stacked.

## Changes

**Routing and thread identity**
- `shared/lib/ai-routes.ts` (`isAiRoute` / `conversationIdFromPath` / `conversationPath`) and the `/ai/c/:conversationId` route; `resolveAiPageId` returns `null` on AI routes, so a legacy `/ai?pageId=` bookmark opens a plain new chat.
- Threads are keyed by **location** (`draft` / `conv:<id>` / `page:<id>`), not by page, and every thread carries an **identity**: `runStream`'s writers dispatch by identity, so a re-key is followed and a replaced thread's write is dropped instead of landing in the fresh draft. `activeThreadId` is the single switch signal (abort-on-switch, Deep Search reset, attachments scope, external URLs).
- The state machine: promotion on the first answer (re-key + `replace` navigation, never from the dock), stale-`conversationId` 404 handled before streaming, a `conversationId: null` frame clears the id without resurrecting the row, and a completed exchange is mirrored into every retained thread holding the same id.
- Hydration of `conv:` threads is keyed on **state, not presence**, with load/error states, **Retry**, and `historyTruncated` from both its sources (reopen and each ask's final frame). A late response can no longer toast, navigate or change the mode of a conversation you have since switched to.

**The pane** (`features/ai/conversations/`)
- `AiConversationsSidebar` (chassis, resize handle, New chat, filter past 8 rows, footer count), `ConversationList` (recency groups, roving tabindex, the three list states, Show more), `ConversationRow` + `ConversationRowMenu` (page chip, kebab, inline rename, delete confirm), `group-by-recency.ts`, `use-conversation-list.ts` (keyset `useInfiniteQuery`), `use-conversation-mutations.ts`, and `shared/hooks/use-list-roving-focus.ts`.
- Mounted by `AppLayout` as the third arm of both sidebar ternaries; `AiContext`'s `useState` mirror of the list is deleted (ADR-009: server data lives in TanStack Query).

**`/ai` page**
- The Pages tree leaves `/ai` (both tree implementations; all three `/ai?pageId=` producers gone, with a guard pinning their absence). Page scope, the context chip, the model select and `+ Sub-pages` are removed from `/ai`.
- **New chat** lives in the `/ai` heading row via `HeaderHost` (owner decision, 2026-08-23 — the 48px header slot this originally targeted was retired by #1377/#1378).
- The action selector on `/ai` offers **Q&A + Generate + the five create skills**; the URL-mode allow-list stays `ask|generate` only, so `?mode=improve|diagram` falls back to Q&A.
- History note ("Older messages… no longer sent to the model") on **both** composers; `unavailable` sources render inert with a title; `SourceThumbnail` is **viewport-gated** (owner decision) so a reopened thread no longer fetches every persisted thumbnail at mount.
- **The dock gains a Sub-pages toggle** (owner decision): PR 2's `/ai` simplification removed the app's only `includeSubPages` writer, and the capability belongs where a page context exists.

**Docs**: `04-frontend-structure.md`, `09-flow-rag-chat.md`, `docs/architecture/README.md`, `docs/USER-GUIDE.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (pane paragraph, the DeepSearchToggle/rail/action-set sentences, and the now-true statement that the dock offers Generate-shaped create skills), the docked-AI spec's second dated amendment, and the #1361 spec's PR 2 flag + Architect's calls 9/10 marked decided.

## Known follow-ups (deliberate, not defects)

- No conversation title is shown while the rail is collapsed or the mobile drawer is closed (the amendment defers it).
- `includeSubPages` remains provider-level and session-sticky — pre-existing and documented in CLAUDE.md as the Deep Search contrast case; a per-question or per-page reset is a follow-up. A dock **chip run** posts the flag with no control on screen.
- The pane's footer count reads `0 conversations` beside a failed-list block (failure-is-not-emptiness, same class the tree learned).
- Picking **Generate** ticks *Custom Draft* (`applyAssistantAction` sets `createSkill: 'custom'`; `createSkill` is non-nullable) — pre-existing on `/ai`, now visible on the dock too.
- Six new `--glass-pill-hover` callsites: the pane copies the tree's recipe verbatim; the ~80-callsite rename stays one mechanical sweep.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added/updated — frontend **299 files / 4,583 tests**, all passing
- [x] Type checking passes (`npx tsc --noEmit`, backend + frontend)
- [x] Linting passes (`npm run lint`, `--max-warnings=0`)
- [x] Documentation updated — `docs/architecture/*`, `docs/USER-GUIDE.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, both specs
- [ ] Screenshots attached — pending (UI change; no browser available to the agent that built it)
- [x] No secrets committed

## Related Issues

Relates to #1361 (PR 2 of 3 — the issue closes with PR 3). Builds on #1365.

author: frapercan
body:
This is **the second half of PR #800**. The first half merged on 20 August; this commit was left behind on a local branch, which is how `benchmarkView.ts` and its test came to be sitting **untracked in the live checkout** where I found them today.

## What moves

Forty lines of intermediate consts inside a 1,133-line component. Every one is a decision about what a reader sees, and two are fallbacks whose whole job is to stop the page going blank. **A fallback nobody can test is a fallback nobody knows still works.**

They become pure functions in `lib/benchmarkView.ts` with 20 tests over the cases that actually matter:

- a lineage chip matching no category falls back to the unfiltered list **and reports the fallback** rather than applying it silently (this fires on a benchmark with only NK rows when the reader clicks "PK only")
- `"all"` with one eval set names that set; `"all"` with several names none, because naming one would be a lie about what is on screen
- "curation hid everything" stays distinguishable from "there is nothing", since only the first should point at the Show all escape hatch

## Rebasing it

Three conflicts against current develop. The import conflict kept both sides. The block conflict resolved to the refactored form after checking, const by const, that develop had gained no logic the lifted functions lack.

## Verification

`apps/web`: **286 tests pass**, typecheck clean on the touched files.

The turbopack build is **not** run here and I am not claiming it: inside a worktree `node_modules` is a symlink pointing outside the tree and the build fails for that reason alone. Same caveat the original commit carried.

author: dima-spectorr
body:
feat(ci): give the anchor's consumers a fallback, because an empty pg is routine

The first adopter (#288) read the contract against a real repository and found
the gap. The anchor degrades on three branches -- a fork pull request, a host
older than the contract, and a host another run already holds -- and on all
three it publishes `pg` EMPTY and brings up no stack. The document stated the
consequence for the FORK branch only, and the example read `pg` straight into a
URL with no fallback at all.

The fork branch is the rarest of the three. The anchor is deliberately unpinned,
so it lands on any free slot including a free slot on a host somebody else's run
has pinned; `ci-pin-hold` answers `pinned=0` and the run continues without a
stack. On a private repository the fork branch never fires and that one fires
whenever two pull requests are in flight. So an adopter copying the example
would get `postgres://ci@127.0.0.1:/app` on an ordinary busy afternoon, and a
red required check on a run where nothing was wrong.

`.github/actions/shared-infra-db` is the fallback, published once for the same
reason the anchor is: five repositories writing it themselves is five copies of
every later fix. It hands back the shared stack's band port when there is one
and starts a throwaway Postgres on this job's own runtime when there is not, so
the suite cannot tell the difference. It also reports `shared`, which is worth
logging -- a run where every job reports 0 is a fleet problem currently wearing
a green tick.

A composite ACTION and not a reusable workflow, for the reason
`.github/actions/playwright-ui` already gives: shipping steps rather than a job
keeps `runs-on` and `timeout-minutes` in the consumer's own workflow as literals
its own gate can read.

It tears nothing down, deliberately. `slot-reset.sh completed` already removes
every container on the slot's daemon at the end of every job and fails closed if
it cannot, sparing only a held slot. A teardown step would duplicate a host-side
guarantee that has to be right anyway, since a job that dies does not run its
own cleanup either.

The Windows leg gets no fallback and cannot: there is no container runtime on a
Windows host. Its `if:` in the example now also requires a non-empty `addr`, so
a degraded run skips that leg instead of dialling a URL with a hole in it.

Local: example checker 7/7, action pins clean, workflow permissions clean,
generic literals clean, docs pins green, pipefail readers 0 findings.

Refs #248, #288

author: t-kalinowski
body:
## Summary

Allow a code-bearing `send` call to declare additive R packages, Python packages, and DuckDB extensions that must be prepared before the cell runs. This removes the need to split a package-dependent cell across `session(action = "prepare")` and `send` while preserving explicit, retained requirement declarations.

## User-facing changes

- Add `send.requirements` with the same shape, validation, limits, and trust policy as session requirements.
- Treat declared requirements as preconditions of the cell for initial, running, stopped, and restart-required sessions. Successful combined calls return normal cell output; failed preparation does not dispatch the cell.
- Apply `timeout_ms` only after the cell is dispatched, preserve preparation-before-stdin and stdin-before-evaluate ordering, and record requirements in the original `send` journal event.
- Clarify that preparation does not import, attach, or load packages or extensions. Cells are not inspected for requirements and missing-package errors are not retried.

## Internal changes

- Add one exclusive pre-evaluation operation that covers requirement deltas, host resolution, live or pre-start preparation, and evaluation reservation and launch. Ordinary sends keep their existing admission path.
- Share requirement-delta calculation and pre-start resolution with restart while keeping their different commit rules separate.
- Extend public and server-relay transcript coverage for validation, live-state preservation, idempotence, failure and output ownership, cancellation and replacement races, session recording, and the timeout boundary.

author: ruancarvalhoo
body:
Closes #456

## Tipo de mudança

(Selecione apenas uma opçaõ)
tipo:

- [ ] marco-no-projeto
- [x] nova-feature
- [ ] bug-fix

## Checklist

- [x] O código foi testado localmente
- [x] Foram adicionados testes relevantes
- [x] Não quebrou nenhuma funcionalidade existente
- [ ] A documentação foi atualizada

## O que muda

A API passa a encerrar na inicialização, com mensagem explícita e código de saída 1, quando `SECRET_KEY` está ausente ou tem menos de 32 caracteres. `back/.env.local.example` deixa de trazer um segredo literal.

## Por que

O segredo era lido sem verificação nenhuma (`back/src/auth/constants/constants.ts:2-4`), e nada no bootstrap conferia o valor antes de `app.listen`. Duas consequências:

**Sem `SECRET_KEY` a aplicação subia normalmente.** `JwtModule.register({ secret: undefined })` não reclama na inicialização, então a falha só aparecia no primeiro login, como `500` sem indicação da causa, e na verificação do token virava `401 Token expirado` (`back/src/auth/auth.guard.ts:73`), mensagem que não corresponde ao problema.

**Um segredo fraco permite forjar tokens.** O algoritmo é HS256 e o token fica no `localStorage` e no cookie do navegador, portanto é quebrável offline quando o segredo é curto e de alfabeto reduzido. Quem obtiver o segredo assina tokens com `id_level: 1` que o `AuthGuard` aceita como legítimos. O `back/.env.local.example` trazia exatamente esse tipo de valor, `abcdefghijklmnopq`, 17 caracteres de letras minúsculas sequenciais, enquanto `.env.development.example:19` e `.env.production.example:19` já usam placeholder e declaram o requisito de 32 caracteres.

## Como

`back/src/common/validate-secret-key.ts` expõe `validateSecretKey`, que lança quando a variável está ausente e quando o comprimento é menor que `MIN_SECRET_KEY_LENGTH`, informando o valor recebido. `back/src/main.ts` chama a função como primeira instrução do `bootstrap`, antes de `NestFactory.create`, e o `catch` que já existia converte a exceção em mensagem e `process.exit(1)`.

O tratamento segue o precedente do próprio repositório: `back/src/database/prisma.service.ts:8-11` e `back/prisma/seed.ts:5-8` já derrubam a execução quando `DATABASE_URL` falta.

## Verificação

Comportamento verificado com a aplicação compilada:

| Cenário | Saída |
| --- | --- |
| Sem `SECRET_KEY` | `Erro ao iniciar a aplicação: Error: SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set`, código 1 |
| `SECRET_KEY` com 17 caracteres | `Erro ao iniciar a aplicação: Error: SECRET_KEY environment variable must have at least 32 characters, got 17`, código 1 |
| `SECRET_KEY` com 40 caracteres | segue o boot normalmente, `Starting Nest application...` |

Testes: `back/test/common/validate-secret-key.spec.ts`, seis casos, cobrindo o limite de 32 caracteres, segredo mais longo, variável ausente, string vazia, segredo curto e a leitura de `process.env` quando a função é chamada sem argumento.

- `npm run lint` em `back/`: passa.
- `npm test` em `back/`: 237 testes, 40 suítes, todos passam.
- `npm run build` em `back/`: passa.

author: yusufaf
body:
Stacked on #1 (find-in-article) -- second half of the two-phase plan. Adds reading-position sync: your scroll position closes as a reserved annotation, rides the existing annotation sync queue to the server, and shows up as a highlight in wallabag's web reader.

**Why an annotation and not a new server field:** stock wallabag has no reading-progress field (wallabag/wallabag#2643 is open since 2016, unmerged), and this repo isn't patching the server. An annotation is a real feature the server already supports end-to-end, so reusing it needed zero server-side or sync-layer changes -- just a fixed sentinel text (`Left off here — wallabag-android`) to recognize it, and a filter so it doesn't clutter the in-app annotation list.

**Why XPath+offset and not the existing percentage-based position:** the app already saves/restores a pixel-scroll percentage (`Article.articleProgress`) -- that part isn't new. But a percentage is device/font/reflow-dependent and never reaches the server. The anchor format here matches annotator.js's own xpath-range serialization (traced through the minified `annotator.min.js` bundled in this repo), so it resolves identically in this app and in the web reader. The percentage-based restore still runs as a fallback when there's no anchor yet, or resolution fails.

**A real bug found along the way:** `addAnnotation()`/`deleteAnnotation()` bind to a service via `bindService()`, and that only completes if the calling Context is still alive when `onServiceConnected()` fires. The capture in `onStop()` is kicked off from an async `evaluateJavascript()` callback, which can land after the activity has started finishing (e.g. back button) -- so the bind silently never connects and the write is lost. Fixed by using `getApplicationContext()` for these specific calls.

Verified on-device (synthetic seeded article, no real server available in this environment):
- Capture on close, skip-when-unchanged, delete+replace-on-move (confirmed via logcat, no duplicate/leaked annotations)
- Anchor-based restore on reopen lands exactly at the captured paragraph
- Reserved annotation stays out of the in-app annotation list; a real annotation created independently still renders fine
- `compileDebugJavaWithJavac` + `lintDebug` both clean

**Not verified in this pass** (needs a real wallabag server, out of scope for this environment): the actual web-UI round-trip -- that the highlight renders correctly in the browser reader from the synced XPath+offset range. That's the one part of the original plan's verification checklist not covered here.

author: kaeawc
body:
Follow-up to #4577.

## What this is (and isn't)

Reviewing the code showed that **#4577's core ask was already satisfied by #4649**. At this module's Kotlin language version (`build-kotlin-language = "2.3"`), a non-exhaustive `when` over the `StaleFrameContextAction` enum is a **compile error** — in statement *and* expression form. So the typed-enum dispatch #4649 introduced already made it structurally impossible to route a stale-frame rejection through an unsupported action without a correlated response.

This PR is therefore a **small readability/robustness follow-up**, not a new guarantee:

- Extract the dispatch out of the coroutine lambda into an expression-bodied `broadcastStaleFrameRejection`. Expression form keeps exhaustiveness compiler-enforced even if the language version is ever lowered below the level where non-exhaustive `when` **statements** became errors (pre-2.0 they are only warnings).
- Behaviour is unchanged: identical per-action response envelopes for `tap`, `swipe`, `drag`, `set_text`, `ime_action`, `global_action`; same coroutine scope; same error text.
- Extend `StaleFrameContextRejectionWiringTest` to assert the delegation, and keep the meaningful source guard: **no `else ->`** (a catch-all is the one way to defeat the compiler's exhaustiveness and reopen the silent-timeout window), all six actions routed, per-action envelope shapes, typed call sites.

## Codex P2 addressed

Codex correctly pointed out that a source-shape assertion requiring the *expression body* would wrongly fail a safe block-bodied refactor, since at language 2.3 a block-bodied statement `when` is equally exhaustive. Verified locally: converting the dispatcher to a block body with a missing branch fails to compile (`'when' expression must be exhaustive`). The expression-vs-block assertion has been **removed**; the no-`else ->` guard remains.

## Validation

- `:control-proxy:testDebugUnitTest --tests "*StaleFrameContext*"` — pass
- Sibling `*BroadcastGuardScanner*` — pass
- `ktfmt --google-style` — clean; `:control-proxy:detekt` — pass
- Rebased on latest `main`.

If preferred, an equally valid outcome is to **close #4577 as already-resolved by #4649** and close this PR — its remaining value is modest.

author: iderex
body:
Closes #82.

Approving is the moment something else is asked to fetch the title, and nothing asked. Two types took the bridge, one to say whether a service is configured and one to say whether it answered, and neither handed anything over. There was nowhere to keep an answer either: neither the model nor the store carried the word.

    git grep -n 'IRequestBackend' 21c7232 -- Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/ | grep -v ':Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/Bridge/'
    21c7232:Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/Api/CapabilitiesController.cs:37:    private readonly IRequestBackend _backend;
    21c7232:Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/Api/CapabilitiesController.cs:45:    public CapabilitiesController(IInstallSettings settings, IRequestBackend backend)
    21c7232:Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/Api/HealthController.cs:39:    private readonly IRequestBackend _backend;
    21c7232:Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/Api/HealthController.cs:58:        IRequestBackend backend,
    21c7232:Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/PluginServiceRegistrator.cs:85:        serviceCollection.AddSingleton<IRequestBackend, NoRequestBackend>();

    git grep -in 'backend' 21c7232 -- Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/Model/ Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/Storage/ ; echo "exit=$?"
    exit=1

## What is here

`MediaRequest.Backend` carries what a service called the request and which service said so. `BridgeSubmission` is the one place that writes it, and the approval path is the one place that calls it.

It runs after the decision has been written and never instead of it. A submission that failed leaves an approved request carrying no reference and an error in the log, and the approval is not undone: the operator decided, the queue already holds the decision, and rolling it back because a service on another machine was down would be the plugin overruling a person.

**Submitting the same request twice is refused, and the request refuses it.** That is the answer this issue asks to be stated. A reference is written only after a service answered, so a request carrying one has already been handed over. Harmless was the other available answer and it is the wrong one: a second submission of an accepted request is a second copy of the same download over there, and nothing on this side could tell the two apart afterwards.

The one case that needs somebody to look is the service accepting a request and the reference then failing to be written back. Nothing retries, because retrying is the duplicate the rule above exists against, and the log line carries the identifier the service issued so the two can be reconciled by hand.

On a server with no external service none of this happens and none of it is reported. The shipping bridge hands back no reference, which is an answer rather than a failure.

## What was watched failing

Every guard here was watched red for the reason it names, by mutating the tree and running the suite. All of them on `net9.0` at the head of this branch.

The register comparison, run before `BridgeSubmission` had a row in `docs/bridge.md`:

    Assert.Equal() Failure: Values differ
    Expected: CapabilitiesController | HealthController
    Actual:   BridgeSubmission | CapabilitiesController | HealthController

The submission removed from the approval path, leaving the class and its tests in place:

    SubmittingAnApprovalTests.AFailedSubmissionLeavesTheRequestApprovedAndSaysSoInTheLog [FAIL]
    SubmittingAnApprovalTests.AnApprovalWithAServiceConfiguredIsHandedOverOnceAndTheReferenceIsKept [FAIL]
    Assert.Single() Failure: The collection was empty

The refusal to submit twice deleted, so the check is only on the state:

    SubmittingAnApprovalTests.ARequestThatWasAlreadyHandedOverIsNotHandedOverAgain [FAIL]
    Assert.Single() Failure: The collection contained 2 items

A failure rethrown instead of being reported, which is the one-line mistake that turns a decision that was taken into a call that reports failure:

    SubmittingAnApprovalTests.AFailedSubmissionLeavesTheRequestApprovedAndSaysSoInTheLog [FAIL]
    System.InvalidOperationException : This service is not taking anything today.

And the rule that keeps the request a value with nothing to resolve, with the new field taken out of the widened line:

    MediaRequestTests.EveryFieldIsAPlainValueSoTheRecordCannotFetchAnything [FAIL]
    Assert.Empty() Failure: Collection was not empty
    Collection: ["Backend is BackendReference"]

The tree passes, on both server lines. The runner reports in the language this machine is set to, and its output is pasted rather than translated:

```
dotnet test Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests.sln --configuration Release -warnaserror

Bestanden!   : Fehler:     0, erfolgreich:   665, übersprungen:     0, gesamt:   665, Dauer: 16 s - Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests.Tests.dll (net10.0)
Bestanden!   : Fehler:     0, erfolgreich:   665, übersprungen:     0, gesamt:   665, Dauer: 17 s - Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests.Tests.dll (net9.0)
```

658 on the base and 665 here, which is the seven legs this adds.

## The size, and why it was not split further

    git diff --numstat origin/master...HEAD | awk '{a+=$1;d+=$2} END{print a" added, "d" deleted"}'
    753 added, 22 deleted

That is over the 400-line proxy and it is not claimed as an exception, because none of the declared shapes covers it: nothing here is generated, vendored, moved, imported as evidence, or one substitution rule applied everywhere. What it is instead is a change whose parts only make sense together. A field with nothing writing it, or a submitter with nowhere to keep its answer, is not reviewable alone, and this issue has already been re-planned once for exactly this reason: the operator-facing half was split out and is #283.

Where the size actually is:

    git diff --numstat origin/master...HEAD | sort -rn | head -5
    312     0       Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests.Tests/Bridge/SubmittingAnApprovalTests.cs
    139     0       Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/Bridge/BridgeSubmission.cs
    76      0       Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests.Tests/Doubles/AServiceThatKeepsWhatItIsHanded.cs
    60      0       Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests.Tests/Doubles/AServiceThatWillNotTakeAnything.cs
    35      1       Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests.Tests/Doubles/ABridgeSubmission.cs

Fifteen of the twenty-six files are one line each: the controller took one more dependency, and every test that builds it hands one in.

## What this does not do

**No adapter is added and nothing leaves any server.** The only implementation of the bridge in this tree is still the one for a server that has no service, and the plugin still holds no HTTP client outside the notification sink:

    git grep -n ': IRequestBackend' -- Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/
    Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/Bridge/NoRequestBackend.cs:23:public sealed class NoRequestBackend : IRequestBackend

    git grep -ln 'HttpClient\|IHttpClientFactory\|WebRequest' -- Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/
    Jellyfin.Plugin.Requests/Notify/OutboundSink.cs

`docs/personal-data.md` was read against this and is unchanged. Its bridge row says the path is not built and is off until a backend is set, and both still hold: what is built is the caller, and there is nothing behind it to call.

**Nothing was run against an external service or against a Jellyfin server.** No such service exists in this tree to run against, and the suite reaches none. What is measured is what this plugin hands the interface and what it keeps of the answer, which is narrower than watching a request arrive in a real service.

**Which failures an adapter tells apart is not decided here.** Unreachable, a refused credential, an unknown title and a version this adapter does not know are #86, and what is settled here is only that none of them loses an approval.

**No second reader has read this.** Nothing on this board tonight is a second pair of eyes, and the evidence above stands in place of one rather than beside one.

author: automateintelligence
body:
Makes the dual-host spec's definition of done executable, then closes it. **7/7 green.**

Before this branch the spec's seven assertions were prose. Nothing ran them, so "is the dual-host design done?" had no machine-checkable answer.

    CONDUCTOR_GATE_SLUG=2026-08-10-codex-dual-host-conductor-design-5f6520fc ./bin/conductor assert run
    SUMMARY: 7/7 green -> gate DONE (exit 0)

## What the gate found

Each assertion turned up a real defect, not bookkeeping:

- **A-DH-1** — `driver.py` compared a session prompt against the literal `/conductor:autodev`, a Claude slash command deciding core control flow. Latent on Codex (that leg returns early), but wrong the moment any non-Claude scheduled-task mechanism is wired.
- **A-DH-4** — the worker launch was **unbounded on both hosts**, inside `flock -n 9`. A host that never answers held `resume.lock` forever and every later tick exited 0 silently. This affects Claude users today.
- **A-DH-6** — `branches.py` returned the literal `"main"` on any resolution failure, so a repo whose default branch is anything else could be merged into wrongly.
- **A-DH-7** — `finish`/`resume`/`heartbeat`/`status` did not exist, so nothing enforced that Conductor never completes the final PR.

## The two changes needing scrutiny

**A frozen assertion was re-derived.** `a10` required `default_branch()` to return exactly `"main"` on failure — the behaviour A-DH-6 forbids. Both were machine-checked; they could not both hold. `a10` was re-derived, not deleted: it kept the never-empty half, **tightened** it (failure-path stdout must now be byte-empty), and gained a never-a-literal-fallback clause. Exactly one digest moved; 17 of 18 byte-identical, 0 added, 0 removed.

**One spec bullet was narrowed.** §"Failure handling" required every actionable failure to report a run key. A-DH-4's Claim governs preflight, which runs at step 0 to decide whether a run may start — it cannot name the run whose existence it is authorising. The bullet now reads "when the failure occurs within a resolved run; a pre-run capability probe reports the host id and the project root in their place". The recogniser is **conditional, not relaxed**: seven mutations confirm it, including one where naming the project root but not the host goes red.

## How A-DH-4 was closed

Not with a timeout. A real fire in a production log ran **2h58m with zero bytes written until the final second**, so no wall-clock ceiling separates a long fire from a dead one. The fire is bounded on **silence** — CPU consumed by the process group OR bytes appended to the log, either resets the clock. 120s before first sign of life, 1800s after. Both signals are required: headless Claude prints nothing for hours but burns CPU; `codex exec` streams from second one.

Supervision lives in the mechanical layer, so `resume_fire_command()` is unchanged and **the Claude byte-pins pass unmodified** — the proven invocation is byte-for-byte what live fires run.

## Verification

7/7 dual-host · 18/18 flat gate · `[GATE] done-gate baseline intact` · 1283 passed / 1 skipped · pyright 51 (main's baseline) · ruff clean on changed files

## Known gaps

- `.assertions.md` is on `main` and not an ancestor of this branch, so it still describes the unamended clause. The two must be reconciled before merge.
- `gate freeze` cannot run in this repo (two legacy `*.assertions.md` in `docs/specs/` with no `goal.md` to disambiguate). The a10 re-freeze used `freeze.record()` directly with the same value `_assertions_source` returns for a repo with no candidates. Pre-existing defect, worth its own fix.
- A-DH-7's argument table is hand-maintained; the verbs are enumerated but bash declares no arguments.

author: rebecca554owen
body:
## Summary

Channel (Telegram etc.) turns currently go silent during execution: text streams only at the end in one burst, tool calls are invisible until the turn completes, and there is no live reasoning view. This PR brings the channel surface to parity with a CLI/Hermes-like experience:

- **Live text streaming** (`send_streaming` on the Telegram adapter): first chunk posts a message, subsequent deltas edit it in place with `StreamThrottle` coalescing and flood backoff; falls back to batched `send` on failure or 4096-overflow so no content is lost.
- **Edit reconcile fix**: `streaming_reply_kwargs` routes replies to the originating chat; `edit()` accepts the explicit `chat_id` kwarg so terminal snapshot replacement no longer fails with `TypeError` (`stream_terminal_reconcile_failed`).
- **Hermes-style progress bubble**: one silent, accumulating status message per turn (edited ~every 1.5s) interleaving:
  - tool lines via the `ToolHook` path (`before_tool`/`after_tool` fire synchronously at execution time — the public ToolUse events are transactional/buffered, hence unusable for live progress): `⚙ tool arg` → `✓`/`✗`
  - thinking lines from the unbuffered stream sink: `💬 <latest reasoning snippet>`
- **Runtime registry** (weak-ref, keyed by channel id) binds the active channel relay to the turn's `ToolContext`; non-channel callers (CLI/cron) get a zero-cost no-op hook.
- Opt-out via `[channels] tool_progress = false` in config.toml.

## Testing

- Offline unit simulation of the full notify chain: thinking → tool start → tool end interleaving, accumulating edits, error marking, ref extraction from Telegram `sendMessage` responses.
- Live-validated against a real Telegram channel turn with multi-tool loops.
- Verified CLI path unaffected (hook resolves to `None` for non-channel callers).

Fixes the "silent until done" channel UX reported by users watching long tool loops.

author: sebastian-w-klein
body:
Two breaks came back clean that should not have. In both cases Rule 6 — the rule whose whole job is proper nouns — returned **OK**, and the *correct* break read identically in the report, so the proofreader had nothing to go on either way.

## `Word-/sworth`

Rule 6.2 was one-sided: it fired only when the break fell *inside* a name's terminal morpheme. `Word-/sworth` leaves `-worth` whole and is still wrong — the linking s belongs to `Words`, and carried over it makes a second element nobody set.

The morpheme boundary is now treated as a **seam**, and a break short of it answers to the element in front — which, unlike the name itself, is often an ordinary word MW carries.

- **MW knows the element** → the break must be one of *its* division points. `but·ter` licenses `But-/terfield` and rejects `Butt-/erfield`; `words` is dotted nowhere, so `Words-/worth` is the only place Wordsworth divides.
- **MW does not know it** → the letters the break would carry over must at least be able to form a syllable, which means containing a vowel. `Farn-/sworth` and `Islin-/gton` strand a bare consonant on the morpheme; `Isl-/ington` carries `ing` and is left alone.

```
Word-/sworth   VIOLATION  “Words”, the element before “-worth”, is undivided in MW,
                          so the seam is the only place “Wordsworth” breaks;
                          break at “Words-worth” instead
Words-/worth   OK         breaks at the seam before “-worth”
```

## `Sha-/ron`

Rule 6.3 accepted any break after a vowel. `Sha-/ron` follows a vowel exactly as `Ma-/rina` does and one of the two is wrong, so the last letter of the fragment cannot be the whole test. Nothing the tool can reach settles Sharon — MW carries it only inside multi-word headwords, which are dropped — so the honest answer is to stop blessing it.

TeX's en-US patterns are now consulted before that guess is called a pass: where they divide the name elsewhere, or as with Sharon find nowhere to divide it at all, the row goes to a human instead.

```
Sha-/ron   NEEDS CHECK  the break follows a vowel, but that alone does not make it
                        right — “Sharon” has no MW entry, and TeX en-US patterns
                        find nowhere at all to divide “Sharon”; decide this one by
                        hand (Rule 6.4)
Ma-/rina   OK           the break follows a vowel (Rule 6.3)
```

TeX never *licenses* a break here and never raises a violation — it omits legitimate points as readily as it withholds bad ones — so the worst it can produce is `NEEDS CHECK`. This is the one place TeX is consulted after MW has been asked and had no entry (`Dictionary.tex_positions`); Rule 1 still may not see it, since a Rule 1 verdict resting on a guess is what that rule forbids.

## What this costs

No break that was clean is newly flagged. A proper noun MW does not carry is already `NEEDS CHECK` under Rule 1, so what changes is the reason the report gives, not which rows appear — except `Word-/sworth`, which is now a violation with the fix named.

The offline path (no MW key) is degraded but not wrong: without MW the element check cannot run, and only the stranded-consonant test fires. `Word-/sworth` is still caught.

## Changes

| File | |
|---|---|
| `src/editools/hyphen/rules.py` | Rule 6 restructured: seam handling in 6.2, TeX corroboration in 6.3 |
| `src/editools/hyphen/dictionary.py` | `tex_positions()`, with a note on why Rule 6 may see it and Rule 1 may not |
| `src/editools/hyphen/textutil.py` | `has_vowel()` |
| `docs/hyphen/RULES.md` | Rule 6 section rewritten to match |
| `tests/hyphen/` | 5 new cases, including both reported misses |

260 tests pass.

body:
Twelve defects found by re-running the accuracy spot-check with its evidence caps lifted, each verified against cached primary evidence before the edit.

## What changed

**Content corrections**

author: ilteoood
body:
## Summary

Add a Dockerfile that layers every install step from `claude-code.sh` into the `ilteoood/claude-code` image at build time so containers boot in seconds instead of re-downloading and reinstalling Rust, Node, Go, Bun, gh, plugins, and tokensave on every start.

## What it does

- **FROM** `ilteoood/claude-code:latest` (Debian 12 base, runs as root)
- **RUN** every step of `claude-code.sh` as image layers:
  - apt full-upgrade + base packages
  - Rust via rustup
  - GitHub CLI apt repo + Node 24 (nodesource) + Go (kerolloz installer) + Bun
  - `gh`, `nodejs` via apt
  - `gh auth setup-git`
  - npm globals: `skills`, `pnpm`, `lighthouse`
  - `skills add ilteoood/harness`
  - claude plugin marketplace + 5 plugins (wakatime, typescript-lsp, rust-analyzer-lsp, ponytail, claude-mem)
  - tokensave downloaded from GitHub releases and installed
  - `gh extension install github/gh-stack`
  - git identity
- **COPY** `entrypoint.sh` into the image and **ENTRYPOINT** it, preserving the base image's entrypoint so the runtime can be customized without rebuilding the image.

The boot cost drops from minutes (full install + download) to seconds (just ctx7 + daemon start).

## Files

- `Dockerfile` — multi-layer build baking every install step
- `entrypoint.sh` — runtime wrapper: `ctx7 setup` (when `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` is set) then `paseo daemon start --foreground`
- `.dockerignore` — keep build context small (excludes `skills/`, `.tokensave/`, `.git/`)

## Test Plan

- [x] `bash -n entrypoint.sh` and `bash -n claude-code.sh` syntax check pass
- [x] `git diff` reviewed
- [x] Dockerfile layered so cache survives any single step change
- [ ] Docker build to be run by maintainer (`docker build -t ilteoood/claude-code:baked .`)

author: keyurgolani
body:
**Atom:** `PP-16` — "one status vocabulary". **The atom is BLOCKED** on an owner decision, and so is the
enum merge itself — recorded 2026-08-18: *"one status vocabulary end-to-end (blocked on owner decision 2
above)"*. This is slice 3 of a multi-slice clause (a frontend registry unification and an action-guard
mirror already landed), and **two enums deliberately remain**.

## The conflict was not drift — it was two properties collapsed into one set

`TERMINAL_STATUSES` = `{COMPLETE, STOPPED}`, so a loop's `FAILED` is **resumable**.
`TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES` includes `FAILED`, so a run's `FAILED` is **terminal**. Same word, opposite
meaning, and `store.py:437`'s transition guard depends on which set you consult.

Separating the two properties resolves it without merging either:

- **phase** — has it stopped producing? A property of the *state*, so it is shared.
- **terminality** — may it still transition? A property of the *noun's lifetime*, because **a run is one
  attempt and a loop is a campaign of attempts**. Retrying a run means creating another run; "retrying" a
  loop means the same loop moves again.

`LifecyclePhase` (`PRELAUNCH`/`ACTIVE`/`ATTENTION`/`ENDED`) is declared once for both nouns; each noun
declares one phase map plus which ended states stay resumable, and **every membership set is derived**:
four loop sets and `TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES`, all **value-identical** to the literals they replace
(verified at runtime before committing). 68 referencing modules, **zero edits**.

That the asymmetry is structural rather than cosmetic is independently evidenced: the run side's
`request_cancel` refuses an already-ended run while `delete_run` refuses one that is not — two guards
only coherent together while nothing leaves an ended run — whereas `ACTION_SOURCE_STATES["resume"]`
accepts `FAILED` and re-arms the same loop. Merging either way is a behaviour change, so **neither was
taken**.

## A live defect found and fixed

**There was a FOURTH terminality set** — `store.py:452`'s anonymous inline tuple
`(COMPLETE, STOPPED, FAILED)`, disagreeing with `TERMINAL_STATUSES` about `FAILED` with nothing stating
why. `FAILED` was ended enough to stamp `completed_at` and non-terminal enough to be left, and **nothing
cleared the stamp on the way out** — so a resumed loop ran with a `started_at` *later* than the moment it
supposedly finished. That stale stamp is the single observable cost of "ended" and "terminal" having been
one word. Fixed: leaving an ended status un-ends the loop.

## Why the enum merge is not attempted here

`STATUS_VOCABULARY_DELTA` measures **7 loop-only** members and **3 run-only** — not a superset
relationship, so a merge costs a decision *per orphan*, not a rename. Extending `RunStatus` by 7 also
destroys its ability to reject `RunStatus("intake")` for an entity that can never hold it. The remainder
is independently measured at **9,045 lines across 43 files**, which is multi-session, and doctrine says a
slice that cannot finish must not begin. What this slice does instead is make the eventual merge
mechanical: both vocabularies now consume **one contract**, and the `FAILED` divergence lives in exactly
one line per noun with its reason attached.

## Gate

`make lint` 0 (mypy 960 files) · targeted **53 passed** (15 new) · runtime import sweep **68/68** clean,
and the real call paths exercised on both branches (`update_spec` allow+refuse, `rebind_workspace`
allow+running-refuse+terminal-refuse, `update_status` stamp+un-end).

Three falsifications: zeroing `RESUMABLE_ENDED_STATUSES` reds `test_a_failed_loop_can_still_resume` with
`TransitionError: failed -> running` (**so resumability is genuinely pinned**); dropping a phase row reds
the exhaustiveness rails; and reverting the `completed_at` clear reds with *"a resumed loop kept the
completed_at its failure stamped"* — **which is the proof the defect pre-existed**.

**Full `make test`: 3 failed, 24131 passed.** The 3 are `tests/test_subagent.py` SEL-logging tests, the
documented subagent-SEL xdist flake. Reporting counts, not a verdict — but the evidence is strong: that
file has zero references to any surface touched here, it is **66/66 green in isolation on this branch and
on `origin/main`** (I re-ran both), and the drive reproduced the same 3 failures with its new rail file
**entirely removed**.

author: jomkz
body:
## Problem

Two halves of the same duplication, landed together as the issue asks.

**The steering tail, verbatim in seven controllers** - pursuit, lead pursuit, lag pursuit, guns employment, waypoint, swarm and formation. Identical block, differing only in the bank constant and one role-specific comment line. Each also dragged its own copy of the four-line #1143 rationale, so the reason the aileron is a bank-ANGLE command rather than a rate command was restated seven times - and could be edited in one place without the other six noticing.

**LeadPursuitController and LagPursuitController were the same file twice.** A diff shows only include/class/member renames and one operator: `leadPos += vel * ttc * navGain` against `lagPos -= vel * ttc * lagFraction`. The time-to-intercept clamp and the entire tail were byte-identical.

## Change

`steerTowardPoint(ctrl, quat, ownPos, ownVel, tgtPos, R, maxBankRad)` in `Guidance.h`, with the #1143 rationale stated once. `maxBankRad` stays a caller argument - it is the one thing the seven genuinely disagree about, and each site keeps its own one-line reason for the limit it picked.

`pursuitOffsetPoint(out, ownPos, ownVel, tgtPos, tgtVel, gain)` takes a **signed** gain: positive leads, negative lags. Lead and lag become thin wrappers, so `AiControllerFactory` and every existing test are untouched.

Two deliberate shapes:

- The helpers take **raw arrays**, not `EntityState`. `Guidance.h` is currently free of `engine-entity` and depends only on `engine-flight`; taking `EntityState` would have widened that for no gain.
- **Throttle is not the tail's business.** Some callers hold a fixed throttle, formation closes a station-keeping speed loop, and swarm matches the flock mean. That is a real difference rather than a copy, so it stays at the call sites.

## Bit-exactness

Verbatim composition throughout. The one place worth stating: the lag path negates the *gain* rather than the product. Negation is exact in IEEE and `a + (-x)` is `a - x`, so `-= v*t*frac` and `+= v*t*(-frac)` are the same float.

The guard is preserved too - `std::max(m_navGain, 0.f)` reproduces the old `m_navGain > 0.f` exactly, including for a nonsensically negative gain.

## Deliberately not changed

These seven still close altitude through `pitchErrorFromAlt` + `elevatorFromPitchError` rather than `elevatorForAltitudeHold`. Swapping them is a control-law change that wants the closed-loop harness and measurement, not a mechanical substitution inside a consolidation PR - and it is now a one-line change in one place instead of seven. Flagging it rather than doing it.

## Verification

- The lead/lag sign is already pinned by `test_ai_controllers.cpp` (`lagInp.aileron < pureInp.aileron`, and a `lagFraction=1` case that computes the aim point behind the attacker) - the assertion most likely to catch a sign error in this rewrite, and it passes.
- `test_ai_turn_law.cpp` pins the #1143 behaviour for these controllers and passes unchanged.
- New cases in `test_guidance.cpp` for the primitives directly: the gain's sign as the lead/lag difference, the closing-speed floor and 30 s TTC cap that stop a non-closing target throwing the aim point off the planet, the 0.1 m range guard, and that a tighter bank limit asks for less roll from the same heading error.
- Full `ctest --preset debug` green locally (4885/4885); `-Wshadow -fsyntax-only` clean on all 8 changed TUs; `clang-format` and `lint_test_names.py` clean.

Closes #1259

author: iderex
body:
Closes #249.

The closing section of `docs/storage.md` is the argument for the table above it.
It tells a reader that everything this plugin reads is embedded in the assembly
and read rather than kept, so an absent store is a property of the plugin and
not an omission. It counted two tables and the project declares four.

## What was wrong

    git show origin/master:docs/storage.md | sed -n '50,52p'
    The store does not. Nothing in this plugin writes anything to a disk today. The
    two files it does read, the field register and the provider identifier table,
    are embedded in the assembly and are read rather than kept, which is the

    git grep -c "EmbeddedResource Include" origin/master -- Jellyfin.Plugin.MetadataSync/Jellyfin.Plugin.MetadataSync.csproj
    origin/master:Jellyfin.Plugin.MetadataSync/Jellyfin.Plugin.MetadataSync.csproj:5

Five declared resources, one of which is the configuration page and four of
which are tables. The conflict rules and the reference comparison arrived after
that sentence was written and it was not re-run.

## What the section says now

It names each table with the file it is in, and states that the list is not
maintained by hand. The claim about a disk is kept and is given the command that
shows it, so the negative half stays negative and is now derived rather than
asserted.

## What holds it up

`StorageStatementTests` compares the tables the section names with the embedded
resources the plugin project declares, as a set and in both directions. A table
added to the assembly with no line in the document reddens, which is the
direction this defect took. A line left behind by a table that moved reddens
too. The claim that nothing writes to a disk is re-derived over the plugin's
sources rather than read.

Existence of a named file is not checked and does not need to be: an
`EmbeddedResource` naming a file that is not in the tree fails the build, so the
comparison is already against files that exist.

The project file reading is a method on `PluginProjectFile` rather than a second
reader of the same file, for the reason that type already states in its own
remarks: two readings of one file drift, and the copy a failing test happens to
use is then the one that is wrong.

## Proved by breaking it, restored between each

    VSTEST_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=300 DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE=en dotnet test Jellyfin.Plugin.MetadataSync.sln --nologo

    a fifth table embedded with no line in the document  -> 1 red, 1306 green
    a line naming a table the assembly does not carry    -> 1 red, 1306 green
    a plugin source naming a write                       -> 1 red, 1306 green
    the empty result dropped from under the command      -> 1 red, 1306 green
    the fence the comparison reads renamed               -> 2 red, 1305 green
    restored                                             -> Failed: 0, Passed: 1307, Total: 1307

The baseline before this change was 1304 on each target, so the three legs are
what the total gained. The first break was made against a real embedded
resource, with a fifth JSON file added to the plugin and declared in the
project, because that is the shape the next table will have.

One thing about the fourth break, because it is the trap this repository counts
rather than a detail of the run. It reported green the first time. The guard was
not the reason: the edit that was supposed to drop the line had not applied,
because the file had been left with one line ending and the patch was written
for the other. Reading the file afterwards rather than accepting the green is
what found it, and the run above is the one where the edit landed. A green from
a break that did not happen is indistinguishable from a guard that works.

## What this does not reach

It judges the paths and never the sentence beside each one, so a table described
wrongly passes. It reads one section rather than the file. And the absence of a
write is judged by the spelling of a call, so a write reached through a type the
list does not name is outside it, which is the same bound `docs/personal-data.md`
states for its own token reading. All three are written at the guard.

This is the sixth document here found describing a tree that had moved under it,
after `docs/field-register.md` twice, `docs/reconciliation.md`, `README.md`,
`SECURITY.md` in #245 and `docs/threat-model.md` in #248, which is open. What is
still true after this lands is that four documents in this tree are read by
nothing.

No second reader looked at this. The commands above are the evidence in place of
one.

author: outofcoffee
body:
Adds a health indicator to fleet dashboard node tiles that reflects whether an engine can actually serve requests, not just whether its process is running.

## Summary
- The daemon background-checks a running engine's own `/health` endpoint (`llamacpp`/`vllm`) and reports `ready`/`not-ready`/absent on both `/v1/status` and `/v1/metrics`, reusing the existing activity-sampler loop rather than a new background goroutine
- Each dashboard tile shows a small coloured status glyph next to the node name: green (healthy), yellow (attention — no refresh yet, an action in flight, or `running` but confirmed not ready), red (unhealthy — crashed or a failed outcome)
- An older daemon, or a runner with no known health-check convention (`omlx`, for now), reports no readiness at all; the tile falls back to today's behaviour rather than showing a tier the daemon can't back
- `docs/openapi.yaml` updated for the new field, verified against the Go structs by the existing contract test

## Implementation details
`state: running` only means the supervisor's process is alive — llama.cpp can still be loading weights, vLLM may not have bound its port yet. There was previously no persistent signal for this reachable from the dashboard's steady-state polling (only transient checks used during a fresh `start`). The new field is a tri-state string (`ready`/`not-ready`/absent), not a bool, since `omitempty` on a bool can't distinguish "confirmed not ready" from "field absent" — both are needed to degrade gracefully for an older daemon or an unchecked runner. The health-check probe is deliberately unauthenticated: a gated engine correctly answers 401, which counts as ready, matching the cloud Lambda's own health-check rule.

author: johnson-zs
body:
## Root Cause Analysis

The platform version `Platform_VolumeSlider::paintEvent` (`src/widgets/platform/platform_volumeslider.cpp:379-384`) unconditionally calls `fillRect`, missing the X86 QPainterPath decoration branch (rounded rect + triangle pointer) that the non-platform `VolumeSlider::paintEvent` (`src/widgets/volumeslider.cpp:370-416`) draws. Additionally, `showEvent` uses hardcoded offsets (`x+=50; y+=30`) for compact mode instead of the proportional calculation (`volumeslider.cpp:351-352`). The trigger path is deterministic: X86 + specific GPU (Arise/MT/JM/Sietium/ljmcore) → `composited()==false` → `Platform_MainWindow` → `Platform_VolumeSlider`, producing a plain rectangle instead of the expected styled shape.

## Fix Approach

Two targeted changes in `src/widgets/platform/platform_volumeslider.cpp`: (1) add an X86 branch to `paintEvent` using `QPainterPath` to draw the rounded rect + triangle pointer, matching the non-platform version's geometry (`radius=20*dRation`, `triHeight=30*dRation`); keep the non-X86 path as plain `fillRect`. (2) Replace the hardcoded compact-mode offset with the proportional calculation (`TOOLBOX_HEIGHT*(1-0.66)` / `TOOLBOX_BUTTON_WIDTH*3*(1-0.66)-6`) used by the non-platform version.

## Change Safety Assessment

### Code Safety

- **Risk Level**: Low
- Both `paintEvent` and `showEvent` are Qt event overrides with zero application-level callers (`References=0`); only Qt's event dispatch invokes them.
- The X86 drawing logic is copied verbatim from the non-platform version, which has been in production long-term, proving correctness.

### Business Impact Scope

Affects the volume slider visual style on X86 platforms with non-composited GPUs (Arise/格兰菲, JM, MT, Sietium, ljmcore). In compact mode, the slider position now adapts proportionally to resolution/DPI scaling. Non-X86 platforms see no behavior change.

### Verification Suggestion

Test on X86 with a non-composited GPU (e.g., 格兰菲/Arise) — verify the volume slider renders with rounded corners and triangle pointer. Test compact mode positioning at different DPI/scale settings. Confirm no regression on non-X86 or composited GPU environments.

---

## 根因分析

平台版 `Platform_VolumeSlider::paintEvent`（`src/widgets/platform/platform_volumeslider.cpp:379-384`）无条件调用 `fillRect`，缺少非平台版 `VolumeSlider::paintEvent`（`src/widgets/volumeslider.cpp:370-416`）在 X86 平台绘制的 QPainterPath 圆角矩形 + 下三角指针装饰分支。此外 `showEvent` 紧凑模式使用硬编码偏移（`x+=50; y+=30`）而非非平台版的比例计算（`volumeslider.cpp:351-352`）。触发路径为确定性代码路径：X86 + 特定 GPU（Arise/MT/JM/Sietium/ljmcore）→ `composited()==false` → `Platform_MainWindow` → `Platform_VolumeSlider`，绘制纯矩形而非预期样式。

## 修复方案

在 `src/widgets/platform/platform_volumeslider.cpp` 中做两处针对性修改：(1) 为 `paintEvent` 补充 X86 分支，使用 `QPainterPath` 绘制圆角矩形 + 下三角指针，与非平台版几何参数一致（`radius=20*dRation`、`triHeight=30*dRation`）；非 X86 路径保持纯 `fillRect`。(2) 将紧凑模式硬编码偏移替换为非平台版的比例计算（`TOOLBOX_HEIGHT*(1-0.66)` / `TOOLBOX_BUTTON_WIDTH*3*(1-0.66)-6`）。

## 改动安全评估

### 代码安全评估

- **风险等级**: 低风险
- `paintEvent` 和 `showEvent` 均为 Qt 事件覆写，引用搜索 `References=0`，无应用层直接调用，仅由 Qt 事件分发调用。
- X86 绘制逻辑与非平台版完全一致，非平台版已在生产环境长期运行，证明正确性。

### 业务影响范围

影响 X86 + 非合成 GPU（Arise/格兰菲、JM、MT、Sietium、ljmcore）环境下的音量条视觉样式。紧凑模式下音量条位置按比例自适应分辨率/DPI 缩放。非 X86 平台无行为变化。

### 验证建议

在 X86 非合成 GPU 环境（如格兰菲/Arise）测试音量条是否显示圆角和三角指针；测试不同 DPI/缩放下紧凑模式定位是否正确；验证非 X86 或合成 GPU 环境无回归。

## Summary by Sourcery

Align the platform volume slider’s appearance and compact-mode positioning with the standard volume slider across supported display configurations.

Bug Fixes:
- Restore the rounded volume slider shape and pointer on X86 platforms using non-composited rendering.
- Correct compact-mode volume slider positioning to scale proportionally across display sizes and DPI settings.

author: giuliastro
body:
Follows #295, which merged before this landed on it. Same interface pass, the parts that are not mobile-specific: the chat width asymmetry reported from a browser, and what auditing the 2.x tree turned up as quietly missing.

# The chat did not widen symmetrically

Widening the browser did not widen a reply. Agent block prose was capped at `62ch` while the user bubble was deliberately left uncapped — the reasoning recorded next to the rule was that a bubble is framed by its own border and would look unbalanced with the text stopping short of it. In practice that made the bubble the only element in the transcript tracking the window: past roughly 700px every extra pixel went to the prompt and none to the answer, so the more screen the app was given the more lopsided the thread looked.

Claude and ChatGPT both answer this the same way, and so does this change: **one reading column shared by both roles, with surplus window width becoming margin rather than longer lines.**

- The measure is a single token applied without regard to role, raised slightly to ~96 characters per line.
- The user bubble is bounded by that measure plus its own padding and border.
- The row drops from 1280px to the 1040px `work-thread-detail.css` already used, and the composer tracks the same column so the input lines up with the conversation above it.
- Code blocks, tables, diffs and tool cards stay **outside** the measure and keep the full body width — for a coding client that is the point of a wide window.

The reference widths come from those two clients' behaviour, not from measurement, so the exact column is the part most worth a second opinion on a wide monitor.

# What 3.0 dropped from 2.x

`App.tsx` and its components (`session-composer`, `session-list`, `panels`, `shell`) are the 2.x tree, and nothing in the running app imports them any more. Anything that lived only there left the product without any single change ever looking like a removal.

## Copy — restored

`clipboard.ts` was one of those: written carefully for this app's plain-http LAN case, where `navigator.clipboard` is absent rather than merely refused, and then called by nothing. 3.0 shipped with no way to copy anything out of a conversation at all.

Copy is back on whole messages, on fenced code blocks and on tool output, going through that helper rather than the API directly. It copies the source text rather than the rendered text, and for tool output the whole of it rather than the 4000-character on-screen truncation — a stack trace clipped at 4000 characters is the half you cannot paste anywhere useful. The control sits in the block's own corner instead of appearing on hover, because a hover-revealed button does not exist on the devices this app is mostly used from, and it is 40px on touch.

## Attachments — not here

`attachments.ts` and the entire bridge path behind it are intact: the bridge validates `file` parts, enforces type/size/count, forwards them as ACP image blocks, and reports the capability from the live ACP handshake. What changed is the route. 2.x sent turns to `/v1/sessions/:id/prompt`, which accepts parts; 3.0 sends them to `/v1/tasks/:id/continue`, which carries `prompt` as a bare string.

Restoring it means run options, the run store and all three transports in `task-launcher.js` have to carry attachments, plus surfacing the capability per-agent in the machine snapshot — a feature change across client and bridge rather than a UI fix, and one whose interesting failures are all at the transport boundary I cannot exercise here. It is recorded at the top of `v3-v2-parity.test.mjs` so it stays visible instead of being rediscovered later. Happy to do it as its own PR against a real harness.

Also genuinely absent since 2.x, listed for your call rather than changed here: the command palette and its key bindings, and the `todowrite` checklist rendering that 2.x drew inside tool calls.

# Verification

Cascade analysis, plus the resolved widths read back out of the **emitted bundle** rather than the sources — this cascade has several same-specificity rules for `.uw-message` where load order alone decides the winner, so the sources do not tell you what applies. `tsc` clean, production build clean, rebased onto the current integration head and re-run there.

`v3-v2-parity.test.mjs` is new (6 guards): it records the 2.x audit and guards the copy restore, including that the copy goes through the LAN-safe helper and that the wrapper added for the copy button does not drag code blocks inside the reading measure.

`v3-conversation-readability.test.mjs` previously asserted the *opposite* of this fix — that a user bubble must not be capped. That assertion encoded the defect, so it is rewritten to assert the shared measure, and it now range-checks the measure against the characters-per-line figure the stylesheet itself records.

Two suites were already failing on the base branch before any of this work: their assertions are written with `\n` while `core.autocrlf` gives a Windows checkout CRLF against an LF index, so they passed in CI and could never pass locally. Both read helpers normalise now — which is also what lets the new assertions in those same files be trusted on either platform. **All front-end suites pass, including those two.**

Not exercised against a real browser or a real harness in this pass.

author: paxipu
body:
Fixes #74.

## What was wrong

`wxFrame::ShowFullScreen()` hides the menu bar for `wxFULLSCREEN_NOMENUBAR`
but leaves it attached, which is the normal state for a plain frame.

`wxMDIParentFrame::OnInternalIdle()` maintains the rule that the parent menu
bar is visible exactly when no child menu bar is, and it recognised that state
by visibility alone:

```cpp
if ((m_frameMenuBar) && (m_frameMenuBar->IsShown() == visible_child_menu))
{
    if (visible_child_menu) { Show(false); Detach(); }
    else                    { Show(true);  Attach(this); }   // <-- here
}
```

A hidden parent menu bar with no child menu bar visible therefore looked like
a state it had to correct. It showed the bar again — undoing the full screen
switch — and called `Attach()` on a bar that was still attached:

```
../src/common/menucmn.cpp(1007): assert "!IsAttached()" failed in Attach():
menubar already attached!
```

Two symptoms, one cause. Note the loop over the child frames a few lines above
already guards its own `Attach()` for exactly this reason, with a comment
saying so.

**This is not a GTK4 regression.** GTK+ 3 reproduces it identically; the code
is shared `src/gtk/mdi.cpp`.

## The change

`OnInternalIdle()` now only restores a menu bar it hid *itself*, which it
recognises by that bar also being detached — it always detaches when it hides.
A bar that is hidden but still attached was hidden by someone else (full
screen, or application code calling `Show(false)` on it) and is left alone.
`Detach()` is guarded the same way so the mirror image cannot assert either.

This deliberately does not consult `wxFrame::m_fsSaveFlag`: that member is
private, and the state-based rule is both narrower and correct for the other
way a menu bar can end up hidden from outside.

## Verification

**Reproduced first, in the real sample.** `samples/mdi`, GTK4 4.22.4 on a
private Xvfb, `Ctrl-F` delivered as a real XTEST key press. A GUI application
shows an assert as a dialog rather than on stderr, so the driver enumerates
the windows afterwards:

```
--- windows now on screen ---
  [4194309] 'wxWidgets MDI Sample'   500x400
  [4194313] 'wxWidgets Debug Alert'  1005x154
--- sample stdout/stderr ---
../src/common/menucmn.cpp(1007): assert "!IsAttached()" failed in Attach(): menubar already attached!
```

After the change the same run produces the main window only, no debug alert,
and the screen capture shows the menu bar, tool bar and status bar gone — the
client area starts at y=0. (The window keeps its 500x400 size because Xvfb has
no window manager to honour `gtk_window_fullscreen()`; the GTK+ 3 and GTK+ 2
runs, which do resize without one, also show no assert.)

**Standalone reproducer**, an MDI parent frame with a menu bar and no child,
taken in and out of full screen:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| GTK4 / X11 | `fullscr: shown=1 attached=1 asserts=1` | `shown=0 attached=1 asserts=0` |
| GTK4 / Wayland | `shown=1 attached=1 asserts=1` | `shown=0 attached=1 asserts=0` |
| GTK3 / X11 | `shown=1 attached=1 asserts=1` | `shown=0 attached=1 asserts=0` |
| GTK3 / Wayland | `shown=1 attached=1 asserts=1` | `shown=0 attached=1 asserts=0` |
| GTK2 / X11 | not measured before the change | `shown=0 attached=1 asserts=0` |

**The regression test was red first**, against the unchanged source, for the
right reason — the assert propagates out of idle processing and Catch2 reports
it:

```
tests/toplevel/toplevel.cpp:136: FAILED:
due to unexpected exception with message:
  menubar already attached! in Attach() at src/common/menucmn.cpp:1007
```

After the change it passes 9 assertions on GTK4/X11, GTK4/Wayland, GTK3/X11
and GTK3/Wayland.

**Complete GTK4 GUI suite on X11:**

```
test_gui "~[wxStyledTextCtrl]~[.]"
test cases:   521 |   502 passed | 19 failed
assertions: 45560 | 45505 passed | 55 failed
```

The recorded baseline for this branch point is 520 cases / 501 passed / 19
failed / 55 failed assertions. The difference is exactly the test this PR adds,
which passes; no test changes state.

**GTK3 3.24.52 regression:** complete static library, `test_gui` and mdi sample
rebuild, 0 errors. `[tlw]~[.]` has one pre-existing failure on both backends,
`tests/persistence/tlw.cpp:155` ("Timed out waiting for frame to be iconized"),
which needs a window manager the private Xvfb does not provide and is unrelated
to this file.

**GTK2 2.24.33 regression:** complete static library and mdi sample rebuild,
0 errors, sample driven with Ctrl-F, no assert.

**Static analysis:** `clang-tidy` with `clang-analyzer-*,bugprone-*,cert-*` on
`src/gtk/mdi.cpp` reports nothing at any changed line; its findings are
pre-existing and come from GTK's `G_TYPE_CHECK_INSTANCE_CAST` and wx's own RTTI
macros. The file compiles with no new warning.

## Known limitation, left out deliberately

Entering full screen while an MDI *child's* menu bar is visible still leaves
that child menu bar on screen: `wxFrame::ShowFullScreen()` only knows about
`m_frameMenuBar`. That is a separate behaviour question from the assert this
issue reports and is not touched here.

author: buildd-ai[bot]
body:
## Problem

When the `[Conflict Retry #N]` chain exhausts its 3-attempt cap, the observed behaviour was **nothing** — no Pushover, no card in Waiting on You, no note. PRs #1697, #1759, and #1763 all silently stalled.

Root causes:
1. `escalateConflictExhaustion` gated everything behind `if (task?.missionId)` — tasks without missions (all three real-world stale PRs) produced no output.
2. The race-condition merge path in `auto-merge.ts` discarded the `dispatchConflictRetry` result entirely with `.catch(console.error)` — no escalation if exhausted during a merge-time conflict.
3. Call sites C (`github/pr`) and D (`prs/merge`) returned HTTP errors but triggered no proactive human notification.

## Solution

Same escalation doctrine PR #1689 introduced for merge-rejection — no parallel implementation.

### `escalateConflictExhaustion` (now exported)
- **Atomic dedup**: JSONB CAS on `tasks.context.conflictExhaustedHeadSha` ensures exactly one Pushover and one `reviewer_escalated` note per `(taskId, headSha)`, safe under concurrent webhook retries.
- **Pushover** (`tasks` app, priority 0) fires regardless of whether the task has a mission.
- **`reviewer_escalated` missionNote** created when `task.missionId` is set → PR surfaces in the "Waiting on You" inbox with Resolve/Close-as-superseded/Abandon choices.

### Call site fixes
| Call site | File | Before | After |
|-----------|------|--------|-------|
| B — race-condition merge | `auto-merge.ts` | result discarded | handles `exhausted`, calls `escalateConflictExhaustion` |
| C — MCP `merge_pr` | `github/pr/route.ts` | HTTP error only | + `escalateConflictExhaustion` before returning |
| D — human merge | `prs/[prNumber]/merge/route.ts` | HTTP 409 only | + `escalateConflictExhaustion` before returning |

(Call site A — auto-merge safety check — already called `escalateConflictExhaustion`; that code path was correct but the function itself was broken.)

## Tests

8 new unit tests for `escalateConflictExhaustion` in `auto-merge.test.ts`:
- Task not found → early return, no Pushover
- CAS succeeds → Pushover fires, note inserted (when missionId present)
- CAS fails (duplicate) → no Pushover, no note
- Idempotence: 3 concurrent calls → exactly 1 Pushover
- No missionId → Pushover fires, no DB note insert
- With missionId → both Pushover and `reviewer_escalated` note
- Iteration count appears in Pushover message
- Task URL in Pushover points to buildd task page

`tsc --noEmit` clean. All 35 tests in `auto-merge.test.ts` + `conflict-retry.test.ts` green.

author: copilot
body:
The battle system summed dice totals and converted them into damage, requiring mental math and giving no sense of "hands." Replaced this with a Cee-Lo-inspired three-dice system where each side rolls, identifies a named hand, and the higher-ranked hand wins the round.

## New rules engine
- Added `scripts/battle/dice_rules.gd`: a UI-free module owning all hand logic — sorting, identifying `TIDAL_ROLL` (4-5-6), `TRIPLE`, `POINT` (pair + unmatched die), `WASHED_OUT` (1-2-3), and `NO_POINT` (non-scoring).
- `HandType` enum is ordered `NO_POINT < WASHED_OUT < POINT < TRIPLE < TIDAL_ROLL` so a stray `NO_POINT` can never outrank a real hand.
- `compare_hands()` centralizes comparison (type first, then point value), returning 1/0/-1. `calculate_damage()` derives 2/3/4 damage by hand type plus a +1 bonus if the loser rolled `WASHED_OUT`.
- Kept isolated from UI/state so the same rules can back future PvP.

## Battle flow rewrite (`scripts/battle/battle_manager.gd`)
- Both Octo and Crab now roll 3 dice each round (Crab's armor and 2-dice roll removed).
- New `BattleState` enum (`PLAYER_TURN/PLAYER_ROLLING/ENEMY_ROLLING/RESOLVING_ROUND/VICTORY/DEFEAT`) gates the Roll button and prevents overlapping/duplicate rounds.
- `NO_POINT` rolls auto-reroll (up to 20 attempts, then a safe highest-die fallback) without requiring extra player input.
- Removed the old sum-based `calculate_player_damage`/`calculate_enemy_damage` entirely; damage now comes from `DiceRules.calculate_damage`.
- Round messaging shows the named hand and result, e.g. `POINT 5 beats POINT 4! 🐙 LITTLE OCTO WINS THE ROUND`.

## Scene updates (`scenes/battle/Battle.tscn`)
- Added Crab's 3rd die and hand-name labels for both creatures.
- Added a `?` Rules button opening a popup explaining Tidal Roll / Triple / Pair + Point / Washed Out.

```gdscript
var octo_hand := DiceRules.evaluate_hand([3, 3, 5])   # POINT 5
var crab_hand := DiceRules.evaluate_hand([2, 2, 4])   # POINT 4
var result := DiceRules.compare_hands(octo_hand, crab_hand)  # 1 -> Octo wins
var damage := DiceRules.calculate_damage(octo_hand, crab_hand)  # 2
```

## Summary

- Позволяет создавать документ начисления ЗП (документ + строки) прямо в портале — bulk-ввод за период, без внешнего источника. Существующий импорт из n8n (`N8nPayrollLineUpsertView`/`N8nPayrollLineBatchUpsertView`) остаётся полностью рабочим и не изменён по логике.
- Новая опциональная tenant-настройка `create_payment_request_on_payroll_accrual`: при включении автоматически создаётся одна заявка на оплату (с полноценной цепочкой согласования) на сумму всего документа начисления — для нативно созданных документов и для загруженных через n8n.
- `PayrollDocument.doc_id` стал nullable — нативные документы не имеют `doc_id` (в отличие от импортированных из внешней системы).

## Реализация
