author: vixygrey
body:
Part of #337. Step two of the agreed three-part ordering — **three checks, not four**, for a reason
set out at the bottom.

## Summary

The balance sweep's twenty findings all accumulated without failing anything. `item-curve` is why
the value curve held perfectly while everything else drifted; these give the same treatment to the
numbers players actually feel.

| check | findings | catches |
| ----------------- | -------: | ----------------------------------------- |
| `armor-curve` | **19** | #318, #319, the vambraces and the cloaks |
| `stat-discipline` | 0 | #321's entire defect class |
| `finesse-visible` | 0 | a repeat of #366 |
| `Stat` column | 0 | the 65 stale doc cells from #365 |

Each inherits `tier_of`, `is_chip` and `is_base_object` from #354 rather than rolling its own
name-matching, which is why that landed first.

## `armor-curve`

Holds AV against §3.2.1's per-slot ceiling. Shields are looked up on their own `Shield` part — the
omission that shipped the first version of that table without a Shield column, and the reason #319
had nothing to be a defect against.

Merges are checked as well as new objects, because that is where most of the drift is:
`Zetachrome Apex`, `Gloves` and `Pumps` at 6 against a ceiling of 4, and `Zetachrome Lune` at 10
against 8.

**A stated limitation, so nobody assumes otherwise.** The ceiling is per slot and not per tier, so
this cannot catch top-tier AV appearing early — `Crysteel Shardmail` at AV 8 in tier 6 passes. That
is faithful to §3.2.1, which says plainly there is no AV *curve* to check: vanilla's tier-4 body
armour runs AV 0 to 5, so a per-tier rule does not exist to be enforced.

## `stat-discipline`

The two halves are deliberately different rules.

**A new weapon may state Strength or leave it unset.** `MeleeWeapon.Stat` is a field initialised to
`"Strength"`, and vanilla omits the attribute on 208 of its 402 declarations — so requiring it would
report 28 perfectly correct weapons. What is refused is any *other* value, which is the whole defect
class: all 61 of #321's swaps were explicit.

**A merge states nothing at all**, which is stricter, and on purpose. CI has no game, so the check
cannot tell a merge restating vanilla's value from one changing it — and only the second is a
defect. Refusing the attribute outright is a line the check can actually hold, and it costs nothing,
because a merge restating vanilla's own value changes nothing by definition. It also protects the
three vanilla weapons that roll against **Ego**, which a flat "always Strength" rule would have
quietly rewritten — the #366 mistake, arriving through the check this time instead of the code.

It reports **0**. One redundant `Stat="Strength"` on the `Chute Crab Claw` merge came off rather
than going into the baseline.

It **parses rather than greps**, per the note on #337: `MeleeWeapons.xml` carries a commented-out
block with two vibro war hammers still on `Stat="Agility"`, and a line-based check would report two
violations nobody can fix without touching code marked for rework.

## `finesse-visible`

Holds a `Finesse` tag and its rules text to implying each other, **both directions**. A tag with no
text is a feature the player cannot discover — which is exactly how #366 surfaced, from a play
session whose only symptom was a dagger description that said nothing. Text with no tag is a promise
the game does not keep.

`Value="*delete"` counts as untagged, so the vibro wristblade is correctly quiet.

## And a fourth checked column

`Stat` joins `ITEM_COLUMNS` in `check_docs`, taking verified item-table figures from 739 to **741**.
When #365 reverted 61 `Stat="Agility"` declarations, **65 table cells still said Agility and nothing
failed** — a larger drift than any checked column has ever carried.

## Why three and not four

**`damage-ceiling` is not buildable in CI, and I stopped rather than ship one that looks like it
works.** A merge carries no `Inherits` and no `Skill`:

```
Cudgel8th     Load=Merge  Inherits=None  MeleeWeapon Skill=None dmg='5d6+2'
Long Sword8   Load=Merge  Inherits=None  MeleeWeapon Skill=None dmg='2d8+2'
```

`Cudgel8th` takes its `Skill` from vanilla's `BaseCudgel`, which is not in this mod's files — and
**25 of the 26 damage violations are merges**. Only `Raven_Iron Mace` is new content. A CI check
would catch 1 of 26 while appearing to cover damage, which is worse than no check.

Agreed next step is a small **`vanilla-blueprints.json` snapshot** — name → `Inherits`, `Skill`,
`Tier` — refreshed by a maintainer tool, the same pattern as `qud-api.json` and `dynamic-pools.json`.
That unblocks `damage-ceiling`, `weight-curve` and `table-share` in CI rather than exiling all three
to a maintainer-only tier.

## The baseline

The 19 `armor-curve` findings go into `tools/validation-baseline.json` against **#318** and **#319**,
with the cloaks attributed to `DESIGN_balance.md` §9.3's cloaks-stay decision. Reported, tracked, not
failing — so every fix from here has a check to satisfy rather than a prose rule to remember.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools` — **175 tests**, all pass
- [x] Twelve new tests, each proving its check **fires on something broken and stays quiet on
      something sound**, including the boundary case where AV equals the ceiling
- [x] `python3 tools/validate_mod.py` — OK, 149 known defects tracked
- [x] `python3 tools/check_docs.py` · `ruff check` · `ruff format` · `typos` · `gitleaks`
- [x] `check_check_names` passes, so §10's check table names only checks that exist
- [x] All pre-commit hooks

One mod content change: a redundant attribute removed from `Chute Crab Claw`, with no behavioural
effect.

author: drethegeek
body:
Closes #6.

Production regression: a Powerade barcode photo ended up as `Snack, Mixed Berry Bar`, with 2264 kcal, while the scan breadcrumb said `Mountain Berry Blast Gatorade`.

## Fix

- A successfully decoded UPC/EAN that is not found in the local corpus/Open Food Facts now fails closed. The same barcode-only image is not handed to vision for identity guessing.
- Ambiguous barcode/back-label vision is explicitly classified as product and asks for a closer barcode, front label, or Nutrition Facts image instead of inventing an identity.
- Smart Scan prompt bumped to `smart-scan.v7`, invalidating the prior photo cache.
- Typed correction and product clarification no longer go through the natural-language meal parser. A dedicated server action resolves exactly one asserted food identity through the trusted nutrition pipeline.
- USDA name grounding now requires multi-word identity coverage before scoring. A single shared token such as `berry` cannot turn `Mountain Berry Blast Gatorade` into `Snack, Mixed Berry Bar`.
- Client still cannot supply macros. All nutrition values come from authoritative server-side food rows.

## Verification

- Branch is 5 commits ahead of current main and 0 behind.
- Diff is limited to four nutrition files: `photo-scan.tsx`, `external-foods.ts`, new `food-correction-actions.ts`, and `smart-scan.ts`.
- Vercel preview for head `7e0eefe33f543817398b2821ef04f5f7f616c311` is READY.
- Vercel production build command completed successfully on preview, including Next.js compilation and TypeScript.
- No migrations, auth, billing, workflows, or secrets touched.

## Regression behavior

For the reported barcode photo:
1. If ZXing reads the barcode and OFF has the product, show that exact product.
2. If ZXing reads the barcode but OFF does not have it, ask for exact product name/front label/Nutrition Facts. Do not call vision on the barcode-only frame.
3. If ZXing cannot decode it and vision sees a barcode/back label, return product clarification. Do not reinterpret it as a meal.
4. If the member types the product, resolve that identity directly. Do not run the meal parser.

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #40, which merged before this commit landed on the branch — #40 shipped the Library search-clear button (2.7.0) but not this fix for it.

- Root cause: the vertical scrollbar only renders when the Library list is tall enough to need scrolling. Every time the list crossed that threshold — which typing into search or clicking clear does constantly — `document.documentElement.clientWidth` shifted by the scrollbar's width (~15px on Windows Chrome), moving every right-anchored element on the page, including the "✕" search-clear button (`right: 6px` inside `.search-wrap`), right as a click landed on it.
- Fix: `html { overflow-y: scroll; }` forces the scrollbar to always render, so viewport width never changes regardless of list length.
- Bumps `APP_VERSION` to `2.7.1`; no data schema change. `ARCHITECTURE.md`/`CHANGELOG.md` updated per the doc-sync rule.

## Test plan
- [x] Reproduced directly: `document.documentElement.clientWidth` measured 1280 with a short (no-scroll) Library list vs. 1265 with a tall (scrolling) list in the same window
- [x] Confirmed the clear button's bounding-rect X position shifted between those two states before the fix
- [x] After the fix, both list states measure `clientWidth` 1265 and the button's X position is identical regardless of list length

author: hedi-comcompass
body:
`cc-regime-brief` failed tonight (2026-08-23 19:55), for session 2026-08-21:

```
BriefLeakError: press_summary leaks internals ['modèle'] — refusing to render the brief
```

Not a deploy regression — the job succeeded on 08-19, 08-20, 08-21 and 08-22.
Tonight's press review simply used the word **« modèle »**.

## The design flaw

`_assert_safe` ran ONE forbidden-token list over two sources with two completely
different threat models:

| source | fields | can it leak our engine? |
|---|---|---|
| **our own prose** | `conclusion`, `eco`, `confidence_rationale` | yes — the narrator is an LLM we prompt, and "modèle"/"algorithme"/"IA" are exactly the words it reaches for when it starts describing itself |
| **third-party text** | `press_summary` (+ the weather bulletin) | no — written by other agents summarising real articles and real measurements; they never see our engine |

`« le modèle coopératif ivoirien »`, `« un algorithme de tri des fèves »`,
`« l'intelligence artificielle dans l'agriculture »` are ordinary cocoa
journalism. The guard was policing a source it was never designed for, and the
first article that used a perfectly normal French word killed a job whose
decision had already been computed.

## The fix

Two tuples:

- `_FORBIDDEN_OWN_PROSE` — unchanged, still broad, still applied to the narrator's
  three fields. **The guard is not loosened where it was designed to bite** — a
  test pins that.
- `_FORBIDDEN_THIRD_PARTY` — only tokens that could not plausibly appear in cocoa
  journalism and would therefore mean our vocabulary escaped into another agent's
  output: `regime router`, `routeur`, `prob_up`, `p(up)`, `soft-gate`, `lightgbm`,
  `orchestrator`, `o4-mini`.

`_assert_safe(…, forbidden=…)` **defaults to the strict list**, so a new call site
is policed strictly unless it opts out explicitly — the safe direction to be wrong
in.

### Blind spot closed while here

Only `press_summary` was checked. `press_impact`, `press_sentiment`,
`meteo_summary`, `meteo_impact` and `weather_body` all render into the brief and
were **unchecked**. They are now covered by the narrow list — free once it exists,
and it closes the path a genuine leak through the meteo agent would have taken.

## Blast radius: contained by design

`render_brief` runs **before** `write_narrative` in `main.py`, so the abort left
the DB untouched: session 2026-08-21 keeps the narrative written by the 08-22 run,
and its Drive `.txt` is still there. Nothing partial, nothing corrupted — the
fail-loud ordering did its job. What was lost is the refresh: tonight's brief would
have folded in the weekend press.

`cc-regime-shadow` succeeded at 19:50, so the decision and adapter rows for
2026-08-21 exist.

## Tests

`TestLeakGuardBySource` in `tests/test_regime_brief.py`:

- our own prose still aborts on `modèle` — the guard is intact where it matters;
- **the exact 2026-08-23 sentence now renders** («  modèle coopératif ivoirien … un
  algorithme de tri des fèves ») — the regression test;
- all six third-party fields abort on `prob_up=0.61`, each named in the error;
- the narrow list still catches `regime router`, `soft-gate`, `o4-mini`, `LightGBM`.

1076 backend tests pass, `poetry run lint` (ruff + pyright) clean.

author: sektek
body:
## Summary
Discovered while extracting `@sektek/generator` into its own repo (SEK-44): `.mocharc.cjs`'s `spec: ['**/*.spec.ts']` is unscoped. Inside this monorepo it never matched anything under `node_modules` (hoisted to the workspace root, outside each package's own directory), so the bug was silently masked here.

A standalone extracted repo has its own local `node_modules`, and `yeoman-generator` → `latest-version` → `@pnpm/npm-conf` transitively ships a raw `env-replace.spec.ts` that matches the glob and crashes mocha via Node's own type-stripping refusing files under `node_modules`.

All 5 packages (`libs/generator`, `libs/generator-test`, `generators/generator-base`, `generators/generator-js`, `tools/gen`) share this exact `.mocharc.cjs`, so every future extraction would hit the same landmine — fixed at the source now rather than patching each extraction copy individually.

## Fix
Add `ignore: ['**/node_modules/**']` to each package's `.mocharc.cjs`.

## Verification
Reproduced and confirmed fixed in the actual `@sektek/generator` extraction copy (`npm test` failed before the fix, passes after). `templates/template-ts` intentionally untouched (out of scope, per prior discussion).

author: kpal002
body:
**Stacked on #102 (SIM-415 foundation)** — base is the SIM-415 branch, so this shows only the EDGAR diff and can't reach `staging` until #102 merges (handover: "no source adapter merges until the foundation lands"). GitHub will retarget this to `staging` automatically when #102 merges.

The first real `CorroborationSource` behind SIM-415's interface.

## What it does
Given a financial claim, resolve its company → CIK (exact normalized-title match against EDGAR `company_tickers.json`) and compare the claim's figure to EDGAR **XBRL company facts** for the same period:
- **Agrees** within 0.5% (EDGAR XBRL is a filed exact number, so a genuine match is near-identical).
- **Disagrees** on a material delta — recording both values + `discrepancy_delta` in the event `result`, so the conflict view can show them.
- **No-signal** (`None`, records nothing) for everything it can't compare — not an EDGAR filer, ambiguous name, unmapped attribute, no reported fact for the period, or a non-USD unit. **Absence is never a conflict** (handover 9.3.5).

## Handover alignment
- **Deterministic** (C-10/C-11): name→CIK is an exact match, never a model guess; the roll-up never sees a model-derived value. The fuzzy / name-history AI-propose seam (5.1) and former-name resolution are a documented follow-up.
- Required **User-Agent** set; SEC's ~10 req/s cross-call rate-limiting is the corroboration pass's job when registered.
- **Not registered** in `CORROBORATION_SOURCES` yet — it goes live only once the pass's I/O placement is settled (SIM-253), so a network call never sits inside the verify transaction.

## Testing
9 hermetic tests (injected `fetch`, no network/DB): agree / material-disagree+delta / not-a-filer / ambiguous-name / unmapped-attribute / no-fact-for-period / non-USD / fetch-raises, plus the 10-K-and-latest-filed restatement pick. `ruff` + `pyright` clean.

## Scope note
XBRL comparison is most useful for later-stage (EDGAR-listed) deals; the handover notes alpha's pre-seed design-partner deals will mostly exercise internal-consistency, not registries. This lands the registry path so it's ready when mid-market deals arrive.

author: holyscotsman
body:
The completion of `R170`. Tags enter this book three ways, and until now only two of them were guarded:

| | what it does about the book's spelling |
|---|---|
| **Tag mode's Add tags** | **imposes** it — `067`: *"bulk tagging must not mint near-duplicates"* |
| **typing into a tags field** | **offers** it, since `R170` |
| **a video import** | nothing at all |

So a model answering `scottish` against a book that already says `Scottish` minted exactly the twin the other two exist to prevent — and the extractor's own prompt steers it that way, since its one worked example of a tag is `air fryer`, lower case, beside a book whose cuisines are all title case.

It is the one path where tags enter the book **without a person choosing them**, which is what makes imposing right here and offering right there: there is nobody to offer it to.

### One reader, not a third copy

`bulk-apply` had carried three lines of its own since `067`. They are the same three lines, so they are now the same function (`R124`). `canonTags` dedupes, which the inline version never needed and this one does: a model answering `["italian","Italian"]` would otherwise put *Italian, Italian* in front of the reader.

### The placement is the decision, and it has its own check

The obvious home is `normalizeDraft`, the boundary for everything the kitchen server says (`R87`). It is also the **restore** path (task `084`) — and a restored draft's tags are the reader's own words coming back from a refresh. Rewriting those is precisely what `R170` decided not to do, so the fold lives in `openVideoDraft`, where the words are the model's.

A reader who types `scottish` into the review screen and refreshes gets `scottish` back. The mutation that moves the fold up one level fails by name, with the reader's own casing rewritten in the message.

No flag, for `R162`'s reason: `scottish` → `Scottish` is the same tag spelled the way the book spells it, exactly as `joan` → `Joan` is the same person. The reader sees the field before Save either way.

### Verified

The known tag is taken **from `recipes.json` at run time** so the check cannot go stale when the content changes, with a floor if the book is ever untagged. Three mutations fail by name: no fold at all, the fold moved into `normalizeDraft`, and a fold that reshapes tags the book has never seen.

**video 276 → 281; battery 1871 → 1876**, all clean locally — kt 372, feat 98, add 136, relay 21, quick 84, polish 384, sec 62, plan 95, video 281, backend 328, zoom 15. Contrast: 0 AA failures across every screen × theme × Easy-Read combination, and on paper.

author: 0spinboson
body:
Closes #523.

`match_mollie_settlement` gated on

```python
transaction["bank_account"] != self.config.get_bank_account_gl()
```

Those are different namespaces. `Bank Transaction.bank_account` is a Link to **Bank Account**;
`Mollie Settings.mollie_bank_account` — what `get_bank_account_gl()` returns — is a Link to
**Account**. Both verified on the meta. `Bank Account` autonames `account_name + " - " + bank`,
`Account` autonames `account_name + " - " + abbr`, so the strings coincide only when a bank's
name equals the company abbreviation.

It never did. On veg11: **0 of 409** Bank Accounts satisfy the comparison, and across **7,664**
Bank Transactions the pipeline has posted nothing — 0 Journal Entries and 0 Payment Entries
carrying `custom_mollie_settlement_id`. Every transaction was rejected at the gate. This
independently explains #194's zero-fee-JE probe and #345's idle scheduler.

## The fix tests membership, not a resolved docname

Both ways of *picking* one Bank Account are wrong, and both were measured rather than reasoned
about:

| approach | what happens |
|---|---|
| `get_value(... {"account": gl})` | **ambiguous.** ERPNext enforces one Bank Account per GL account only in `validate_account()`, reachable solely from `validate_is_company_account()` and so gated on `if self.is_company_account:`. `account` has no `unique` flag and no index. Verified: flag=1 then flag=0 on one GL account both insert, while a second flag=1 is rejected — the control. `Bank Account` sorts `creation DESC`, so the newest wins and a transaction on the older row stops matching. |
| adding `is_company_account: 1` | **closes the gate.** On test_site_4 the only Bank Account on the company's default GL account has the flag *clear*, so the filtered lookup returns `None` and nothing can ever match. |

Membership needs neither choice: the money lands in the configured GL account whichever Bank
Account names it, and the amount/keyword/settlement checks do the discriminating work. An
accountless transaction is excluded because `None not in [...]` holds — `Bank Transaction.
bank_account` is not mandatory, and without that guard such a transaction is matched to a
settlement at **0.98 confidence**, which is worse than the original bug. Pinned by its own
test.

`test_a_later_party_bank_account_does_not_capture_the_gl_account` reddens under **both**
rejected shapes, verified by mutation.

## Why the tests never caught it

Four tests in `TestMatchMollieSettlementLive` assigned the GL name over
`txn["bank_account"]`, one carrying the comment *"force account equality with the configured
Mollie account"* — an explanation sitting next to the defect. The fixture already modelled the
real relationship (`get_eur_bank_account` keys its Bank Account on
`Company.default_bank_account`), so the overwrite was not merely wrong-namespace, it was
unnecessary. Removed in all four.

Two of those assert `assertIsNone` and so stayed green once the gate began rejecting — passing
at a branch other than the one they name. Both now reach their own logic, proved by mutation.
Two more in the sibling suite were measured with a branch probe rather than assumed: one made
vacuous by this fix, and one that was **already** vacuous before it, silently duplicating the
test above it.

## What this does NOT do

**It does not make the settlement pipeline work.** It removes the gate as the reason it
cannot. Reviewers should weigh three things before treating this path as live:

- **#545** — every Mollie API call from veg11 returns HTTP 400 despite a present, correctly
  shaped test key. All four endpoints fail identically (the control), so it is client/credential
  wiring. `get_settlements_by_date_range` wraps the call with `fallback_value=[]`, so with the
  gate open the matcher iterates nothing. Net change on veg11: one Error Log row per candidate
  transaction, still no accounting.
- **#540** — veg11 has `mollie_bank_account == mollie_clearing_account ==
  '10440 - Triodos 1 - TPIC - TPIC'`, whose company is `TEST-Payment-Integration-Company`.
  Anything this path books there books into a **test** company's ledger. It resolves to a Bank
  Account with 0 Pending unallocated transactions today, so blast radius is currently zero.
- **#546 / #547** — opening the gate makes two latent behaviours live: the matcher downloads
  Mollie's entire settlement history once per candidate transaction, uncached; and it
  auto-reconciles on amount + ±3 days + one keyword with **no counterparty check**, at a
  confidence above the auto-match threshold. Neither is introduced here.

Also deliberately not fixed: **#544** (the two sibling resolvers carry the same latent
ambiguity — they need a single docname, so membership does not apply, and the plausible filter
is a regression there too) and **#548** (three tests coupled through Mollie Settings Singles
state, which this change extends rather than fixes).

## Verification

- **160 tests green** across the four modules touching the matcher or its caller
  (55 + 74 + 11 + 20), on test_site_4.
- Both Mollie modules re-run under `scripts/testing/run_without_credentials.sh` — this bench
  carries gateway keys and CI does not, so the plain green would not have proved CI's path.
- Skeptical review run **before** opening this PR. It found the ambiguity above, which my
  original commit had wrong; verifying its recommended fix myself is what surfaced the
  test_site_4 regression, so the shipped fix is neither its suggestion nor my first one.

author: mdwhite365-ops
body:
The corrected reading gave `PA3KQN57WVXY` a cumulative excess of **+0.069%** over nine sessions and `PA3HEG2CLXLU` **−0.043%**.

Neither is interpretable on its own. The module computed per-session excess, summed it, and **threw the series away** — and the series' *dispersion* is what decides whether a cumulative seven basis points is anything at all.

## The point of the card: one definition, not two

It reuses the Evaluator's `sharpe` rather than reimplementing it.

The promote gate scores a backtest's IR with that function over an active-return series. Computing the live one any other way produces a number that **cannot be set beside the evaluation that admitted the strategy** — which is the entire reason the metric exists. A second definition of the firm's central statistic is the same bug class as `market_value / price` standing in for a share count that was already in a column.

There's a test asserting the live IR equals `sharpe(excess_series, TRADING_DAYS_PER_YEAR)` exactly, so the two cannot drift apart silently.

## Two refusals

- **`None` rather than `0.0`** when the series is too short or perfectly flat. `sharpe` returns `0.0` for both, and *a zero IR is a finding while an undefined one is an absence of data.*
- **`ratio_is_meaningful` gates on 20 sessions**, mirroring `forward_score.DEFAULT_MIN_SESSIONS_FOR_RATE`. Annualising multiplies by √252, so nine sessions yield a confident-looking figure from nothing. Below the floor the CLI prints it flagged `NOT MEANINGFUL` **instead of** beside the 0.50 promote floor — printing it next to the floor invites exactly the comparison it cannot support.

## New dependency, stated

The CLI now pulls **numpy** through that import. `strategy-runner` already carries numpy and pandas so it runs there; a lighter container fails on import. The module docstring says so (runbook §1e — the trap that cost an hour on `shrap-strategy-stage`).

Correctness over import purity here: the container already pays for numpy, and divergence from the gate is the more expensive failure.

## Verification

**1560 tests. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean. `mypy --strict` clean on 231 files.** Four new tests: same-function equality with the gate, the short-window flag, the flat-series `None`, and that the series sums to the reported excess so the two cannot disagree.

## Deploy

```
cd /mnt/Archive/shrap/shrap_firm && git pull && cd infra && sudo docker compose up -d --build --force-recreate strategy-runner
sudo docker compose exec strategy-runner shrap-live-benchmark --start 2026-08-06 --end 2026-08-19
```

Expect `NOT MEANINGFUL` on both accounts. That is the correct output for nine sessions, and it is the first time the tool will say so rather than leaving the reader to work it out.

body:
## Summary

Customer billing mutations are gated on a reviewed account **cohort** — right for a sandbox, wrong for a self-service launch, where opening billing would otherwise mean pasting every account into an allowlist. The gate now also accepts **general availability**.

**The default is unchanged.** Absent or `false` leaves the cohort as the only way in, and the zero configuration (no allowlist, no GA) still admits nobody.

## Two configurations are refused, not silently widened

- **A non-empty allowlist alongside GA.** This is contradictory, and the dangerous reading is the *reassuring* one: an operator would believe billing is still restricted to that cohort while it is in fact open to everyone.
- **A Stripe test clock with GA.** A test clock rewrites time for every customer attached to it — an acceptance tool for a single sandbox account, never something to leave running while billing is open.

## Tests

Fail-closed default in both spellings (`""` and `"false"`), refusal of a non-boolean value, both contradiction refusals, and that every account (including never-listed ones) is admitted once GA is on. Mutation-tested: defaulting GA to true, or dropping the allowlist contradiction guard, each fail.

`make check` green.

## Needs Scott (launch cutover)

Setting `WITSELF_CP_BILLING_GENERAL_AVAILABILITY=true` with an empty allowlist is part of the billing cutover in `docs/launch-readiness.md`, after the live Stripe keys, webhook, portal config, and Tax activation are in place.

Found while running the platform for a live owner test of the WhatsApp bridge.

**1. No volume on WAHA.** The paired session lived only in the container's writable layer — any recreate (image pull, compose edit) silently unpairs the phone and forces a new QR scan. Now on a named `waha-sessions` volume.

**2. The key that half-breaks the bridge.** WAHA 2026.x generates a random API key at every start and 401s everything without it. With `WAHA_API_KEY` empty, *inbound still works* (the webhook is WAHA→API) while outbound replies fail 401 — a bridge that looks alive and silently never answers a guest. Documented in `.env.example` and the runbook with a verification curl.

**3. Provider default.** `WHATSAPP_PROVIDER` defaults to `cloud_api`, so replies go to Meta even when a WAHA session is paired and receiving. Now called out in both docs.

Verified live on the paired session: inbound webhook → pipeline → AI reply → WAHA `/api/sendText` 201 → message on the phone.

author: sharkyger
body:
## What

Removes `CLAUDE.md` from this public repository and ignores it by name.

## Why

`CLAUDE.md` is the per-repo instruction file for agent sessions. It carries internal detail with no business in a public repo:

- the orchestrator layout under `~/agency-system` and how handoff briefs flow
- the Slack channel and script paths used to report progress
- internal memory filenames
- a reference to a fingerprint denylist of the operator’s non-persona identities

No credentials, keys or tokens. But it describes how the fleet is run, and the last item signals that separate identities exist and are actively filtered, which is the kind of hint that invites digging.

Ignoring it by name means a `git add -A` cannot republish it by accident. Same fix already applied in `safe-fetch` and `claude-code-cve-gate`.

## Limit, stated plainly

This removes the file **going forward only**. It remains in this repository’s history and in any existing fork or clone. Genuinely erasing it would need a history rewrite and a force-push, which breaks every clone — a separate decision, deliberately not taken here given the content is embarrassing rather than dangerous.

Found by sweeping all 13 public repos for `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/`, `*.local.md`, handoff docs and `.mcp.json`. Three repos carried it: `mcp-safe-fetch`, `pip-cve-gate`, `composer-cve-gate`.

author: wishborn
body:
Prism 0.113 shipped a `Thread` contract — a stored conversation it can read history from. This is the Eloquent implementation behind it, and the first working code in this package.

```php
$thread = Thread::forParticipant($user, 'support');

$response = Prism::text()
    ->using(Provider::Anthropic, 'claude-sonnet-4-5')
    ->withThread($thread)              // everything said so far
    ->withPrompt('And after that?')    // the turn being taken now
    ->asText();

$thread->record($response->messages);  // the full exchange, tool steps included
```

## Addressed by participant *and* scope

One user holds several unrelated conversations at once — a support chat and a coding session are not the same thread and must not bleed into one another — so scope is part of the address, not a label hung off it.

Resolution is `firstOrCreate`, because a session is *resolved*, not constructed: a fresh worker asking for the same address has to land on the same conversation rather than starting a new one. That is the property the whole durable-session design rests on.

## The storage format is ours, not Prism's

Prism's `toArray()` exists to feed telemetry and debug output, and is free to change for presentational reasons. Persistence cannot be, so it does not ride on it. Two consequences:

- **Content parts carry their concrete class.** `Media::toArray()` records where a file lives but not what it *is* — an Image and a Document serialise to byte-identical arrays. Without a discriminator, every attachment would come back as whichever type we guessed.
- **Anything unmappable throws `UnmappableContent`.** Writing the row minus what would not map produces a thread that loads *without error* and replays an incomplete conversation. That failure is invisible where it happens and surfaces much later as a model that has inexplicably forgotten something.

## Three traps this had to get right

Each has a test, because each fails silently rather than loudly.

**User text would have doubled on every round trip.** `UserMessage::__construct` appends `Text($content)` to `additionalContent`, and `toArray()` emits it. Store that copy, pass it back, and the constructor appends a second one — and `text()` concatenates parts. Compounding, for as long as the thread lives.

**Ordering needs an explicit `position` column.** Neither `id` nor `created_at` is safe to order a conversation by: timestamps tie when a multi-step tool loop writes several messages inside one second, and a tie can load a tool result ahead of the call it answers.

**Tool calls, tool results, artifacts and pending approvals round-trip whole.** Lose any and a run interrupted mid-tool cannot resume — the case threads exist to serve. A pending approval especially: it has to outlive the request that created it.

## Security notes

- Models declare explicit `$fillable` rather than `$guarded = []`, so a host app reaching for `Thread::create($request->all())` cannot set the participant columns from request input and address someone else's conversation.
- Media rehydration is restricted to Prism `Media` subclasses via `is_subclass_of`, but the **locator is data**: a row carrying a `local_path` or `url` becomes a file read or an outbound fetch at replay time. Unreachable without database write access, but it makes Prism's abstract warning concrete, and the README now says where the boundary is — treat `harness_thread_messages` as trusted storage and never let request input write to it directly.

## Verification

**18 tests / 60 assertions**, PHPStan level 6 clean, Pint clean.

The suite runs with SQLite foreign keys **on**. They default off, which is not a database any real app runs — and with them off the cascade-delete test passed a schema whose cascade never fires. That was a bug in my test environment, not the schema, and it is fixed rather than asserted around.

## Closes the harness half of s22

Remaining on the story: nothing. Threads are addressable by participant and scope, and message shape survives tool calls and results — both requirements the story called out.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 design : rendre lisibles dans **les deux thèmes** les écrans mobiles cassés, sans embellissement et **sans neutraliser une seule couleur de domaine**. Le critère est mesuré, pas jugé à l'œil : chaque encre est comparée à son fond réel (composition alpha comprise) par `src/theme/contrast.ts`, avec `4,5:1` pour le texte et `3:1` pour les glyphes.

Périmètre : `NotificationSettingsScreen`, `DailyTournamentDetailScreen`, `TimerRunScreen` — plus `CompetitionScreen`, ajoutée parce que la vérification y a mesuré `1,33:1` sur son grand bouton (« un écran cassé dans l'un des deux thèmes » est exactement le critère retenu).

**Trois choses que la mesure a imposées et qui valent plus que les couleurs elles-mêmes.**

**1. La cause racine des Notifications illisibles en clair n'était pas dans l'écran : c'était la coque.** Douze piles de navigation figeaient `contentStyle: { backgroundColor: '#0a0a0a' }`, et le thème React Navigation était en dur. Un écran clair s'affichait donc sur un fond noir — titre à `1,12:1`. La coque suit maintenant le thème :

```diff
-screenOptions={{ headerShown: false, contentStyle: { backgroundColor: '#0a0a0a' } }}
+screenOptions={shell}          // useShellScreenOptions() → theme.background
-theme={NAV_DARK_THEME}
+theme={navThemeFor(mode, theme.background)}
```

**2. Rendre `GlassBackground` derrière Notifications réparait le clair et cassait le sombre.** Les arrêts du dégradé (`#022c22 → #0d1f17 → #14532d`) ne portent pas `textMuted` à `4,5:1` — mesuré à `3,30–3,55:1`. Notifications prend donc un fond **plein** (`t.background`) ; les écrans qui possèdent leur propre dégradé le gardent. `shellBackground.test.ts` mesure les deux faits : le texte courant passe sur les arrêts, le texte atténué **non** — ce qui justifie le choix au lieu de l'affirmer.

**3. L'heuristique d'encre du minuteur était fausse par construction.** Elle comparait une luminance à un seuil médian ; sur `#2DB80E` (palette Lime) elle choisissait l'encre la moins lisible. Elle compare maintenant les deux candidates :

```ts
inkOn(bg) = contrast('#000000', bg) >= contrast('#FFFFFF', bg) ? '#000000' : '#FFFFFF'
```

et `inkOnSecondary(bg)` **cherche** l'opacité qui atteint `4,5:1` au lieu de supposer `0.5` (qui échouait sur la palette Blanc). Les dix palettes utilisateur sont intactes : seule l'encre posée dessus s'adapte.

**Ce qui n'a pas changé, volontairement.** Les couleurs de domaine restent des couleurs de domaine (`LevelColors`, médailles, RX, `#C9A227` inter-box, les 12 teintes de catégories de notification, les dix palettes du minuteur). Les variantes **claires** de ces teintes ont été assombries d'un cran (`src/theme/hues.ts`, `palette.ts`) parce qu'elles étaient calibrées pour le sombre : même sens, même famille, lisible. Un nettoyage qui les aurait grisées serait le bug inverse.

`CompetitionScreen` : `#fff` sur l'accent argenté (`2,56:1`) → `theme.onAccent` ; `#fff` sur `ctaBg` (`1,33:1`) → `theme.text` ; et deux libellés qui utilisaient `theme.accent` **en texte** (`2,31:1`) → `theme.accentText`.

`lightTheme.textMuted` passe à `#646b78` : `#6b7280` ne dépassait le seuil que de `0,03` sur les blocs réellement mesurés, donc la marge est prise et non espérée. L'écart encre-à-encre avec `textSecondary` tombe à `1,41:1` — la hiérarchie reste distinguable, mais c'est le plafond.

## Vérification

- Jest **47 suites / 802 tests** ✅, `tsc` ✅, ESLint sans erreur.
- Cinq suites neuves sont **discriminantes** : elles mesurent aussi les défauts historiques (`#fff` sur l'accent, `#EAB308` sur carte claire, `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` sur la palette Blanc, `#fff` sur `ctaBg`) — un contrôle qui ne sait pas échouer ne prouve rien.
- Vérification E2E au pixel dans les deux thèmes (arbre applicatif complet, A/B par permutation de bundles) : mesures avant/après et captures dans les commentaires de la PR. Une **baisse assumée** y est nommée : le CTA sombre passe de `10,83` à `10,36:1` — le défaut « blanc sur aplat clair » n'existait pas en sombre, donc le correctif n'y est pas un gain.
- Hors périmètre, mesuré et **non corrigé** (phase 2, couleur de domaine) : le bandeau doré clair à `~3,50:1` et les pastilles `+25` à `4,04–4,16:1`.

author: rome-1
body:
### Summary

A pattern written `for ($K in $OBJ)` also matches `for..of` source in JavaScript/TypeScript. Since `for..of` over an array is one of the commonest loops in modern JS, any rule keying on for-in to mean *"iterating object keys"* over-matches heavily.

### Reproduction (1.22.0)

```yaml
# rule.yaml
rules:
  - id: forin-only
    languages: [javascript]
    severity: WARNING
    message: matched a for-IN loop
    patterns:
      - pattern: |
          for ($K in $OBJ) { ... }
```

```js
// forof.js
const arr = [1, 2, 3];
for (const x of arr) {
  console.log(x);
}
```

```
$ opengrep scan -f rule.yaml forof.js
1 finding     # expected 0
```

The conflation is one-directional — a `for..of` pattern correctly does **not** match `for..in` source:

| pattern | vs `for..in` source | vs `for..of` source |
|---|---|---|
| `for ($K in $OBJ)` | 1 ✅ | **1 ❌ (expected 0)** |
| `for ($K of $OBJ)` | 0 ✅ | 1 ✅ |

### Cause

`js_to_generic.ml` desugars both loops into `ForEach`, but asymmetrically:

```ocaml
| ForIn (v1, t, v2) -> ... G.ForEach (pattern, t, v2)                       (* bare *)
| ForOf (v1, t, v2) -> ... G.ForEach (pattern, t,
      G.Call (G.IdSpecial (G.ForOf, t) |> G.e, fb [ G.Arg v2 ]) |> G.e)     (* wrapped *)
```

So a for-in pattern has a bare metavariable in the iterated position, and `$OBJ` binds to the entire marker call. The reverse works because a for-of pattern carries a marker that for-in code lacks.

### Why this can't be worked around in a rule

Adding `pattern-not` for the for-of form does not suppress it — the negation is subject to the same conflation. Only a text-level `pattern-not-regex: 'for\s*\([^)]*\bof\b'` works, which rule authors are unlikely to discover.

### Fix

In `m_for_each`: if the target is a for-of and the pattern is not, they are different loops, so fail before matching. Languages that never emit the marker (Python's `for x in xs`, Go, PHP, Java, Scala) are unaffected — neither side is wrapped.

I considered instead marking `for..in` symmetrically in `js_to_generic`, which is arguably tidier, but that changes the generic AST shape for every JS for-in loop and so touches `Meta_AST`, `AST_generic_to_v1`, `AST_to_IL` and the v1 interface. This fix is contained to the matcher. Happy to switch approaches if you'd prefer the AST-level one.

### Tests

`tests/patterns/js/misc_forin_not_forof.{sgrep,js}` — one for-in loop and one for-of loop with identical bodies, so only the loop keyword can distinguish them.

### What I verified, and what I did not

Verified: the defect and its direction empirically against 1.22.0; the cause by reading `js_to_generic.ml` and `m_for_each`; that the patched `Generic_vs_generic.ml` parses (`ocamlc -stop-after parsing`), including confirming that check rejects a deliberately broken edit.

**Not verified: I did not build opengrep locally** — the opam switch and submodule fetch were more than the shared machine I'm on could reasonably take — so I have not type-checked the change or run the test suite. I'm relying on CI, and I'll iterate promptly on anything it reports.

### How I found it

While measuring false-positive rates for a rule pack across a corpus of open-source repositories. Three prototype-pollution rules keyed on for-in were producing large numbers of false positives; roughly half traced to this.

body:
Every Moon release has shipped `latest.json` with `"notes": ""` - the field the in-app updater shows as "what's new". tauri-action fills it from `releaseBody` **at build time**, and the workflow never passed one; the cut-release flow's hand-written notes edit the release page *afterwards*, which never reaches `latest.json`. So auto-updaters - the users who never visit the releases page - saw nothing, including for releases whose notes carried behavior warnings (the 0.0.73 machine-access flip is the case that exposed this). ## What changed ```mermaid flowchart LR A["git log prev-tag..tag"] -->|new step, pre-build| B["releaseBody"] B --> C["initial release page body"] B --> D["latest.json notes
= what the updater shows"] E["hand-written notes
(cut-release flow)"] -->|after build, unchanged| C ``` - `checkout` gains `fetch-depth: 0` - the changelog diffs against the previous `moon-v*` tag, which a depth-1 clone cannot see. - A `Generate updater changelog` step builds "Changes since moon-vX.Y.Z" from `git log --no-merges` (capped at 40 lines), on both trigger paths (tag push and workflow_dispatch). - `tauri-action` receives `releaseBody`, landing it in both the initial page body and `latest.json`. The richer hand-written notes still replace the page body after the build exactly as before - this changes what the **updater** shows, from nothing to the commit list. Takes effect on the first `moon-v*` tag built after this merges (i.e. 0.0.76).

body:
## What

Removes `CLAUDE.md` from this public repository and ignores it by name.

## Why

`CLAUDE.md` is the per-repo instruction file for agent sessions. It carries internal detail with no business in a public repo:

- the orchestrator layout under `~/agency-system` and how handoff briefs flow
- the Slack channel and script paths used to report progress
- internal memory filenames
- a reference to a fingerprint denylist of the operator’s non-persona identities

No credentials, keys or tokens. But it describes how the fleet is run, and the last item signals that separate identities exist and are actively filtered, which is the kind of hint that invites digging.

Ignoring it by name means a `git add -A` cannot republish it by accident. Same fix already applied in `safe-fetch` and `claude-code-cve-gate`.

## Limit, stated plainly

This removes the file **going forward only**. It remains in this repository’s history and in any existing fork or clone. Genuinely erasing it would need a history rewrite and a force-push, which breaks every clone — a separate decision, deliberately not taken here given the content is embarrassing rather than dangerous.

Found by sweeping all 13 public repos for `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/`, `*.local.md`, handoff docs and `.mcp.json`. Three repos carried it: `mcp-safe-fetch`, `pip-cve-gate`, `composer-cve-gate`.

author: steipete
body:
Three small fixes: the last unreachable timeout in the Connect path, and both open CodeQL alerts.

### Dealer WebSocket ignored the configured timeout

`getConnectionID` hardcoded `context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)`, so `--timeout` / `SPOGO_TIMEOUT` never reached the dealer handshake. It was the remaining way `spogo status` could fail on a slow link regardless of what the user configured. The client's timeout is now threaded through from `ensureConnectDevice`, following the same semantics #48 established for the cookie-token client: zero falls back to the shared 10s default, a positive value becomes the deadline, and a negative value stays unlimited.

### CodeQL #2 (high): incomplete multi-character sanitization

`tocFromHtml` in `scripts/build-docs-site.mjs` stripped heading anchors with a non-global `replace`, so only the first anchor per heading was removed. `escapeHtml` downstream meant this was not a live injection, but the sanitizer is now a straightforward tokenizing pass that drops every anchor, including repeated and nested ones, rather than a regex that reconstructs markup.

All 14 existing tables of contents render byte-for-byte identically after the change, and the new path was checked against repeated anchors, nested anchors, multi-heading pages, ordinary links, and literal `#` characters.

### CodeQL #1 (medium): workflow without permissions

`ci.yml` had no `permissions:` block, so its jobs ran with the repository default. The build job only checks out and runs Go tooling, so the workflow now declares `contents: read`.

## Verification

`./scripts/lint.sh` reports 0 issues, `./scripts/check-coverage.sh 90` passes at 90.7%, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, and `go test -race ./internal/spotify` are green, and `make docs-site` builds cleanly.

## Summary
- Adds `doc/plan-auth-chrome-and-verification-codes.md`, a living step-by-step plan for two bundled efforts, no code changes in this PR.
- **Verification codes**: stop letting Cognito generate/email signup and password-reset codes. Our own `auth-api` lambda generates the code, stores it, sends it via SES, and uses Cognito's admin API to declare the user verified once the code checks out — Cognito never sees the code. Rationale for the chosen approach (vs. SES-inbound email capture, vs. `AdminCreateUser`/`AdminConfirmSignUp` sequencing) is written into the doc's Context section, grounded in AWS's documented Cognito trigger behavior.
- **AuthChrome**: implements the Claude Design handoff (themeable brand-panel chrome around the existing unstyled auth forms) with TDD (Vitest/RTL) and BDD (Cucumber/Playwright) matching this repo's existing conventions. Once the verification-codes work lands, e2e can drive the *real* happy path for signup-confirmation and password-reset instead of negative-path-only coverage.
- Steps are numbered and dependency-ordered (backend → frontend → integration → e2e). Each future session implements one step, updates this doc's checkboxes/Progress Log, and stops for review — the doc, not conversation history, is the source of truth across sessions.

## Test plan
- [ ] This PR is doc-only; nothing to run. Review the plan itself, especially:

author: hammergs
body:
> #8804 has merged, so this is retargeted to `main` and stands on its own.

## What this changes

The bots now switch their own heat-generating equipment off when a unit runs hot and back on once it cools. Until now they shed stealth armor and nothing else, so three other concealment systems ran permanently at 6 to 10 heat a turn each, Nova CEWS at 2, and the radical heat sink was never switched on at all - a unit carrying one fought on roughly half the cooling it was built with. A human player flips all five by hand every turn.

Closes #8802

**What gets managed**

- Null Signature, Void Signature and the Chameleon Light Polarization Shield are shed at 14 heat, where shutdown rolls begin, and restored at 5 heat or below. The gap between the two thresholds is deliberate: a single threshold would switch a unit sitting on it on and off every turn.
- Nova CEWS is shed only once nothing cheaper is left to drop. Switching it off costs the unit its network link, and at 2 heat a turn it buys much less relief than a concealment system does.
- The radical heat sink is switched on while the unit needs the cooling and the odds are still better than even - three consecutive uses at 3+, 5+ and 7+, then a turn of rest rather than a 10+ roll that destroys the system permanently. Resting drops the stress counter on its own.
- Stealth armor behaves exactly as before, including its range and TSM branches.

**Where it lives**

`BotClient.toggleStealth()` moves into a new `BotHeatEquipmentManager` rather than growing `BotClient` further, taking `wantsStealthHeatForTsm()` and `isAdjacentToEnemy()` with it. `BotClient` loses 149 lines and gains a field and a one-line call. The stealth decision itself is unchanged - only renamed out of `check_ent` / `mEquip` / `total_bv` into readable locals.

This covers **both bots**: the manager hangs off `BotClient`, so Princess and CASPAR get it identically.

**Follow-up to #8775, in the same change**

Those five switchable loads come out of `Princess.recurringHeat()`. That method exists to answer "what heat can this pilot not stop paying", and after this PR the bot stops paying all five before a unit is stalled badly enough for the question to be asked. Radical heat sinks are deliberately **not** credited on the dissipation side: three turns and a roll that can destroy the system is a reprieve, not a reason to believe a unit will keep cooling.

## Testing

`./gradlew test --tests "megamek.client.bot.*"` - 476 tests, 0 failures. That includes 17 new ones in `BotHeatEquipmentManagerTest` covering shed, restore, the do-nothing band between the thresholds, each of the three concealment systems, Nova CEWS waiting its turn and then going, units that ignore heat, units owned by another player, and the radical heat sink switching on, resting once the odds turn, switching off on cooling, being left alone when already running, and being ignored once destroyed.

`BotClientStealthTest` is repointed at the new class and still passes unchanged, which is what pins the stealth move as a move rather than a rewrite.

The four `PrincessTest` cases that asserted these systems were unavoidable heat are replaced by one that asserts the opposite, which is the behaviour change this PR makes. The other 16 `CanRecoverMobilityTests` are untouched and still green.

`./gradlew compileJava compileTestJava checkstyleMain` clean. `./gradlew javadoc` run separately, clean.

**Headless.** Two scenarios were built and run through `AIMatchRunner` at 40 rounds, because no single one reaches every path.

The first puts the concealment systems on units that really carry them - Exterminator EXT-4C for the Null Signature System and the Chameleon shield, Raptor II RPT-2X for the Void Signature System, Cephalus A - against a Doloire DLR-OA lance supplying plasma. Carriers are doubled up; a single one dies before it can finish a heat-up, shed, cool-down and switch-back cycle.

The second exists because two paths cannot be reached by the first. Nova CEWS is only shed once nothing cheaper is left, and every Cephalus also carries a Null Signature System and a Chameleon shield, which always go first - so it needs a Nova-only carrier, the Pariah (Septicemia) B-Z. And a radical heat sink on a Doloire is spread across the arms and tends to be shot out by critical hits before its carrier is hot enough to want it, so it needs a sturdier home: the Lament LMT-2R.

Across both:

| System | On | Off | Heat at each switch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Null Signature System | 4 | 4 | on at 0, 1, 2, 5 - off at 16, 18, 18, 19 |
| Chameleon shield | 4 | 4 | on at 0, 1, 2, 5 - off at 16, 18, 18, 19 |
| Void Signature System | 0 | 1 | off at 16 |
| Nova CEWS | 0 | 1 | off at 14, on a Pariah (Septicemia) B-Z |
| Radical heat sink | 4 | 0 | on at 16, 18, 21 (Doloire) and 16 (Lament) |

Every one of the five systems switches in a real game, and every switch landed where it should: 5 heat or below to restore, 14 or above to shed. Nothing switched in the 6-to-13 band, so the hysteresis holds - no unit hovering near the shed point ever flapped. Every radical heat sink activation reported "next failure roll needs 3", the first-use band.

## What is not proven yet

**The radical heat sink is never seen resting in a real game.** Every activation in the headless logs is a first consecutive use at 3+, because units died or games ended before any of them cooled back under the threshold. The stop-at-three rule is covered by unit test - `radicalHeatSinkIsRestedOnceTheOddsTurnAgainstTheMek` drives `manageOwnedUnits()` with three uses banked and asserts the switch-off and the packet - but it has not run in play.

Not tested in a live GUI game or a campaign. This is new bot behaviour across five systems and it wants real play before release, so it does not carry the **AI ready for Review** label.

Roughly half the headless games came back with `rounds=-1` and no result at all, at every scenario size tried. The bot log shows the switches still happening in those games, so they ran; what fails is `GameManagerSaveHelper`, where an XStream `EnumMap` converter cannot open `java.util` on a headless run. That is pre-existing and nothing to do with this PR, but it halves the yield of any headless measurement taken on this setup and is worth an issue of its own.

The 14-and-5 thresholds are a judgement call, not a rule. 14 is where shutdown rolls start; 5 is below the first movement penalty. Whether a unit should give up its concealment that early, or hold it longer and accept the heat, is exactly the sort of thing play will answer and unit tests will not.

The radical heat sink stop-at-three rule follows the IO p.89 odds, but nothing here measures whether spending three turns of stress at 14+ heat actually beats saving the system for a worse moment.

---

- [x] This PR is focused on one issue or RFE. Large refactoring or accessibility work is in its own PR
- [x] Every file in the diff has a deliberate change (no stray formatting, no unrelated files)
- [x] Tests added or updated, if this implements a rule or changes game state
- [x] Javadoc literals use `{@code true}` / `{@code null}` rather than bare or quoted text
- [x] Dev team only: if AI tools were used, the **AI Assisted Development** label is applied, and I can explain and have verified the result

author: murrayhack
body:
## Summary

Scrolling felt slow. Worth being precise about why, because the obvious explanation was wrong: **there was no artificial delay to remove.** The wait is `displayPartial()` writing the framebuffer over SPI and polling the busy pin — a few hundred milliseconds of physics.

What *was* wrong is that **every press rendered**. Five quick `down` presses queued five separate refreshes, and the panel stepped through all five intermediate positions in turn. The cursor should move five rows and the panel should draw once.

## How

Menu draws are deferred to a render thread. `Ui` takes an `on_dirty` notifier; with one, navigation marks the menu stale instead of drawing, and `flush()` renders the current state. The frontend waits `input_coalesce_ms` (default 80) after the first notification, so a burst lands before it draws.

Without a notifier `Ui` still draws inline. That keeps the existing tests asserting on a real side effect rather than a deferred one, and means the change is opt-in rather than something every caller has to know about.

## A second benefit

Rendering no longer happens on the actor thread. A full refresh takes seconds on a Pi Zero, and it was blocking the actor — so Mopidy's playback events were queueing behind the SPI bus. They no longer are.

## The floor

`input_coalesce_ms = 0` draws on every press, if you want that. But no setting makes a partial refresh faster than the panel can physically do it. If scrolling still feels like it is catching up, raise the value rather than lowering it — a longer gather means fewer, later refreshes that are each more correct.

## Verification

**Not yet run.** Five new tests cover the deferral, that a burst collapses to one draw, that `flush()` is a no-op when nothing changed, and that it will not draw over a locked panel.

```sh
pytest tests/
mopidy
```

Then open the web remote and tap `down` quickly several times. The cursor should jump to where you left it in one refresh, rather than walking there.

body:
Multica-Package: NIL-323
Delivery-Slices: NIL-341
Package-Session: 9f2f2258-95fe-4ff0-85c5-1eac93065891
Impact-Manifest: generated from git diff
Visual-Evidence: provided

## Outcome

The Team/Ownership target model exists in `main`: a `Team` singleton anchor,
a single-authority team vocabulary in `authz/team.ts` (membership from
`User.isActive`, role from `User.role` -- deliberately not duplicated into a
new table/column), a `GET /team` roster endpoint, and the fix for the one
real gap the current model had: deactivating a member used to leave their
boards and collections owned by an account that could no longer administer
them. Also fixes the `isOwner` naming split across `drawingReadRoutes.ts` and
the frontend `Sidebar`/`CollectionTeamBar` (NIL-489): a required boolean
instead of an optional three-state value nobody had written the "undefined
means owned" convention down for.

This is PR 1 of NIL-323's two planned PRs (model first, per the package's
`Erwartete Lieferung`). PR 2 builds Team Home / Canvas Shell (NIL-342-347) on
top of this.

## Scope

Changed: `Team` schema + migrations (both dialects), `authz/team.ts`
(new), `authz/boards.ts` (`transferOwnedBoards` gets a
`detachFromCollection` option, new `transferOwnedCollections`),
`routes/dashboard/team.ts` (new, read-only roster),
`auth/adminUserRoutes.ts` (deactivation now reassigns what the departing
member owned), `routes/dashboard/drawingReadRoutes.ts` (local rename,
no behavior change), frontend `Collection.isOwner` tightened to a required
boolean with every read site simplified accordingly.

Deliberately not touched, and why: `docs/architecture/OWNERSHIP_MODEL.md`
has the full list (Library/`teamId` is NIL-326's decision; no Team Home UI,
board switcher, or canvas-shell chrome -- that's NIL-323's second PR; no
team-role management UI, since there's nothing to manage that the existing
admin user-role screen doesn't already edit).

## Delivery slices

NIL-341 (Zielmodell fuer Workspace, Team, Rollen und Board-Ownership): Team
entity, membership/role vocabulary, Board Owner vs. Creator reaffirmed as
deliberate (unchanged), Collection-as-organization documented as a deliberate
design choice, offboarding fixed for both the full-deletion and plain-
deactivation paths so a departing member never leaves an ownerless or
unreachable board/collection, negative tests for both paths (see
Deliberately triggered failures), migration verified on both dialects, empty
and populated. Full write-up in `docs/architecture/OWNERSHIP_MODEL.md`.

## Contracts and data

- New model: `Team` (singleton, id `"default"`).
- New migrations: `backend/prisma/migrations/sqlite/20260823211349_add_team`,
  `backend/prisma/migrations/postgresql/20260823211543_add_team`. Applied and
  verified on an empty database and on a populated one (existing users/boards
  intact afterward) on both dialects.
- `authz/boards.ts`: `transferOwnedBoards` signature grew one optional field
  (`detachFromCollection?: boolean`, default `true` -- the existing call site
  in `userOffboarding.ts` is unaffected). New `transferOwnedCollections`.
  Both used only by `adminUserRoutes.ts`'s deactivation path in this PR.
- New route: `GET /api/team` (auth required, read-only).
- No changes to `getDrawingAccess`, `getDrawingMembership(s)`,
  `controlsDrawing`, `canViewDrawing`, `canEditDrawing`, `isOwnerAccess`,
  `getDrawingRosters`, `getCollectionRoster`, or `getDrawingMemberProjections`
  -- the signatures NIL-324/325/326 depend on are untouched.

## Impact and visual evidence

```
PR_BASE_SHA=3604cb4ea25d13a8fdc9e0000683bfebd4285887 \
PR_HEAD_SHA=8b7cd5442f0de4b092d6606c6d60f59e26c8a3c4 \
PR_LABELS_JSON='[]' node scripts/delivery-v2.cjs impact
```
-> `visual_evidence.decision: "required"` (`frontend-product-diff`):
`Sidebar.tsx`, `CollectionTeamBar.tsx`, `useDashboardDrawingActions.ts`,
`types/index.ts`.

Three screenshots attached (final PR head), taken against a seeded local
instance (two accounts, one owned-private collection, one owned+shared
collection, one shared-with-me collection at each of edit/view role):

1. **Desktop, owner's view** (1280x1100, Chromium headless) -- sidebar shows
   "Personal Notes" (Owner), "Roadmap" (Shared -- owned and shared out),
   "Sketches" (Viewer -- shared with this account at view role). Expected:
   badges match the `isOwner`/`isShared`/`sharedRole` combination described
   above; observed: matches.
2. **Desktop, non-owner member's view**, same seed data (1280x1100) --
   "Sketches" (Shared -- this account's own, shared out) and "Roadmap"
   (Editor -- shared to this account at edit role); no "Admin" nav entry, this
   account is not ADMIN. Expected/observed: matches.
3. **Mobile, owner's view** (390x844, drawer opened via the "Open menu"
   button, sidebar's own internal scroll region scrolled to show every item)
   -- same three collections and badges as (1), inside the mobile drawer.
   Expected/observed: matches.

Not covered: the isOwner-gated context menu itself is not shown in a
screenshot (asserted directly in `Sidebar.test.tsx` instead -- opening a
context menu mid-screenshot-flow adds little a static image doesn't already
show via the badges). No dark-mode screenshot; the badge/grouping logic
touched here is theme-independent and Sidebar.tsx's dark: classes are
unchanged.

## Verification

- `cd backend && npm test` -- 838/838 passed.
- `cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit` -- clean.
- `cd backend && npm run format:check` -- clean.
- `cd frontend && npm test` -- 539/539 passed.
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` (`tsc -b`) -- clean.
- `cd frontend && npm run lint` -- 2 pre-existing errors / 15 pre-existing
  warnings, all in files this PR does not touch (`Editor.tsx`,
  `Settings.tsx`, `dashboard/shared.tsx`, three `pages/editor/*` files);
  zero issues in any file this PR changed.
- Migration applied and verified on an empty database and on a populated one
  (seeded users + a board), on both sqlite and postgresql (`postgres:16-alpine`
  in a throwaway container): exactly one `Team` row seeded, zero data loss,
  `prisma migrate status` reports no drift against `schema.prisma` on either
  dialect afterward.

## Deliberately triggered failures

- `adminUserDeactivation.test.ts`: reverted the reassignment calls in
  `adminUserRoutes.ts`, confirmed the new "reassigns boards and collections"
  test fails (`prisma.drawing.updateMany` never called) -- proving the test
  would have caught this exact regression. Restored, re-verified green.
- `Sidebar.test.tsx`: reverted `isTeamCollection` to a plausible-looking but
  inverted variant (`collection.isOwner && collection.isShared === true`
  instead of `!collection.isOwner || collection.isShared === true`),
  confirmed the grouping test fails (a shared-with-me collection lands in the
  wrong section). A first version of this test only asserted presence of
  each collection name and did *not* catch that same inversion (both groups
  render collections identically, so presence alone proves nothing about
  which group); rewritten to assert document order relative to the "Team"
  header instead, then re-verified the red probe catches it.
- Postgres migration: applied the full pre-Team migration history, seeded two
  users and a board, then applied the Team migration on top -- confirms it
  runs against a populated database, not just an empty one, on both dialects.

## Remaining risks / non-goals

- No Team Home UI, board switcher, command palette, or canvas-shell context
  chrome. PR 2 of NIL-323.
- No `Library.teamId` migration -- NIL-326's decision to make; this PR only
  gives it a `Team` row to attach to later.
- `GET /team` has no consumer yet in this PR (PR 2 wires it into the shell).
  Covered by its own route test in the meantime.
- The reassignment on deactivation always targets the acting admin (the
  person performing the deactivation) with no choice of a different
  successor, unlike full offboarding's explicit successor picker. Judged
  proportionate: d

author: tfausak
body:
Proves CR 716.2b's last clause -- "Levels are not a copiable characteristic" -- at gameplay level with two cards already in `data/cards/`. No engine change, no new card: the diff is one spec case, one comment. Closes #2165.

**CR citations.** 716.2b (the clause), 716.2d (the default of 1 that makes the two readings differ), 707.2 (the copiable-values list this is an exclusion from), 707.5 / 614.12a (the copy choice is made as the permanent enters), 205.3h (Class is an enchantment type), 716.2a (the level bar's activated half, which is the observable).

**The board.** alice's Paladin Class is levelled to 2 FIRST, then her Copy Enchantment (`EntryR AsCopy`, `eligible = HasCardType Enchantment`) resolves as a copy of it. Levelling first is what makes the two readings differ: on an unlevelled original both say 1.

**The observable is CR 716.2a's ACTIVATED half, not its static one, and that is a finding.** The first draft read the level-2 section's +1/+1 off a Goblin Piker and went green under the mutation. The cause: `Pawl.Types.ProjectedCharacteristics` carries `activatedAbilities`, `replacementEffects` and `triggeredAbilities` and NO static list, so `Pawl.Engine.Projection.permanentParts` reads `Face.staticAbilities` off `Game.faceOf` -- the object's PRINTED face. A copy therefore never acquires the copied card's static abilities (CR 707.2a). Filed as #2177 and cited inline; the Piker's P/T is still asserted, marked at the site as a fence rather than as coverage, and it becomes load-bearing when #2177 lands.

What the case reads instead is which level bar the copy may activate and where that activation lands: a copy at CR 716.2d's default of 1 is offered the {2}{W} bar and reaches level 2; a copy carrying the original's level would be offered the {4}{W} bar and reach level 3.

**Design calls.** The copy is put on the stack and resolved rather than cast, since {2}{U} off a Plains board would need a second colour and the mana supply exists to make the bars affordable. The entered permanent is found by a battlefield set difference rather than by name. The copy choice is pinned by id (`copyNamed`, Pawl.CopySpec's posture) so no answerer can repair a mutation. Rejected: asserting the section's +1/+1 as the proof (green, see above), and a three-seat board (nothing here turns on "an opponent").

**Verified.** Suite 6730 -> 6731 on the original base; after merging origin/main (#2176), measured again: 6732 -> 6733.

- Mutation 1, the load-bearing one -- `Pawl.Engine.Event`'s `EntryR AsCopy` stamp also writing `Object.classLevel` from the copied source, modelling "levels are copiable". Reddened `CR 716.2d the copy's own first bar takes it to level 2, not to 3` -- the gameplay-level assertion, first in the case -- with `Just 3` where `Just 2` was expected. Run against the whole suite: 1 of 6731 failed, this case and nothing else, so no other test in the tree observes a copied level. Re-run against the merged state: same assertion, same values.
- Mutation 2 -- `filter (const False)` over `Replacement.legalCopyTargets`' result, so the Copy Enchantment copies nothing. Reddened the SAME first assertion with `Nothing` (no bar to offer, so the activation is a no-op), which is what shows the case cannot pass on a copy that copied nothing.
- Mutation 3 -- the same stamp clearing the SOURCE's `classLevel`, modelling "copying moves the level". Reddened `CR 707.2 writes the COPY: the original still holds the level it gained`.
- No mutation came back green; the one that did during derivation is #2177 above, and it is reported as a gap rather than counted as coverage.

Does the rules core case on an effect's identity: no.

**`-Werror`-invisible sites.** No constructor and no field added, so neither the `Arm.tagged` codec fallthrough (#1715) nor positional record construction (#2009/#2021) is in play. `designationSpec`'s signature needed `Monad n` once it held two cases; `-Werror` did name that one.

**Censuses and citations.** #875, #876 and #877 carry no CR 716 or CR 707 row (#876's only 707 mention is inside the Ring row, about CR 701.54b). The bare number `2165` appeared at exactly one site, `Pawl.ClassSpec`'s header bullet, rewritten here. #2165 blocks nothing.

**Deferred / filed.** #2177 (CR 707.2a, static abilities are not copied) -- found here, cited inline, not fixed: it needs a new `ProjectedCharacteristics` field and a pass over the layer fold, which is its own unit. Folded in: `Object.classLevel`'s note now cites the test that proves the clause, and the retention section's "the second card this file needs" count was dropped rather than left false by a third card.

## Resumen de cambios

Implementacion de resiliencia para notificaciones push en dos capas (FRONTEND-ONLY):

1. **Capa A — Auto-reparar al abrir la app:**
   - En \src/lib/pushNotifications.ts\, se agrego \epairSubscriptionIfNeeded()\.
   - En \src/context/AuthContext.tsx\, al autenticarse el usuario (\user !== null\), se invoca de forma silenciosa en segundo plano una vez por sesion de auth.

author: wiktorstarczewski
body:
Closes #312.

Batching proved every transaction on the main thread while single submits offloaded to the Web Worker, so a large batch froze the UI for its full duration. This routes the batch call through the worker like every other write.

## What changed

`submitNewTransactionBatch` reached the worker shim only through `createClientProxy`'s fallback, which runs the call on the main-thread WASM instance. It is now an explicit method on `WebClient` that forwards to the worker, with a `MethodName` entry and a handler on the worker side. One batch call executes and proves every transaction plus the batch proof, so this is the single longest-running WASM call the SDK makes.

`MockWebClient` deliberately keeps batching on the main thread. Mock submits round-trip the serialized mock chain through the worker, but `MockChain`'s serializer does not write `pending_batches` and its deserializer resets the field to empty — so forwarding a mock batch would discard it while the shared store had already recorded its per-transaction updates, advancing the nonce on a chain that never saw the batch. Mock clients exist for tests, where a blocked main thread costs nothing.

Request bytes are normalized once on the main thread, ahead of the worker/in-thread branch, so both paths accept exactly the same input. `normalizeSerializedRequests` lives in `js/utils.js` and is unit-tested.

## Behaviour notes

- A free main thread is not a concurrent client. The call holds `_serializeWasmCall` for the whole round trip, so reads, syncs, and other forwarded methods still queue behind it. What changes is that the page keeps painting.
- Building the requests still happens on the main thread; the builders are `SYNC_METHODS`.
- With `useWorker: false` batching still runs in-thread, exactly as before.
- Batching becoming a forwarded method carries two consequences shared with every other forwarded method: external-keystore signature callbacks now sit behind the worker's 30s-per-callback ceiling, and `lastAuthError()` no longer reports a failed batch's auth error.

## Documentation corrections

Review turned up several public claims about batching that were simply wrong, all corrected here:

- The returned number is the node's chain tip **as of submission**, not the block the batch commits in. Seven surfaces said the opposite, and `waitForConfirmation` polls against it — so it confirms only that the client caught up to the submission point. Behaviour is unchanged; the docs were wrong. Filed as #314.
- Batches always prove locally: the V1 batch API takes no prover, so `ClientOptions.proverUrl` applies to `submit()` but not to batching. The public docs said the opposite: the resource JSDoc claimed the batch used the client's configured prover, and the `submitBatch` JSDoc listed a `prover` setting that was never declared.
- The same-account rule is this wrapper's constraint, not the Rust client's — `BatchBuilder::push` takes an account per request.
- Mixing accounts does not throw, as the docs claimed. A `TransactionRequest` carries no account at all, so there is nothing per-operation to conflict with the batch-level account.
- Anchored the batch atomicity guarantee to its source. Review twice argued from `miden-client`'s per-transaction *sealing* language that a batch is not all-or-nothing on chain; the node's own RPC contract settles it the other way (`miden-node-proto-build 0.16.0-rc.1`, `rpc.proto:61`: "All transactions in this batch will be considered atomic, and be committed together or not all"). The docs now quote it, so the claim stops being re-derived from the wrong layer.

## Tests

- 13 unit tests for `normalizeSerializedRequests`, including cross-realm views and a prefix view that pins the half of the copy condition nothing else covered (verified by applying the mutant).
- `batch.browser.test.ts` spies on `Worker.prototype.postMessage` and asserts the batch **is** forwarded. It was in no shard, so CI never ran it; it is now in `ci-shard-1-tx-flows`.
- `miden_client_api.test.ts` asserts the mock batch is **not** forwarded, with `syncStateMock` as a positive control so the assertion cannot pass vacuously.

Unit suite: 399 passing.

## Deliberately not fixed here

- **Two defects in the worker's external-keystore callback bridge** (#316). A rejection thrown as a non-nullish value with no truthy `.message` — a bare string, or a wallet-style `{ code: 4001 }` — loses its reason: the bridge sends `error.message`, the worker reads the resulting `undefined` as success and resolves `undefined`, and Rust then rejects it with the generic `sign callback must return a Uint8Array` — so a user rejection surfaces as what looks like a bug in the consumer's callback. And the 30s per-callback ceiling is fixed, which batching sharpens: signing happens at push time and this wrapper treats a failed push as fatal, so one slow hardware-wallet approval fails the whole batch. Both live in the bridge shared by every worker-forwarded method, so a batch-scoped fix would leave the other ~40 broken — same reasoning as #315.
- **A dead or terminated worker wedges the client** (#315). Batching now joins the set of methods affected by this, but it is the shared worker lifecycle for all ~40 forwarded methods and needs a terminal failure state, not a flush. A version scoped to batching alone would leave the other methods silently broken.
- **`waitForConfirmation` is broken on batches** (#314). Two separate defects: its poll calls `syncStateWithTimeout`, which does not exist anywhere in the crate, so it cannot advance the sync height and times out; and even once that is fixed it would only confirm the client reached the submission tip, not that the batch committed. Review also found that the unit test covering it invents the missing method on its mock and then asserts it was called, which is why it passed. All of that is reported on #314. This PR documents the option as broken across every public surface and drops it from both examples, but does not fix the code — it is pre-existing and `#waitForBlock` is not on the batching path this PR changes.
